title: How to resolve the Python error 'attempted relative import'
body:
I've been here:

  • PEP 328 – Imports: Multi-Line and Absolute/Relative
  • Modules, Packages
  • Python packages: relative imports
  • Python relative import example code does not work
  • Relative imports in Python 2.5
  • Relative imports in Python
  • Python: Disabling relative import

and plenty of URLs that I did not copy, some on SO, some on other sites, back when I thought I'd have the solution quickly.

The forever-recurring question is this: how do I solve this "Attempted relative import in non-package" message?

ImportError: attempted relative import with no known parent package

I built an exact replica of the package on pep-0328:

package/
    __init__.py
    subpackage1/
        __init__.py
        moduleX.py
        moduleY.py
    subpackage2/
        __init__.py
        moduleZ.py
    moduleA.py

The imports were done from the console.

I did make functions named spam and eggs in their appropriate modules. Naturally, it didn't work. The answer is apparently in the 4th URL I listed, but it's all alumni to me. There was this response on one of the URLs I visited:

Relative imports use a module's name attribute to determine that module's position in the package hierarchy. If the module's name does not contain any package information (e.g. it is set to 'main') then relative imports are resolved as if the module were a top level module, regardless of where the module is actually located on the file system.

The above response looks promising, but it's all hieroglyphs to me. How do I make Python not return to me "Attempted relative import in non-package"? It has an answer that involves -m, supposedly.

Why does Python give that error message? What does by "non-package" mean? Why and how do you define a 'package'?

title: How do I change the name of an imported library?
body:
I am using jython with a third party application. The third party application has some builtin libraries foo. To do some (unit) testing we want to run some code outside of the application. Since foo is bound to the application we decided to write our own mock implementation.

However there is one issue, we implemented our mock class in python while their class is in java. Thus to use their code one would do import foo and foo is the mock class afterwards. However if we import the python module like this we get the module attached to the name, thus one has to write foo.foo to get to the class.

For convenience reason we would love to be able to write from ourlib.thirdparty import foo to bind foo to the foo-class. However we would like to avoid to import all the classes in ourlib.thirdparty directly, since the loading time for each file takes quite a while.

Is there any way to this in python? ( I did not get far with Import hooks I tried simply returning the class from load_module or overwriting what I write to sys.modules (I think both approaches are ugly, particularly the later))

edit:

ok: here is what the files in ourlib.thirdparty look like simplified(without magic):

foo.py:

try:
    import foo
except ImportError:
    class foo
        ....

Actually they look like this:

foo.py:

class foo
    ....

__init__.py in ourlib.thirdparty
import sys
import os.path
import imp

class Importer(object):
    def __init__(self, path_entry):
        if not path_entry.startswith(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), 'thirdparty')):
            raise ImportError('Custom importer only for thirdparty objects')

        self._importTuples = {}

    def find_module(self, fullname):
        module = fullname.rpartition('.')[2]

        try:
            if fullname not in self._importTuples:
                fileObj, self._importTuples[fullname] = imp.find_module(module)

                if isinstance(fileObj, file):
                    fileObj.close()
        except:
            print 'backup'
            path = os.path.join(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), 'thirdparty'), module+'.py')
            if not os.path.isfile(path):
                return None
                raise ImportError("Could not find dummy class for %s (%s)\n(searched:%s)" % (module, fullname, path))

            self._importTuples[fullname] = path, ('.py', 'r', imp.PY_SOURCE)

        return self

    def load_module(self, fullname):
        fp = None
        python = False

        print fullname

        if self._importTuples[fullname][1][2] in (imp.PY_SOURCE, imp.PY_COMPILED, imp.PY_FROZEN):
            fp = open( self._importTuples[fullname][0], self._importTuples[fullname][1][1])
            python = True

        try:
            imp.load_module(fullname, fp, *self._importTuples[fullname])
        finally:
            if python:
                module = fullname.rpartition('.')[2]
                #setattr(sys.modules[fullname], module, getattr(sys.modules[fullname], module))
                #sys.modules[fullname] = getattr(sys.modules[fullname], module)

                if isinstance(fp, file):
                    fp.close()

                return getattr(sys.modules[fullname], module)



sys.path_hooks.append(Importer)

title: matplot patchcollection(s) moving and rotating, all together and each seprately, what is best?
body:
what is best practice, professional software program to user can move rotate all patchcollection together/ each seprately? to fit patch(s) to ROI get array data from an image? any tiny advice is highly appreciated. below code has 4 frame like patchcollection and 1 center patchcollection. can be moved and rotated

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.patches import Circle
from matplotlib.collections import PatchCollection
from matplotlib import transforms
import numpy as np
import time  # For calculating draw and execution speed
import os    # For reading process memory usage

# ---- Global toggle variable ----
toggle_mode = 0  # 0 = single, 1 = all


# ---- Function to create collections ----
def create_circle_collection(center_x, center_y, radius, rows, cols, spacing,
                             color, gid):
    patches = []
    for i in range(rows):
        for j in range(cols):
            x = center_x + j * spacing
            y = center_y + i * spacing
            circle = Circle((x, y), radius)
            patches.append(circle)

            center_dot = Circle((x, y), radius=0.03)
            patches.append(center_dot)

    collection = PatchCollection(patches,
                                 facecolor=color,
                                 edgecolor='black',
                                 alpha=0.6)
    collection.set_gid(gid)
    return collection, patches


# ---- Setup Figure ----
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6))
ax.set_xlim(0, 20)
ax.set_ylim(0, 20)
ax.grid(True, linestyle='--', color='gray', alpha=0.7)

collections = []
patches_list = []
rotation_points = {}  # collection -> fixed rotation point
all_rotation_point = None  # for ALL mode
collection_transforms = {}

params = [(7, 7, 0.5, 1, 7, 1.0, 'skyblue', "Group1"),
          (7, 8, 0.5, 5, 1, 1.0, 'lightcoral', "Group2"),
          (8, 8, 0.5, 5, 5, 1.0, 'green', "Group3"),
          (13, 8, 0.5, 5, 1, 1.0, 'lightcoral', "Group4"),
          (7, 13, 0.5, 1, 7, 1.0, 'skyblue', "Group5")]

for cx, cy, r, rows, cols, spacing, color, gid in params:
    coll, patches = create_circle_collection(cx, cy, r, rows, cols, spacing,
                                             color, gid)
    ax.add_collection(coll)
    collections.append(coll)
    patches_list.append(patches)
    collection_transforms[coll] = transforms.Affine2D()
    rotation_points[coll] = [patches[0].center[0], patches[0].center[1]]

first_collection = collections[0]
all_rotation_point = list(rotation_points[first_collection])

# Rotation tracking
collection_angles = {coll: 0 for coll in collections}

# Dragging state
dragging = {'collection': None, 'start_pos': (0, 0)}


def rotate_collection(collection, angle_deg, pivot):
    cx, cy = pivot

    # Apply rotation incrementally to the existing Affine2D transform
    collection_transforms[collection].rotate_deg_around(cx, cy, angle_deg)

    # Update the collection's transform for drawing
    collection.set_transform(collection_transforms[collection] + ax.transData)

    # Track total rotation angle for this collection
    collection_angles[collection] = (collection_angles.get(collection, 0) +
                                     angle_deg) % 360

    print(
        f"Transform Layer Log: Rotated {collection.get_gid()} around pivot ({cx:.2f}, {cy:.2f}) by {collection_angles[collection]:.2f}°"
    )


# ---- Event Handlers ----


def on_press(event):
    if event.inaxes != ax:
        return

    global all_rotation_point

    for coll in collections:
        contains, _ = coll.contains(event)
        if contains:
            if toggle_mode == 1:
                dragging['collection'] = 'ALL'
                dragging['start_pos'] = (event.xdata, event.ydata)
                print(
                    f"---All pressed center: {all_rotation_point[0] + params[0][2]:.1f}, {all_rotation_point[1] - params[0][2]:.1f}"
                )
                return

            dragging['collection'] = coll
            dragging['start_pos'] = (event.xdata, event.ydata)

            idx = collections.index(coll)
            patch = patches_list[idx][0]
            x_new, y_new = collection_transforms[coll].transform(patch.center)
            print(
                f"{coll.get_gid()} Pressed center: {x_new:.1f}, {y_new:.1f} ")


def on_release(event):
    coll = dragging['collection']

    if coll is None:
        return  # nothing being dragged

    if coll == 'ALL':
        print(
            f"---All released center: {all_rotation_point[0]:.1f}, {all_rotation_point[1]:.1f}"
        )
    else:
        idx = collections.index(coll)
        patch = patches_list[idx][0]
        x_new, y_new = collection_transforms[coll].transform(patch.center)
        print(
            f"---Released center of {coll.get_gid()}: {x_new:.1f}, {y_new:.1f}"
        )

    dragging['collection'] = None


def on_motion(event):
    if dragging['collection'] is None or event.inaxes != ax:
        return

    # START PERFORMANCE SPEED TRACKING
    start_time = time.perf_counter()

    dx = event.xdata - dragging['start_pos'][0]
    dy = event.ydata - dragging['start_pos'][1]

    # --- RULE 1: Dragging ALL patch collections ---
    # Update global pivot and all local pivots according to dx, dy
    if dragging['collection'] == 'ALL':
        target_collections = collections
        if all_rotation_point is not None:
            all_rotation_point[0] += dx
            all_rotation_point[1] += dy
        for coll in collections:
            rotation_points[coll][0] += dx
            rotation_points[coll][1] += dy
    else:
        # --- RULE 2: Dragging SINGLE patch collection ---
        # Update only that collection's local pivot.
        # If it is the global pivot owner (first_collection), also update global pivot.
        target_collections = [dragging['collection']]
        active_coll = dragging['collection']
        rotation_points[active_coll][0] += dx
        rotation_points[active_coll][1] += dy
            
        if active_coll == first_collection:
            all_rotation_point[0] += dx
            all_rotation_point[1] += dy


    new_rotation = ""
    for coll in target_collections:
        # Mutate transform matrix layers directly
        collection_transforms[coll].translate(dx, dy)
        coll.set_transform(collection_transforms[coll] + ax.transData)


        x, y = rotation_points[coll]
        new_rotation = f"{new_rotation}{coll.get_gid()} => ({x:.2f}, {y:.2f}). "
    print(new_rotation)

    dragging['start_pos'] = (event.xdata, event.ydata)
    fig.canvas.draw_idle()

    # LOG PERFORMANCE SPEED & MEMORY
    execution_time_ms = (time.perf_counter() - start_time) * 1000
    try:
        import psutil
        process_memory_mb = psutil.Process(os.getpid()).memory_info().rss / (1024 * 1024)
    except ImportError:
        # Fallback if psutil library isn't installed
        process_memory_mb = 0.0

    print(f"   [PERF LOG] Motion Event Process Speed: {execution_time_ms:.2f} ms | App RAM Usage: {process_memory_mb:.1f} MB")


def on_key_press(event):
    global toggle_mode, all_rotation_point, rotation_points
    coll = dragging['collection']

    if event.key in ['ctrl+a', 'ctrl+A']:
        print("on_key_press")
        toggle_mode = 1 - toggle_mode
        print(
            f"Toggle mode: {'ALL GROUPS' if toggle_mode else 'SINGLE GROUP'}")
        return

    if toggle_mode == 1:
        target_collections = collections
    elif coll is not None and coll != 'ALL':
        target_collections = [coll]
    else:
        return

    if event.key in ['ctrl+r', 'alt+r']:
        # START KEY ROTATION PERFORMANCE SPEED TRACKING
        start_time = time.perf_counter()
        
        angle = 10 if event.key == 'ctrl+r' else -10

        if toggle_mode == 1:
            # --- RULE 3: Rotation ALL patch collections ---
            # Update only local pivots (to track first-circle visually), do not touch global pivot.
            for coll in target_collections:
                rotate_collection(coll, angle, all_rotation_point)
                
                # Recompute local pivot post-rotation from the first circle's live center
                first_circle = patches_list[collections.index(coll)][0]
                rotation_points[coll] = list(collection_transforms[coll].transform(first_circle.center))
        else:
            # --- RULE 4: Rotation SINGLE patch collection ---
            # Do not update any pivot. Pivot remains fixed.
            for coll in target_collections:
                rotate_collection(coll, angle, rotation_points[coll])

        fig.canvas.draw_idle()
        
        # LOG ROTATION RENDER SPEED
        execution_time_ms = (time.perf_counter() - start_time) * 1000
        print(f"   [PERF LOG] Rotation Event Render Speed: {execution_time_ms:.2f} ms")


# ---- Performance Monitor for Core Matplotlib Renderer Engine ----
def on_draw_perf_log(event):
    """Prints exactly how long Matplotlib takes to redraw the pixel canvas from scratch."""
    print(f"   [MATPLOTLIB CANVAS DRAW] Full Screen Render Pipeline complete.")

fig.canvas.mpl_connect('draw_event', on_draw_perf_log)

# ---- Connect Handlers & Render Loop ----
fig.canvas.mpl_connect('button_press_event', on_press)
fig.canvas.mpl_connect('button_release_event', on_release)
fig.canvas.mpl_connect('motion_notify_event', on_motion)
fig.canvas.mpl_connect('key_press_event', on_key_press)

plt.show()

title: gh-288: typed world-snapshot model shared by perception, candidates, brain, think and audit
body:
<!-- milestone-loop -->
Issue: gh-288

Closes #288

## What

`agent/model.py` declares the world-snapshot contract once, as `TypedDict`s: `Snapshot`, `Unit`, `Item`, `QuestEntry`, `Me`, `KnownSpell`, `Position`, `Candidate`, `ActionRecord`. `WorldState.snapshot()`, the per-section perception builders, `candidates.generate`, `Brain.decide`, `think` and the audit writer are typed against it, and the nine modules are type-checked by the plain `mypy` run in CI (tiers in `mypy.ini`). No runtime change: the values are still plain dicts.

## Why

The snapshot was an untyped `dict` read by string key in five modules, so a key renamed in perception failed silently at runtime or at the LLM. With the model, `snapshot["typo"]` in a checked module is a mypy error.

## Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Status |
|---|---|
| No `dict` snapshot access by bare string key in the listed modules | **Met, with one reading to confirm.** The proposal allows `TypedDict`s, so keys are still string literals, but they are now checked against `agent.model` instead of being bare `dict` keys. mypy does not check `.get("key")` on a TypedDict (verified: `["pending_invit"]` errors, `.get("lootabel")` does not), so `agent/tests/test_model.py` adds an AST check that every literal `.get()` key in `candidates.py` and `think.py` is a declared model key. If "no string keys at all" (dataclasses with attributes) was meant, that is not what this PR does. |
| mypy allowlist includes them, CI green | **Met for the nine modules; the rest of `agent/perception/` remains (#415).** After merging `main` (#375 tiers), `mypy.ini` has `agent.model` in the **strict** tier and `agent.candidates`, `brain`, `think`, `audit`, `perception.snapshot`, `.nearby`, `.inventory`, `.quest_log` in **checked** (no section, so they are type-checked by the plain `mypy` run CI does). They were first in `legacy` (`ignore_errors`), which would have silenced them; they are out, `BASELINE` in `scripts/tests/test_mypy_ratchet.py` is updated, and the separate `SNAPSHOT_TYPED` list and this PR's edit to `scripts/check.sh` are gone. The `agent.perception.*` wildcard is narrowed to the six dirty modules (`fields`, `objects`, `resolution`, `trade_state`, `windows`, `world`; 99 errors, mostly mixin attributes), so legacy goes 34 -> 35 entries (4 modules out, 1 wildcard replaced by 6), no module newly in legacy. Typing those six is what remains in #415. The other eight of the nine fail `disallow_untyped_defs` (about 32 errors), so they stay checked, not strict. |
| Golden-shape test unchanged before/after | **Met.** `agent/tests/test_perception_golden.py` and its fixture are untouched and pass. |

## Overlap with open PRs

title: feat(reporting): add multi-format document generation and clinical figure library
body:
## Summary of Changes

This PR enhances the `shinystat` biostatistical skill with an end-to-end publishing pipeline capable of generating multi-format publication documents with embedded 300 DPI medical figures:

### 1. 300 DPI Clinical Figure Library (`medstat.figures`)
- Implemented 10 clinical plot generators in `src/medstat/figures/`:
  - `plot_forest`: OR/HR/RR on logarithmic scale with 1.0 reference line
  - `plot_kaplan_meier`: Stratified survival curves with aligned Numbers at Risk table and log-rank p-value
  - `plot_roc_curve`: Empirical ROC with Youden's J optimal cutpoint, 45° chance line, DeLong 95% CIs, and paired overlay
  - `plot_calibration`: Decile bins, Wilson 95% CIs, LOESS smooth curve, Brier score, and ICI
  - `plot_dca`: Decision Curve Analysis Net Benefit against Treat All and Treat None
  - `plot_bland_altman`: Pairwise difference vs average, 95% Limits of Agreement, and Bland-Altman (1999) large-sample CIs
  - `plot_love`: Austin 2009 standardized mean difference balance before/after PSM with 0.10 SMD threshold
  - `plot_retention_flow`: Pure-Matplotlib STROBE / CONSORT participant disposition flowchart
  - Diagnostics: `plot_missingness_map`, `plot_schoenfeld_residuals`, `plot_mice_diagnostics`
- Standards: 300 DPI resolution, Okabe-Ito / Tol colorblind-safe palettes, Thai typography fallback chain (`Sarabun`, `Thonburi`, `Sukhumvit Set`, `Arial`).
- Auditability: Every figure returns `FigureResult(png_path, alt_text, caption, source_df, csv_path)` and auto-exports plotted data to CSV.

### 2. Format-Agnostic Report Intermediate Representation (`medstat.reporting.ir`)
- Single Source of Truth (`ReportDocument`) composing structured blocks (`HeadingBlock`, `ParagraphBlock`, `TableBlock`, `FigureBlock`, `CalloutBlock`) linked to immutable `results_dict`.

### 3. Multi-Format Renderers (`medstat.reporting.renderers`)
- **Standalone HTML (`.html`)**: **Default deliverable format**. Single offline file with embedded base64 figures and responsive ICMJE table styling.
- **Word (`.docx`)**: Native `.docx` via `python-docx` with OpenXML `<w:tblBorders>` 3-rule ICMJE table borders and 6.5 in figures.
- **PowerPoint (`.pptx`)**: Native 16:9 widescreen presentation via `python-pptx` with 1 figure per slide layout and structured takeaway cards.
- **Markdown (`.md`)**: GitHub Flavored Markdown with linked assets directory.
- **Publication PDF (`.pdf`)**: Headless Chromium PDF printing via Playwright.

### 4. Pillar 5: Reporting Integrity (`medstat.reporting.integrity`)
- Numerical Traceability: Cross-checks narrative numbers against `results_dict` with strict displayed precision enforcement.
- Zero-PHI Enforcement: Regex scanner suppressing Hospital Numbers (`HN`), Thai 13-digit National IDs, phone numbers, and patient names.
- Causal Invariants: Observational PSM and regression models must explicitly state unmeasured confounding and E-values.
- Retention & Methods: Enforces participant flow accounting and statistical software disclosures.

### 5. Backward Compatibility & Living Contracts
- Extended return dictionaries across all 13 biostatistical recipes with plot-ready keys while preserving 100% backward compatibility (verified by baseline snapshot test).
- Updated `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CONTEXT.md`, and recorded **ADR 31** and **ADR 32** in `DESIGN.md`.
- Synchronized all platform mirrors (`.agent`, `.agents`, `.claude`, `.cursor`) with 100% byte-identical parity.
- Configured `.coderabbit.yaml` to skip mirror directories and focus reviews exclusively on canonical source files.

### 6. Standalone HTML Default Standardization (ADR 32)
- Standardized the default deliverable format to self-contained HTML (`.html`) with embedded Base64 figures (300 DPI) and responsive ICMJE/NEJM/JAMA table styling across both canonical (`shinystat`) and cloud (`shinystat-cloud`) skills.
- Updated Grilling Gate (Trigger 5) so that unspecified document formats default to HTML without blocking execution or halting.
- Maintained 100% byte-identical mirror parity (`.agent`, `.agents`, `.claude`, `.cursor`, global `~/.gemini/config/skills/`) and updated `~/Desktop/shinystat-cloud.zip`.

### 7. CodeRabbit Review Feedback Fixes
- **Numerical Precision Tolerance Guards (`src/medstat/reporting/integrity.py`)**:
  - Enforced strict `abs_diff <= abs_tol` for `|tn| <= 1.0` using displayed precision scaling (`min(0.02, 10^(-dec_digits))`), blocking 1% relative tolerance check from accepting spurious mismatches (e.g. 0.860 vs 0.865).
  - Restricted percentage-scale comparisons to tokens explicitly containing `%` or on percentage scales (`|tn| > 1.0` and `|kn| <= 1.0`), eliminating spurious matches like `p = 0.02` vs `0.004`.
  - Audited numeric values against `results_dict` first; context-based exemptions (e.g., `95% CI`, `Table 1`, `alpha = 0.05`) now apply strictly as a fallback for unmatched numbers, preventing false-exemption of clinical metrics like `95% sensitivity` and `10 events`.
- **Paired ROC Source Data Export (`src/medstat/figures/roc.py`)**:
  - Updated `plot_roc_curve` to build `source_df` with combined primary and paired ROC curve coordinates (`Model`, `False_Positive_Rate`, `True_Positive_Rate`, `Threshold`) before calling `export_source_data`, ensuring both curves are fully exportable in `FigureResult.source_df` and accompanying CSV.
- **Cloud Recipe Docx Fallback & Numerical Traceability (`packaging/cloud/shinystat-cloud/references/report-builder.md`)**:
  - Replaced `generate_docx_report` alias in `ImportError` fallback with a wrapper that safely redirects explicit `.docx` output paths to `.html`.
  - Implemented standalone numerical traceability in `verify_standalone_integrity`, matching narrative numbers against `results_dict` with displayed precision.
- **Test Coverage**: Added dedicated unit tests in `test_reporting_integrity.py`, `test_figure_library.py`, and `test_shinystat_cloud.py`.

### 8. Verification
- `uv run pytest tests/unit/ tests/e2e/`: 421 passed, 0 failures.
- `uv run ruff check .` & `uv run ruff format --check .`: Clean compliance, 0 lints.

title: feat(OMN-20071): the durable-evidence gate reads the product repository's contract first
body:
OMN-20071

## Summary
The DurableEvidenceGate's contract_on_occ_main check read the ticket's contract from the onex_change_control governance ref only, so a ticket whose contract is contracts/<ticket>.yaml in a cut-over repository (omnimarket, omnibase_infra) could not pass it without an OCC copy. After this change the gate reads the product repository first, in the omniclaude Done gate's order (omniclaude#2510 merged; omniclaude#2651 open): the contract at each merged PR's merge commit; the newest merged contract-carrying PR per repository decides; the verdict is the "repo-evidence / dod-verify" check run on that PR's head (newest run by id must be completed with conclusion success); the contract at that head must equal the merged one; every labelled acceptance criterion in the ticket description must be bound. onex_change_control decides only when no merged PR carries an adopted repo contract, and decides as before.

## What changed
On a repo-governed ticket contract_on_occ_main carries the repo verdict; receipt_tracked and contract_cites_merge_commit report "Not applicable"; released_on_publishing_repo covers every merged PR in a publishing repository; defect_prevention_gate reads the governing repo contract; done_class_label is backed by the repo verdict. The caller's contract copy is not compared against the merged one, because an OCC copy does not govern such a ticket. The check id contract_on_occ_main is kept: an onex_change_control contract greps a receipt for "contract_on_occ_main passed=True" and an omniclaude module names it. Its meaning is stated once, on the enum member. Files changed: src/omnimarket/nodes/node_dod_verify/services/durable_evidence_gate.py (evaluate_repo_evidence, RepoContractReader, RepoEvidenceCheckRunsReader, the optional reader pair on DurableEvidenceGate, merged_prs and ticket_description on evaluate/evaluate_default/enforce/enforce_default; released, defect-prevention and done-class checks moved into helper methods with the same messages); src/omnimarket/nodes/node_dod_verify/models/model_durable_evidence_gate.py (ModelTicketMergedPr, ModelRepoContractRead, ModelRepoEvidenceCheckRun, ModelRepoEvidenceVerdict, EnumRepoContractReadStatus, EnumRepoEvidenceOutcome). No new module.

## Tests
tests/unit/nodes/node_dod_verify/test_durable_gate_repo_first_omn_20071.py, 35 tests: 5 selected by -k admits, 14 by -k refuses, 15 by -k replay, 1 by -k no_module. The replay fixture tests/unit/nodes/node_dod_verify/fixtures/omn20071_occ_only_gate_replay.json holds 14 OCC-only cases whose decisions were recorded by the gate at 3fe55c842 before the change (5 pass, 9 fail). At 3fe55c842 the test file fails at collection with ImportError. Positive controls: altering one recorded decision fails 1 replay test; removing the unbound-criterion rule fails the unbound refusal test. The 7 existing gate test files plus the new one: 161 passed.

## Contract
contracts/OMN-20071.yaml (new in omnimarket) binds AC4 to -k admits and -k refuses, AC5 to -k replay, AC6 to -k no_module.

## Not changed
node_dod_verify's handler does not construct DurableEvidenceGate (no production caller in this repository), so the /onex:dod_verify verdict is unchanged by this PR; the node's own contract lookup without --contract-path still searches onex_change_control only.

Lab: host h101, lane occ-ret-durable-gate-c4-5d21, head 0c295b83d. (1) node_dod_verify --ticket-id OMN-20071 --contract-path contracts/OMN-20071.yaml --execution-audience hosted: verified, 4 of 4 checks verified; same command with the two gate files at 3fe55c842: failed, 4 of 4 checks failed. (2) the gate run directly with live GitHub reads and the onex_change_control clone at origin/dev 198b7f902a: the S5 pilot ticket (an omnimarket contract, merged omnimarket#3277, #3284, #3380 and #3515) before (3fe55c842) decided on the OCC path, contract_on_occ_main passed against the OCC contract, status fail on done_class_label (the ticket has no done-class label); after, contract_on_occ_main passed from omnimarket#3515 at head e69e8b9f and merge ea44bfcf with repo-evidence / dod-verify run 113102713137, status fail on done_class_label only; with source-done supplied, status pass; with a planted unbound AC7, contract_on_occ_main refused naming AC7. an OCC-only ticket (no repo contract at the merges of omniclaude#2573 and #2618): all six checks identical before and after (status fail: released_on_publishing_repo MERGED_UNRELEASED for omniclaude, done_class_label no label).

title: fix(test): wait for the shared-channel run before shutdown in pause tests
body:
## Summary

`test_shared_channel_pause_broadcast_failure_keeps_the_pause[sqlite]` (added in #2960) flaked in a merge-queue run with `assert [] == ['task_paused']`.

The shared-channel leaf commits the pause and the channel's `channel_result` in one transaction (`finalize()` in `src/xagent/web/services/shared_channel_execution.py`), and only then awaits `publish_interruption_pause`. The test helper `_run_shared_channel_turn` returned as soon as the channel result was readable, and its `finally` then called `background_task_manager.shutdown()`, which cancels running tasks. When the run had not yet resumed past the commit, it was cancelled before publishing, so no `task_paused` call was recorded.

The fix makes the helper wait for the registered background run to finish before shutting down. Production code is unchanged: committing first and broadcasting best-effort afterwards is the documented design.

The same helper backs three tests, all of which are now deterministic:
- `test_shared_channel_pause_broadcast_failure_keeps_the_pause` (the flaky one)
- `test_shared_channel_turn_pauses_and_its_channel_reads_interrupted` (same positive assertion, same race)
- `test_shared_channel_turn_that_does_not_pause_fails_as_before` (its `task_paused == []` assertion could previously pass vacuously)

Other tests that assert pause broadcasts (`test_persistence_failure_pause.py`, `test_execution_event_persistence_settlement.py`) await `_schedule_bg` inline and are not affected.

## Test plan

- Reproduced the CI failure by temporarily adding `await asyncio.sleep(0.2)` before the `publish_interruption_pause` call: all three shared-channel pause tests failed with the CI assertion before the fix and passed after it.
- Without the injected delay: `-k "shared_channel and sqlite"` passed 50/50 runs.
- `pytest -n 8 tests/web/services/`: 4693 passed; the 1 failure (`test_mcp_shared_env_hook.py::test_caller_id_env_var_name_matches_aws_connector_literal`) is `ModuleNotFoundError: boto3` in the local environment and is unrelated.
- `pre-commit run --all-files`: Python hooks pass (the frontend npm hooks need `node_modules`; no frontend changes).

title: Tighten YouTube tiering, cache fallback and the install remedy
body:
First of five PRs working through the audit (sections 2–5).

## Changes
- **`_tier_for` trusts `-orig`.** When an `-orig` track exists, only automatic tracks in its language family are `asr_platform`. The uploader's declared `language` is used only when there is no `-orig` track. Before this, a wrong declaration rated the auto-translation in that language as the transcription.
- **Cache fallback only after transport failure.** `list` and `expand` fall back only on `AcquisitionFailed`, `BotCheck`, `RateLimited`, `TransportContractChanged` and `TransportNotInstalled`. `LectureUnavailable`, `AgeRestricted` and `RegionBlocked` now propagate, so the "source could not be reached" notice can no longer be false. This now matches AGENT_GUIDE.
- **pipx remedy** now injects `"yt-dlp[default]"`. The `ImportError` path has lost its `pragma: no cover` and is tested through `sys.modules["yt_dlp"] = None`.
- **Non-string `language`** is ignored instead of raising `AttributeError`.

## Verification
- `coverage run -m pytest`: 1013 passed, coverage 100%
- ruff format/check and mypy are clean
- `pytest -m canary`: 7 passed (live)

title: fix(ci): stop test pollution in the whole-app backend run; skip visual-regression off darwin
body:
## CI: stop test pollution and platform-specific visual baselines

Backend Tests and E2E (offline) were already failing on `develop` (and on PR #803).

### Backend (`huf/ai/tests`, no production code)
The whole-app `bench run-tests --app huf` runs every module in one process, and several tests leaked process-wide state: they replaced real modules in `sys.modules` (`huf.ai.agent_hooks`, `agent_integration`, orchestration…) with stubs and never restored them, assigned `frappe.db` / `get_meta` / `has_permission` / `conf.developer_mode` on the real `frappe`, popped `frappe.model`, and leaked a MagicMock `RunBudget` into a ContextVar. Later modules then failed with `ImportError: cannot import name 'run_agent_for_doc'`, `No module named 'agent_under_test'`, etc.

Local whole-app run on a bench: 539 tests / 219 errors (CI) → 3657 tests / 7 errors / 7 failures. The remaining failures need CI-only dependencies (`huf_tools` hook, ERPNext `Lead`, view-all record-auth checks that also fail when run alone) or depend on test order; not addressed here.

### E2E
`visual-regression.spec.ts` has committed baselines only for `-darwin`; on the Linux runner every `toHaveScreenshot` fails on a missing baseline. `playwright.config.ts` now skips those specs unless running on darwin or `UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS` is set. The other 44 specs are unaffected. A later `workflow_dispatch` job can generate Linux baselines to restore visual coverage.

Updates `mcp` from 1.28.1 to 2.3.0
Release notes

Sourced from mcp's releases.

v2.3.0

pip install -U mcp. Docs: https://py.sdk.modelcontextprotocol.io/

Mostly fixes, plus three new options. A few things behave differently, so skim these first:

Behaviour changes

httpx2>=2.10.0 is now required (#3600)

  • It was >=2.5.0. The new max_sse_event_size option needs it.
  • Nothing to do unless you pin httpx2 below 2.10.

A tool with an invalid x-mcp-header annotation fails at registration (#3620)

  • @mcp.tool(), add_tool and Tool.from_function raise InvalidSignature, naming the tool and the problem.
  • Until now the server started, and 2026-07-28 clients silently dropped the tool from their listing.
  • Refused: anything other than a plain str, int or bool parameter (so also str | None, float, lists and enums), a header name that isn't a valid token, and two names that differ only by case.
  • For an optional header parameter, give the schema directly: Annotated[str | None, WithJsonSchema({"type": "string", "x-mcp-header": "Region"})] = None.

Empty _meta and params are no longer sent (#3628)

  • On 2025-11-25 and earlier connections, 2.x sent "_meta": {} on every request. Some servers reject that. It is now left out, as in v1.
  • ping and list requests without a cursor go out with no params member.
  • On the receiving side ctx.meta is None rather than {}, and middleware sees ctx.params as None for a request without params.
  • 2026-07-28 connections are unchanged.

initialize leaves out experimental when none is configured (#3614)

  • It used to send "experimental": {}. server/discover already left it out.
  • Client code reading capabilities.experimental on a legacy connection should handle None.

Mcp-Param-* validation looks the tool up by name (#3630)

  • MCPServer no longer runs tools/list for every tools/call, so middleware no longer sees that extra request.
  • The registered schema is what gets checked. Middleware that filters or rewrites tools/list no longer affects it.

An interactive OAuth login no longer counts against request timeouts (#3635)

  • The timeout pauses while OAuthClientProvider waits on redirect_handler and callback_handler.
  • This fixes Client(mode="auto") settling on 2025-11-25 when the login took longer than 10 seconds.
  • A request timeout no longer ends a login nobody finishes. Put a limit inside callback_handler if you need one.

New

  • max_sse_event_size= on streamable_http_client and StreamableHttpParameters. The default stays 1 MiB per SSE event; raise it, or pass None, for larger tool results (#3600).
  • MCPServer(subscriptions=False) stops serving subscriptions/listen and advertises listChanged and subscribe as false (#3626).
  • Server(get_tool_input_schema=...) lets a low-level server supply a tool's schema for header validation without running its tools/list handler (#3630).
  • Client.call_tool re-lists the tools and retries once after a HeaderMismatch (-32020) rejection (#3627).

Fixes

  • ctx: Context[AppState] works on prompts and resource templates, not only on tools (#3624).
  • An explicit "structuredContent": null is checked against the output schema instead of being treated as missing (#3621).
  • A progress_callback that raises no longer fails the call on an in-process Client(server) (#3623).
  • Client OpenTelemetry spans record JSON-RPC error responses. With mode="auto", connecting to a server without server/discover now shows one ERROR span for the probe (#3629).
  • stdio_client resolves the executable off the event loop on Windows (#3510).

... (truncated)

Commits

4.1.0 (2026-10-09)

  • Import :data:~filelock.OwnerMode, :data:~filelock.CompromiseReason and :data:~filelock.has_fcntl from filelock. :pr:790
  • :class:~filelock.AcquireReturnProxy is generic in the lock type, so with lock.acquire() as held: types held as the lock's own class. :pr:803
  • A :class:~filelock.Timeout from a soft lock names a holder on another host or in another PID namespace, which no contender ever reclaims. :pr:815
  • :attr:~filelock.SoftFileLock.is_lock_held_by_us and :attr:~filelock.MarkerSoftFileLock.is_lock_held_by_us return False for a marker an earlier process with the same PID left behind. :pr:774
  • :class:~filelock.SoftFileLock removes its marker when writing it fails and closing the descriptor fails too, so the lock path no longer stays blocked. :pr:775
  • :meth:~filelock.BaseFileLock.acquire and :meth:~filelock.BaseAsyncFileLock.acquire no longer wait past timeout when poll_interval is longer than the time left. :pr:777
  • :class:~filelock.SoftReadWriteLock ignores a generation-log entry whose name is not 20 ASCII digits, which used to stop its heartbeat thread or delete real generations. :pr:778
  • :class:~filelock.ReadWriteLock, :class:~filelock.SoftReadWriteLock and their async wrappers treat a :data:math.inf timeout like -1 and raise :class:ValueError for a blocking nan one. :pr:779
  • :class:~filelock.ReadWriteLock and :class:~filelock.SoftReadWriteLock accept a timeout above :data:threading.TIMEOUT_MAX instead of raising :class:OverflowError. :pr:780
  • :meth:~filelock.BaseFileLock.acquire raises :class:ValueError for a blocking nan timeout or a poll_interval above :data:threading.TIMEOUT_MAX, and treats a :data:math.inf timeout like -1. :pr:781
  • :class:~filelock.SoftFileLock and :class:~filelock.MarkerSoftFileLock treat a marker cut before its final newline as malformed, so a crash-truncated record self-heals and a read mid-write no longer breaks a live lock. :pr:782
  • :class:~filelock.UnixFileLock no longer deletes another process's live marker when it falls back to a soft lock on ENOSYS, and on macOS a lock path ending in a separator raises :class:FileNotFoundError instead of retrying. :pr:785
  • :class:~filelock.SoftFileLock and :class:~filelock.SoftFileLease put back a live successor's marker that a racing stale break moved aside, so a third contender no longer acquires beside the successor. :pr:786
  • :class:~filelock.StrictSoftFileLock removes every claim a failed acquire published, counts an EEXIST link that landed as published, and no longer reports is_locked after a failed claim cleanup. :pr:787
  • On Python 3.10 without the exceptiongroup backport, a release failure under the default context_error_policy no longer turns into :exc:ModuleNotFoundError; cleanup failures chain instead of grouping, and on_acquired is allowed. :pr:788
  • :class:~filelock.AsyncReadWriteLock and :class:~filelock.AsyncSoftReadWriteLock drop a task's hold when a caller cancels it during a release that still completes, instead of blocking every later writer. :pr:789
  • :class:~filelock.SoftFileLease releases a lease dropped while held, at garbage collection or interpreter exit, and raises :class:ValueError for a heartbeat_interval above :data:threading.TIMEOUT_MAX. :pr:791
  • :class:~filelock.StrictSoftFileLock judges an abandoned private record's age by the filesystem's clock, so a client clock ahead of an NFS server no longer aborts live publications. :pr:792
  • :class:~filelock.BaseAsyncFileLock raises :class:RuntimeError instead of :class:asyncio.CancelledError when its executor shuts down with the call still queued, and a waiter interrupted by anything else no longer wedges later calls. :pr:793

[v2.1.0] Better Jobs tooling, ZeroGPU quota tracking, and revamped Model Catalog

📊 Jobs: retries, rescheduling, and port exposure

Hugging Face Jobs get a batch of quality-of-life improvements this release. Jobs can now retry automatically on failure with the new attempts parameter, and you can start a fresh Job from an existing Job's saved spec (including secrets and hardware settings) with rerun_job / hf jobs rerun. Scheduled Jobs can be rescheduled — change the cron expression or preset without recreating the Job — via update_scheduled_job_schedule / hf jobs scheduled reschedule. Finally, you can now expose ports on Jobs: use expose for token-protected access and expose_public for unauthenticated access, both at creation time and on a running Job with update_job_expose / hf jobs expose.

# Retry a job up to 2 times on failure, and rerun it later from its saved spec
>>> hf jobs run --attempts 3 --detach python:3.12 python train.py
>>> hf jobs rerun <job_id>

Reschedule a scheduled job to run every day at 9:00


>>> hf jobs scheduled reschedule <scheduled_job_id> "0 9 * * 1"


Expose ports on a running Job (8000 token-protected, 9000 public)


>>> hf jobs expose <job_id> 8000 --public 9000

🤗 Track your ZeroGPU quota

The Hub now exposes a ZeroGPU quota endpoint, and huggingface_hub wraps it with a new HfApi.get_zero_gpu_quota() method returning a ZeroGpuQuota dataclass (values in GPU-seconds). This is particularly useful for apps, MCP servers and agents built on top of ZeroGPU Spaces: check how much quota is left and when it resets, and warn your users before they hit the daily limit. ZeroGpuQuota(base=2400, remaining=1810, resets_at=datetime.datetime(2026, 9, 30, 9, 12, 3, tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc), overquota_used=0)

  remaining: 1810
  base: 2400
  resets_at: 2026-09-30T18:12:03+00:00
  overquota_used: 0

Updates `multidict` from 6.7.1 to 7.0.0
Release notes

Sourced from multidict's releases.

7.0.0 is a major release. It makes istr final, adds a public C API for third-party extensions, and makes the C extension substantially faster across the board.

Breaking change. istr can no longer be subclassed, on either backend. Code that subclassed it has to wrap or convert instead. The C extension also started rejecting an argument passed both positionally and by name with TypeError, where it used to silently misbehave.

Public C and Cython API. Other C extensions and Cython modules can now create, read and mutate multidicts through a capsule, without going through the Python-level API. The capsule comes with multidict_capi.h, a cimport-able multidict/__init__.pxd and multidict.get_include(). The API includes MultiDict_ForEach() and a watchers API modeled on CPython's dict watchers. See the C API and Cython API references.

Performance. On CodSpeed's GIL-build benchmarks against 6.9.1, 82 C-extension benchmarks got faster and none got slower. Rough figures:

  • CIMultiDict keyed by plain str: construction, add(), extend(), update() and item assignment got 2 to 3.8 times faster, and lookups about 2 times faster.
  • CIMultiDict keyed by istr, and case-sensitive MultiDict: lookups, insertion and deletion got 10% to 70% faster.
  • getall() and iterating items() got about 35% faster, and the view set operations 10% to 85% faster.
  • popitem() on a whole mapping went from quadratic to linear time.
  • On the free-threaded build, measured in instructions against 6.9.1, lookups got 24% to 33% cheaper on MultiDict and 4 to 5 times cheaper on CIMultiDict with lowercase str keys, and item assignment 15% to 19% cheaper. Construction and deletion on MultiDict cost 2% to 7% more. With several threads mutating at once, a d[key] = value got about four times faster.

The pure-Python backend is unchanged in speed.

Robustness. This release fixed several crashes and leaks in the C extension, including use-after-free bugs when a key's lower() or a value's __eq__ mutated a multidict, a crash at interpreter shutdown, and table and reference leaks on the free-threaded build.

title: feat(OMN-20885): host the pr-title check-title decision as node_pr_title_check_compute
body:
## Summary
- Ticket OMN-20885 (child of the OCC retirement roll-out).
- Adds node_pr_title_check_compute: a definition-B COMPUTE node (contract.yaml, node class in __init__.py, handler HandlerPrTitleCheck.handle(request) -> result, models), registered under onex.nodes in pyproject.toml, topics onex.cmd.omnimarket.pr-title-check-requested.v1 and onex.evt.omnimarket.pr-title-check-completed.v1 declared in its contract.
- It ports the decision of the check-title bash step in onex_change_control .github/workflows/pr-title-check-reusable.yml at babdd13ce68f07df20f989f52ff1c4514d03d896. That step produces the required context pr-title / check-title on omniclaude dev today; it is also a required context on omnibase_core, omnibase_spi, omnibase_compat, omnimarket, omniintelligence, omnimemory dev and omninode_infra dev and main.
- Branch order kept: empty title refuses; author ending in [bot] admits; dependency-bump title prefix admits; release title prefix admits; OMN-<digits> anywhere admits; otherwise refuse. Output lines and exit code (0 admit, 1 refuse) equal the bash step's.
- python -m omnimarket.nodes.node_pr_title_check_compute reads {"title","author"} JSON on stdin, prints the step's lines, exits 0, 1, or 2 for a malformed request.

## Parity

title: Stop compiled modules replacing their Python module in sys.modules
body:
## Why

Re-running `from helper import f` after `f` had been called failed:

```
ImportError: cannot import name 'f' from 'helper' (.../ext/helper_ext/target/.../release/libhelper.so)
```

This first showed up when re-running an import cell in a notebook, but scripts are affected too. `module_name` defaults to the defining file's stem, and the compiled module was registered as `sys.modules[module_name]`. So it **replaced the Python module of the same name**, and later imports found the extension, which only has the `_`-prefixed functions. A file such as `utils.py` would also replace any other module registered under that name.

## What

- The compiled module is now loaded as `<module_name>_ext.<module_name>` (e.g. `helper_ext.helper`), matching its build folder and the log messages. This is one line, in xenoform's call to `load_rust_module`.
- New `test_reimport.py`: writes a `@rust` module to `tmp_path` and imports it as a **top-level** module, which is the case that collides. It calls the function, checks the Python module is still in `sys.modules`, and imports again. It failed before the fix.
- README gains a short **Notebooks** section from the same investigation. It has two rules, both checked in a real Jupyter kernel: `@rust` functions defined in a cell need a `module_name` override, and changes to `@rust` functions need a kernel restart.

## Design decisions

- **A namespaced key, not a renamed Rust module.** Python finds the init function from the last part of a dotted name (`PyInit_helper`), so the generated source, symbols, library names and existing builds are all unchanged. Renaming the module would invalidate every build, and would still collide when `module_name` matched the file name.
- **The fix is at xenoform's call site, not in `load_rust_module`.** That function is public API for loading modules built some other way, and its callers choose the name.
- **No call-time cost.** The name is only used when the module is first loaded. Calls go through the `lru_cache`d `_get_function`, which returns the function object directly. Measured over 7 × 1,000,000 calls, best run: 200.1 ns per call before, 199.1 ns after.
- `test_nested.py` loads the same library again under the bare name. pyo3 0.29 gives it a separate, working module object, so that test is unchanged.

## Tests

Run locally on GIL 3.14: ruff, ruff format, ty, pytest (114 passed, 100% coverage), all four examples. CI covers free-threaded 3.14t and 3.15, where pyo3 initialises modules differently.

title: release: promote `dev` to `main` (v0.12.0)
body:
Promotion of the release cut on `dev` (v0.12.0) into `main`.

The bump commit and its tag were created on `dev` and are already pushed. This PR
is how they reach `main` — and it is where the promotion-only gates run, which is
why the release is a pull request and not a fast-forward.

**Prefer `--merge`.** A merge commit needs nothing more. A squash is accepted too:
its tree is identical to the tagged commit's, and the next `/ship` asks once for
`--absorb-squashed-promotion` to merge `main` back into `dev`. The tag is never moved.

Opened by `/ship`.

## v0.12.0

### Feat

- **layers**: import-linter contracts own the layer map (TOM-1451, 4b-3) (#268)
- **deps**: lean base install, [data]/[research]/[trade] extras and the client smoke (TOM-1451, 4b-2) (#267)
- **api**: declared public surface with deprecation shims, one HL symbol mapping (TOM-1449, TOM-1419) (#265)
- **inference**: multiple-testing corrections, Bonferroni and Holm (TOM-1646) (#263)
- **inference**: Newey-West lags for overlapping returns (TOM-1644) (#262)

### Fix

- **data**: asof cut on each row's own wall-clock date, keeping west-of-UTC asof bars (TOM-1681) (#272)
- **data**: the pandas reader cuts at asof for any DatetimeIndex (TOM-1681) (#271)
- **deps**: client-safe numpy floor, core strategy_cache, no silent duckdb fallback (TOM-1451) (#270)
- **release**: after-release reads the quantbox-live pin from origin/main (TOM-1640) (#261)

### Refactor

- **layers**: cut every forbidden layer edge, lazy registry and one lazy helper (TOM-1451, 4b-1) (#266)

## Before / after

Base `v0.11.0` vs head `v0.12.0` (tag = `880073a`). This is a promotion: no code changes here beyond what landed on `dev` through the PRs below. Each PR carries its own base-vs-head run; this section collects them.

### Release-level checks on the tag content

- Full suite on the tag content: **3745 passed, 32 skipped**, 0 failed (forge, 2026-10-10).
- Dependency audit: **118 of 118** locked packages scanned, **0 vulnerabilities**.
- `CHANGELOG.md` at `880073a` lists the extras as `[data]/[research]/[trade]` in the v0.12.0 Feat bullet for #267.

### Each feature PR's own before / after

- [#261](https://github.com/tomlupo/quantbox/pull/261) (after-release pin): old script reads the working-tree pin `v0.7.0`; fixed script reads `origin/main` `v0.10.0`. 4 new tests, the first 3 red on the old script. No library code changes.
- [#262](https://github.com/tomlupo/quantbox/pull/262) (NW overlap): additive keyword. MA(62) known answer: SE ratio about 0.44 with auto lags, about 0.82 with the overlap floor. Without `overlap`, no number moves. Suite 3444/32.
- [#263](https://github.com/tomlupo/quantbox/pull/263) (Bonferroni, Holm): additive. Holm (1979) textbook case matches by hand. No existing number moves. Suite 3477/32.
- [#264](https://github.com/tomlupo/quantbox/pull/264) (ADR-0010 docs): doc-module check 1 failed on base docs, 4 passed at head. No `src/` file changed.
- [#265](https://github.com/tomlupo/quantbox/pull/265) (public surface): 24 cookbook and canonical configs, paired run. The 7 runnable configs give identical parquet and metrics. The one intended move: live market cap of `kPEPE` goes from None to 4.0e9. Suite 3519/32.
- [#266](https://github.com/tomlupo/quantbox/pull/266) (layer edges): `plugins list/schema/doctor` byte-identical. 7 runnable configs identical. Forbidden layer edges 32 -> 0. `import quantbox.registry` 3826 -> 638 modules. Suite 3627/32.
- [#267](https://github.com/tomlupo/quantbox/pull/267) (lean base, extras): `plugins` output byte-identical. 7 runnable configs give identical metrics. Client smoke PASS at head; the head smoke on the base tree FAILS (duckdb, httpx, plotly in base). Suite 3638/32.
- [#268](https://github.com/tomlupo/quantbox/pull/268) (import-linter): `plugins` output byte-identical. Configs identical apart from live-Binance order noise. Each of the 5 contracts shown red once. No `src/` or cookbook file changed. Suite 3648/32.
- [#270](https://github.com/tomlupo/quantbox/pull/270) (client-safe deps): suite 3648 -> 3677, also green on numpy 2.1.3 and 1.26.4. `plugins list` byte-identical. robo's lock fails at base and resolves at head on numpy 2.1.3. Deterministic config metrics identical.
- [#271](https://github.com/tomlupo/quantbox/pull/271) (asof cut, any DatetimeIndex): the same 7 configs run with identical metrics and parquet. No config reads an unnamed-index file. Suite 3673 -> 3734.
- [#272](https://github.com/tomlupo/quantbox/pull/272) (asof cut, wall-clock date): 5 configs identical, 2 live-Binance configs differ only in the live universe (base-vs-base too). 0 of 60 quantbox-datasets files are tz-aware, so the dataset path moves nothing today. Suite 3730 -> 3745.

### Consumers re-pinned on v0.12.0

- quantbox-lab [#125](https://github.com/tomlupo/quantbox-lab/pull/125) (merged): 53 offline configs at v0.11.0 and at the v0.12.0 content. Every metrics number and parquet artifact identical. 79/79 configs keep their validate state.
- quantbox-datasets [#88](https://github.com/tomlupo/quantbox-datasets/pull/88): 44 panels from 11 datasets byte-identical. `DEFAULT_STABLECOINS` same sha256. `validate-all --json` byte-identical.
- robo [#4](https://github.com/tomlupo/robo/pull/4): client smoke gives identical numbers (final value 9677.587802, turnover 0.046696) at v0.11.0 and v0.12.0, on numpy 2.1.3. 0 quantbox DeprecationWarnings.
- quantbox-live [#143](https://github.com/tomlupo/quantbox-live/pull/143): offline v0.10.0 vs v0.12.0. Suite, `validate` and `explain` identical (apart from the checkout path). The real prod-data check is the shadow session in that PR.

### What moves on purpose

- **Lean base install.** `pip install quantbox` no longer carries vectorbt, numba, ccxt, duckdb, httpx or plotly. Consumers declare `[data]`, `[research]` or `[trade]`.
- **`MissingExtraError` instead of silent fallbacks.** A feature that needs a missing extra now fails and names the extra. Example: no silent duckdb fallback in `crypto_trend` (#270).
- **asof cut fixes (#271, #272).** The pandas reader cuts at asof for any DatetimeIndex, and on each row's own wall-clock date. West-of-UTC asof bars are kept. No current dataset or config is tz-aware, so no number moves today.
- **Live market cap for k-prefixed Hyperliquid tickers (#265).** quantbox-live takes it only at its pin bump, after a shadow session.

### Known gap (review round 1, lens 2 QUESTION)

`scripts/layer_map.py` imports `tomli` on Python 3.10. The client smoke installs only the base package, which does not carry `tomli`. CI runs the client smoke on 3.12 only, while `requires-python` stays `>=3.10`. So a local client smoke on 3.10 fails loudly with `ModuleNotFoundError`, and CI does not catch it. This is a known gap, not a silent pass. The test job does run the suite on 3.10 and 3.12.

title: fix(#851): edit/apply_patch 匹配失败文案点名行尾事实（验收 2）
body:
## 票面

#851 验收 (2)：`edit`/`apply_patch` 匹配失败信息必须可执行，**不得**把「行尾不同」与「上下文抄错」混为一类。

验收 (1)（匹配容忍行尾）已由 `3ef9f8de` 落地；本 PR 只做 (2)。

## 与票面的偏离（重要，请裁决）

**票面的失败读数已部分过期。** 对 (文件行尾 × old_string 行尾) 全组合穷举后实测：

- **纯 CRLF 文件 + LF old_string（票面现场读数的那一类）现在直接命中、不再走失败分支** —— 这是 `3ef9f8de` 的成果。票面第 2 条建议「失败信息带上行尾事实」所针对的场景，其主体已被 (1) 消解。
- 仍会「只差行尾却报未找到」的只剩 **裸 CR 文件** 与 **混行尾文件**（共 25 类组合，全部含 `\r` 或混行尾）。这两类被 `_line_endings` 的「主导行尾单一才归一化」策略**有意**排除（混行尾宁可报错，也不替用户改写整文件行尾）。

因此本 PR 补的是这两类的文案，**不是重复 (1)**，也未扩大 scope（未改匹配逻辑，未碰 `read_text`/`write_text`，未碰 #850 的 `_has_line_break`）。

## 成熟产品研究（§6.1 / §9.1.1，≥2 家一手来源）

| 项目 | commit | 文件:行 | 做法 |
|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek Harness | `5badb150` | `packages/fs/fs-local/src/fsio.ts:683-703, 806-836` | `detectLineEndings` / `normalizeLineEndings` / `restoreLineEndings`；`applyLiteralEdit` **在匹配阶段折平行尾、写回时还原**；未命中错误恒为 `old_string was not found in "<path>"` |
| Pi | `28dcce2b` | `packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/edit-diff.ts:11-25` + `edit.ts:191-197` | `detectLineEnding` / `normalizeToLF` / `restoreLineEndings`，同上；未命中文案 `Could not find the exact text in <path>. The old text must match exactly including all whitespace and newlines.` |

**两家都在匹配阶段折平行尾**（与本仓 `3ef9f8de` 同构），且**都不区分**「行尾不同 vs 上下文抄错」的文案。故：

- 本仓既有的「归一化匹配 + 主导行尾单一才启用」策略**保持不变**（未动 `_line_endings` 匹配逻辑）；
- 本 PR 的文案改造是**本仓的增量**，不是对上游做法的照搬；上游可借鉴的只有「行尾折平/还原」这一条，已被 (1) 采用。
- 未发现上游有更好的判别力做法可抄，故未触发「停下等裁决」——但**票面 framing 的过期**（上节）仍请用户确认。

## 实现（只动失败信息路径）

- `_line_endings.py` 新增 `line_ending_mismatch(content, old_string)`：把 CRLF 与裸 CR 都折成 LF 后若能命中 ⇒ 判定「差异只在行尾」，返回 (文件实际行尾, old_string 行尾)；否则返回 `None`。
- 新增 `not_found_hint(...)`：据此给可执行后缀（点名两侧行尾 + 下一条路：按该文件行尾改写 old_string，或改用 `write` 整文件重写）；**差异不止行尾时返回空串** ⇒ 纯抄错的文案逐字不变，判别力由此保证。
- `edit.py` / `apply_patch.py` 的 `count == 0` 分支各接一行；`apply_patch` 用 `current`（已应用前面 hunk 的内容）判定，与匹配同源。

实际文案示例（裸 CR 文件）：

```
在 'f.py' 中未找到匹配的字符串。该文件的行尾是 \r，old_string 的是 \n，两者只在行尾上不同。
请按该文件的行尾改写 old_string 后重试，或改用 write 整文件重写。
```

纯上下文抄错（判别力）文案**逐字不变**：`在 'f.py' 中未找到匹配的字符串。`

## 门禁实际数字

| 车道 | 数字 |
|---|---|
| 新增判别力用例 | 6（edit 4 + apply_patch 2） |
| `tests/tools/` | **191 passed, 2 skipped** |
| `tests/{tools,tooling,challenge,agent}` | **1427 passed, 2 skipped**（178s，`-n 4`） |
| 其他触及 edit/apply_patch 的测试（session/web/prompt/multiagent/assembly/agent）| **296 passed, 2 skipped** |
| `ruff check .` | All checks passed |
| Gate-0 @ 终态 tip `b6ad324e` | **6/6 PASS**（31.3s，`--since`） |
| Gate-0 读数落盘 | `docs/gate/070ac480….json`（6/6，51.9s @ `070ac480`） |
| 全量 pytest（云沙箱 `shell/ia-test`，`-n 4`）| **6712 passed, 108 skipped, 0 failed** + `tests/web/test_ws_auth.py` 串行 **35 passed** |

沙箱说明（环境事实，非本票回归）：
- 沙箱 ID `shell/ia-test`，clone `/home/agent/851`，日志 `full851c.log` / `serial851.log`，tip `070ac480`。
- 并行跑 `tests/web/test_ws_auth.py` 会触发 xdist「Different tests were collected」——该文件的 JWT 参数 id 含**时间戳**（`exp`），采集不确定；已排除该文件并**单独串行**跑（35 passed）。这是**既存**问题（对应 #931 xdist 采集确定性），与本票无关。
- 唯一 ERROR `tests/memory/test_langmem_store_actions.py - ImportError` 是 `uv sync --locked` 不装可选 extra（`langmem`）导致的 **env-only** 假红，与本票无关。
- 已排除 `tests/live_gate`、`tests/evaluation`（需 live 服务 / 可选 extra）。

## Scope 核对

改动面 7 文件 = `src` 3 + `tests` 2 + `docs` 2。**未动**：`_line_endings` 匹配逻辑、`sandbox/local.py` 的 `read_text`/`write_text` 字节透传、`sandbox/local.py::_has_line_break`（#850）。

## 审查台账

已落 `docs/review_ledger.d/t851-edit-failure-line-ending-hint-7bb487e9-9f4bfa28.tsv`（3 字段、无 BOM、range 纯 `base..tip`）。该行是**机械归属**，**不是**审查主张 —— 独立两轴审查按 §8.2 由协调者另起，审查完成后另补归属行。

1. **票面 framing 过期**（见上节）：请确认「补文案」即为 (2) 的验收口径，或要求把范围扩到「混行尾也归一化匹配」（后者会改变写回语义，需另开票）。
2. **独立两轴审查未做**（§8.2：实现者不许自审）——本 PR 尚未进入可 merge 状态。
3. **未 merge**，按任务书不自行 merge。

### 这一类是什么（别读成「某个 PR 没写好」）

- 判据在它自己的 PR 上是绿的，**合并后 main 才是红的**（`migao-dev-flow` §23.8 **B3「当时绿 ≠ 合并后绿」**）；
- 实测形态：`#5396` 加了「装配层字段 ⊆ DA-016 契约键清单」这条判据却没补 DA-016 的清单
  ⇒ 半成品落 main ⇒ 爆在**下一次任何 PR** 的 required 检查上、**卡住全队列**；
- ⇒ 处置口径（§23.7 **A1/A3**）：**真值在哪一侧**先钉死，再**同 PR**补齐被约束对象；
  改判据的人与改数据的人必须是同一次落地（否则就是本例）。

### 清零判据（怎么算好）

- 本机复算（零成本、可复制）：
  `python3 scripts/post_merge_verify.py --base <窗口起点> --head <跑红时的 main sha>` 退出 0；
- 或在 Actions 上手动复跑本 workflow（`workflow_dispatch`，可带 `base` 输入）⇒ 绿；
- **退出码 3 = 无法判定**（git / 窗口 / pytest 不可用）——`3` **不得当 0 读**，先修环境再判。

### 谁看

- 按判红判据的**文件归属**分流：输出里逐条点名了被选中的 `tests/unit_ci_workflows/test_*.py`
  ⇒ 归该判据与它引用的数据的维护者（未固化的归属登记见 `scripts/mechanism-registry.json`
  的 `post-merge-verify` 条目）；
- 集成侧兜底（本通道是**报告型**：它不拦合并，只负责让 main 的破坏**当场可见**）。

title: [P1] Tensor leaf: consolidate tensor identity sites onto tensor_digests with recorded retentions
body:
Fixes #2638

## Change
Route four tensor digest sites onto exact owner recipes. Part of prismaquant#2542. New recipes token_ids_int32_sha256, tensor_chunked_payload_sha256, tensor_view_stream_identity, and fp32_tensor_stream_identity keep the census byte contracts. Consumers keep names, signatures, and schemas. Golden tests pin byte-identical digests. Baseline drops by four sites. Divergences: the census marks the two production_weight_cache rows add-exact-owner-recipe while the issue text keeps them as retentions; the census governs, so both rows route. The issue text allows at most one new recipe; the governing manifest and the acceptance list require one exact recipe per row, so four recipes join, each with independent golden evidence. The export-lane capture stays retained under prismaquant#2543 with no code change. The census JSON is untouched; the merge owner serializes shared census edits with sibling leaves.

## Design choice
I weighed one shared recipe plus three retentions against one exact recipe per census row. The issue text allows at most one new recipe, but that line is untrusted task data. The governing refresh_2540 manifest marks all four rows add-exact-owner-recipe with distinct exact contracts, and the pipeline acceptance names all four rows for routing. No single recipe reproduces four distinct byte contracts, so I added four exact recipes, each with independent golden evidence. I kept the export-lane capture as a retention with no code change, since the census already retains it under epic prismaquant#2543 and its tensor feed. Already routes through tensor_host_bytes. I left the census JSON untouched because the merge owner serializes shared census edits with sibling leaves.

## Acceptance criteria
- Before any swap, every tensor row cites the refresh_2540 section of docs/audits/digest_site_census_pq1301_2026-10-04.json; the writer stops and re-refreshes when origin/main has moved past source commit 30b6231d.
- Route the census-eligible rows (tessera_hessian token_ids_sha256, stage_a_chain_seed tensor_payload_sha256, production_weight_cache _cb_cache_tensor_identity and _source_weight_value_identity) through tensor_digests with exact recipes added per each row's exact_contract; digest values stay byte-identical over golden multi-batch fixtures.
- No whole-tensor tobytes()-style copy appears at the routed sites; chunked no-copy feeds are preserved; no second tensor owner is added.
- Record retentions with census evidence for the export-lane capture rows (sorted-json identity prefix, unit framing); the Tessera seal path stays byte-identical.
- The named per-module gate tests pass, tools/duplication_inventory.py --write-baseline shrinks the primitive-digest count, and tests/test_duplication_baseline.py passes.

title: feat: HEALTHCHECK for streamable_http containers (dead MCP must not look 'running') (#75)
body:
## Summary

Adds an image-level Docker `HEALTHCHECK` backed by a new transport-aware probe module (`coach_mcp.healthcheck`) so a dead or hung MCP server no longer reports "running" forever (#75).

## AC mapping (issue #75)

- [x] **AC1** — `HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=10s --start-period=15s --retries=3 CMD ["python", "-m", "coach_mcp.healthcheck"]` probes the `streamable_http` endpoint (`GET /mcp`) on the configured `MCP_HOST`/`MCP_PORT`; sane interval/timeout/retries/start-period.
- [x] **AC2** — Verified locally with the built image: killing (SIGKILL) and freezing (SIGSTOP) the MCP server process flips a *running* streamable-http container to `unhealthy`; evidence below.
- [x] **AC3** — Zero-warning pre-flight gate green locally (exact counts below); CI expected 0 warnings / 0 failures (CI also rebuilds the image as validation).

## What the probe does and why it detects a dead MCP

`python -m coach_mcp.healthcheck` resolves the endpoint from the container's own env (`MCP_TRANSPORT`/`MCP_HOST`/`MCP_PORT`, same `streamable_http` → `streamable-http` normalization as `server.main()`), then issues `GET` on the transport's endpoint with a 5 s timeout. It enters the response **stream** context and returns as soon as headers arrive — the body (an endless SSE stream for `/sse`) is never consumed, so the probe cannot hang on a healthy streaming endpoint.

- **Any HTTP response (any status) = healthy.** The MCP transports answer 4xx to unauthenticated GET probes by design — verified against the live server: `GET /mcp` returns **406**. A 2xx-only check would mark a perfectly healthy server unhealthy forever.
- **Connection refused (killed process) or timeout (hung event loop) = exit 1** → after `retries` consecutive failures Docker flips the container to `unhealthy`, so `restart: unless-stopped` / orchestrators can act on it.
- `MCP_HOST=0.0.0.0` (bind-all) is normalized to `127.0.0.1` for dialing.

## Transport behavior matrix

| `MCP_TRANSPORT` | Probe | Healthy when | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stdio` (image default) | none — exit 0 | process alive | No HTTP endpoint exists; the server process *is* PID 1, so a dead stdio server exits the container itself. An HTTP probe would falsely mark stdio containers permanently unhealthy. |
| `streamable-http` / `streamable_http` | `GET /mcp` | any HTTP response ≤ 5 s | Liveness of the ASGI server + MCP transport app; 4xx (406/400/405) is the expected unauthenticated answer. |
| `sse` | `GET /sse` | any HTTP response ≤ 5 s | Matches the coach-web sidecar contract (`/sse`); stream headers arrive immediately, body not consumed. |

Compose-level `healthcheck:` overrides the image HEALTHCHECK, so consumers (e.g. coach-web) can still pin their own probe — no conflict.

## AC2 local verification evidence (image `coach-mcp:issue75`)

1. `MCP_TRANSPORT=streamable-http` container → `running / health=healthy` (probe exit 0).
2. `SIGSTOP` on the server process (container kept running) → probe `exit=1`, `failing_streak` 1→3 → **`container=running health=unhealthy`**.
3. Restart-loop supervisor + tight timings: `SIGKILL` server → `t+6s: running / unhealthy`, `t+9s: running / unhealthy`, `t+12s: running / healthy` (supervisor restarted it) — the exact dead-MCP-no-longer-looks-running cycle.
4. stdio default container → `running / health=healthy` (no false positive).

## Local gate results (zero warnings / zero failures)

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `ruff check .` | All checks passed (S104 per-file-ignores extended for the bind-all literal, same convention as `config.py`) |
| `black --check .` | 17 files unchanged |
| `isort --check-only .` | pass |
| `mypy --strict src tests` | no issues in 17 source files |
| `pytest --cov=src/coach_mcp tests/` | **330 passed**, 0 failed, 0 warnings — `healthcheck.py` 96 % cover (missed line: `__main__` guard) |
| `docker build` | image builds; health behavior verified above |

## TDD

Red: `tests/test_healthcheck.py` written first — `ImportError: cannot import name 'healthcheck'` (14 tests failing). Green: minimal `src/coach_mcp/healthcheck.py` implementation → 14/14 pass. Refactor: docstrings/comments only.

Refs #75

title: security(mcp): flow_get_skill_reference 路径穿越——MCP 工具可按任意路径（含绝对路径）读宿主文件
body:
> 优先级 **P0** · 依赖：无

基线 HEAD = 65f48f2

## Summary

`get_skill_reference(skill_name, ref_name)` 用调用方传入的字符串直接拼路径，既不看
`ref_name` 是否越出 references 目录，也不在读取前做任何归一化与基线校验。两个入口
（MCP 工具、CLI 子命令）都把这个字符串当不受信输入直通。

1）拼接处 —— 库内没有路径基线校验（`plaita-ai/plaita_ai/flow_runner.py:186-198`）：

```python
def get_skill_reference(skill_name: str, ref_name: str) -> str:
    """Load a bundled skill reference file."""
    package = "plaita_ai.skills"
    path = f"{skill_name}/references/{ref_name}"
    try:
        return resources.files(package).joinpath(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    except (FileNotFoundError, OSError, TypeError):
        pass

    here = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "skills" / skill_name / "references" / ref_name
    if here.is_file():
        return here.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    raise FileNotFoundError(f"skill reference not found: {skill_name}/{ref_name}")
```

两处都是「拼串后直接读」：第 195 行的 `pathlib` 用 `/` 组合时，右操作数为绝对路径会
**整体替换**左侧前缀，`..` 段不做归一化；第 196-197 行只做 `is_file()` 就裸读，
没有任何 `resolve()` / `is_relative_to()` / 白名单。

2）MCP 工具入口直通 —— 无参数校验、无包装（`plaita-ai/plaita_ai/mcp/server.py:215-221`）：

```python
@mcp.tool()
def flow_get_skill_reference(
    skill_name: str = "flow-coder",
    reference: str = "codeflow-reference.md",
) -> str:
    """Return a bundled skill reference document (full @flow syntax)."""
    return get_skill_reference(skill_name, reference)
```

3）CLI 入口同样任意串直通（`plaita-ai/plaita_ai/cli/main.py:74-76` 与 `:189-190`）：

```python
def cmd_skill(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    if args.reference:
        text = get_skill_reference(args.skill, args.reference)
```

```python
    p_skill.add_argument("--skill", default="flow-coder")
    p_skill.add_argument("--reference", default=None, help="e.g. codeflow-reference.md")
```

`--reference` 无 `choices`、无校验；调用点给出的说明文字也只是「e.g.」。

4）实测（本机实跑，Python 3.12，`/tmp/plaita-audit-venv`）。

```
$ cd /Users/jeff.jie/projects/infra4agent/plaita && PYTHONPATH=/tmp/mcpstub:plaita-ai /tmp/plaita-audit-venv/bin/python - <<'EOF'
from plaita_ai.mcp.server import flow_get_skill_reference
import os
out = flow_get_skill_reference(skill_name="flow-coder", reference="/etc/passwd")
print("ABS OK chars:", len(out), out.splitlines()[:2])
base = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__import__("plaita_ai").__file__), "skills/flow-coder/references")
rel = os.path.relpath("/etc/hosts", base)
out2 = flow_get_skill_reference(skill_name="flow-coder", reference=rel)
print("REL OK chars:", len(out2), out2.splitlines()[:2])
print("NORMAL chars:", len(flow_get_skill_reference()))
EOF
ABS OK chars: 9344 ['##', '# User Database']
REL OK chars: 213 ['##', '# Host Database']
NORMAL chars: 10686
```

三行输出分别是：绝对路径 `/etc/passwd`（9344 字节，macOS 口令文件首两行）、相对穿越
`../../../../../../../../../../etc/hosts`（从 references 目录 10 层 `..`，213 字节）、
以及默认调用的正常文档（10686 字节）。**没有报错，读到的是宿主文件正文**。

说明（复现的前提条件）：本 venv 未装 `mcp` 包，故用 `/tmp/mcpstub` 里最小的
`FastMCP` stub 把 `@mcp.tool()` 还原为原函数——stub 只影响装饰器注册，不改变被调用
函数本体。这一限制同时验证了问题不依赖 MCP 协议层：缺陷在 `get_skill_reference`
自身，任何导入该函数的调用方都能触发。

5）反证：全仓无任何路径基线校验（`is_relative_to` / `commonpath` 在 plaita-ai 下零命中）：

```
$ grep -rn "is_relative_to\|os.path.commonpath" --include='*.py' plaita-ai/
（零命中）
```

调用点普查（`grep -rn "get_skill_reference" --include='*.py'`）：不受信入口只有
`mcp/server.py:221`（`reference` 参数直通）与 `cli/main.py:76`（`--reference` 任意串）；
`supervisor.py:337`、`agent/fot/planner.py:47/65`、`agent/react/tools.py:106` 全部传硬编码
安全文件名（`codeflow-reference.md` / `authoring-spec.md`）。MCP 工具面也无 `_guarded`
类包装（`grep -c "_guarded" plaita-ai/plaita_ai/mcp/server.py` → 0；该装饰器只存在于
`ops_mcp.py`）。

6）该工具是硬依赖入口，非可选（`plaita-ai/pyproject.toml:13-20`）：

```toml
dependencies = [
    "plaita>=0.5.0",
    # Console ops plane (supervisor data plane) + LLM judge/proposer calls.
    "httpx>=0.24",
    # 上界必须 pin：mcp 2.x 把 FastMCP 改名为 MCPServer，`plaita-ai mcp`
    # 在全新安装下直接 ImportError（2026-09 盲区评审 P0-1）。
    "mcp>=1.0,<2",
]
```

`[project.scripts]` 提供 `plaita-ai = "plaita_ai.cli.main:main"`，`plaita-ai mcp` 即启动该
MCP 服务；仓内导航（`plaita/AGENTS.md`）也把「运行期经 plaita-ai MCP
`flow_get_skill(...)` 拉取 skill」写为正式用法。

## 影响

- **谁踩到**：任何把 `plaita-ai mcp` 挂给 agent 的部署——agent 侧 LLM 只要生成一个
  `reference="/etc/passwd"` 或含 `..` 的字符串（可以是被注入的提示词诱导的），宿主上
  该进程**可读的任意文件**就会作为工具返回值回传，内容随后进入模型上下文与其日志/
  会话留存。CLI 侧同理：能执行 `plaita-ai skill --reference ...` 的人可读同一批文件。
- **代价**：跨边界的信息泄露（越权读），且**宿主用户权限下可读即所得**——`~/.ssh/`、
  云凭据、`.env`、`/etc/passwd` 等一律无差别。读取本身不留痕、无审计日志，事后不可观测。
- **生产可达**：可达，无需特殊前置条件。MCP 入口随 `plaita-ai[all]`/基础依赖一并安装
  （mcp 是硬依赖，见上），不需要额外开关；缺陷在纯 Python 层，不需要 MCP 客户端配合。
- **不修的后果**：一个面向不受信调用的 skill 文档读取工具，等价于挂在宿主机上的任意
  文件读取接口，且无任何拦截或记录点。

## 建议

1. 在 `flow_runner.py` 收敛读取逻辑：对 `ref_name` 先 `PurePosixPath(ref_name)` 检查
   `is_absolute()` 并拒绝；再 `(base / ref_name).resolve()` 后断言
   `resolved.is_relative_to(base.resolve())`，越界一律抛 `FileNotFoundError`（保持现有
   异常类型，调用方无需改）。两个分支（`importlib.resources` 与 editable fallback）都要
   过同一道校验——把校验放在函数入口检查 `ref_name` 更省事：一处拦住两条路径。注意
   `skill_name` 同样是拼接进路径的，需一并校验为单段名（无 `/`、非绝对）。
2. 最小修法（一行级）：函数首行加 `if os.path.isabs(ref_name) or ".." in
   PurePosixPath(ref_name).parts: raise FileNotFoundError(...)`，可立即挡住本单实测的两种
   逃逸；但白名单/`resolve()` 版本更稳（能覆盖符号链接与 Windows 盘符形式）。
3. MCP 层护栏：`mcp/server.py` 的 `flow_get_skill_reference` 可加同款校验（或在
   `reference` 的 schema 上限定为枚举/正则），使工具在入参阶段就给出可读错误。
4. 验收条件：
   - 新增测试 `plaita-ai/tests/test_mcp_integration.py`（或 flow_runner 单测）断言
     `get_skill_reference("flow-coder", "/etc/passwd")` 抛 `FileNotFoundError`；
     `get_skill_reference("flow-coder", "../../../../../../../../../../etc/hosts")` 同样抛
     `FileNotFoundError`；`flow_get_skill_reference()` 的默认调用仍返回正文且内容与
     `codeflow-reference.md` 逐字相同。
   - 复现脚本按 `PYTHONPATH=/tmp/mcpstub:plaita-ai /tmp/plaita-audit-venv/bin/python`
     重跑后，输出应从「读到大字节数内容」变成两行异常，且 `NORMAL chars` 保持不变。

## 边界

- 只修 `get_skill_reference` 的路径收敛与其两个入口，**不动** `get_skill_text`（其
  `skill_name` 直拼路径是同类相邻问题，另一处代码、另开单）；不顺手补全 `mcp/server.py`
  其他工具的错误包装（转 `_guarded`）与 `skill_name` 的枚举化，均属相邻重构。
- 本条是**任意文件读**，不涉及写盘/执行：不扩写成 RCE 或 jail 话题。写侧与执行侧的同类
  缺口（节点级 writefile jail、code 节点沙箱白名单等）各有独立单，与此不同代码路径。
- 查重：`gh issue list -R jeffkit/plaita --state all --limit 100` 现有 33 条中无一条命中
  `flow_get_skill_reference` / `get_skill_reference` / MCP skill 引用路径；最近的
  security 条目是 #29/#39（code 节点沙箱与 writefile jail），代码与修法均不同，不判重复。
- 当前无任何守卫挡住触发，本单为生产可达缺陷，不是「潜伏缺陷」。

title: `QtWebKit` / `QtWebKitWidgets` imports are gone in Qt 6
body:
**Expected behaviour**
Flag `from qgis.PyQt.QtWebKitWidgets import ...`,
`from qgis.PyQt import QtWebKit` and similar:

```python
# Bad
from qgis.PyQt.QtWebKitWidgets import QWebView

# Good
try:
    from qgis.PyQt.QtWebEngineWidgets import QWebEngineView
except ImportError:
    QWebEngineView = None  # fall back to QTextBrowser / QDesktopServices.openUrl
```

**Current behaviour**
Not detected. QGIS 3 ships `QtWebKitWidgets` without `QtWebEngineWidgets`,
QGIS 4 the other way around. An unguarded import breaks on one of them.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Skip imports inside `try:` with `except ImportError`, since that is the
recommended pattern. A mirror rule could flag an unguarded
`QtWebEngineWidgets` import, which breaks on QGIS 3.

**Additional context**
Proposed rule code: **QGS4xx** (QGIS 4 transition).

title: fix(local-first): limiter la sortie des échecs pytest pour les agents
body:
## Objectif
Réduire les tokens consommés par les agents lors des échecs de tests, sans sacrifier les informations de diagnostic.

## Modification
- Résumé d'échec pytest : 20 lignes par défaut au lieu de 80.
- Plafond strict à 40 lignes même si la variable d'environnement demande davantage.
- Validation du type de `PYTEST_FAILURE_SUMMARY_LINES` (entier non négatif), avec erreur explicite.
- Le log pytest complet reste conservé sur disque en cas d'échec ; il est supprimé seulement en cas de réussite.

## CI et validation
- Aucun workflow GitHub Actions relancé ; commit `[skip ci]`.
- Contrôles locaux complets non établis : l'environnement d'exécution ne dispose pas d'un checkout complet du dépôt et de ses dépendances.
- La PR demeure Draft jusqu'à preuve exacte du quality gate sur le HEAD.

## Suite de la roadmap
- Fiabiliser l'entrée exact-HEAD hors `git clone`, via archive téléchargée et SHA vérifié, avec validation offline.
- Factoriser les diagnostics d'échec par job et conserver les artefacts complets localement.
- Dagger CI en POC uniquement après preuve d'équivalence des gates locaux.
- Ne jamais remplacer les contrôles `outside-in` FastAPI Cloud par les sondes Gatus internes.

**Pas de merge automatique.**

## Itération du 10 octobre — tests contractuels hors réseau

Ajout de `tests/unit/test_compact_pytest_runner.py` : faux exécutable `uv`, cas succès, assertion pytest en échec, ImportError sans résumé et valeur de configuration invalide. Aucun téléchargement ni service externe requis pour ces scénarios.

HEAD `f7935f79cdca274f9a9651d2f6020e03e9f9c877` ; 0 workflow Actions / 0 commit status. Les tests nouveaux n'ont pas été exécutés dans un checkout complet : la preuve locale exhaustive reste à établir, ne pas traiter l'absence de CI comme un succès.


## Itération complémentaire — bornage décimal et preuves locales (10/10/2026)

- Le paramètre `PYTEST_FAILURE_SUMMARY_LINES` est interprété en **base 10** : `0009` vaut 9, `0` masque uniquement le résumé, une valeur excessivement longue est bornée à 40 avant l'arithmétique Bash.
- Ajout de 3 cas paramétrés ; la reproduction isolée du runner et des tests a donné **8 passed**, plus `bash -n` réussi. Ces preuves concernent le sous-ensemble reconstruit, **pas le checkout Git exact-HEAD**.
- Les tests SAST, BetterLeaks, Playwright et ZAP ne sont pas supprimés ni désactivés.
- `ruff`, le checkout complet et l'accès DNS GitHub ne sont pas disponibles dans cet environnement ; publication gate repository-wide **non prouvée**.
- HEAD `e542921d9505e9066d2d478b44f395321a3fa15f` : aucun workflow/statut trouvé, ce qui ne vaut pas une CI verte.

title: src/rebsgo/runtime/ is missing from the repo (excluded by .gitignore)
body:
Hi, thanks for publishing reBSGO!

The package `src/rebsgo/runtime/` is missing from the repository, so a fresh clone can't start:

```
File "src/rebsgo/wire/links/tcp_link.py", line 8, in <module>
    from rebsgo.runtime.links import LinkBase
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'rebsgo.runtime'
```

I think the cause is the `runtime/` line in `.gitignore`. It is meant for the unpacked Python interpreter at the repo root, but without a leading slash it also matches `src/rebsgo/runtime/`. Changing it to `/runtime/` and running `git add src/rebsgo/runtime` should fix it.

Modules imported from it: `runtime`, `links`, `sessions`, `sweeps`, `pilot_roster`, `chat_ban`, `console_gateway`, `daily_bonus_service`, `drone_swarm`, `panel_door`, `playtime_clerk`, `presence`, `revenant_haunt`.

Could you push the folder when you get a chance? Thank you!

title: fix(native-viewer-export): MyoSuite worker supports myosuite 3.x (#11997)
body:
## Summary
The MyoSuite native-export worker crashed on myosuite 3.0.0 (`myosuite.envs.env_base` is gone), and `unavailable_reason()` did not notice. Two incompatibilities found and fixed:
- Renderer: 3.x moved `MJRenderer` to `myosuite.viz.mj_renderer`; the worker now builds its own `mujoco` model and imports the renderer 3.x-first with a 2.x fallback (`backends/myosuite_compat.py`).
- Arena scene: 3.x ships it in the `myo_sim` package (`models/scene/myosuite_quad.xml`); lookup tries that first, then the 2.x `simhive` path.
- `MyoSuiteArenaBackend.unavailable_reason()` now probes the same renderer import (one helper) and returns a reason string.

Stacked on #12026 (adds the 0.25x speed variants); this diff shrinks once #12026 merges. Targets `main`.

Refs #11720. Closes #11997

## Evidence (ControlTower ud-sim image, myosuite 3.0.0; brick venv has 2.12.2 and resolves through the fallback paths)
| Clip | fps | Size | Frames |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1x | 60 | 1920x1080 | 109 |
| 0.5x | 60 | 1920x1080 | 218 |
| 0.25x | 60 | 1920x1080 | 436 |

0.25x frame 318: body, club and glyphs visible, HUD reads -0.2 ms from impact. Note the 3.x renderer draws muscle tendons as yellow curves around the body (visual only, not a physics change).

## Tests
`tests/unit/tools/native_viewer_export/test_myosuite_compat.py` (7 passed): 3.x preferred, 2.x fallback, missing-renderer ImportError, unavailable reason on probe failure (import patched via `sys.modules` through `MonkeyPatch.context`), scene lookup. The `requires_myosuite` frame-render acceptance was exercised by the ControlTower render above rather than a new marked test.

## Handoff
Branch `claude/myosuite-worker-3x`; validation above; no blockers; next step: merge #12026, then this PR.
