[diffusion] comfyui: fix 12 bugs in the SGLDiffusion ComfyUI plugin
body:
## Summary

Twelve bugs found during an audit of `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/apps/ComfyUI_SGLDiffusion/` (the ComfyUI client plugin for the SGLang diffusion server), each fixed in its own commit below. All are confirmed against the actual pre-fix code (reproduced directly, not just read), fixed, covered by a new regression test, and reviewed.

## Issues fixed (one per commit)

1. **GGUF detection hardcoded to MiniMax-H3.** Any `.gguf` file was treated as MiniMax-H3 for ComfyUI's architecture detection, regardless of what model it actually was — a Flux/Qwen/Z-Image GGUF either failed with an H3-specific error, or silently built the H3 model around the wrong weights if an H3 BF16 file happened to be present. Fixed by inferring the real architecture from an `SGLDOptions.model_type` hint or the filename, and raising a clear error when it can't be determined.
2. **`.gguf` leaking into ComfyUI's global `diffusion_models` registry.** `SGLDUNETLoader` enabled `.gguf` by mutating `folder_paths.folder_names_and_paths` at import time — shared global state — so ComfyUI's own stock "Load Diffusion Model" node started offering GGUF files it can't load. Fixed by building this node's own file list locally instead.
3. **Server-mode nodes sending local paths a remote server can't read.** The generic video node sent a local temp-file path as `input_reference` and a client-side temp dir as `output_path`; the H3 node built `file://` URIs for keyframes/references. None of that is readable by an SGLD server on another machine. Fixed: upload local references via multipart, never send `output_path` (let the server pick its own and download the result if needed), embed H3 image conditions as base64 `data:` URIs, and raise clearly for local video/audio references against a confirmed-remote server.
4. **`enable_cache_dit` silently ignored outside MiniMax-H3.** It's a generic `SamplingParams` field, but only `MiniMaxH3Executor` read it — Flux/Qwen-Image/Z-Image users toggling it got no effect and no warning. Fixed by moving the plumbing into the shared executor base class.
5. **Bare `None` from detection failure causing a confusing `TypeError`.** `get_comfyui_model` returned `None` on two failure paths, but callers always unpack 3-4 values — users saw "cannot unpack non-iterable NoneType object" instead of the real error. Fixed to raise `ValueError` with the model path and detected type.
6. **`SGLDVideoInput` didn't implement ComfyUI's `VideoInput` contract.** `get_components()` returned a bare list instead of a `VideoComponents`, so any downstream node reading frames/audio would crash; `save_to` silently dropped `format`/`codec`/`metadata`. Fixed by preferring ComfyUI's own file-backed `VideoFromFile` and making the fallback fail loudly instead of returning/doing the wrong thing.
7. **Reported video width/height could be wrong.** The generic video node always reported the *requested* size even when the server resolved a different one (e.g. to match an image-to-video input's aspect ratio). Fixed by reading the server's resolved `size` field. (Same commit as #6, since the `VideoFromFile` fix also makes dimensions self-correcting.)
8. **Missing-runtime import guard disappearing all nodes silently.** `executors/minimax_h3.py` imported `sglang.multimodal_gen` unguarded at module scope — breaking the "stay importable without the runtime" pattern the rest of the executors follow — and `core/generator.py` imports every executor unconditionally, so this took Flux/Z-Image down too. `__init__.py`'s `except` branch then swallowed the resulting `ImportError` with zero logging, so every node just vanished from ComfyUI with no clue why. Fixed by guarding the import (mirroring `base.py`'s pattern) and logging the failure.
9. **Hardcoded 300s timeout on image requests.** No way to raise it for a large job or a first request that triggers `torch.compile` warmup. Fixed with a configurable `image_timeout` param (default unchanged).
10. **Batched image inputs silently truncated to the first image.** `get_image_path` saved only `image[0]` from a batch, dropping the rest with no warning. Fixed to raise a clear error instead.
11. **LoRA strength not settable in server mode.** The server's `/set_lora` endpoint accepts a `strength` field; the client and node never exposed it. Fixed by threading it through both.
12. **Inconsistent VRAM accounting across model types.** `SGLDModelPatcher.model_size()` returned a hardcoded guess for `flux`/`lumina2` and `0` for everything else, so ComfyUI freed VRAM inconsistently across SGLD model types even though the weights live in the worker process. Fixed by computing the real byte size from the checkpoint header at load time (falling back to the old table only when that's unavailable), and sizing GGUF loads from the actual GGUF file rather than the BF16 companion used only for architecture detection.

## How each bug was verified

- 8 of the 12 were reproduced directly against the actual pre-fix code (not just read): GGUF-detect defaulting to H3, the global `.gguf` registry mutation, `get_comfyui_model` returning bare `None`, `SGLDVideoInput`'s broken contract, the hardcoded 300s timeout, batch truncation, missing LoRA strength, and the hardcoded VRAM table.
- The remaining ones (local `file://` paths, `enable_cache_dit` H3-only, the import-guard fragility) were confirmed by direct source inspection plus, for the import guard, a real traceback showing the original `executors/__init__.py` drags in the entire `sglang.srt` LLM-serving stack just to import Flux/Z-Image.
- An independent review pass (fresh context, no knowledge of the implementation) caught a real bug introduced while fixing #12 — GGUF model size was computed from the BF16 companion file instead of the actual GGUF — which is now fixed and covered by its own regression test.

## Tests

- `test/test_sgld_bugfixes.py` (new): 25 tests, one or more per bug above, run against stubbed `comfy`/`folder_paths` modules so they don't need a ComfyUI install or a GPU.
- `test/test_h3_request.py` (existing): updated for the behavior changes in #3/#6/#7 (base64 image URIs instead of `file://`, real temp files instead of fixed fake paths since the client now validates `file_path` locally); all pre-existing assertions preserved.
- 37/37 passing locally (CPU only).

title: fix: resolve Ledger resources in native plugin namespaces
body:
## Summary

Fix both packaged-resource readers to anchor on the executing module's `__package__` rather than a fixed top-level `review_ledger` name. Add isolated namespace/collision regressions and a persistent real-Hermes model-dispatch regression.

This is the runtime implementation complementary to the already-merged documentation PR [#13](https://github.com/JoaoMarcos44/hermes-review-ledger/pull/13), not another loop detector or a rewrite of that investigation.

## Observed problem

Native directory plugins are imported below `hermes_plugins.<slug>` (with profile-specific suffixes where applicable). The baseline protocol and critic prompt readers resolve `importlib.resources.files("review_ledger")` instead of their executing package.

- Without a canonical top-level package, resource lookup raises `ModuleNotFoundError` and the normal tool boundary projects it as sanitized `internal_error`.
- With a conflicting canonical installation, the reader can silently return the other copy's resources.

- `review_ledger/critic_contract.py:54`: sibling critic prompt reader now resolves its own package.

- `Critic.prepare` and critic prompt-hash validation consume the sibling reader.
- Migration, bundled-skill and installer readers already use their module/source paths and do not resolve this fixed top-level package name. They were inspected but not changed.

No `graphify-out/` exists in this Ledger checkout; source tracing was direct. No graph update or graph coverage is claimed.

Affected: package resource identity in native plugin namespaces and conflicting canonical installations.

Preserved: normal canonical imports, protocol/prompt content, version/hash semantics, critic response contract, authorization, run ownership, SQLite schema/data, profile settings and the existing sanitized exception boundary.

No core Hermes change, global alias, credential access, database reset, dependency, scheduling/retry policy, auxiliary model call, automatic loop detector, or live-profile deployment is included. No official security advisory/classification is claimed.

## Solution and alternatives

Use the standard-library package-aware resource loader with `files(__package__)` in both existing readers. This is the smallest correction at the resource-identity boundary.

Alternatives examined:

1. Install a canonical alias or inject global `PYTHONPATH`/`sys.modules`: rejected because it masks absence and can route resources to a conflicting copy; the collision regression demonstrates the latter.
2. Change Hermes' loader to publish a bare module: rejected because native plugin/profile namespaces are intentional ownership boundaries and this unnecessarily expands core scope.
3. Use cwd or a fixed installation path: rejected because resource ownership is package-relative and must preserve relocation/loader semantics.
4. Add a new resource-manager abstraction: unnecessary for two readers already served by the standard library.
5. Add retry limits or reset Ledger state: unrelated to the demonstrated lookup defect and not supported by the working bookkeeping paths.

The branch finalizes the existing user-owned uncommitted correction rather than duplicating or copying another contributor's patch. Fresh all/open PR and exact-head searches returned no overlapping runtime PR before publication. Related merged #13 documents the diagnosis; #12 handles GitHub pagination, not resource imports.

title: chore(deploy): set the edge body limit to the upload bound + 1 MiB (#2144)
body:
## Summary

Closes the last open item of #2144, audit gap **G-10**: the edge request-body limit. Measuring it turned up a functional defect as well as a hardening gap. Neither nginx configuration set `client_max_body_size`, and nginx's default is **1 MiB**. That covers `src/frontend/nginx.conf` in the image and the `default.conf` that the chart's ConfigMap mounts **over** `/etc/nginx/conf.d` in every Kubernetes release. So every upload above 1 MiB was refused with `413` at the frontend nginx, which is the only path the backend NetworkPolicy admits (#1159). The backend's own limit is 25 MiB.

Measured on `origin/develop` 6f93331f2 (2026-10-09). Both configurations ran in the pinned `nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.31-alpine@sha256:b9241c6e…` image, with a POST to `/api/v1/…` and no backend behind it:

| body | image `nginx.conf` | chart `default.conf` |
|---|---|---|
| 1 MiB | 502 (forwarded) | 502 (forwarded) |
| 2 MiB | **413** | **413** |
| 25 MiB | **413** | **413** |
| 30 MiB | 413 | 413 |

**Chosen limit: `storage.maxFileSizeMb + 1` MiB = `26m` by default.** It is derived from the settings, not taken from the issue:

- The largest legitimate body is an attachment upload. `storage_max_file_size_mb = 25` is a MiB bound (`* 1024 * 1024` in `AttachmentService`), plus the multipart framing (boundaries, `category`, `capture_device`, a few hundred bytes).
- Every other upload bound is smaller: identification and CV images 5 MiB, pest images 8 MiB, CSV import 10 MB (`MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE_BYTES`), MCP image 4 MiB raw (about 5.4 MiB as base64 JSON). Per-category overrides only change MIME lists, not sizes.
- With +1 MiB of headroom the proxy never cuts a request the backend would accept. A body between 25 and 26 MiB still reaches the backend and gets its typed `413` (`FileTooLargeError`), and anything larger stops at the edge. That includes JSON bodies, which Starlette would otherwise read completely. The backend has no global body bound, so "≤ the backend's bound" can only mean the per-route upload bound. Exact equality would cut legitimate full-size uploads because of the multipart overhead, hence the 1 MiB slack. The issue's `26m` holds as the default value.

## Changes

- `src/frontend/nginx.conf`: `client_max_body_size 26m;` at server level, so every location inherits it.
- `helm/kamerplanter/values.yaml`:
  - The chart's `default.conf` now sets `client_max_body_size {{ add (int .Values.storage.maxFileSizeMb) 1 }}m;`, so the limit follows the upload bound.
  - New `ingress.main` defaults carry the same expression as `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-body-size`. ingress-nginx also defaults to 1 MiB.
  - `enabled` renders `true` only when `ingress.main.hosts` is set. A default install still renders no Ingress, values with hosts but no `enabled` keep their Ingress, and `enabled: false` still wins.
  - Traefik and Contour/Envoy ignore the annotation and set no default body limit. On those, the frontend nginx is the edge limit.
- `scripts/ci/assert_chart_contracts.sh`: a new #2144 block checks the rendered result.
  - The default render gives nginx `26m` and no Ingress.
  - With hosts, the Ingress annotation is `26m`.
  - `storage.maxFileSizeMb=50` gives nginx `51m`, the annotation `51m` and the backend `STORAGE_MAX_FILE_SIZE_MB=50`.
  - `enabled=false` still switches the Ingress off.
  - The `values-dev` Ingress carries `26m`.
- `scripts/ci/probe_proxy_body_limit.sh` (new): the 413 probe.
  - Runs the image's and the chart-rendered nginx config in the image pinned by the frontend Dockerfile.
  - 2 MiB and the largest upload (max + 64 KiB) must be forwarded: 502, because nothing listens upstream.
  - 30 MiB must answer `413`.
- `.github/workflows/skaffold-verify.yml`: runs the probe after the chart contracts (docker is on `ubuntu-latest`).
- `.taskfiles/deploy.yaml`: new `task verify:proxy-body-limit` target with the same script.
- `src/backend/tests/unit/guards/test_proxy_body_limit.py` (new): static guard.
  - The image's nginx sets the limit exactly once, inside `server {}`, equal to the Settings default + 1 MiB.
  - The chart's `storage.maxFileSizeMb` equals the Settings default.
  - The chart's nginx limit references `.Values.storage.maxFileSizeMb`.
  - The ingress annotation is the same expression as the chart's nginx directive.
  - Premise check: no other upload bound reaches the attachment bound.
- Docs, DE canonical + EN mirror:
  - `deployment/helm.md`: new "Upload-Grenze (Request-Body)" / "Upload limit (request body)" section.
  - `deployment/argocd.md`: corrected the nginx-ingress note, which recommended `proxy-body-size: "10m"`. That is too small for 25 MiB attachments.
  - `changelog/unreleased.md`: Fixed entry with an upgrade note.

Second commit (follow-ups found while measuring G-10, kept in this PR at the operator's request):

- `src/backend/app/common/upload_bounds.py` (new): one shared early `Content-Length` reject for upload routes.
  - `declared_body_exceeds(request, max_file_bytes)` allows `MULTIPART_ENVELOPE_BYTES = 64 KiB` on top of the file limit.
  - Until now the check compared the whole multipart body (file + boundaries + form fields) with the file limit, so a file of exactly the allowed size got `413` before it was read.
  - Used by all six routes: attachments, plant photos, task photos, IPM pest images, recognition reference images, CV diagnosis. It replaces four copies of the header parser.
  - The bounded read still refuses one byte over the file limit, so the file limit itself stays exact.
  - 64 KiB matches the probe's "max + 64 KiB" body and stays below nginx's 1 MiB headroom. A body between the two bounds still gets the backend's typed `413`.
- Ingress examples now send `/` including `/api` to the frontend. This covers `docs/{de,en}/deployment/helm.md`, `argocd.md`, `kubernetes.md` (incl. the topology diagram) and `helm/kamerplanter/values-dev.yaml`.
  - Before, they routed `/api` straight to the backend Service, which the backend NetworkPolicy (#1159) does not admit. That path also skips the edge body limit and the `TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS: "1"` depth.
  - In dev, Vite proxies `/api` to `VITE_BACKEND_URL` (`kamerplanter-backend:8000`, which the dev frontend egress already allows).
  - `helm.md` (DE/EN) now explains why `/api` must not bypass the frontend.
- `scripts/ci/assert_chart_contracts.sh`: every in-chart Ingress (values-dev, and the default chart with hosts) routes only to `kamerplanter-frontend`.
- Changelog DE/EN: an API fix entry and a docs/dev-chart entry.

## Linked issues

Closes #2144. G-10 is the last open item per the issue's own comment ("Still open: **G-10** … Keeping this issue open for that item only"). All MT items landed in #2202.

## Testing

Each check was run RED first against the unchanged files (cp backup/restore, no `git stash`), then GREEN:

- `test_proxy_body_limit.py`: RED 3 failed / 2 passed (the two premise tests). GREEN 5 passed. Falsified afterwards, each red:
  - ingress annotation set to `10m`
  - directive moved into `location /api/`
  - image value `25m`
- `assert_chart_contracts.sh`: RED "5 chart contract(s) violated". GREEN "Every chart contract holds". The `10m` annotation drift gives 3 violations.
- `probe_proxy_body_limit.sh` with the pinned digest: RED "4 body-limit probe(s) failed". GREEN "Both nginx configurations forward the largest upload and refuse 30 MiB with 413". An image value of `25m` gives 1 failure (the largest upload gets 413).
- `helm lint` (default and `values-dev.yaml`): 0 failed.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check`: clean.
- shellcheck v0.11.0 `--severity=warning` and at default severity: clean. actionlint 1.7.12: clean.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed>`: all hooks passed.
- `tests/unit/guards` (local): 2716 passed, 19 skipped. 4 failures in `test_log_redaction_has_no_residual_gaps.py` and `test_uncaught_exceptions_are_redacted.py` come from the local venv: it lacks `prometheus_client` (added in #2129), and those tests import `app.main` in a subprocess (`ModuleNotFoundError`). This change does not touch them; CI installs the locked dependencies.

- Content-Length envelope, RED with the old routers (cp backup/restore):
  - `test_a_file_of_exactly_the_limit_is_accepted` (attachments, 1 MiB limit): 413 `FILE_TOO_LARGE`.
  - `test_diagnose_accepts_an_image_of_exactly_the_limit` (CV, 5 MiB): 413 `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`.
  - GREEN after the change. The one-byte-over tests stay 413 before and after.
  - Falsified with `MULTIPART_ENVELOPE_BYTES = 0`: 3 failed.
  - `tests/unit/common/test_upload_bounds.py` pins the predicate's boundary.
  - `tests/unit/api` + `tests/unit/common` + the touched API tests: 1688 + 424 passed.
  - mypy: no findings in the touched code.
- Ingress routing contract: RED with the old `values-dev.yaml` ("the dev ingress routes every path to the frontend — expected [\"kamerplanter-frontend\"], rendered [\"kamerplanter-backend\",\"kamerplanter-frontend\"]"). GREEN after the change. `helm lint -f values-dev.yaml`: 0 failed.

## Risk / rollout notes

- **Behaviour change:** uploads between 1 MiB and 26 MiB now reach the backend in Docker and Kubernetes. Until now they were refused at nginx. Bodies above `maxFileSizeMb + 1` MiB are refused by nginx with an HTML `413` instead of reaching the backend.
- **Chart upgrade note:** `ingress.main` now has chart defaults. An Ingress under another key than `main`, or an external `HTTPProxy`/`IngressRoute`, does not inherit the annotation. The docs say to set it there.
- The new skaffold-verify step changes that job's spec hash. The weekly `lane-inputs.yml` recording will propose the manifest refresh as usual; nothing is hand-edited.
- No change to required checks.
- Upload routes now accept a declared body up to file limit + 64 KiB before reading. The file bytes themselves are still bounded exactly.
- `values-dev.yaml`: the dev ingress no longer reaches the backend directly. The dev backend's open `:8000` rule is unchanged, because co-located dev consumers such as Home Assistant may still use it.
- Dispatched specialist: nolte-engineering:fullstack-developer

title: fix(deploy): harden doctor/setup against broken deps and invalid config
body:
Follow-up to #8 (WP7). That PR merged while its AO review was still running, leaving two findings open. This PR fixes them in `src/voxoracle/cli.py` (+ tests only).

## Findings fixed

### 1. `doctor`: DocOracle check was not wrapped by `_safe`
`doctor()` wrapped the wake-word and mistral-key checks with `_safe()`, but called
`asyncio.run(diagnostics.check_docoracle(settings))` unguarded. An invalid
`docoracle.url` (e.g. a bad port like `http://localhost:notaport`) makes
`httpx.AsyncClient(...)` raise `httpx.InvalidURL` **inside the `DocOracleClient`
constructor**, which is outside the `except DocOracleError` guard in
`check_docoracle` (that guard only covers the request phase). The exception
escaped as a raw traceback, skipped the mistral-key check, and printed nothing.

Fix: a `_safe_all()` helper (the multi-result sibling of `_safe`) turns any
exception into a single FAIL `CheckResult`. The DocOracle check is now wrapped
with it.

### 2. `setup`: `check_wakeword` was called unguarded
`setup()` called `model = diagnostics.check_wakeword(settings)` unguarded while
`doctor()` wraps the same call. A broken openWakeWord install (unimportable
module raising `ImportError` from the lazy import inside `check_wakeword`)
crashed `setup` with a traceback.

Fix: `setup()` now runs the same call through `_safe()` and renders the result
with a `[fail]`-style severity mark. Setup still exits 0 (prep-only role) but
never crashes.

## Tests
- `test_cli_doctor_survives_invalid_docoracle_url` — invalid `docoracle.url` in
  `config.yaml`; asserts a `[fail]` line naming `InvalidURL` and that the later
  `mistral key` check still ran.
- `test_cli_setup_survives_broken_wakeword_dependency` — mirrors
  `test_cli_doctor_survives_broken_wakeword_dependency`; asserts a `[fail]` line
  with `ImportError`, setup exits 0, and `Next steps` is still printed.

Both mirror the existing `test_cli_doctor_survives_broken_wakeword_dependency`.

## Scope / note
Diff is limited to `cli.py` and tests. No workflows, no tts/mistral backend lanes
(WP5 review is in flight on #9). The `ruff format` pre-commit hook also
normalised pre-existing formatting drift in the touched files so
`pre-commit run --all-files` is clean; those lines are mechanical only.

## Gates run locally
- `uv run pytest --cov=voxoracle --cov-report=term --cov-report=xml:coverage.xml` — 133 passed, 92% coverage
- `uv run ruff check .` — clean
- `uv run basedpyright` — 0 errors
- `openspec validate --all --strict` — pass
- `pre-commit run --all-files` — all hooks pass

title: feat(oled): 多页轮播下移 B 板固件，B 每 15s 主动拉取数据 (V2.12)
body:
## 背景
旧 OLED 多页轮播跑在香橙派侧，每 15s 切页、逐行调用 `oled` 工具，每页向 B 板下发 4~8 条串口命令。这种「Pi 逐行推送 + B 逐行 SPI 刷新」的持续串口流量，是此前怀疑「OLED 刷新导致 B 板复位」的来源。

前置核查结论：仓库固件**并未禁用 OLED**（`CommandDispatcher::begin()` 无条件 `_oled.begin()`），引脚定义正确；真正关闭的是香橙派侧轮播（`engine.oled_enabled` 默认 `False`）。

## 变更
- **固件 Module B V2.12**：新增 `OledCarousel.{h,cpp}`，3 页（Environment/Devices/Safety）排版与 15s 轮播硬编码进固件，文案全走 PROGMEM；`Protocol` 每拍上行一帧 `{"module":"output","type":"oled_req","id":N}`，新增按首字符 `@` 分流的紧凑帧解析（早于 JSON 解析，不触发 `parse_error`）。
- **上位机 MCP**：新增 `_compose_oled_frame` / `_push_oled_frame` 与 `oled_req` 分支；回帧 `@D<id>,<t10>,<h10>,<light>,<smoke>,<rain>,<touch>,<motion>`（温湿度 ×10，读不到 `-32768`，帧长恒 <64B）。写帧用非阻塞 `_b_lock`，拿不到锁即丢帧，绝不阻塞读线程。
- **上位机 Web**：停用 `engine` 的逐行轮播线程 `_oled_loop`；OLED 配置与 `oled_carousel` 保留作存档与 `{}` 占位符格式化。
- **文档**：`docs/serial-protocol.md` 新增「B 板新增 OLED 数据拉取（V2.12）」，同步 CHANGELOG / README / DEPLOYMENT。

## 验收
- 单测：新增 `test_oled_pull.py`（9 项）、`test_oled_startup.py` 新增 1 项；全量套件仅剩与基线一致的 6 项环境 ImportError。
- 固件：`pio run` 通过（RAM 80.9% / Flash 86.1%）。
- 真机（香橙派，分支部署）：B 板烧录 V2.12 后 `READY version=V2.12`；`oled_req` 每 15s 一次；回帧 `@D2,272,280,1017,0,0,0,1` 与 A 板快照一致；稳态 180s 内 0 复位；`MCP -> oled` 调用数 0；屏上人工确认「正常轮播，数值合理」。

## 影响
串口流量从「每页 4~8 帧」降到「每 15s 2 帧」。`oled/show_text`、`oled/clear` 保留但会被下一拍切页覆盖（仅调试用）。未升级 B 板固件时上位机收到 `oled_req` 也只回一帧、不影响旧行为。

title: [Core] Add cost-aware replica routing for heterogeneous diffusion workloads
body:
## Purpose

Add an opt-in `cost-aware` replica-routing policy for heterogeneous diffusion workloads, addressing #5135.

The existing random, round-robin, and least-queue policies balance request count. They cannot distinguish a short image request from an 81-frame, many-step video request, so equal queue lengths can represent very different remaining work. #5135 reports a median ~27% makespan gap on mixed 17/49/81-frame Wan2.2 traffic.

This follows a common design principle in KV-aware serving routers: cache/locality signals must be combined with projected active work instead of routing every request as unit cost. Relevant implementations include NVIDIA Dynamo's combined cache-overlap and active-load cost, AIBrix's cache/load blending, and llm-d's weighted prefix, queue, and KV-pressure scorers.

## Design

- Estimate relative diffusion work as `(height * width / 512^2) * frames * steps * outputs`.
- Allow callers to provide an explicit `estimated_cost`; missing, invalid, non-finite, or non-positive metadata safely falls back to unit cost.
- Track exact outstanding work for requests assigned by the current head.
- Reconcile that ledger with coordinator queue depth for requests assigned by other heads:

  ```text
  unknown_count = max(queue_length - locally_tracked_count, 0)
  effective_load = locally_tracked_work + unknown_count * representative_cost
  ```

- Use the mean active local cost as `representative_cost`, falling back to the incoming request cost when the local ledger is empty.
- Release reservations idempotently on completion, cancellation, submission failure, and replica invalidation.
- Support both coordinator-backed distributed pools and local replica pools. Existing local routing remains unchanged unless `--omni-lb-policy cost-aware` is selected.
- Preserve sticky request/CFG affinity and all existing policies.

## Commit structure

1. `fd8358a2` — lifecycle-aware cost estimator and balancer with deterministic workload coverage.
2. `475a3d79` — StagePool task propagation and reservation cleanup.
3. `1af4f600` — CLI/factory wiring and operator documentation.
4. `70f683ec` — local replica-pool routing, added after review found the initial implementation only affected coordinator-backed pools.
5. `b42006d9` — incremental per-replica aggregates, keeping normal selection O(replicas) instead of O(active requests + replicas).

## Test plan

Target CI commands:

```bash
pytest -q tests/distributed/omni_coordinator/test_load_balancer.py \
  tests/engine/test_stage_pool_cost_aware.py \
  tests/engine/test_load_balancer_factory.py \
  tests/entrypoints/test_serve.py \
  -m "core_model and cpu" \
  -k "cost_aware or estimate_cost or omni_lb_policy"

ruff check \
  vllm_omni/distributed/omni_coordinator/load_balancer.py \
  vllm_omni/distributed/omni_coordinator/__init__.py \
  vllm_omni/engine/stage_pool.py \
  vllm_omni/engine/stage_runtime.py \
  vllm_omni/entrypoints/cli/serve.py \
  tests/distributed/omni_coordinator/test_load_balancer.py \
  tests/engine/test_stage_pool_cost_aware.py \
  tests/engine/test_load_balancer_factory.py \
  tests/entrypoints/test_serve.py
```

## Local results

- Core estimator/balancer target tests: **21 passed**.
- StagePool target tests: **10 passed**.
- `ruff check`: passed for all changed Python files.
- `ruff format --check`: all 9 changed Python files formatted.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Syntax compilation: passed for all changed Python files.

The local machine has Python 3.9 and no installed vLLM package, so normal repository pytest collection stops in the existing fixture import with `ModuleNotFoundError: vllm`. The two target groups above were run through an isolated CPU harness that loaded the exact changed modules and replaced only unavailable vLLM imports with inert stubs. Full repository collection and the real parser/factory tests are therefore left to CI; they are not claimed as locally passed.

No GPU performance run was available. The policy is opt-in, and the deterministic CPU simulation verifies projected peak work improves from `243` to `164` for the mixed 17/49/81 workload ordering. This is an algorithmic regression test, not a substitute for the A800 benchmark in #5135.

## Review notes

- The cost model is intentionally relative and model-agnostic; it does not claim exact latency prediction.
- A coordinator reports global request count, but not the shapes of work assigned by other heads, hence the explicit representative-cost approximation.
- Local pools have an exact head-local binding count. Multi-API diffusion is currently unsupported, so there is no hidden cross-head local diffusion ledger.
- Composable-parallel `RouteByStage` remains unchanged because it currently documents stateless policies; this PR exposes the stateful policy through `--omni-lb-policy` only.

AI assistance: Relay (`model_api/experimental_0723`) produced the initial implementation and tests from a detailed design specification. I reviewed every changed path, fixed incorrect/flaky makespan tests, overflow and empty-ID handling, submission-failure cleanup, the missing local-replica execution path, and an O(active requests) routing hot path, then reran the checks reported above.

title: feat(webui): client status and crawl controls on the dashboard
body:
Lower in this stack, a status loop started reading each client every minute: per channel, whether it is on its network and whether peers can connect to us, and whether the client's API answers at all. It feeds two gauges and alerts on a degraded state that lasts, but the webui showed none of it. The webui's `/controls` page, meanwhile, was down to three buttons (pause, resume, restart) once the force-cycle button went, and it did not even say whether the crawl was paused. This block puts both on the dashboard: - **A "Clients" section**: per client its version and whether its API answered, and per channel `on network` / `connectable` as yes, no or unknown. - **A "Crawl" section**: "The crawl is running" or "paused", and the three buttons. The `/controls` page and its menu entry go; the `POST /controls/*` routes stay and redirect to `/`, where their banner now shows. **How the status reaches the webui.** The webui runs on its own thread and never calls a client: a second session from it would double the API traffic and the 401 lockout risk. The status loop publishes each reading to an in-memory board, and the webui reads that board. ```mermaid flowchart LR loop[status loop, crawler thread] -- "publish(reading)" --> board[(StatusBoard)] board -- "readings()" --> webui[dashboard, webui thread] ``` Each publish replaces the board's map with a new one instead of changing it, so the webui's thread always reads one whole snapshot, with no lock. Before its first reading, a client shows "No reading yet". A reading older than two status periods (120 s) shows its time and nothing else: a dead crawler loop must never leave yesterday's "yes" on screen as if current. The board owns that rule, beside the period it derives from, so the webui knows neither the period nor a clock. The docs follow: the routes table in `docs/operate.md`, and the pages that sent the operator to `/controls` for the restart button.
Block report, for the handoff **Block 200, `feat/webui-dashboard-status`** (spec D20, D21). - **Gate**: `uv run poe check` exit 0 at `aec0f15` (crawler 1090 passed, 15 deselected, 100 % branch coverage; matching 342; vex_guards 73; amule_bump 53; ruff, mypy strict, sqlfluff, template-check clean; no warning). `uv run poe docs-build` clean. - **CI**: started on the push of `f07371b` (this PR). - **Budget** (workflow command, against `feat/download-lifecycle-fields`): 478 changed lines, 17 files (estimate 400 / 14). The handoff draft is outside the counts. **Watched failing.** Tests first: collection failed on `ImportError: cannot import name 'ClientReading' from 'mulewatch.application.status_loop'`, then 31 composition tests failed before the composition passed the board. Then each rule by mutation, restored after: | Rule disabled | Failing test, its line | |---|---| | the status loop given its own board instead of the webui's | `test_the_webui_reads_the_status_loops_board_and_the_pause_gate`: `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'status'` | | current up to two periods inclusive (`<` instead of `<=`) | `test_a_reading_older_than_two_status_periods_is_not_current`: `assert False` at 120 s | | publish mutates the map in place | `test_publishing_replaces_the_snapshot_and_never_changes_one_already_read`: `assert {'amuled': Cl... status=None)} == {'amuled': None}` | | an unreachable reading not published | `test_each_reading_is_published_with_its_time[reading1-None]`: the board kept the previous reading | | `is_paused` inverted | `test_is_paused_reads_the_pause_gate`: `assert False` | | an old reading shown as current | `test_dashboard_never_shows_an_old_reading_as_current`: `assert '
Out of date: last reading at 2026-06-12 00:00Z.
' in ...` | | the crawl always "running" | `test_dashboard_shows_a_paused_crawl`: `assert 'The crawl is paused.' in ...` | The client-blind acceptance: the dashboard test drives a channel `x` (`xnounknown`). `GET /controls` answers 404, `POST /controls/pause` redirects to `/?done=paused` (webui tests). **Departures from the spec** - The board and its reading type live in `application/status_loop.py`, beside the period. The webui imports them: its first import of the application layer (it imported ports only). - The board is seeded with the client names at construction, so a client never read shows "No reading yet."; it also holds the freshness rule (`is_current`, two periods inclusive) with the crawler's clock. - An out-of-date reading shows no value at all (version and API "unknown", no channel line), not the old values marked old. - A reading is stamped when it is published, after `status()` answers or fails. **Class 1 fixes**: `AGENTS.md`'s subsystem table named `/controls`. `docs/troubleshooting.md`'s Low-ID entry now says the dashboard shows `Connectable: no` on `ed2k`, which a fresh Low-ID node will read. **Class 2 questions**: none. **Pitfalls**: a composition test that GETs the captured webui app leaks the webui's `ReaderProvider` connections into a `ResourceWarning` in the next test; the wiring test captures `build_webui_app`'s arguments instead. **Handoff**: drafted in this block, `agents/handoffs/2026-10-10 - handoff - stage 2 ports.md`, from the reports of #127 to #151 and this one; its "Holistic review" section is left to the closing block. **Not verified**: the dashboard in a browser; the board fed by a real amuled.

title: feat(adapters): aMule's start() and downloads() on a generic download port
body:
The download loop talks to aMule through `MuleDownloadClient`: it hands over an ed2k link, reads aMule's queue and shared list, and decides completion itself from a byte count (`size_done >= size_full`) combined with presence in `/shared`. That rule is aMule's, sits in the core, and has a false positive: amuled shares partfiles, so a partfile with every byte received but still hashing or moving passes it.

This block adds the generic download port the loop will switch to in the next block, and aMule's side of it. Nothing calls it yet.

```python
class DownloadClient(Protocol):
    async def start(self, request: DownloadRequest) -> None: ...   # FileKey, filename, size
    async def downloads(self) -> tuple[DownloadStatus, ...]: ...    # every download the client knows
```

A `DownloadStatus` carries the file's `FileKey`, its byte counters, `completed`, and two reasons: `waiting_reason` (why it waits, shown to the operator) and `failure_reason` (the one that will change the loop's behaviour).

**Completion is the client's positive signal, never bytes.** For aMule, a download is completed when its queue row's status is `completed` (the one status amuleapi reserves for "verified, moved, awaiting clear"), or when it is in `/shared` and the queue no longer lists it (completed then cleared). The queue is read before `/shared`, so a file cleared between the two reads shows up as shared rather than vanishing from both.

| queue row | in `/shared` | completed |
|---|---|---|
| `completing`, every byte received | yes | no |
| `completed` | either | yes |
| absent | yes | yes |

**Reasons** come from amuleapi's status first, then the sources: `insufficient_disk` is `disk_full`; `paused`/`stopped` is `paused`; `waiting`, `hashing`, `allocating` and `completing` are `local`; otherwise no source at all is `no_source`, and sources with none transferring is `remote_queue`. `erroneous` is the only client-reported failure (`error`); `rejected` and `lost` belong to the core. A completed or failed download carries no waiting reason.

`start()` builds the ed2k link with the shared `build_ed2k_link` and queues it; a refusal raises the generic `DownloadRejectedError`.

**Gate**: `uv run poe check` exit 0 at the tip `da3cee5` (crawler 1091 passed, 16 deselected, 100 % branch coverage; matching 342; vex_guards 73; amule_bump 53; lint, mypy strict, sqlfluff, template-check clean).

**Watched failing** (each by mutating the implementation, then restored):
- The D10 false positive, `test_a_full_partfile_still_completing_is_not_completed_though_shared`, with today's byte rule added to `completed`: `assert [(FileKey(...), True)] == [(FileKey(...), False)]`.
- `test_downloads_reads_the_whole_queue_before_the_shared_files` with `/shared` read first: `assert ['/api/v1/shared', '/api/v1/downloads'] == ['/api/v1/downloads', '/api/v1/shared']`.

- D12's first-match list read literally gives `no_source` or `remote_queue` to a `completed`, `erroneous` or `completing` row whose sources are gone. A completed or failed download is not waiting, so it gets no waiting reason; `completing` (aMule hashing then moving the file) reads `local`, like `hashing`.

title: feat(adapters): aMule's status(), per channel, behind the StatusClient port
body:
Until now the core read aMule's state through `network_status()`, an aMule shape (an eD2k id, a High-ID flag, a four-state Kad enum) that the search cycle turned into "can this instance search?". Later clients (slskd, gtk-gnutella, BitTorrent) report other things, so the core needs a status it can read without knowing the client.

This block adds that port and aMule's implementation. The status loop that consumes it (alerts on a degraded state that lasts) is the next block, so for now `status()` is tested and called by nothing.

```python
ClientStatus(version="3.0.1", channels=(
    ChannelStatus(channel="ed2k", on_network=True, connectable=False),  # Low-ID
    ChannelStatus(channel="kad", on_network=False, connectable=None),   # not joined: unknown
))
```

- **One line per channel**, which is the same unit the search uses (`ed2k`, `kad`), with two questions every network can answer: have we joined it, and can peers reach us. `connectable=None` means the client cannot tell. aMule says so while a channel is off its network, because `high_id: false` then means "no id yet", not Low-ID.
- **Reachability is `status()` not raising.** amuleapi keeps answering `GET /status` from its cache after amuled dies, with `ec_connected: false` and the last states, which still say "connected". The adapter therefore raises `ClientUnreachableError` unless `ec_connected` is `true`, so a dead amuled never reads as a healthy, connectable node.
- **Version** is amuled's `daemon_version` from `GET /version`, and `None` when it is empty (EC down).
- The status carries no address: the public IP and server IP are dropped.

**Block 70, `feat/client-status-read`** (spec section 5, row 70; D14, D22).

title: refactor(ports): generic client errors
body:
Stage 2 of the multi-network work makes the crawler's search, download and status ports generic, so a second client (slskd, AirDC++...) can implement them without the core branching on it. This first block of the stack does the groundwork every later block builds on: the error contract the application catches.

Today that contract is named after aMule (`MuleClientError`, `MuleUnreachableError`, `MuleSearchFailedError`) and has no word for a refused download: the download loop marks a rejected link `failed` by catching `MuleSearchFailedError`, an error named after search. The next blocks raise and catch these errors from new generic ports, so they are renamed once, here.

`ports/client_errors.py` now holds the contract, one failure per port:

| Error | Raised when | The caller |
|---|---|---|
| `ClientUnreachableError` | the client's API does not answer | degrades and backs off the whole client |
| `SearchFailedError` | the client refused a search | backs off that channel |
| `DownloadRejectedError` | the client refused a download | fails that download |

All three derive from `ClientError`. The amuleapi adapter's errors re-parent onto them. amuleapi answers a refused search and a refused link with the same `400 amuled_rejected`, so `ApiRejectedError` is both a `SearchFailedError` and a `DownloadRejectedError`, and each consumer catches the one its port names. `ApiAuthError` stays under `ClientError` but outside the three loop errors: a wrong password fails fast at startup. Behaviour is unchanged.

The commit also carries the stage 2 spec, and adds `(Corrected: ...)` markers to the umbrella spec where stage 2 departs from it (D9: no persistent or passive search port yet, no stop; D14: per-channel status fields, no Low-ID edge alert exists today).

title: fix(delegation): staged handshake budgets, liveness-aware timeout triage, and bootstrap error classification
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes the recurrence family behind the delegate-session continuity incidents: each emergency "continuity repair" re-armed the same prevention because the underlying defect survived every repair (1,458 consecutive FAIL evaluations of the prevention contract, re-armed by three separate repairs).

**Root cause:** delegate-session handshakes used a single fixed 30s budget. A delegate Pi that was slow but **alive** (cold bootstrap, loaded host, provider retry) hit the ceiling and was aborted as "timed out"; a genuinely dead process could burn the whole budget first. The abort/re-spawn churn fed the spool-starvation loop (queue latency ~2.5e6 ms, abort storms up to 216s, get_state 30.9s) that kept re-triggering the continuity machinery.

**Approach:** adopt-and-extend of the two prior delegate-liveness remediation layers (error classification + health checks; stall liveness-triage), conflict-resolved onto the current base and completed with a stage-budget architecture:

- **Staged handshake budgets** replace the fixed 30s at all five handshake sites (start, same-id retry, recovery, `get_messages`, `steer`): a 30/90/240s ladder, each rung clipped to `min(600, effective)`; `abort` stays a fast unstaged `min(10s)`. A slow-but-alive session now gets up to the ladder instead of dying at 30s; a dead one fails at the first rung.
- **Between-stage liveness probes** (`agent/pi_rpc_client.py::_request_pi`): before advancing a rung the Pi process is probed — a dead process converts immediately to a transport error instead of consuming the remaining budget; the existing `TimeoutError` prose is preserved verbatim.
- **New pure module `agent/delegate_start_budget.py`** (ladder, clip-to-effective, respawn jitter RNG seam) with a dedicated red-first test suite (9 tests).
- **`bootstrap_timeout` classification** (`agent/delegate_errors.py`): the marker `did not answer command` is ranked before the generic timeout markers and kept outside `PROVIDER_FAILURE_CLASSES`, so a slow boot retries instead of being misfiled as a provider failure.
- **Respawn jitter** (0.5–2.0s, injectable RNG) before same-id retries and fresh native re-spawns, so recovery bursts no longer stampede.
- **Delegate-health circuit breaker** (fail-open) + status surface carried from the adopted layer.
- **`transform_tool_result` kept single-shot on the concurrent batch path** (`agent/tool_executor.py` reverted to the upstream blob): the adopted layer fired the hook publisher-side on the premise that inline dispatch never applies it — false on this base, where `invoke_tool`'s inline branch fires it dispatch-side, so batched results got the hook twice. title: Run in browser: faster chapter 5 clicks, a Pyodide pin in conf.py, and Chromium CI
body:
Three follow-ups to the "Run in browser" buttons. Each commit is one step.

## 1. Faster first clicks in chapter 5

The slow pages were not slow because of the OMARS design. Their examples did not need it at all. `block_deps` counted any name read inside a loop as needed from earlier examples, including the loop's own target. Chapter 5's FDS plot loops `for design, label in ...`, so a click on the judging page ran the whole worked study first.

`uses` now comes from a small definite-binding walk:

- A loop target, and a name the loop body bound a line earlier, are bound for the body.
- A name bound in every branch of an `if`, or by `with ... as`, is bound after it.
- A `try` or a loop body binds nothing after it.

| Page | Prelude before | Prelude after | First click before | First click after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Judging and comparing designs | 32 steps | 2 statements | 168 s | 18 s |
| Comparing design families | 38 steps | 2 statements | 202 s | 84 s |
| OMARS worked study | 16 steps | 2 statements | 70 s | 52 s |

First clicks were measured in headless Chromium on GitHub's runner, four pages at a time. The remaining time on comparing design families is that page's own first example generating its designs.

It also fixes a soundness gap: a function's globals that its own example bound were never resolved where the function is called, so a later example rebinding one was missed.

`make check-run-deps`: 0 differences on all six chapters (187 examples, 49 pages). On GitHub that job now takes 3.75 minutes instead of 6.5. A persistent browser cache was the original idea for this part. With the dependencies fixed at the root it would save under a second, so it is not built.

## 2. Pyodide pin in `conf.py`

`run_in_browser_pyodide = "314.0.7"` replaces the URL hard-coded in the worker. It goes through the manifest to the worker's URL, and the worker accepts only a version number there. `-D run_in_browser_pyodide=<version>` builds against another release without editing a file.

## 3. Every button, clicked in headless Chromium, in CI

`tools/check_browser.mjs` serves the built book and clicks every button as a reader would, four pages at a time. A button fails on:

- an error;
- a "Differs from the book" check;
- a figure that does not draw;
- no result within the timeout.

A page fails when it has fewer buttons than runnable examples, so nothing passes by clicking nothing.

Python warnings printed in the browser are listed, not failed: they come from Pyodide's package versions. The run writes a summary table to the GitHub run page and a JSON report as an artifact. `make check-browser` runs it locally after `make html`.

`run-in-browser.yml` runs it in two modes:

- **Pinned (the gate):**
  - On a PR it covers the chapters the PR touches, or all of them when the runner changes.
  - Every Monday it covers all chapters, because process-improve and plotly reach the browser from PyPI.
- **Newest (advisory):** on the schedule and by hand, it builds against the newest Pyodide release and ends its summary with whether bumping the pin is safe.

**Its first run found a real bug.** Chapter 4's `scatter_matrix(..., diagonal="kde")` failed with "No module named 'scipy'". pandas imports scipy inside its KDE code, where the worker's import scan cannot see it. The example only worked because an earlier example in the old, larger prelude imported scipy. CPython has every package installed, so no Python-side check could see this. The fix has two parts:

- `LAZY` maps pandas' KDE spellings to scipy.
- For the next library that imports late, a `ModuleNotFoundError` for a package Pyodide ships now loads the package and tells the reader to click "Run again". It does not rerun the example by itself, since running a half-finished example twice could leave state the book never had.

Both parts were checked in Chromium: the fallback alone recovers on the second click, and with the rule all 44 least-squares buttons pass on the first click. The GitHub run of the commit before the fix failed on exactly that button, which shows the gate catches it.

**Also surfaced (not failures):** two examples print a `MatplotlibDeprecationWarning` in the browser, from inside statsmodels' `plot_acf` on Pyodide's matplotlib 3.10:

- `process-monitoring-exercises.rst:812`
- `least-squares-exercises.rst:712`

## Checks

- `pytest tests/test_block_deps.py tests/test_run_in_browser.py tests/test_check_run_deps.py`: 29 passed, including 6 new block_deps cases.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean.
- `make check-run-deps`: 0 differences, all six chapters.
- `node tools/check_browser.mjs` locally: 187 buttons, 186 passing before the KDE fix, then the least-squares chapter 44 of 44 after it.

title: Fix ChatGPT token exchange: add PyJWT (Fixes PODSKRIFT-N)
body: ## Summary Production ChatGPT connect was failing: `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'jwt'` because deploy never ran `pip install`, and real ChatGPT token calls were returning 401 without Sentry visibility. This PR fixes the install path and the auth/CSP gaps. ### Fixes 1. **PyJWT in prod (PODSKRIFT-N)** — Pin `PyJWT[crypto]==2.15.1` and `cryptography==50.0.2` in `requirements.txt`. Deploy now runs `.venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt` after pull and before restart (fails the deploy if pip fails). CI installs `requirements.txt` first. Smoke test imports `jwt` + `RSAAlgorithm` and round-trips RS256. 2. **Harden `private_key_jwt`** — RS256-only; short assertion lifetime; `client_id` from assertion iss/sub when omitted; JWKS refetch throttle; keep `client_secret_post` in discovery. 3. **Dual CIMD auth (ChatGPT)** — When `token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported` includes both `none` and `private_key_jwt`, accept either: verify assertion when present, otherwise public-client + PKCE. Clients that only declare `private_key_jwt` still require an assertion. 4. **Sentry on refusals** — Every refused authorize/token response `capture_message` at warning with tags `oauth_step`, `reason`, `client_id_host` (never tokens/assertions/codes). 5. **Consent CSP (PODSKRIFT-M)** — Allow the validated `redirect_uri` origin in `form-action` on both enforced and report-only CSP for the consent response. Also folds the What’s-new removal of the internal ChatGPT OAuth changelog entry. **Do not merge until CI is green.** No new changelog feature entry.

title: Fix packaged app SDK sources and manager runtime dependencies
body:
The published minimal app could not deploy because its manifest retained an expanded local SDK source table. Once that was removed, its GUI-generated RUN failed because the manager environment did not declare the orchestration SDK. Fix both packaging and the shared dependency gap across the public builtins and templates.

## Repro

Deploy a copied packaged minimal app outside the AGILAB checkout. The source path in `[tool.uv.sources.agi-web]` is absent. After removing the override, RUN raises `ModuleNotFoundError: agi_cluster` in the app's manager environment.

## Root Cause

The build sanitizer only handled inline source entries. Manager manifests declared pieces of the SDK but omitted the `agi-core` bundle required by generated orchestration snippets.

Strip expanded and quoted SDK source tables from generated manifests. Declare `agi-core` for 14 builtin managers and five template managers, and document the manager/worker dependency boundary. Keep source checkout overrides and dynamic worker loading intact.

## Regression Test

- 72 targeted tests passed: dependency hygiene and wheel sanitizer.
- 143 app contract checks passed across all 14 builtins.
- Candidate minimal wheel and sdist contain identical sanitized manifests; the worker bytes match source.
- Simulated sanitization of all 33 public app/worker manifests preserves project metadata and valid TOML.
- A real published GUI deployed the candidate app manifest and completed RUN on 1,000 input rows, producing 1,000 Parquet rows. Its deployment also installed local SDK sources; this is not qualification of a wholly PyPI-sourced stack.
- All eight discoverable app-local suites passed: 62 tests, no failures or errors. Six other builtins have no app-local test target; all 14 passed the 143 contract checks.

Cython compilation, GPU/RAPIDS execution and Linux execution are outside this manifest fix's qualification. No new release is claimed.

## Agent Metadata

- Tokki: 1.0.68.
- Agent/runtime: Codex, private client 0.162.1.
- Model and reasoning effort: not exposed by the runtime.
- /fast: not used.
- Confirmed human operator: Jean-Pierre MORARD (`jpmorard`); authenticated GitHub actor checked.

## Review Evidence

Primary agent source review plus deterministic dependency, packaging and loader-contract checks. No sub-agents were used. The review preserved worker imports, worker manifests and dynamic Python/Cython selection.

title: Apworld uploads: static inspection, worker import test, approval
body:
## What does this change?

Closes #21

Admins can upload custom `.apworld` files. Each one goes through three stages (DESIGN.md §4, Apworlds):

1. **Static inspection in the web service, with no code run** (`apsui/apworld_inspect.py`, standard library zipfile and json only):
   - the file is a valid zip with everything inside one folder named after the file, which must be a Python module name (`my_game.apworld` → `my_game/__init__.py`);
   - no absolute, `..` or symlinked paths;
   - size limits: 64 MB, 256 MB unpacked, 5000 entries;
   - `archipelago.json` is found the way AP finds it and parsed (64 KB cap); it must name the `game`, and its versions must be well formed;
   - `compatible_version` is at most 7;
   - `minimum_ap_version` and `maximum_ap_version` are checked against the pinned AP version, which the image now sets as `APSUI_ARCHIPELAGO_VERSION`;
   - the file is hashed with SHA-256.

   A failure rejects the file on the spot. The record stays, for the upload log (#23).
2. **Worker import test:** a new `test-apworld` job loads the world in its own process and its own custom worlds folder, with no network. It reports whether the world loaded, which games it registered, whether it replaces a built-in world, and the full traceback if not. A world that fails to load, or registers a different game than its manifest names, is rejected.
3. **Approval:**
   - The apworld then waits as *needs approval*.
   - With `APSUI_APWORLD_APPROVAL=auto` it goes straight into the library, except one that replaces a built-in world, which **always** waits.
   - Approved files are stored in `/data/library/apworlds/<sha256>.apworld`. What's stored is always the uploaded bytes, never a copy back from the worker.
   - The same bytes can't be uploaded twice while one copy is checking, pending or in the library; after a rejection they can be tried again.

**API:** `POST /api/apworlds` (202), `GET /api/apworlds`, `GET /api/apworlds/{id}` (the approval screen's data), `POST /api/apworlds/{id}/approve`, `POST /api/apworlds/{id}/reject`.

**UI:** a new Apworlds card on the admin page.
- Each row has a label in the design's format (`Game · custom · v1.2.0 · a3f9c1`), a status badge, and a *replaces built-in* badge where it applies.
- **Review** opens the approval screen: manifest fields, the SHA-256, the uploader, the import test result and traceback, the file list and the raw `archipelago.json`, with Approve and Reject.
- A built-in replacement shows an orange warning with the built-in's version.

**Replacing a built-in world needed a workaround.** AP 0.6.8 loads built-in worlds first and *skips* a custom apworld whose game is already loaded. So the import test unregisters the built-in world in its own child process (dropping its modules when the folder names collide, e.g. `apquest.apworld`), then loads the apworld the way AP does.

Validation, generation and MultiServer need the same treatment before an approved replacement can actually be used. I raised that as **#77** (Alpha 1) rather than widening this PR.

**Not in this PR:**
- YAMLs choosing a library version, and version locking (#22). `validate-yaml` still sees built-in worlds only.
- Removing an apworld from the library: whether one is in use only becomes known with #22.
- The approval setting moves to the settings page with #25. The uploader is always `admin` in Alpha 1.

## How was it tested?

- **Backend: 106 tests** (33 new).
  - Every static inspection rule, including symlinks, `..` paths, a misnamed folder, a missing `__init__.py`, bad or missing manifests, and the AP version range.
  - The API flow: check → pending → approve into the library; admin reject; rejection by inspection with no job submitted; import failure with traceback; failed job; unreadable worker output; built-in replacement flagged; auto approval, which still waits for a replacement; duplicate refused, then allowed again after a rejection.
- **Worker:** 15 tests. **Server:** 6. **Frontend:** 14 (new: approval screen with the built-in warning, then approve). ruff, mypy, oxlint, Prettier and tsc are clean.
- **Smoke test against real AP 0.6.8** in the image: four sample apworlds, built from source in `worker/tests/apworld/` (no binaries committed), go through the worker:
  - `loaded__apsui_test_world`: loaded `['APSUI Test World']`
  - `replaces__apquest`: loaded and flagged as replacing built-in APQuest 2.0.0, with the folder name colliding with the built-in's
  - `failed__apsui_broken`: `ModuleNotFoundError` reported
  - `failed__apsui_mismatch`: the manifest names a different game than the world registers
- **Compose test, end to end:** all four uploaded through the web API to the real worker. Two wait (APQuest flagged `replaces_builtin: 2.0.0`), two are rejected. Approving one puts it in `/data/library/apworlds/<sha256>.apworld`. All the isolation checks still pass.

## Checklist
- [x] Lint and tests pass
- [x] No ROMs, saves, player YAMLs or secrets committed. The sample worlds are a few lines written for these tests.
- [x] Touches uploads, worker or server isolation? Explain the security impact above
  - The web service still never imports AP code; inspection reads only the zip directory and the manifest, under size caps.
  - Apworld code runs only in the worker's `test-apworld` job: its own process, its own custom worlds folder, no network, the usual time limit.
  - The worker's result is parsed strictly and only decides the status. The library always gets the uploaded bytes.
- [x] Docs updated (README / DESIGN.md) if behaviour changed: DESIGN.md §4 (decisions made while building it) and CONTRIBUTING (sample inputs).

title: fix(llms): resolve broken imports in llms provenance wrappers
body:
## Description

The four `*WithProvenance` LLM wrappers in `semantica/llms/llms_provenance.py` import the class they wrap lazily, inside `__init__`, from module paths that exist nowhere in the repository: `.groq_llm`, `.openai_llm`, `.huggingface_llm`, and `.lite_llm`. The real modules are `.groq`, `.openai`, `.huggingface`, and `.litellm`. Because the import lives inside `__init__`, importing the wrapper classes succeeds and only instantiating one raises `ModuleNotFoundError`, and every surrounding test guards construction with `except ImportError: pytest.skip(...)`, so the breakage never turned the suite red. This PR points the four wrappers at the real modules and adds a regression test that fails, rather than skips, when a wrapper cannot resolve its target class.

Making the wrappers instantiable also made two latent gaps reachable, and this PR closes both. First, the wrappers only overrode `generate()`, so `generate_structured()` and `generate_typed()` fell through `__getattr__` to the wrapped LLM and wrote no provenance entry. Second, the token and cost extraction inside `generate()` reads `response.usage` and `response.cost`, but the OpenAI, Groq and LiteLLM providers returned a plain `str`, so the recorded metadata had `None` for token counts and cost. Both were reported by Qodo on this PR.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Performance improvement
- [ ] Code refactoring

## Related Issues

No existing issue covers the import defect. It is the same defect that #1872 fixed for the ingest and parse wrappers, originally reported in a comment on #1383 by @eeee2345, which noted that these imports sit inside `__init__` so the classes import fine and only instantiation would raise. That comment named the ingest wrapper, #1872 extended the same fix to the parse wrapper, and this PR extends it to the four llms wrappers. The two follow-on gaps were reported by Qodo in review on this PR.

## Changes Made

- `semantica/llms/llms_provenance.py`: `GroqLLMWithProvenance.__init__` now imports `Groq` from `.groq` (was `GroqLLM` from the non-existent `.groq_llm`); `OpenAILLMWithProvenance` imports `OpenAI` from `.openai` (was `OpenAILLM` from `.openai_llm`); `HuggingFaceLLMWithProvenance` imports `HuggingFaceLLM` from `.huggingface` (was `.huggingface_llm`); `LiteLLMWithProvenance` imports `LiteLLM` from `.litellm` (was `.lite_llm`). The class name changes for the first two; only the module path changes for the last two.
- `semantica/llms/llms_provenance.py`: all four wrappers now override `generate_structured()` and `generate_typed()` and route both through a shared `_track_generation()` helper on the mixin, so neither falls through `__getattr__` any more. Return values are passed through unchanged, and the typed entry records the retry budget (`max_retries`) next to `generation_mode`.
- `semantica/semantic_extract/providers.py`: added `ResponseText`, a `str` subclass that also carries `usage` and `cost`. `OpenAIProvider.generate()` and `GroqProvider.generate()` now return it instead of a plain `str`, so the provider response's usage survives to the caller without changing the public return type.
- `semantica/llms/litellm.py`: `LiteLLM.generate()` now returns a `ResponseText` too, taking `cost` from the response's `_hidden_params['response_cost']`.
- `tests/provenance/test_llms_provenance_imports.py` (new): instantiates all four wrappers and asserts `self._llm` is the real implementation class, deliberately without the `except ImportError: pytest.skip(...)` guard the surrounding suites use. The providers behind each class are stubbed so the tests stay offline and do not require the optional `groq` / `litellm` packages.
- `tests/provenance/test_llms_provenance_tracking.py` (new): drives the wrappers with a stub LLM and a recording provenance manager to pin both follow-on fixes. One group asserts `generate_structured()` / `generate_typed()` each write exactly one entry with the right `generation_mode` and preserve the wrapped return value; another asserts the recorded metadata carries `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `total_tokens` and `total_cost` when the response supplies them, and stays `None` when it does not; a third pins `ResponseText` behaving as a `str`.
- `tests/provenance/test_llms_provenance.py`: `TestHuggingFaceLLMProvenance::test_without_provenance` now stubs `HuggingFaceLLMProvider`. With the import fixed that test no longer skips, and without the stub it constructs a real `HuggingFaceLLM`, which downloads `gpt2` on every run. The repository's suite is meant to be offline and service-free.
- Removed trailing whitespace on blank lines, an unused `typing.Dict` import, and two unused locals, and wrapped the over-length lines in the touched files so they pass the repository's flake8 configuration.

## Testing

The chosen targets are the modules' own documented entry classes and their signatures accept how the wrappers call them: `Groq.__init__(model=..., api_key=..., **kwargs)`, `OpenAI.__init__(...)`, `HuggingFaceLLM.__init__(...)`, and `LiteLLM.__init__(model, ...)` (whose `model` is required, so the test passes one). With the fix restored the same 4 pass. For the two follow-on fixes, `tests/provenance/test_llms_provenance_tracking.py` is 17 passed. `pytest tests/provenance/` reports 403 passed, 14 skipped. flake8 with the repository's arguments exits 0 on both test files and adds no new findings on the three source files, and `python -m build --no-isolation` produces `semantica-0.7.0.tar.gz` and `semantica-0.7.0-py3-none-any.whl` (I used `--no-isolation` because this machine has no `venv` module for the default isolated build).

The two follow-on fixes are the same defect surfacing on those four wrappers once they became reachable, so they are kept here rather than split out. title: feat: scale IBM dataset to 120k with global dashboard filters and ful…
body:
Description
Summary of Changes: This PR introduces a major overhaul of our ETL pipeline to ingest real-world data and significantly upgrades the analytics dashboard to support global department filtering and robust error handling.

1. IBM Dataset Integration & Synthesis (ETL)

Kaggle Integration: Added kagglehub to requirements.txt and rewrote synthesizer.py to automatically download the base 1,470 rows of the IBM HR Analytics dataset.
Volume Scaling: Programmatically scaled the dataset up to 120,000 rows using sampling with replacement, while generating unique mock identities via Faker.
Engineered Data Distributions: Implemented a 50/50 split architecture. Half of the dataset retains the exact native IBM distributions (Sales, R&D, HR). The other half is programmatically reassigned to 3 new custom departments (Engineering, Operations, Finance) with mathematically altered attrition and performance scores to create distinct business scenarios.
2. Analytics Dashboard Enhancements (Streamlit)

Global Department Filters: Lifted the department select box to the top of the analytics page. All OLAP SQL queries (get_performance_trends, get_attrition_risk, etc.) now accept and apply this filter globally via WHERE clauses, making the entire dashboard interactive.
Graceful Fallbacks: Fixed an over-sensitive UI bug where an empty chart (e.g., zero active bottlenecks for a specific department) would mistakenly trigger a false database connection failure and override the UI with synthetic CSV data.
3. Bug Fixes & Infrastructure

PyMySQL Type Safety: Fixed a TypeError in Streamlit caused by Python attempting to do math on decimal.Decimal types returned by PyMySQL aggregations (AVG).
Path Resolution: Added sys.path injection to src/run_etl.py to fix ModuleNotFoundError issues when running the script directly from the CLI.
Schema Automation: Added run_schema.py to easily drop/recreate the OLTP and OLAP structures.

title: fix(deps): detect any distribution that provides `cv2`
body:
### Problem

`cv2` is shipped by four mutually exclusive distributions: `opencv-python`, `opencv-python-headless`, `opencv-contrib-python` and `opencv-contrib-python-headless`. `is_dep_available()` resolved the `opencv-contrib-python` **distribution name**, so PaddleX raised `DependencyError` even when a fully working `cv2` was already installed from another build.

On a `python:3.11-slim-bookworm` base image — a very common choice for serving containers — the non-headless builds cannot be used at all. Importing `cv2` from `opencv-contrib-python` fails with:

ImportError: libGL.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory

The slim image ships no GUI libraries, and the wheel links against them even though nothing in a serving workload ever opens a window. So today the options are either to install extra system packages (`libgl1`, `libglib2.0-0`) purely so that an unused GUI backend can load, or to patch PaddleX locally. The headless wheel has no such dependency and is the natural choice for containers — but PaddleX refuses to recognize it.

### Reproduction

In an environment where `cv2` comes from `opencv-python-headless`, any pipeline fails at construction time:

paddlex.utils.deps.DependencyError: OCR requires additional dependencies. To install them,
run pip install "paddlex[ocr]==<PADDLEX_VERSION>" ...

even though `import cv2` works and reports `4.10.0`. The message is misleading: the dependency *is* installed, just under a different distribution name.

### Fix

Check for the `cv2` import package, exactly like the existing handling of `onnxruntime` a few lines above, which has the same one-import/several-distributions shape.

### Compatibility

- **No packaging change.** `paddlex[...]` still depends on `opencv-contrib-python == 4.10.0.84`, so a plain `pip install paddlex[...]` behaves exactly as before.
- PaddleX uses no contrib-only OpenCV API (`cv2.ximgproc`, `cv2.freetype`, `cv2.aruco`, …), so accepting the non-contrib builds loses nothing in practice.
- `is_dep_available("opencv-contrib-python", check_version=True)` is not used anywhere in the codebase; the version pin was already unenforced at runtime, same as for `onnxruntime`.

### Verification

Environment: `paddlepaddle==3.2.0`, `paddlex` installed from this branch, and **only** `opencv-python-headless==4.10.0.84` present (no `opencv-contrib-python`, `opencv-contrib-python-headless` or `opencv-python`).

Running `api_examples/pipelines/test_ocr.py` unchanged:

- **before this patch** — `DependencyError: \`OCR\` requires additional dependencies`
- **after this patch** — 33 text lines recognized, visualization saved correctly

Also checked: `black==24.4.2`, `flake8==7.0.0`, `isort==5.12.0` and the local `.precommit` hooks (`check_imports.py`, `check_license_headers.py`, `check_py38_compat.py`) all pass.

title: fix(agent-server): report the API error the stream named instead of the OOM guess (#3340)
body:
## Description

When Claude Code names an API error in its stream (for example `API Error: 400 Output blocked by content filtering policy`) and exits 1, the stream parser records it on `metadata.error_message`, but the failure path built its detail from stderr only. Stderr is empty on that shape, so the user was told "no diagnostic output — most likely OOM kill" and sent to raise memory limits.

The headless and chat failure paths now report the error the stream named:

- zero-token 503: `Execution failed: API Error: 400 Output blocked by content filtering policy`
- generic 500: `Task execution failed (exit code 1): API Error: …`

A run where neither the stream nor stderr gave a reason keeps today's text. Auth detection still runs first and is unchanged.

**Not fixed here (#2909):** the zero-token case is still a 503, and the backend classifies any 503 from the agent as an auth failure, so SUB-003 still switches subscriptions on a content-filter refusal. This PR makes the message truthful; the classification is #2909.

**Behaviour to know about:**

- A stream-named error now outranks non-empty stderr, a small step beyond the reported empty-stderr case.
- The old guess contained "OOM", which forces the backend's text classifier to "not auth". The new text has no such marker, so on text-classified paths (the 500s) an API error whose text contains `401`, `403`, `forbidden`, `credentials` or `oauth` now reads as auth.
- Billing and model-access errors on the zero-token path keep their wording, but the prefix changes from `Execution failed with no output (exit code N):` to `Execution failed:`. Nothing in `src/` matches on the old prefix.
- The optional plain-wording mapping from the issue (content filter, `overloaded_error`, `invalid_request_error`) is not included.

Codex already falls back to the stream error; Gemini records no stream error, so there is nothing to surface there.

## Related Issue

Fixes #3340

## Journey Impact

Journey Impact: none: bug fix to an error message on an existing failure path; no journey promise is added or changed

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Testing

- [x] I have tested this locally
- [x] New tests added (if applicable)
- [ ] All existing tests pass
- [x] Every new test **executes** the changed path

`tests/unit/test_3340_stream_api_error_detail.py`: 21 passed. Neighbouring unit files (46 files touching the executors, stream parser and classifiers): 915 passed, 2 failed — both in `unit/test_2889_error_code_header.py` (`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tests'`), failing identically without this change. The full `tests/unit` suite was not run locally. The stream line in the test is reconstructed from the real API-error event shape plus the sentence in the issue's log, not a fresh capture.

Mutation: with the four source files reverted, 8 of the 21 tests go red — `test_zero_token_exit_reports_the_api_error_not_the_oom_guess`, `test_the_api_error_wins_over_unrelated_stderr`, `test_a_turn_that_spent_tokens_reports_the_api_error_too`, `test_a_credential_in_the_api_error_is_redacted`, `test_auth_wording_in_a_stream_error_never_reaches_the_new_text`, `test_diagnose_returns_the_stream_error`, `test_chat_exit_1_reports_the_api_error` (both parameters); restored byte-identical.
