title: fix(ai-ml): the dynamic model loads consult the pinned registry, and every B615 suppression is enumerated with its reason (#13034)
body:
Refs #13034

Single-issue rationale: model revision pinning (#13034) is the only open issue whose work touches these from_pretrained call sites and the B615 guard. It shares no file with the other in-flight fork PRs, so it lands on its own.

## Thinking Path

The issue says 16 `nosec B615` hits in 10 files and no pinned-model registry in `ssot_config.py`. Both are stale. Measured on `origin/main@0a4cffce`:

| | count |
|---|---|
| `grep -rn "nosec B615"` hits, repo-wide | 16 across 10 files |
| …of those, actual bandit suppressions | **4**, in **3** files |
| …prose (docs, changelog, two module docstrings) | 12 |

A registry already exists — `autobot_shared/pinned_model_registry.py`, split out of `ssot_config.py` deliberately because that file is ratchet-frozen at 3298 lines. Adding a second one under the issue's original name would be the violation, so this PR extends the existing one.

**AC1 as written is not reachable and should not be the criterion.** `grep -rn "nosec B615" == 0` is satisfied and violated by *prose*: `docs/developer/MODEL_REVISION_PINNING.md`, the changelog and the registry docstring all have to name the marker to explain it, and a single comment discussing the marker would break the check again. A guard keyed on text would forbid documenting the rule it enforces. So the enforceable property here is: the suppression set is **enumerated, reasoned, cannot grow unnoticed, and every entry claiming to be registry-backed really calls the resolver**.

**Why the three dynamic suppressions are not simply deleted.** `layer_inference.py` and `model_inspector.py` take a caller-supplied `model_name` that may be a local path or a provider tag that is not a Hub repo id at all. `bandit/plugins/huggingface_unsafe_download.py` returns early for *any* non-`ast.Constant` `revision=` keyword — "benefit of the doubt". So passing `revision=<expr>` silences B615 whether or not anything was actually resolved. Dropping the suppression on that basis would read as safe over a load that still resolves against a mutable default branch. The honest shape is: pin what the registry knows, keep the suppression for the remainder, and state the remainder.

**I could not establish a revision for any of the three dynamic call sites, and did not invent one.** The model id is not knowable without running the program. `MODEL_REVISION_PINNING.md` names the two mechanisms that would close them — trust-on-first-use pinning, or requiring the caller to supply a revision — and both need a persistence and bump story this registry does not have. That remains #13034's open scope; hence `Refs`, not `Closes`.

## What Changed

- **`autobot_shared/pinned_model_registry.py`** — new `pinned_revision_kwargs(model_ref)`: `{"revision": <pin>}` when the name is registered, `{}` when it is not. The deliberate soft counterpart to `get_pinned_revision`, which still raises for a *fixed* call site so it cannot omit a pin by accident. No second registry; one `_REGISTRY`, two accessors, asserted to agree over every entry.
- **`llm_shared/optimization/layer_inference.py` (2 sites), `model_inspector.py` (1 site)** — each now consults the registry, so a registered model id is pinned even on a dynamic path. The comment each carried — *"revision pinning managed operationally"*, the sentence #13034 was filed about, which nothing implemented — is replaced by a statement of what actually holds. The suppressions stay, for the reason above.
- **`repo_tests/nosec_b615_suppressions_are_registry_backed_13034_test.py`** (new, 16 tests) — enumerates every live suppression with its reason and count; fails on an unrecorded one, a stale entry, a count change, or a `registry_backed=True` entry whose suppressed `from_pretrained` call does not itself pass the resolver pin (AST-checked per call: `revision=` or `**<name>` bound from `pinned_revision_kwargs` in the same function).
- **`docs/developer/MODEL_REVISION_PINNING.md`** — the stale "two of the original 18 remain" section replaced with the measured table, the `{}`-is-not-a-pin rule, and why AC1's literal grep is the wrong criterion.
- **`autobot_shared/pinned_model_registry_test.py`** — 5 unit tests for the new accessor, including one that asserts it can never yield a revision that is not in `_REGISTRY`.
- Changelog fragment.

### The prose trap, handled at the discriminator

The guard's population is built from **`tokenize` COMMENT tokens**, not from file text: a `# nosec B615` is a `COMMENT`, every mention in a docstring, f-string or fixture is a `STRING`. `test_prose_occurrences_in_the_tree_are_not_counted` names three **live tree** files that carry the marker only inside string literals — `pinned_model_registry.py`, `model_revision_pinning_enforced_17804_test.py`, and the guard itself — so the contrast is tree evidence, not only a synthetic fixture. Six further fixtures cover trailing comment / docstring / f-string / error message / standalone comment / absent.

### File-size ceiling, not raised

`layer_inference.py` is pinned at **939** in both `scripts/python_file_size_known_large.py` and `repo_tests/python_file_size_ratchet_baseline.py` — zero slack. The edit is **net zero**: the new import is paid for by collapsing a 3-line `raise ImportError(` with an implicit string concatenation into 2 lines, and both call sites fold the resolver into the existing `kwargs` construction. Final count 939; neither record moved (#17970).

## Verification

```
$ grep -rn "nosec B615" --include=*.py .          # code-only, on this branch
layer_inference.py:198, :565 | model_inspector.py:263 | model_manager.py:120, :124
(+ docstring-only mentions in pinned_model_registry.py, two repo_tests files)

$ bandit -c .bandit -f json <the 4 files>
results 0 | skipped B615: layer_inference.py 2, model_inspector.py 1, model_manager.py 1  (= 4)
no "nosec encountered, but no failed test" warning
```

**Bandit finding worth recording:** a *nested call on the suppressed line* (`from_pretrained(m, **resolver(m))`) makes bandit emit `nosec encountered (B615), but no failed test` for the inner node — the real suppression still fires (`skipped_tests` 1), but it reads as a dead suppression. `model_inspector.py` hoists the resolver call off the load line for that reason, with a comment saying so.

```
$ pytest repo_tests/nosec_b615_..._13034_test.py autobot_shared/pinned_model_registry_test.py \
         repo_tests/model_revision_pinning_enforced_17804_test.py repo_tests/reach_declarations_test.py
356 passed in 112.62s
```

`reach_declarations_test` is the mutation half of the reach floor: it runs this guard's `discover` against an empty tree and requires the floor to fire. Floor 6,000 / band 6,000–6,600 against 6,363 tracked `.py` files today.

### Mutation results — every one reverted afterwards

| # | Mutation | Expected | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | real `# nosec B615` added to a non-allowlisted file (`autobot_shared/paths.py`) | fail | **1 failed**, 12 passed |
| M2 | **contrast** — same string added to the same file, but only inside a docstring | pass | **13 passed** |
| M3 | resolver call removed from `layer_inference.py` (import left in place) | fail | **1 failed**, 12 passed |
| M4 | one `# nosec B615` deleted from `layer_inference.py:565` | fail | **1 failed**, 12 passed |
| M5 | `tokenize` discriminator replaced by a line-substring match | fail | **5 failed**, 8 passed |
| — | restored | pass | **13 passed** |

M2 and M5 are the pair that matters: the guard is not satisfiable by a comment discussing `nosec B615`, and it stops being correct the moment the AST/token discriminator is swapped for text.

Pre-push ran under Python 3.14 (`/home/martins/.venv-python-suite`); no hook bypassed. Push verified: `git merge-base --is-ancestor 810ead0294 origin/issue-13034-model-revision-pinning` → rc 0.

### Review follow-up (written at 62c108b2b9; rebased onto main `8b7de912`; fixtures at `ffcab8986e`; replayed onto the remote branch with current main merged in as pushed head **`9667521485`**)

- **Guard, per call (7da3b29f8e):** the registry-backed check no longer accepts "the file calls the resolver somewhere". Each suppressed `from_pretrained` call must itself carry `revision=` or `**<name>` bound from the resolver in the same function. Contrast pair as synthetic fixtures: resolver called but `**pin` dropped from the load fails; `**pin` passed passes (plus a pin bound in a different function fails, and a resolver call folded into a dict literal passes). Break/restore on the real tree: `**pin` removed from `model_inspector.py:264` gave 1 failed (`test_every_dynamic_suppression_consults_the_registry`, line 264 named); restored byte-identical (`git diff --quiet`), 1 passed.
- **Doc (62c108b2b9):** "The mechanism" now states the dynamic `model_name` sites are the one exception (`pinned_revision_kwargs` returns `{}` on a miss) and links the remaining-scope section, so the doc gives one rule.
- **Guard fixtures (ffcab8986e):** inline `**pinned_revision_kwargs(name)`, explicit `revision=` pass; bare `**kwargs` parameter, `kwargs = {}` and `revision=None` fail. Known limit: a resolver-bound name counts wherever it was bound in the function; a later unpinned reassignment is not tracked.
- Tests: `repo_tests/nosec_b615_..._13034_test.py`, `model_revision_pinning_enforced_17804_test.py`, `autobot_shared/pinned_model_registry_test.py`: 54 passed.

### Not done, stated rather than implied

- The three dynamic call sites still resolve an **unregistered** caller-supplied repo id against a mutable default branch. No revision could be established for them; none was guessed.
- `docs/research/*.md` carry their own stale counts. Not touched — a different owner's scope.
- `autobot-npu-worker/.../model_manager.py` keeps its suppression unchanged: it loads a local directory already verified against its pin (#17087), so `revision=` would be a no-op rather than a guarantee.

## Model Used

Claude Opus 5 (1M context)

title: feat: let score() and score_async() name scores with a dict of scorers
body:
### Problem or current behavior

When rescoring a log, scorer names are generated automatically (`match`, `match1`, ...). Callers cannot choose names that distinguish different configurations of the same scorer; passing a dict raises `TypeError: Unexpected scorer type: <class 'dict'>`.

Fixes #4197.

### Result or new behavior

`score()` and `score_async()` now accept a dict mapping names to scorers, for example `score(log, {"answer_match": match()})`.

Aliases are preserved when recomputing metrics (including through `edit_score()`), recovering logs and overwriting scores through `inspect score` without `--scorer`. List appends to logs with recorded names use consistent generated names across samples.

This picks up the spec here after #4234 was closed as stale, and addresses the two points from its review: rescoring from saved logs, and `Task`'s use of `Scorers`.

### Compatibility and migration

No migration required. Existing single-scorer and list calls behave as before, and logs that never use a dict are written and read as before. Dicts are supported by the post-hoc scoring APIs, not `Task` or `task_with()`, which raise a `TypeError` naming `score()`. The issue suggests extending `Scorers`; it is unchanged instead, and `score()` and `score_async()` take a separate `NamedScorers` type, because `Task` and `task_with()` share `Scorers` and don't accept a dict. The issue's optional `(name, scorer)` tuple form isn't included.

Sample scores, score events, aggregate scorer identities (`EvalScore.scorer`) and reductions use the aliases. Registered scorer names and parameters remain in the log header to rebuild the scorers. The log schema is unchanged: the alias is stored in the header scorer's metadata. Use updated Inspect when recomputing, editing or recovering aliased logs: older versions replay the header's registered names, so they recompute the aliased scores without their scorers' metrics, using default metrics or those of a registered scorer with the same name, and add empty entries under the generated names.

`inspect score` keeps recorded aliases when overwriting without `--scorer`; an explicit `--scorer` isn't rebuilt from the header, so it gets generated names. Appending, the prompt's default, generates names as before, since reusing the aliases would collide.

`__score_name__` is now reserved in scorer metadata: evaluating or scoring with a scorer that sets it raises a `ValueError`. Existing logs containing it are interpreted as recording that name; custom metadata must use another key.

Dict-valued scorers retain their existing component names, so shared value keys can still collide in dataframe columns.

### Validation

Before (`main`): `score(log, {"strict": match(location="end"), "loose": match(location="begin")})` raises `TypeError: Unexpected scorer type: <class 'dict'>`. After: sample scores, `results.scores` and score events use `strict` and `loose`, and `recompute_metrics()` returns the same names, metrics and reductions.

Tests cover aliases, append/overwrite behavior, metric recomputation, recovery, CLI behavior, invalid and colliding names, a dict naming a header scorer that never produced a score, and streamed samples, including a name conflict on a streamed sample that cancels scorers already running on other samples. Each new test fails without the change it covers.

All runs below are at the PR head, `8c4b0a3f0` (merged with `main` at `697fde94e`):

- Focused tests: `OPENAI_API_KEY=placeholder pytest tests/_eval/test_score.py tests/_cli/test_score.py tests/log/test_recover_write.py tests/test_task_with.py --runapi`: 98 passed, 0 failed, 58 skipped.
- `make check`: passes, with `inspect_sentinel` installed from the commit pinned in `build.yml`. It isn't in the dev requirements, and mypy needs it for `src/inspect_ai/_sentinel`.
- `make test`: 15729 passed, 1 failed, 7316 skipped. The failure, `tests/test_extensions.py::test_extension_model` (`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'inspect_package.modelapi'`), fails the same way on `main` (`7de3f8f1d`) in the same environment, so it's unrelated to this change.

Not tested: `inspect score` end to end, with or without `--stream` (its naming step and `score_async()` rescoring are tested separately), multiple epochs and reducers, Scout scanners as dict values, `copy=False`, `edit_score()` directly (covered through `recompute_metrics()`), and older Inspect versions reading aliased logs. `eval_retry()` after an overwrite rescore mismatches names, as it does today for any overwrite rescore.

Checked once with a script, not by tests: an aliased scorer that returns a dict keeps its alias through `recompute_metrics()` and an `.eval` write and read; `HeadlineMetric(scorer=<alias>, score=...)` selects it; score events carry the aliases; an empty dict behaves like an empty list; and a streamed pass with a dict records its names.

### Slow tests

- Trio: `OPENAI_API_KEY=placeholder pytest tests/_eval/test_score.py tests/_cli/test_score.py tests/log tests/scorer --runapi --runtrio`: 591 passed, 0 failed, 2284 skipped (at `8c4b0a3f0`).
- API-gated scoring tests: run with `--runapi` and `OPENAI_API_KEY=placeholder` in the runs above. They build the log's OpenAI model but never call it.
- Not run: live provider tests; this change calls no provider.

### Agent review

Co-authored by Carlos Crespo and Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5). Reviewed by GPT-6.1 (`gpt-6.1-sol`, reasoning `max`), read-only, in six passes: rounds 1–4 via Codex CLI, round 1 in a fresh reviewer context and rounds 2–4 continued in the same reviewer chat; round 5 in a new session (fresh context) in the Codex app, on the final diff, and round 6 continued in that session. Round 7 was a fresh-context review of the ready-for-review head by Claude Fable 5.1 (Claude Code), a different model from the author and from rounds 1–6; it also wrote the round 7 fix, on a separate branch, with a failing test first.

- Round 1, full review: 7 findings, 1 question. Fixed alias handling in recovery and CLI scoring, collision checks, reserved metadata handling, recorded-name validation, generated names next to recorded ones, and Trio coverage. Dismissed: solver-score replay in logs without aliases (pre-existing); rejecting names already used as score names (intended: dataframe columns are keyed by them); pre-change logs carrying the reserved key (documented above); a cancellation test (the up-front validation raises before any await; the per-sample check added in round 3 got one in round 5); `eval_retry()` (pre-existing).
- Round 2, full review: 6 findings, 2 questions. Fixed inconsistent generated names, header-only collisions, validation order and empty-log names; strengthened round-trip assertions. Legacy solver-name replay was dismissed as pre-existing. Shared dict-value dataframe collisions remain out of scope because they are also pre-existing.
- Round 3, focused follow-up: 2 findings. Fixed sample-only name collisions and converted the consistency test to async for Trio coverage.
- Round 4, focused follow-up: no actionable findings.
- Round 5, fresh-context review of the final diff: 1 medium and 2 low findings, 1 question; no implementation defect. Fixed: a cancellation test for a streamed name conflict while other samples' scorers run (medium); Validation now names the commit of every run (low). Dismissed: an end-to-end `inspect score` test (low: its naming step and rescoring are tested separately; listed under Not tested). The question (aliased dict-valued scorers, headlines, score events, an empty dict, a successful streamed pass) was answered with a script; see Validation.
- Round 6, focused follow-up on the round 5 fixes and this description: no findings in the new test; agreed with the round 5 dismissal; 1 low finding, fixed (the overwrite claim for `inspect score` now says "without `--scorer`"); 1 question about access to run logs and review transcripts (kept in the author's working notes; the commands above reproduce the runs).
- Round 7, fresh-context review of `9d0aa448c`: 1 medium, 3 low, 1 question; no finding in the persisted-log contract, the round trips or the existing tests. Fixed (medium, `9f1187438`, failing test first, mutation check): when appending, a dict key equal to a header scorer that never produced a score (a `--no-score` eval, or one that errored before scoring) was rejected as "already in the log" while the list form produced that name on the same log; only recorded header names are reserved now, and header names resolve around the recorded ones, so every header accepted before resolves to the same names. Fixed (low, text): the Compatibility sentence on older versions now says what they compute. Dismissed: no docs paragraph for the dict form (low: not required by AGENTS.md; offered if wanted); `NamedScorers` can't be imported at runtime (low: the pre-existing types-only pattern of `Scorers`); the issue's note on keying `metrics=` by alias (question: `metrics=` isn't keyed by scorer name, so there is nothing to re-key). The fix commit has not had a review pass of its own.

### Design questions

Two decisions I'd like a maintainer to confirm:

1. **Where the alias is stored.** It's a reserved key in `EvalScorer.metadata`, so the log schema and the generated TypeScript types don't change. A dedicated `EvalScorer` field would be more explicit but needs a coordinated `ts-mono` update. I'm happy to switch; the storage is isolated in three helpers.
2. **What `EvalScore.scorer` holds.** It holds the alias, as it holds generated names like `match1` today, and `HeadlineMetric.scorer` matches on it. The review on #4234 suggested the registered name there instead; that would change existing logs with repeated scorers, and headline selection.

title: fix(sci-workflow): install torch-geometric before running recipe
body:
## What

One-line fix to the SCI workflow's install step. Adds `pip install torch-geometric`, which the recipe needs at import time.

## Why

The first dispatch of the SCI pipeline failed at `graf reproduce`:

```
File ".../src/graf/cli.py", line 10, in <module>
    from graf.training.conflict_pairs import run_cross_validation
File ".../src/graf/data/graph_dataset.py", line 9, in <module>
    from torch_geometric.data import Data
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'torch_geometric'
```

`graf.cli` imports `graf.training.conflict_pairs` at module scope, which imports `graf.data.graph_dataset`, which imports `torch_geometric` at module scope. Without that package, the CLI cannot even print `--help`, so the workflow fails before it reaches the recipe.

## Evidence from the run

The download step worked: 1.41 GB (`sci.mp4`) fetched from the `sci-v1` release in ~35 s via `gh release download`. The failure was purely a missing Python dependency in the workflow's own install step.

## What changes

One line added to `.github/workflows/sci-pipeline.yml`. `torch-geometric` is already a documented dependency in `pyproject.toml` (`[project.optional-dependencies].gpu`) and is already installed in every CI job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. This brings the SCI workflow in line.

title: Fix deploy: install requirements.txt so PyJWT reaches production (PODSKRIFT-N)
body: ## Summary Production is failing ChatGPT OAuth token exchange with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'jwt'` ([PODSKRIFT-N](https://nettsmed.sentry.io/issues/PODSKRIFT-N)) on release `4ec0cd0b` (PR #93, which added `PyJWT[crypto]` to `requirements.txt`). The Actions deploy pulled and restarted but never ran `pip install` into the app `.venv`, so the new dependency never reached the server. **Merging this PR will install PyJWT on the server (via the deploy job’s new `pip install`) and resolve PODSKRIFT-N.** Fixes PODSKRIFT-N ## Changes - After `git pull --ff-only` and **before** `systemctl restart podskrift`, the deploy SSH script now runs: - `.venv/bin/pip install -q -r requirements.txt` - `.venv/bin/python -c "import jwt, flask, openai, stripe"` (smoke check) - Failed install or import fails the job under existing `set -euo pipefail` — no restart onto a broken venv. - Drain-before-pull ordering unchanged. - `ops/README.md` updated to match the real order (drain → pull → pip → smoke → restart) and the manual deploy recipe. No application or OAuth logic changes (see open PR #96 for that). ## Test plan - [x] Confirm Sentry PODSKRIFT-N is `import jwt` in `verify_private_key_jwt` on production release with PyJWT in git but missing from venv - [x] Confirm prior deploy.yml had no `pip install` - [x] `python -m pytest test_app.py -q` — 710 passed - [ ] CI test job on this PR - [ ] After merge: deploy job installs deps; `/oauth/token` no longer 500s with `No module named 'jwt'`; PODSKRIFT-N resolves

title: C1-NF paper shadow: tools/c1nf_shadow.py (draft)
body:
## What this is

`tools/c1nf_shadow.py`: the C1-NF (EXP-025) paper shadow. Keyless, no RPC, no transaction. It tails the fast-0 getBlock tip tape, runs the whole-minute decision loop, and writes picks and paper outcomes. Draft: not for merge until the missing items below are closed and `quant-proof` / `reviewer` have looked.

Files:
- `tools/c1nf_shadow.py`, `tools/test_c1nf_shadow.py` (195 tests), `tools/c1nf_vmode_parity.py` + `tools/test_c1nf_vmode_parity.py` (10 tests; quant-proof item 7 harness), `tools/fixtures/c1nf_shadow/pick_example.json`
- `scripts/research/c1nf-shadow.sh` (POSIX sh MiScusi wrapper; out dir `$HOME/data/c1nf-shadow`; `--max-seconds` for smoke runs)

## Behaviour

- **Tailer.** `trades-/creates-/migrations-<hour>.jsonl` in the tip dir. Per-(kind, hour) offsets, a half-written line waits, a shrunk or replaced file (inode) restarts at 0, offsets of hours older than previous/current/next are dropped. A 26 h bootstrap (plain or `.zst`) rebuilds engine state with decisions off, then resumes at the next whole minute. Rows are held 600 ms by `t_recv_ms` so the three kinds of one block arrive together.
- **Universe.** WSOL quote, canonical pool (migration-row pool, or the PDA when `solders` is importable), V band 17.5e9..17.7e9 on the first print. Live (event mode) the band reads that print's own event V `virtual_quote_reserves` and never the tip follower's cached `virtual_quote_reserve`; replay (const mode) reads the `virtual_quote_reserve` that `run_replay` stamps from the tape's V0. Event mode also rejects a pool as `v0_gap` when a follower gap record reaches its opening before its first print seen here. The engine applies its own universe rule as well.
- **Decision.** At the first row whose block_time reaches a new whole minute T: SD = that row's slot. For each alive pool: `features_at(pool, T, SD)`, stage 1, one batched model call (float32), `pred > 0.02` (strict), cap `h_top1 <= 0.5` (NaN dropped) before the book, one position per mint (re-entry 60 s after the estimated exit).
- **Records** (hourly JSONL, strict JSON, `schema` and `t_ms` on each):
  - `c1nf_pick`: `PICK_FIELDS` = type, mint, pool, decision_T_ms, SD_slot, pred, h_top1, stage1, feature_hash (sha256 of the float32 vector), model_sha, **q_lamports, base_reserve, v_lamports, state_slot** (DEC-026 section 6; see below). `validate_pick` and the fixture define the contract.
  - `c1nf_outcome`: entries at 1.3 / 1.9 / 3.0 / 4.0 s (landing = SD + round(lat / s-per-slot)), END and WORST bounds, exit = clock time of the landing + 300 s, then SD(deadline) + ceil(0.55 / s). PumpSwap rows are PRE-trade; price = (vault + V) / base with the print's own V: live, its event V `virtual_quote_reserves` (no fallback to the tip key; a print without it makes the leg incomplete); replay, the stamped V0 `virtual_quote_reserve`. The pick's `v_lamports` / `q_lamports` use the same V. Own trade applied, tier fee on (Q, B), 1.15 x decision-spot guard. P&L variants: no fee, 55k, 505k, 505k + rent. Fail legs are a book statistic and are not applied here. **New:** each END and WORST bound also carries `canary`: the same fill priced at the canary's **0.05 SOL** stake (`CANARY_STAKE_LAMPORTS`; guarded flag, proceeds, gross_ret, and the same four P&L variants at that stake), so the paper twin of DEC-026 section 6 is priced at 0.05 SOL and the 505k fee. The top-level `stake_lamports` stays 250,000,000 (the deciding cell).
  - `c1nf_gap` (clock jump, skipped minutes, silence, follower `gaps.jsonl`), `c1nf_heartbeat` (every 60 s, also `status.json`), `c1nf_start`, `c1nf_stop`.
- **Model pin.** Refuses to start (exit 3) on a sha256 mismatch, a missing file, or a pin that is not 64 hex chars. `--model` + `--model-sha256`, or `--model-manifest` (`{"models":[{"from_day","file","sha256"}]}`, for the daily retrain; every file is hashed at start). No pinned model for a decision day means no pick.
- **EXP-022 section 9 seal (from 2026-10-16T01Z).** A pool whose first print is at or after the window start is followed only if `oracle(mint)` returns exactly `False`. No oracle, an exception, a non-bool, or `staleness_s()` over 60 s (or unknown): withheld. A withheld pool gets **no per-pool record of any kind** (no pick, no outcome, no label) and never enters the book; the only trace is the unlabelled `withheld` count inside the heartbeat/stop counters. If the oracle goes stale after a pick, the outcome is dropped the same way. The oracle is asked again at every decision and again when the outcome resolves. An answer is never frozen: a None at pool open withholds that minute only (tools/cap_pick_oracle.py TIMING). Exception: a False can later become True (a replay source or a second live source picks the mint). If that happens before the outcome resolves, the pick line stays in c1nf-picks-* with no outcome, and only `withheld` counts it. If it happens after the outcome resolves, it is not caught and the outcome stays written. This follows the newest H5 rule as the coordinator described it; H5 branch head `fe7eb43` still emits a labelled suppressed record, so I did not copy that part.
- **EXP-025 5.1 declared observation:** outcomes are logged; the shadow is not the read.

### Added in this push (DEC-026 items 8 and 4; branch merged with origin/main at 12689e6)

- **Decision-time state on the pick (DEC-026 section 6, buy guard).** `q_lamports` (vault quote + that print's V) and `base_reserve` (raw) are the state after the last canonical-pool print with slot < `SD_slot`; `state_slot` is that print's slot. It is `Print.post()` of that print (PumpSwap rows are PRE-trade, so the post-state is the shadow's estimate: constant product with the LP share kept, `LP_FRAC`). A print at or after SD is never used (`before_slot` keeps the previous slot's print for the case where an SD-slot print was read first). Both are positive ints and `validate_pick` rejects a pick without them. **A pool with no such state (no V on the last print before SD) gets no pick at all** and no book entry (counter `no_decision_state`): the executor would refuse it, so the shadow does not log a trade the canary cannot make.
- **Binding outcome guard from 2026-10-10T00:00Z (DEC-026 section 8 and section 11 item 8).** `OUTCOME_START_MS` is a module constant. `outcome_allowed(T_ms)` is True only for T >= 2026-10-10T00:00Z or T inside an exploration range (August/September replay; replay already refuses every other hour). A decision before that instant **still writes its pick** (the executor's input; a pick is not an outcome) and enters the book, but gets **no `Pending`, no price, no label and no outcome record** in any mode (counter `outcome_guard_pre_window`). There is no argument, flag or config that moves it (a test checks the `Shadow` signature and the CLI options).
- **Synthetic class: a separate counts-only stream (EXP-025 Amendment 2 item 5, DEC-026 section 9.3).** The shadow is no-RPC and computes no class itself. With `--synthetic-classifier module:callable` (`classifier(mint, pool) -> synthetic | non_synthetic | unclassified`; an exception or any other value is `unclassified`, never a refusal), each pool is classified once at its first print and the class stays in memory. The only output is `c1nf_synclass_counts` in its own file `c1nf-synclass-<hour>.jsonl`: one record per closed UTC day (written when the stream enters the next day) and one `partial` record at stop, with `universe_<class>` counts only. No mint, pool, price or outcome field. Not in the heartbeat, `status.json`, counters or stop record. **Deliberately no pick count by class:** per-day pick counts by class next to real-time daily outcomes would let an observer split outcomes by class (a day whose picks are all one class). `emit()` drops any pick or outcome record carrying a class-like key at any depth (`class`, `synthetic`, `synthetic_class`, `is_synthetic`, `post_complete_buy_seen`, ...) and counts `class_leak_blocked`; `validate_pick` rejects one. Pools first seen during the restart bootstrap are classified but not counted.
- **Replay.** `--replay-from YYYY-MM-DDTHH --replay-hours N [--decide-from H --decide-to H]` reads `/data/mal/audit-1008/tape` read-only. It refuses forbidden path tokens (fresh-0802/0808/0828, forward-*, walk-2, `/var/lib/mal`, `.env`, helius, keypair) and any hour outside the exploration ranges (08-14T12..08-28T12, 09-03T12..09-15T12, 09-18T23..09-25T07). The tape has no per-print V, so V per pool is `v0_lamports` from `/data/mal/hunt-shared/tokens.parquet`; seconds per slot are measured over the whole UTC hour as the batch does. Needs pandas + pyarrow (audit venv) and lightgbm (wrapper adds the other venv's site-packages).
- **Disk.** Closed hours of outcomes and events are zstd-compressed; picks stay plain (the executor tails them). No tape copies.

### Review fixes (heads 23294fe, 8f12a9a, 0b679c4; reviewer pass on 17a6b81)

- **MEDIUM, decision state fail-closed.** `Print` no longer takes raw amounts with `or 0` as real values: a missing, non-numeric, bool, non-finite or non-positive `quote_reserve`, `base_reserve`, `token_raw` or `sol_lamports` becomes 0 and the print refuses. `pre()` raises unless raw vault quote > 0 and base > 0; `post()` raises unless the side is `buy`/`sell`, `token_raw` > 0, `sol_lamports` > 0 on a buy, and post-trade base > 0. **There is no pre-state fallback in `post()` any more.** `_decision_state` returns no state (counter `no_decision_state`, so no pick, no book entry, no outcome) on any of those, when V is not > 0, or when the rounded post-trade `q_lamports` is not above `v_lamports`. A bad last print before SD is not replaced by an older one. **The pick now carries `v_lamports`** (that print's V), so the executor can repeat H5's `q_lamports >= v_lamports` check (`tools/h5_executor.py:373`); `validate_pick` requires it positive and rejects `q_lamports <= v_lamports`. Tests: missing `quote_reserve`, `base_reserve` and `token_raw` (and null, 0, string, bool, NaN values) on a buy and on a sell, each giving no pick; a buy without `sol_lamports`; a missing or unknown side; V of 0 or negative; `post()` with base going to 0. The same check now also covers paper pricing: a malformed print at or after SD makes the outcome incomplete (`no_spot`, or the leg's `ValueError`) instead of a price (test with no `base_reserve` on the SD print).
- **LOW, twin guard reference.** `Pending` carries the pick's `(q_lamports, base_reserve)`. Each bound's `canary` twin (0.05 SOL) now guards on the pick's state (`guard_ref: "pick_state"`), as the executor will, and records `guarded_at_batch_spot` (the same twin guarded on the batch's spot). The outcome carries `pick_spot` next to `spot`. The 0.25 SOL cell stays on the batch spot. Test: the SD print's quote is halved, so the batch spot is about half the pick's; the 0.25 SOL cell is guarded, the twin is not, and `guarded_at_batch_spot` is True.
- **LOW, classifier off the hot path.** The classifier runs on one worker thread (`ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1)`); results are collected on the row thread once per new block time without blocking. An answer later than `CLASSIFY_TIMEOUT_S` = 10 s (monotonic) is `unclassified` (cancelled if it never started). Stop waits at most that timeout. **No call is made while `decide_enabled` is False** (the 26 h bootstrap); a pool first seen there is never classified or counted. A day's record waits while one of its classifications is pending. Test: a classifier that sleeps 1 s per call, timeout 0.2 s, two pools: the stream to the pick is fed in under 0.8 s, stop takes under 0.8 s, both pools are unclassified. Test: no call during the bootstrap.
- **LOW, outcome guard tied to replay.** `outcome_allowed(T_ms, *, replay)`: the exploration exemption applies only with `replay=True`; the mode has no default. The call site passes `self.replay`. Tests: the boundary table in both modes; a live-mode shadow whose clock is in an exploration hour writes the pick and prices nothing.
- **LOW, pre-window picks.** New `executor_refusal(rec)`: `invalid_pick` (`validate_pick` fails) or `pre_window` (`decision_T_ms` < 2026-10-10T00:00Z), else None. **Executor contract: the executor applies it to every pick line** (imports it or repeats it). `PICK_EXAMPLE` and the fixture moved to `decision_T_ms` 2026-10-10T00:10Z so the example is executable. Test: the midnight stream's 23:50Z pick is `pre_window`, the 00:00Z pick is accepted.
- **LOW, daily class counts.** A UTC day whose synthetic or non-synthetic count is 0 or the whole universe is not written alone; it is merged into the next day(s), and a record covers `day_first`..`day_last`. A span still degenerate at stop is written with `held_back: true`, `counts: null` and only `universe_total`. The record keys are now `day_first`, `day_last`, `partial`, `held_back`, `universe_total`, `counts` (was `day`). This is a code-side answer to the near-join; **quant-proof should still confirm that day granularity for non-degenerate days is acceptable before the final look.**

### Round 2 review fixes (heads 1e07c58, 61094da; reviewer pass on 0b679c4; branch merged with origin/main at c21ba83)

- **MEDIUM, classifier thread could hold the process (1e07c58).** The classifier now runs on `ClassWorker`: one **daemon** thread fed by a queue (no `ThreadPoolExecutor`, whose workers Python joins at interpreter exit). A queued job past `CLASSIFY_TIMEOUT_S` is cancelled before it starts; a running one is abandoned. `finish()` closes the worker; a call that never returns no longer keeps the process alive after `c1nf_stop`. `run_live` passes `CLASSIFY_TIMEOUT_S` at call time. Test: `main()` in a subprocess with `--max-seconds 1.5` and a classifier that never returns exits with rc 0 (1.72 s for the whole test) and writes `c1nf_stop`; the same test on 0b679c4 hits its 60 s subprocess timeout (checked). Still true: one worker, so a hung call leaves later pools unclassified for the rest of the run (calls never overlap).
- **LOW, pre-window picks in the executor's input (61094da), option (b).** `JsonlSink` writes a pick whose `decision_T_ms` is before 2026-10-10T00Z (or not an int) to **`c1nf-prewindow-picks-<hour>.jsonl`**, never to `c1nf-picks-*`. Every line of `c1nf-picks-*` passes `executor_refusal()`, which stays as the second layer. **Replay picks (August/September exploration hours) are in `c1nf-prewindow-picks-*` too**; replay outcomes are unchanged. The executor v2 glob `c1nf-picks-????-??-??T??.jsonl` (#530) does not match the new name. Also new: `_decide` validates the pick before the book entry; a pick that fails `validate_pick` (a code fault, e.g. a non-finite pred) gets no record, no book entry, no outcome (counter `invalid_pick`). Pre-window picks still enter the book on purpose (the rule's book), which can only affect re-entry in the first minutes after 2026-10-10T00Z, and replay.
- **LOW, class counts after a restart (1e07c58).** The `c1nf_synclass_counts` record whose span holds a (re)start's resume day carries `restart_in_span: true` and `bootstrap_unclassified` (that day's pools first seen during the bootstrap). Bootstrap pools are never classified later. Bootstrap pools of earlier days are not reported by the new run. Every record now has both keys. `run_live` resumes through `Shadow.resume_after_bootstrap()`.
- **LOW, modelled vs measured reserves, and LOW, `no_decision_state` vs the read:** measured on exploration tape with a stub engine (below). No code change; the parity miss class and the `sol_lamports` check are listed for quant-proof under "Not measured / missing".

### Round 3 (head b48b5ba; reviewer re-review of 9a80398, quant-proof ruling item 7; origin/main b17dc0b merged in)

- **MEDIUM 1-4, event V everywhere in live.** `Shadow(..., v_source)` takes the mode from the engine (`FeatureEngine.v_source`; a stub without one is "const") and refuses to build when the engine, the argument or the `Universe` disagree. In event mode `print_v(row, True)` = `event_v_of(row)` (no fallback to the tip key) feeds `Universe.accept` (band), `Print.v`, hence the pick's `v_lamports` / `q_lamports` and every outcome price. `set_pool_v` is not called in event mode. Const mode reads only `virtual_quote_reserve` (`v_of` no longer falls back to the plural key). `run_live` builds `Universe(pda, event_v=True)` and passes `v_source="event"`; `run_replay` passes `"const"`. Docstrings fixed (module Pricing, `event_v_of`, `v_of`, `Universe`).
- **Test (item 4).** Real `FeatureEngine` in event mode, rows with `virtual_quote_reserve` = X = 10e9 (out of band) and `virtual_quote_reserves` = Y = 17.58e9 (+1e9 after a later slot): the pool is accepted (band on Y), the engine's V0 is Y, `set_pool_v_ignored_event_mode` stays 0, the pick's `v_lamports` = Y and `q_lamports` = `post()` on Y, the 1.3 s END entry and exit are priced on that print's Y. Also: X in band with Y out of band is rejected `v_out_of_band`; event V lost after SD with X present gives incomplete legs. The engine's own decision is replaced by a fixed vector at one minute (admission, V0 and the event mapping are the engine's).
- **v0_gap (quant-proof, recommended).** Event mode only: a pool whose first print seen here comes after a follower gap record [lo, hi] with lo below that slot and hi at or after the pool's opening (its migration row, else its mint's `complete` row; opening unknown: any gap noted within 25 h) is rejected `v0_gap` (universe count). A gap read after the pool's first print (the two files are tailed apart) stops further decisions on it (counter `v0_gap_late`). A gap without a slot is counted `follower_gap_unplaced`. The hook, the worker thread, the timeout and the stream are tested with stubs only. title: fix(agents,api): bound the manual investigation path and stop the LLM panel claiming Live while every call fails
body:
Fixes #1242.
Fixes #1241.

Two defects in the same subsystem with the same root cause family: **a surface reporting a healthy state it never checked.** A manual investigation had no deadline anywhere on the LLM path, and the LLM panel decided its badge from configuration rather than from whether the provider answers.

---

## Defect 1 (#1242) — a manual AI investigation could stay `running` forever

The 120-second budget at `services/agents/app/graph/runner.py` is reached by exactly two callers, and **neither is the console's path**. `POST /api/v1/cases/{id}/investigate` lands in `app/api/investigate.py`, which writes `status: "running"` and hands `_run_and_store` to `BackgroundTasks`. That function sets a terminal status only on a `done` event, an `error` event, or a raised exception. `ChatOpenAI` is built with no timeout, so a merely-slow model raises nothing and **no terminal status is ever written** — in the process dict *or* in the `investigation_runs` row the Investigation Ledger renders.

### What changed

**One budget, not two.** `_run_and_store` now runs under `asyncio.timeout(default_budget().max_seconds)` — the same `AISOC_INVESTIGATION_MAX_SECONDS` the auto-triage path reads, resolved at call time. Two constants describing one deadline is a shape this repo has been bitten by before, so the number is not restated.

**The terminal status reaches both places.** A new `_fail_run` writes `failed` + the reason to the `_runs` entry **and** closes the `investigation_runs` row via `ledger.complete_run`. This is load-bearing: `asyncio.timeout` cancels the orchestrator's generator with `CancelledError`, which is a `BaseException`, so the orchestrator's own `except Exception` arm never runs and nothing else would close that row. `_fail_run` never downgrades a run that already finished.

**`failed`, not a new word.** `CaseWorkspace.tsx` branches on `idle`/`starting`/`running`/`failed`/`completed`, and the WebSocket tail breaks on `completed`/`failed`. A `timed_out` status would be a run that no surface can finish rendering, so the reason travels in `error` instead.

**A stale-run reaper, because the deadline cannot cover a dead process.** The run store is a module dict: a restart, an OOM kill or a rollout drops every in-flight run while its row stays `running` with nothing left to finish it. `app/investigator/run_reaper.py` sweeps on the `app.playbook.sweeper` pattern (opt-out, capped backoff, `_log_exit` callback), wired into the agents lifespan. Its margin is **derived from the same budget** (`3 ×`, floor 300s) — and that margin is only safe *because* the deadline exists: a run can no longer legitimately outlast its budget. The staleness predicate lives inside the `UPDATE`, so two replicas racing one row close it once.

---

## Defect 2 (#1241) — green "Live" badge while every LLM call times out

Three separate things, honesty first. **I did not reproduce the reporter's 171 s / 682-token measurement** and make no claim about it; what is verified below is that the configuration makes that outcome reachable and that the badge stayed green through it.

### 1. `request_timeout` is now an operator knob

`infra/litellm/config.yaml` had `request_timeout: 60` as the **one bare literal** in a file where every other value resolves `os.environ/...`, so raising it meant editing a mounted file and restarting. It now reads `os.environ/AISOC_LITELLM_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`, with the 60s default supplied by `docker-compose.yml` (all three compose overlays inherit it). Documented in `.env.example` and the env-vars page.

**Two plausible-looking alternatives were tried against a real `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:main-stable` and rejected — evidence below.** LiteLLM's own native `REQUEST_TIMEOUT` is float-coerced but never reaches the proxy's router path; and an *unset* `os.environ/` variable resolves to `None`, producing a gateway that serves `/health/liveliness` 200 while failing every completion. The compose default is therefore load-bearing and a contract test fails if it is removed.

### 2. `num_retries` deliberately stays a literal

The issue asked for this "ideally". It would be a landmine. LiteLLM assigns `router_settings` to `Router.__init__` with **no type coercion** (`router_params[k] = v`), and the retry path evaluates `num_retries > 0` — which raises `TypeError` against the string an `os.environ/...` reference resolves to, at precisely the moment a retry is needed. A test pins it as an `int` so a later "make everything configurable" pass cannot quietly break failover. The knob that matters for slow hardware is the timeout, and that one is now adjustable.

### 3. The status surface reports whether the provider answers

`GET /api/v1/llm/status` places no call; `effective_path` is decided by `key_set` and the air-gap policy alone. New `app/services/llm_health.py` records the outcome of each call made through `safe_chat_completions_request` — the single chokepoint all eight of this service's LLM call sites already use. `/llm/status` gains `recent_health` / `recent_calls` / `recent_failures` / `recent_note`, and the Settings pill reads **Degraded** instead of **Live** when recent calls are failing.

Four deliberate constraints:

- **Not a probe.** Nothing places a synthetic completion. The traffic the product already generates is the signal.
- **No latency number.** `aisoc_run_costs` carries a latency sum, but it is written by `services/agents` for *completed* runs and records nothing about a call that timed out. No measured figure exists for this path, so none is published — and a test fails if a latency-shaped field ever appears.
- **`unknown` is a real answer.** A pod that has observed no call is not rendered as healthy. Rendering an absence of evidence as green is the same defect in a different costume.
- **A contract violation is not a provider failure.** `LLMInputContract` aborts before the network call; counting that would blame the model for a prompt AiSOC deliberately refused to send.

Scope stated rather than implied: the window is **per-process**, so behind several replicas the panel reports what that pod has seen. `Fallback path` still wins over `Degraded` — on the deterministic path no call is attempted, so there is no provider outcome to report.

---

## Evidence

### Defect 1 — test fails on the current tree

```
$ cd services/agents && /tmp/agents-venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_investigation_run_deadline.py -q
E  Failed: _run_and_store did not return within 15.0s against a stream that never completes,
   with AISOC_INVESTIGATION_MAX_SECONDS=0.25. The manual investigation path has no wall-clock
   deadline, so the run stays 'running' forever and the console shows a spinner that never
   resolves (issue #1242).
E  AttributeError: module 'app.api.investigate' has no attribute 'ledger'

FAILED tests/test_investigation_run_deadline.py::test_hung_stream_still_reaches_a_terminal_status
FAILED tests/test_investigation_run_deadline.py::test_deadline_is_the_shared_budget_not_a_second_constant
FAILED tests/test_investigation_run_deadline.py::test_timeout_writes_the_terminal_status_to_the_ledger_row
3 failed in 30.68s
```

Thirty seconds of that is the test's own patience timer expiring twice, which is the defect.

### Defect 1 — after the fix

```
$ /tmp/agents-venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_investigation_run_deadline.py -q
...                                                                      [100%]
3 passed in 1.33s
```

### Defect 1 — negative control

```
$ git checkout HEAD -- services/agents/app/api/investigate.py   # revert, test stays
$ /tmp/agents-venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_investigation_run_deadline.py -q
FAILED tests/test_investigation_run_deadline.py::test_hung_stream_still_reaches_a_terminal_status
FAILED tests/test_investigation_run_deadline.py::test_deadline_is_the_shared_budget_not_a_second_constant
FAILED tests/test_investigation_run_deadline.py::test_timeout_writes_the_terminal_status_to_the_ledger_row
3 failed in 30.54s

$ cp /tmp/nc1-keep.py services/agents/app/api/investigate.py    # restore
$ /tmp/agents-venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_investigation_run_deadline.py -q
3 passed in 1.32s
```

### The reaper — exercised against a real Postgres, not a fake pool

A fake connection answers whatever query it is handed, which cannot tell you that `make_interval` binds, that the conditional `UPDATE` is race-safe, or that the RLS policy lets a cross-tenant sweep see anything. The production schema was `pg_dump --schema-only`'d out of a running AiSOC stack and loaded into a throwaway Postgres (0 errors, `inv_runs_tenant` policy present), and the real `fail_stale_runs` was run against it:

```
$ /tmp/agents-venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_investigation_run_reaper.py -q
7 passed, 3 skipped in 0.78s          # unit half, DB tests skipped with no DSN

$ AISOC_TEST_LEDGER_DSN=postgresql://...:15999/aisoc \
  /tmp/agents-venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_investigation_run_reaper.py -q -m integration
3 passed, 7 deselected in 1.20s
```

Those three assert that an abandoned row is closed with `completed_at` set, a run still inside its budget is **not** touched, a finished run is not reopened, a second pass is a no-op rather than overwriting the first reason, and the sweep sees **both** tenants.

### Defect 2 — the timeout knob, measured against a real gateway

Throwaway `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:main-stable` with this PR's config, pointed at an unroutable provider so the timeout is the only thing that can end the request:

```
AISOC_LITELLM_REQUEST_TIMEOUT=4   → liveliness HTTP 200, completion HTTP 408 after 17s
AISOC_LITELLM_REQUEST_TIMEOUT=20  → liveliness HTTP 200, completion HTTP 408 after 66s
                                     "timeout value=20.0, time taken=20.17 seconds"
```

The knob scales the timeout exactly; the totals are three attempts plus retry backoff, i.e. `num_retries: 2` still working.

**Why not LiteLLM's native `REQUEST_TIMEOUT`** — verified it is read and float-coerced in the image but does not reach the router path:

```
$ docker run --rm -e REQUEST_TIMEOUT=5 --entrypoint python ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:main-stable \
    -c "import litellm; print(litellm.request_timeout)"
5.0
# ...yet a gateway started that way, with no key in litellm_settings,
# was still waiting on the blackholed provider after 200s.
```

**Why the compose default is load-bearing** — with the variable unset, `get_secret` returns `None` and the gateway is healthy-looking and completely broken:

```
AISOC_LITELLM_REQUEST_TIMEOUT unset → liveliness HTTP 200
                                      completion HTTP 500 after 6s
  "litellm.APIConnectionError: float() argument must be a string or a real number, not 'NoneType'"
  startup log: setting litellm.request_timeout=None
```

That is the defect this change exists to fix, so a contract test now fails if the compose default is removed. For context, the config is **already** hard-dependent on its environment — `origin/main`'s version with `AISOC_LLM_MODEL_*` unset does not start at all (`TypeError: argument of type 'NoneType' is not iterable`, `Application startup failed. Exiting.`).

### Defect 2 — status surface, failing then passing

```
$ cd services/api && /tmp/api-venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_llm_status_degraded.py -q
E  ImportError: cannot import name 'llm_health' from 'app.services'
1 error in 0.47s
```

After the fix: `7 passed in 0.32s`.

**Negative control — the strong one.** An `ImportError` only proves a file is absent. Reverting *only* the recording call at the chokepoint, leaving `llm_health.py` and the endpoint change in place, shows the tests detect the missing behaviour:

```
$ git checkout HEAD -- services/api/app/services/llm_safety.py
E  AssertionError: every recent call timed out and the panel would still render the emerald Live pill
E  assert 'unknown' == 'degraded'
E  AssertionError: assert 'unknown' == 'healthy'

$ cp /tmp/nc2-keep.py services/api/app/services/llm_safety.py   # restore
7 passed in 0.37s
```

### Defect 2 — the badge

On the current tree, 3 of 5 fail and the 2 regression controls pass (so the test is not simply broken):

```
× reads Degraded, not Live, when recent calls are failing
× tells the operator why, rather than only that something is wrong
× says calls are unobserved rather than claiming health it has not seen
✓ still reads Live when the provider is answering
✓ keeps the fallback badge winning over the health signal
Tests  3 failed | 2 passed (5)
```

After the fix, and reverting `SettingsView.tsx` as a negative control:

```
after fix:        Tests  5 passed (5)
reverted:         Tests  3 failed | 2 passed (5)
restored:         Tests  5 passed (5)
```

### Config contract — negative controls

```
$ git checkout HEAD -- infra/litellm/config.yaml
E  AssertionError: request_timeout is 60; an operator cannot change that without editing this file
   assert '60' == 'os.environ/AISOC_LITELLM_REQUEST_TIMEOUT'
1 failed, 8 passed            → restored: 9 passed

$ git checkout HEAD -- docker-compose.yml
E  AssertionError: docker-compose.yml must pass AISOC_LITELLM_REQUEST_TIMEOUT to the litellm
   service with a `:-` default; without one an unset variable silently breaks every completion
1 failed, 8 passed            → restored: 9 passed
```

---

## Gates

| Gate | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Ruff lint | `ruff check services/ scripts/ tests/ tools/` | **All checks passed** |
| Ruff format | `ruff format --check .` | **2415 files already formatted** |
| mypy baseline | `scripts/check_mypy_baseline.py` | **OK — no tree got worse** (952 findings, 20 trees) |
| Module reachability | `scripts/check_module_reachability.py` | **OK** — 970/998 reachable (both new modules wired) |
| Comment paths | `scripts/check_comment_paths.py` | **OK** — 2077 checked |
| Attribution | `scripts/check_attribution.py --commits origin/main..HEAD` | **OK — no tool attribution found** |
| Competitor names | `scripts/check_competitor_names.py` | **OK** |
| agents suite | `pytest -m "not integration"` | **1962 passed**, 5 deselected, 219 subtests |
| api suite | `pytest` | **4596 passed**, 61 skipped |
| web suite | `pnpm vitest run` | **860 passed** (85 files) |
| web typecheck | `tsc --noEmit` | **exit 0** |

Gates were run with changes **staged**, since several use `git ls-files`. Ruff's two findings were import-ordering on my own new imports and were auto-fixed; `ruff format` reformatted only the three test files added here.

## Not verified

- **The reporter's 171 s / 682-token figure.** Not reproduced, not claimed, and no CPU-vs-GPU latency statement was added to the docs — no measured figure for that path exists.
- **The throwaway-gateway measurements are against an unroutable provider**, which exercises the timeout and connection path. They are not a measurement of real generation latency on any model.
- **The `llm_health` window is per-process.** Behind several replicas the panel reports what that pod has seen. Stated in the module docstring and the field comment rather than papered over.
- **No live end-to-end console walkthrough.** The badge change is covered by component tests against the real component, and the API change by tests through the real `safe_chat_completions_request`; neither was clicked through on a running deployment.
- **The reaper's Postgres evidence used a schema dumped from a running stack**, not a freshly migrated database. The dump loaded with 0 errors and carries the `inv_runs_tenant` RLS policy, but it inherits whatever state that stack's migrations left.

title: feat(OMN-20864): idle lab slots fall back to pr-land lanes on parked, escalated and unowned-red PRs
body:
## Summary
- Implements OMN-20864 by applying an operator ruling dated 2026-10-10T04:08:23Z that sets pr-land as the default work for idle lab slots on open PRs the landing controller parked, escalated, or left red with no owner.
- Updates node_lab_fill_selection_compute to plan pr-land lanes for slots left idle by ordinary candidates, allowing them to launch through the existing lab-fill effect with a pr-land brief.
- Modifies node_throughput_tick_decision_compute to execute the shared pure rule omnimarket.handlers.rules_lab_fill_pr_land, naming pr-land lanes in its free-slot FIX or writing a NOTE with the reason if none exist.
- Processes typed facts in the request, including pr-state-observed, ci-red-triage-decided, pr-landing-transitioned, controller park and escalation, and hold rows.
- Marks PRs under an in-force HOLD as SKIP_HELD naming the hold id, and treats an unreadable hold source as a typed failure (HOLD_SOURCE_UNREADABLE) that plans nothing.
- Marks PRs red on a base or shared cause, or whose last landing lane was blocked on required-approval, base-red, held, or external-owner at the same head, as SKIP_BLOCKED_UNFIXABLE until a new head or the cause is observed cleared.

## What it does not do
- Adds no topic, no script, and no new node; the dispatch happens through the existing lab-fill effect.
- Does not change the contract.yaml or handlers/__init__.py of node_lab_fill_plan_compute.

## Acceptance tests (OMN-20864)

- AC1: `tests/nodes/node_lab_fill_selection_compute/test_lab_fill_pr_land_fallback.py::test_ac1_zero_candidates_and_a_parked_pr_plan_a_pr_land_dispatch` (zero candidates, one parked PR, pr-land dispatch through the lab-fill dispatch plan), `test_ac1_escalated_and_unowned_red_prs_are_the_fallback_too`, `test_ac1_ledger_escalation_from_a_landing_lane_counts_as_escalated`; `tests/nodes/node_lab_fill_plan_compute/test_lab_fill_pr_land_dispatch.py` (pr-land ranks last, lane named for the PR, pr-land brief)
- AC2: `tests/nodes/node_throughput_tick_decision_compute/test_pr_land_fallback_throughput_tick_decision_compute.py::test_ac2_headroom_fix_with_idle_slots_and_a_parked_pr_plans_a_pr_land_dispatch`
- AC3: `test_ac3_idle_slots_and_no_fallback_pr_plan_nothing_and_record_why`, `test_ac3_no_open_pr_at_all_records_why` (selection); `test_ac3_headroom_with_idle_slots_and_no_fallback_pr_records_why` (tick)
- AC-M1: `test_acm1_a_pr_under_a_stay_out_hold_is_skip_held_naming_the_hold_id`, `test_acm1_the_hold_list_is_read_in_code_from_the_request_hold_source`, `test_acm1_an_unreadable_hold_source_is_a_typed_failure_that_dispatches_nothing`; tick: `test_an_unreadable_hold_source_is_unknown_and_dispatches_nothing`
- AC-M8: `test_acm8_a_pr_blocked_on_an_unfixable_cause_is_not_retried` (all four causes), `test_acm8_a_new_head_makes_a_blocked_pr_eligible_again`, `test_acm8_a_cleared_cause_makes_a_blocked_pr_eligible_again`, `test_acm8_base_red_with_no_triage_read_is_not_cleared`, `test_a_red_every_check_of_which_is_red_on_three_open_prs_is_a_shared_base_red`

RED at origin/dev 3fe55c842: the selection and tick test modules fail at import, the dispatch test fails 5 of 5. At head 699f97b2e: the three new files 40 passed; the four touched node test dirs (selection, plan, effect, tick) 821 passed, on h201 in the lane's worktree. `onex_lab_run.py --via bus` for those four dirs exited 75 (h200 and h201 over the load bar), so the dir run is the in-worktree one. ruff, mypy --strict on the 12 touched source files, and pre-commit on the 17 touched files (76 hooks passed) are clean.

Lab: host=h201, lane=.201 dev lane (broker omnibase-infra-redpanda), command=`rpk topic consume` of onex.evt.omnimarket.pr-state-observed.v1 (101802 records, offsets 48228-150029), onex.evt.omnimarket.ci-red-triage-decided.v1 (1344) and onex.evt.omnimarket.pr-landing-transitioned.v1 (9031) read to their heads at 2026-10-10T10:11:24Z, replayed with the ledger copy's 1014 HOLD/RELEASE rows and 61542 ledger rows through HandlerLabFillSelection at head 699f97b2e with zero ordinary candidates and a simulated idle slot. Observed over 114 open PRs: pr-land eligible 22 (17 escalated, 5 unowned-red), with 1 slot 1 pr-land dispatch (omnibase_infra#4629, escalated) and 21 dispatch-limit, with 4 slots 4 (omnibase_infra#4629, #4772, #4787, omnibase_spi#353); SKIP_HELD 19 (for example omnidash#350 under 2026-10-01T12:15:23Z-dash-stayout-controller, knowledge-base-internal#779 under 2026-09-27T16:26:13Z-repo-drains-83r); SKIP_BLOCKED_UNFIXABLE 13, all base-red, including the three PRs red on delegation-health-check (omnibase_infra#4783 and #4800 as shared across 3 open PRs, #4804 as triage shared_cause) and omni_home#787-791 (omni-home-tests); owned 36, handed-off 20, unchanged-input 4. No pr-land lane was dispatched; replay only.

## Dual owner

The fallback dispatches through the existing lab-fill effect only. The landing controller does not dispatch per-PR lanes for idle slots, so there is no dual owner for that class. Its cause workers own shared causes, which this rule skips as SKIP_BLOCKED_UNFIXABLE (base-red). Per-PR landing lanes dispatched by hand carry a `pr=` CLAIM, which the selection's ledger replay reads as OWNED.

## Overlap with open PRs

This diff does not touch `node_lab_fill_plan_compute/contract.yaml` or `handlers/__init__.py` (omnimarket#3687, #3678). It adds one `pr_land` line to the `inputs:` block of `node_throughput_tick_decision_compute/contract.yaml`. omnimarket#3678 also edits that file, in other hunks (`handler_routing`, `outputs`/`config`, `event_bus`).

## Notes

- `escalated` from the bus is `pr-landing-transitioned` to_state NEEDS_AGENT; on the dev lane the landing orchestrator runs in dry_run and most of those are `companion_declined`.
- The brief's 9 PRs red on delegation-health-check: the bus read at 10:11Z shows 3 open.
- Deploy evidence: `contracts/OMN-20864.yaml` `dod-omn20864-deploy` imports the shared rule inside the dev lane's runtime container. Before this merge it fails with ModuleNotFoundError, and `omnimarket.handlers.rules_merge_sweep` imports there as the positive control.

title: fix(knowledge): answer the /api/v1/index routes instead of 500 [Tier 3]
body:
## Summary

`KnowledgeHandler` lists `/api/v1/index`, `/api/v1/index/embed-batch` and `/api/v1/index/search` in `ROUTES`, so the route index sends them there, but `handle()` had no branch for them and ended in `return None`. The registry turned every such request that passed the permission check into `500 handler_no_result`. This PR answers the family instead:

| Route | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/v1/index/embed-batch` | 500 `handler_no_result` | 200 with `embeddings`, `dimension`, `count`, `batch_count`, `model` from the local embedding model `/api/v1/ml/embed` uses (the shared accessor `get_local_embedding_service()` over `aragora.ml.get_embedding_service()`), batched by `batch_size`; 400 on bad input (including empty strings, more than 100 texts, a lone surrogate, a text longer than 2,000 bytes of UTF-8, or a `model` other than the local one); 415 without a JSON `Content-Type`; 503 `{"error": "ML embeddings not available"}` when the local model cannot load, the same answer as `/api/v1/ml/embed`; 503 `{"error": {"message": "Embedding service unavailable", "code": "service_unavailable"}}` when encoding fails or returns fewer vectors than texts |
| `GET /api/v1/index` | 500 `handler_no_result` | 200 `{"indexes": [], "count": 0}` (no named-index registry exists) |
| `POST /api/v1/index` | 500 `handler_no_result` | 501 `{"error": {"message": "Named vector indexes are not implemented on this server", "code": "not_implemented"}}` |
| `POST /api/v1/index/search` | 500 `handler_no_result`, and it needed `knowledge.write` | 501 with the same body, and it needs `knowledge.read` like `POST /api/v1/knowledge/query` |
| any other method on the three paths | 500 `handler_no_result` | 405 with an `Allow` header |

Authority: operator ruling of 2026-09-28 12:20Z, option A ("small server-side dispatch fix as an operator packet"), and the user decision of 2026-09-30 for this continuation ("land the auth fix first, then one repair on #10212 (merge main, real permission tests, size caps) and one fresh collection"). The SDK, the stability manifest and the contract-drift inventory are untouched.

Path correction: the ruling and the feature text name `aragora/server/handlers/knowledge/handler.py`; the handler that owns these routes is `aragora/server/handlers/knowledge_base/handler.py` (the explorer's line numbers matched that file). This PR changes that file, one new test module, and, since the grant-3 repair, `aragora/server/handlers/knowledge/ml.py` (the shared embedding accessor).

### Repair after review collection 1 (commit `a22e914d`)

Claude's collection-1 review raised three in-scope [P3] findings. One batched commit fixes all three:

1. **Overall time budget for the embed loop.** One 30 s wall-clock budget (`_EMBED_BATCH_BUDGET_SECONDS`) now covers every backend call of a request. Each `run_async` call gets only the time that is left, and an exhausted budget answers 503. I chose a budget over a `batch_size` floor: a floor still allows 1000/floor sequential calls with 30 s each, while the budget bounds the request's wall time whatever the batch size or backend latency. `batch_size` keeps its 1–100 range.
2. **Short backend reply answers 503, not 500.** When a backend returns fewer vectors than texts, `UnifiedEmbeddingService.embed_batch` leaves `None` placeholders and `embed_batch_raw` raises `AttributeError`, which became `500 handler_error`. The except tuple now includes `AttributeError` and `TypeError`, and an explicit length check turns any count mismatch into a `ValueError` (also 503).
3. **Nested 501 envelope.** The 501 body now has the `error_response(..., code="not_implemented")` shape, `{"error": {"message", "code"}}`, with an explicit message. It is still built with `json_response`, because `error_response` replaces every 5xx message with `Internal server error` in production. A test checks that the body equals `error_response(message, 501, code="not_implemented")` outside production and keeps its message under `ARAGORA_ENV=production`.

Claude's collection-1 [P2] was the pre-existing JWT authorization defect. #10224 has since fixed it on main; see `## Authorization (fixed on main by #10224)`.

## Collection-2 repair

Commit `36d0a583` (user decision 2026-09-28 ~22:10Z: "Allow a 2nd repair: cache-free service + zero-vector→503 + 3 small P3s (~50 LOC), then collection 3, then Tier-3 packet"). It fixes Claude's two collection-2 [P2]s and the three remaining [P3]s. No authorization code changed.

1. **[P2] Outages answered 200 with zero vectors.** The base `EmbeddingBackend.embed_batch` (`aragora/core/embeddings/backends/__init__.py:94-123`) catches each failed text and substitutes `[0.0] * dimension`, so any backend that inherits it turned an outage into a 200 of all-zero embeddings. The handler now treats any all-zero vector as a backend failure and answers 503. Empty strings are now a 400, because the hash backend legitimately returns a zero vector for `""`; after this change an all-zero vector can only mean failure. Test: `test_embed_batch_answers_503_when_the_base_backend_swallows_failures` uses a backend that inherits the base `embed_batch` and fails on all texts or on one text, dispatches through the real registry, and expects 503 with nothing written to the shared cache.
2. **[P2] The endpoint shared the process-wide cache.** `get_embedding_service()` with no arguments returns the singleton, whose 1000-entry cache is shared with `ml/quality_scorer`, `agent_router`, `consensus_predictor` and `handlers/knowledge/ml.py`. Requests could read entries other subsystems wrote, fill the cache with request text, and store the zero vectors from item 1. The handler now builds its own service with `get_embedding_service(config=EmbeddingConfig(cache_enabled=False))`; the signature at this head creates a new `UnifiedEmbeddingService(config=config)` for any explicit config, and `cache_enabled=False` gives it no cache. The provider is still auto-detected as before. Test: `test_embed_batch_neither_reads_nor_writes_the_shared_embedding_cache` seeds a stale `[9.0, …]` vector for `"alpha"` in the shared cache, sends `["alpha", "beta"]`, and asserts that the response carries the backend's real vectors, that the shared cache's size, hits and misses are unchanged, and that the singleton is the same object afterwards.
3. **[P3] The 503 message was rewritten in production.** The 503 now uses the same nested envelope as the 501, through a small `_coded_error(message, code, status)` helper that both share: `{"error": {"message": "Embedding service unavailable", "code": "service_unavailable"}}`. The 503 test runs under `ARAGORA_ENV=production` and asserts that exact body.
4. **[P3] `asyncio.TimeoutError` was not caught on Python 3.10.** The except tuple now lists `TimeoutError`, `asyncio.TimeoutError` and `concurrent.futures.TimeoutError`. They are one class on 3.11+ and three on 3.10, where `run_async` raises the asyncio one from `wait_for` and the `concurrent.futures` one from `future.result(timeout=…)` when it hands the call to the pool loop. The 503 test is parametrized over both.
5. **[P3] `read_json_body` instead of `read_json_body_validated`.** The handler now uses `read_json_body_validated`, so a body sent with a non-JSON `Content-Type` answers 415 (`test_embed_batch_requires_a_json_content_type`), and malformed or non-object JSON still answers 400.

The collection-1 budget test's fake service used to return `[[0.0]]`; it now returns `[[1.0]]` so the test still reaches the budget check instead of stopping at the new zero-vector check.

## Collection-3 repair

Two commits on top of `36d0a583`, under the user decision of 2026-09-30 quoted above: the main merge `3c305707` and ONE repair commit `1031fd09`.

1. **Main merge, no rebase.** `3c30570784e085a203761d919f660f62587652ff` merges `origin/main` at `6548e1e59c7f554f18bd7e88422d664278668b69`, which contains #10224's merge `a4a475db`, with `git merge --no-ff`. Git merged it without conflicts. On the merged tree exactly 8 existing tests failed, all of them tests that pinned the old defect or used permission-list doubles the merged checker no longer reads: the 4 `test_real_jwt_callers_get_403_known_pre_existing_defect` cases (owner, admin and member `GET /api/v1/index` and owner embed-batch now answer 200), 2 `test_writes_still_need_write_permission` cases and 2 `test_reads_still_need_read_permission` cases.
2. **Claude collection-3 [P2]: no size bound on embed-batch texts.** Each text may have at most 8,192 characters (`_MAX_EMBED_TEXT_CHARS`), and one request at most 1,000,000 characters in total (`_MAX_EMBED_BATCH_TOTAL_CHARS`). Both answer 400 with a message that states the limit, before the embedding service is created, so no provider call is made. Why these values: 8,192 characters is about 2,048 tokens of English text, the input limit of the Gemini backend's `text-embedding-004` (OpenAI's `text-embedding-3-small` allows 8,191 tokens), so an over-long English text now gets a 400 here instead of a provider error that surfaced as 503. The total cap bounds the provider work one request can buy; before it, only the 10 MB body limit did. Tests at both boundaries: `test_embed_batch_caps_each_text_at_8192_characters` (8,192 → 200, 8,193 → 400) and `test_embed_batch_caps_the_request_at_one_million_characters` (125 × 8,000 = 1,000,000 → 200, 126 × 8,000 → 400). Each 400 case also asserts that `get_embedding_service` was never called.
3. **Real-JWT role matrix in place of the pinned 403.** `test_real_jwt_roles_follow_rbac_v2` replaces `test_real_jwt_callers_get_403_known_pre_existing_defect`. For each of owner, admin, member and viewer it mints a real access token with `create_access_token`, sends it as `Authorization: Bearer` through the real registry dispatch (the dispatcher's own `extract_user_from_request` builds the auth context; the test auth bypass is off via `no_auto_auth`; the RBAC v2 checker is not patched) and asserts the status and body. Only the embedding service (a hash backend) and the persistent token-revocation lookup are stubbed. The 16 cells:

| role | `GET /api/v1/index` | `POST /api/v1/index` | `POST /api/v1/index/search` | `POST /api/v1/index/embed-batch` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| owner | 200 `{"indexes": [], "count": 0}` | 501 `not_implemented` | 501 `not_implemented` | 200 (`count` 1, provider `hash`) |
| admin | 200 | 403 | 501 | 403 |
| member | 200 | 403 | 501 | 403 |
| viewer | 403 | 403 | 403 | 403 |

RBAC v2 grants `knowledge.read` to owner, admin and member and `knowledge.write` only to owner; viewer holds neither. List and search are reads; create and embed-batch are writes. Every 403 body is `{"error": "Permission denied"}`. The same commit removes the 5 tests that used the `_ReadOnlyUser` / `_NoPermissionUser` permission-list doubles (`test_search_needs_only_read_permission`, `test_writes_still_need_write_permission` ×2, `test_reads_still_need_read_permission` ×2); the matrix covers each of their cases with real tokens.

The repair commit changes nothing else: no other handler line, no authorization code, no SDK, OpenAPI or drift file. Claude's other collection-3 findings are not changed by it: the OpenAPI placeholder entries ([P3] C3) and per-request provider detection ([P3] C7) are under `## Risks`; PATCH answering 405 from the index ladder ([P3] C4), the breadth of the except tuple ([P3] C5) and the all-or-nothing zero-vector rule ([P3] C6) are unchanged design choices.

### Human grant 2026-10-09 repair

Authority: the human answers of 2026-10-09 to the Receipt-First mission (recorded 04:30Z): ONE bounded repair of #10212 (cap embed-batch at 100 texts, as `/api/v1/ml/embed` does), made of ONE main merge and ONE repair commit with ONE push, then ONE claude+openai review collection on the pushed head. It answers Claude's collection-4 review of `1031fd09` (two [P2], seven [P3]). Collection 4's openai PASS (#issuecomment-6070948842) belongs to `1031fd09` and is not counted on this head.

Two commits on top of `1031fd09`:

1. **Main merge `cd2641af7121787cd50700414dfb8ba29be585a6`**, no rebase. It merges the local `origin/main` at `accd70554d9eca14f9fedde5f18d496e7fadbd7f` with `git merge --no-ff`. Git merged it without conflicts. `tests/server/handlers/test_rbac_route_rules_dispatch.py` (added on main by #10468) pins no `/api/v1/index` route as unserved, so it needed no change. On the merge it passes together with this PR's module: `745 passed, 1 xfailed`.
2. **Repair `e4147ecc60fae74096e62b935ef7899c7d480447`.** `_MAX_EMBED_BATCH_TEXTS` goes from 1,000 to 100 (`aragora/server/handlers/knowledge_base/handler.py:147-149`). That is the limit `/api/v1/ml/embed` already enforces (`aragora/server/handlers/knowledge/ml.py:569-570`: `"Maximum 100 texts per batch"`, 400). The check stays where it was (`handler.py:400-401`), before the embedding service is created (`handler.py:426`), so 101 texts answer 400 `"At most 100 texts per request"` without any provider call. No other production line changed.

Tests: `test_embed_batch_caps_the_request_at_100_texts` (`tests/server/handlers/knowledge_base/test_index_dispatch.py:206-220`) sends 100 texts (200, `count` 100) and 101 texts (400 with that message, `get_embedding_service` never called). The existing 1,001-text payload case (`:181`) still answers 400. One consequence: 100 texts of at most 8,192 characters total at most 819,200 characters, so the 1,000,000-character total cap (`handler.py:156`, `:406-410`) no longer binds at the default caps. **Answers to Claude's collection-6 findings** (line numbers at `5ea4a631`):

A failed encode still answers one 503 for the whole request (`:431-433`).
