title: [P2] Enforce CLI error conventions repo-wide (stderr, exit 2, network timeouts) with a lint gate
body:
## Summary

CLAUDE.md ("Error Handling in Scripts") requires:

- diagnostics written to stderr
- exit code 1 for errors
- exit code 2 for missing runtime dependencies, with a hint pointing at `requirements.txt`
- network calls that can't hang

#480 fixes this for institutional-flow-tracker only. The audit found the same pattern across many skills. A one-time sweep plus a cheap lint gate would close it for good.

Audit baseline: `origin/main` @ `eab8d5c` (2026-10-10).

## Evidence

**1. Error messages printed to stdout.**

A narrow grep finds 27 hits: `print("Error…` / `print(f"ERROR…` without `file=sys.stderr`, in non-test code. A broader scan finds about 64. Examples:

- `skills/pead-screener/scripts/screen_pead.py:723`
- `skills/edge-hint-extractor/scripts/build_hints.py:472`, `:504`, `:526`
- `skills/edge-concept-synthesizer/scripts/synthesize_edge_concepts.py:749`
- `skills/portfolio-manager/scripts/check_alpaca_connection.py:23`, `:37`, `:234`

**2. Missing dependency exits with 1 instead of 2.**

`skills/institutional-flow-tracker/scripts/track_institutional_flow.py:32-35` handles `ImportError` for `requests` by printing to stdout and calling `sys.exit(1)`.

**3. Network call without a timeout.**

`skills/economic-calendar-fetcher/scripts/get_economic_calendar.py:58` calls `urllib.request.urlopen(request)` with no `timeout=`, so it can hang indefinitely. The AST scan found 0 untimed `requests.get/post` calls, so this one is the outlier.

## Proposal

1. Add a small AST-based checker to `scripts/hooks/` or `scripts/` and wire it into pre-commit and CI. Run it over `skills/*/scripts/**/*.py`, excluding tests. It flags:
   - `print(...)` whose first arg string starts with `Error` / `ERROR` / `FATAL` and that has no `file=sys.stderr`
   - `except ImportError` blocks at module top level that call `sys.exit(1)`
   - `urlopen(...)` / `requests.*(...)` calls without `timeout`
2. Fix the existing violations. An allowlist with reasons is acceptable for any intentional cases.
3. Update the CLI regression tests that currently pin stdout behavior, as #480 notes for PR #475.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Checker runs in pre-commit and CI and fails on new violations
- [ ] Existing violations fixed or explicitly allow-listed
- [ ] `get_economic_calendar.py` uses a bounded timeout and has a test for the timeout path
- [ ] Missing-dependency paths exit 2 with a `requirements.txt` hint

## Related

#480 (single-skill instance; PR #492) · #357

title: [fsdp] fix: prevent NPU parameter corruption during FSDP2 CPU offload
body:
### What does this PR do?

Prevent parameter corruption when offloading an FSDP2 model from NPU to CPU with uneven parameter shards.

With `model.to("cpu", non_blocking=True)`, the NPU-to-CPU transfer can still be in progress when FSDP2 repads the local shard. This repadding happens inside `FSDPModule._apply`, before `model.to()` returns: it allocates padded CPU storage and copies the transferred values into it. Reading the unfinished transfer can therefore persist incorrect parameter values in the new storage. Synchronizing after `model.to()` returns is too late to repair them.

This PR uses blocking CPU transfers on NPU and applies the same policy to both runtime offloading and `fsdp2_load_full_state_dict`. The CUDA non-blocking transfer path is preserved.

The issue was identified while investigating a multi-node Qwen3-Omni accuracy drop related to [vllm-omni#8039](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8039). A 4304-element vision bias divides evenly across 16 ranks, but requires padding across 32 ranks: the nominal shard size is 135 and the final rank owns 119 elements. The investigation localized parameter corruption to this uneven tail during CPU offloading.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs:
  - [FSDP2 offload](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+FSDP2+offload)
  - [NPU non_blocking](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+NPU+non_blocking)
  - [repadding](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+repadding)
- [x] The title follows `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

No open PR addressing this transfer-completion issue was found in these searches.

Related work:
- [#7347](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7347) introduced non-blocking FSDP2 model transfers. This PR adds an NPU-specific correctness fix.
- [#8057](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/8057) makes `CPUOffloadPolicy.pin_memory` configurable to address host allocation failures. It does not address CPU reads before an asynchronous transfer completes.

### Test

Completed locally:

- Ruff lint and formatting checks passed for all three changed Python files.
- Python syntax, license, test-layout, and workflow YAML checks passed.
- `git diff --check` passed before committing.
- A supplementary local harness ran 13 mocked transfer-contract checks successfully; the pre-change implementation failed four NPU cases. This harness isolates function bodies and does not validate PyTorch execution or NPU numerical correctness.

Attempted:

```bash
python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider \
  tests/utils/test_fsdp2_model_transfer_on_cpu.py
```

Collection was blocked by `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'torch'` in the local environment.

NPU regression added to this PR, pending execution on hardware:

```bash
PYTHONPATH="$PWD:$PYTHONPATH" \
torchrun --standalone --nproc-per-node=2 \
  tests/special_distributed/test_fsdp2_npu_model_transfer.py
```

The regression requires no model weights. It checks complete BF16 vectors for 27 uneven/even parameter pairs, covering:

- Initial sharding and full-state loading with CPU offload.
- CPU local shards and reconstructed full parameters.
- Repeated offload/reload cycles.
- Round trips without intervening host reads or synchronization.

The uneven vectors exercise repadding with two ranks and reproduce the 4304-element, 135/119 shard layout with 32 ranks.

The existing CUDA pinned-transfer regression has not been rerun for this commit. Full pre-commit execution and end-to-end NextQA accuracy validation also remain pending.

### API and Usage Example

No public API or configuration changes are required. Existing callers automatically use blocking NPU-to-CPU transfers through the FSDP2 offload helper.

NPU offloading now waits for transfer completion; its performance impact has not yet been measured.

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/utils/fsdp_utils.py`
  - Set `non_blocking=False` for NPU CPU offloading.
  - Reuse the helper in `fsdp2_load_full_state_dict` with `empty_cache=False`.
  - Explain why synchronization after the whole-module transfer is insufficient.
- `tests/utils/test_fsdp2_model_transfer_on_cpu.py`
  - Cover NPU/CUDA transfer policies, cache-release behavior, and full-state loading with and without CPU offload on rank 0 and other ranks.
- `tests/special_distributed/test_fsdp2_npu_model_transfer.py`
  - Add exact numerical checks for uneven and evenly sharded parameters.
- `.github/workflows/npu_unit_tests.yml`
  - Run the new regression on two NPU ranks against the checked-out source.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] The human submitter has reviewed every changed line and this description.
- [x] Read the contribution guide.
- [ ] Complete the targeted PyTorch CPU and NPU regressions.
- [ ] Run the existing CUDA pinned-transfer regression.
- [ ] Run full pre-commit checks.
- [x] Add regression coverage to the CPU tests and NPU CI workflow.
- [ ] Request CI according to the project contribution process.

### AI Assistance Disclosure

OpenAI Codex assisted with the implementation, tests, and this PR description. Human review and hardware validation are pending as recorded above.

title: autobot-infrastructure/shared is not in pytest.ini testpaths — 14+ collection errors, 2 fatal sys.exit() crashes
body:
## Summary

`pytest.ini`'s `testpaths` (and the CI test invocation) omit `autobot-infrastructure`, so nothing under `autobot-infrastructure/shared/` is collected by the automated test gate — despite the directory holding real `test_*.py`/`*_test.py` files, some pre-dating this finding.

Discovered while adding tests for #14047 (3 of that PR's new test files live under `autobot-infrastructure/shared/` and, while individually correct, do not run in CI as a result of this gap).

## Evidence

Attempting to collect the tree directly surfaces two separate problems:

**1. Two files crash pytest's collector entirely** with an uncaught `SystemExit` at module import time (both call `sys.exit(0)` at module level — a standalone-script pattern, not written to be pytest-collected):
- `autobot-infrastructure/shared/scripts/test_alertmanager.py`
- `autobot-infrastructure/shared/scripts/test_grafana_integration.py`

```
INTERNALERROR>   File ".../shared/scripts/test_alertmanager.py", line 56, in <module>
INTERNALERROR>     sys.exit(0)
INTERNALERROR> SystemExit: 0
```

**2. With those two ignored, 11 more files still error on collection** (import errors — missing modules, broken relative imports, stale references to functions that no longer exist):

```
autobot-infrastructure/shared/scripts/analysis/test_chat_debug.py
autobot-infrastructure/shared/scripts/analysis/test_data_layer_debug.py
autobot-infrastructure/shared/scripts/analysis/test_failsafe_sequence.py
autobot-infrastructure/shared/scripts/analysis/test_frontend_errors.py
autobot-infrastructure/shared/scripts/analysis/test_gui_chat_visual.py
autobot-infrastructure/shared/scripts/analysis/test_llm_config.py
autobot-infrastructure/shared/scripts/analysis/test_npu_code_search.py
autobot-infrastructure/shared/scripts/analysis/test_web_research_security.py
autobot-infrastructure/shared/scripts/test_phase2_migration.py
autobot-infrastructure/shared/scripts/test_prometheus_metrics.py
autobot-infrastructure/shared/tests/integration/test_architecture_compliance.py
```

Sample errors:

```
E   ImportError: cannot import name 'development_speedup' from 'agents.development_speedup_agent'
E   ImportError: attempted relative import beyond top-level package
E   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'monitoring.claude_api_monitor'
E   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'monitoring.metrics_adapter'
E   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'utils.redis_client'
```

**3. Separately**, `--import-mode=importlib` (set in `pytest.ini` `addopts`) does not add a test's own directory to `sys.path` — the exact trap `pytest.ini` already documents for `pipeline-scripts` (lines 10-13, fixed for #13368/#13879/#13880). Any test file under `autobot-infrastructure/shared/` doing a bare `from <sibling_module> import ...` fails the same way those did:

```
E   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'start_monitoring'
E   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'manage_system_knowledge'
E   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'index_documentation'
```

(Those three are now fixed via explicit-path `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location` loading in #14047's PR, so they are individually correct and collect cleanly on their own — they just still don't run automatically because of the `testpaths` gap.)

**4. A duplicate-name hazard**: `index_documentation.py` exists at both `autobot-infrastructure/shared/tools/index_documentation.py` and `autobot-infrastructure/shared/scripts/utilities/index_documentation.py`. A bare `import index_documentation` from a test resolves whichever directory is first on `sys.path` — order-dependent, silently binds to the wrong file. Worth a look as a consolidate-never-fork candidate independent of the testpaths gap.

## Why this matters

`#13368`/`#13879`/`#13880` fixed the identical class of bug for `tools/`, `scripts/`, and `pipeline-scripts/` — directories that held passing tests nothing ran. `autobot-infrastructure/shared/` is the same shape: real test files, silently never executed, so a red test here has been red for as long as the bug it covers and nobody noticed.

## Suggested fix

Two independent pieces:
1. Quarantine or fix the 2 fatal `sys.exit()` files and the 11 broken-import files (or explicitly exclude via `pytest.ini`'s existing exclude mechanism if some are legitimately standalone scripts, not tests, misnamed `test_*.py`).
2. Add `autobot-infrastructure/shared` to `pytest.ini` `testpaths` (and the CI test-invocation step) once (1) is clean, mirroring how `tools`/`scripts`/`pipeline-scripts` were wired in.

## Related

- #14047 — surfaced this while adding 3 test files under this tree
- #13368, #13879, #13880 — same defect class, different directories

title: fix(custom)!: refuse a custom indicator whose module name is already taken
body:
## What

`custom.import_dir()` refuses a custom indicator whose name already resolves to another module.

- Before anything is imported, the name is resolved the way `importlib.reload` resolves it: through `sys.meta_path`, ignoring the `sys.modules` cache. The result must be the file itself. Otherwise `ImportError` names both paths, and neither `sys.path` nor any module is touched.
- The check runs before the category directory is added to `sys.path`.
- A file name that is not a module name (`ab.cd.py`) raises `ImportError` saying so.
- Re-importing an edited indicator still reloads it.

## Why

Modules are imported by their bare name, and the category directory is appended to the end of `sys.path`. On `main` this goes wrong in three ways:
- `trend/statistics.py` re-executes the stdlib `statistics` module (`importlib.reload`), then fails with "has no function named 'statistics'".
- A file named after an installed package reloads that package.
- With one name in two categories, nothing fails: the second file resolves to the first, so `ta.<name>` runs the first file's code, and `Category` lists the name under both categories.

## Measurement

- `test_import_dir_rejects_a_stdlib_module_name` and `test_import_dir_rejects_one_name_in_two_categories` fail with the package from `main` and pass on the branch.
- The first version of the check used `importlib.util.find_spec`, which reads the cached `sys.modules` spec. Review found it was not enough: a same-named file put earlier on `sys.path` after a first `import_dir` passed the check, and `reload()` then ran it under this indicator's category (`pq(10)` gave 3000 instead of 20). Three tests were added in review, each red before the fix:
  - the shadowing file is refused;
  - `sys.path` is unchanged after a refusal (the category directory used to stay appended);
  - `ab.cd.py` gives a clear `ImportError` instead of a bare `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'ab'`.

## Gates

- `black --check --diff pandas_ta_classic/`: pass
- `ruff check .`: pass
- mypy, both passes of `make typecheck` (`--python-version 3.12`): pass
- Checklist greps 1–9: clean (grep 7 in the form of #256)
- `core.pyi` pipeline: no diff
- `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 pytest tests/ -n 8`: 9030 passed, 4 skipped, 9 xfailed, on Python 3.13 with TA-Lib installed

## BREAKING

A custom-indicator directory that holds one of these files now raises `ImportError`:
- a file named after a stdlib or installed module;
- one file name in two categories;
- a file name that is not a module name.

Before, such a directory loaded with the wrong code. The CHANGELOG entry is marked **BREAKING**.

## Open points (not in this PR)

- `import_dir` is not atomic: categories processed before a refused file stay imported and bound. It raises on the first bad file, but does not roll back the earlier ones.
- If the regression ever returned, `test_import_dir_rejects_a_stdlib_module_name` would detect that the stdlib `statistics` module was re-executed, but it would not restore it for the rest of the xdist worker.

title: pip-installed zview fails with ModuleNotFoundError
body:
**Describe the bug**

Installing zview with "pip install ." result in some ModuleNotFoundError because some packages and modules are missing from the wheel.

**To Reproduce**
From my venv, installing from main (commit 1f859ad):
```
(zephyr_venv) pjn@prome:~/git/zview$ zview --help
bash: /home/pjn/.venv/zephyr_venv/bin/zview: No such file or directory
(zephyr_venv) pjn@prome:~/git/zview$ pip install "git+file:///home/pjn/git/zview@1f859ad"
Collecting git+file:/home/pjn/git/zview@1f859ad
  Cloning file:///home/pjn/git/zview (to revision 1f859ad) to /tmp/pip-req-build-nl4z_kb_
  ...
Installing collected packages: zview
Successfully installed zview-0.22.3
(zephyr_venv) pjn@prome:~/git/zview$ zview --help
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/pjn/.venv/zephyr_venv/bin/zview", line 3, in <module>
    from zview_cli import main
  File "/home/pjn/.venv/zephyr_venv/lib64/python3.14/site-packages/zview_cli.py", line 12, in <module>
    from frontend.zview_tui import tui_run
  File "/home/pjn/.venv/zephyr_venv/lib64/python3.14/site-packages/frontend/zview_tui.py", line 24, in <module>
    from frontend.tui.views.base import (
    ...<6 lines>...
    )
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'frontend.tui'
(zephyr_venv) pjn@prome:~/git/zview$
```

There are no `__init__.py` in `src/frontend/tui` and `src/frontend/tui/views`, making the packages not
accessible (because `namespaces = false` in pyproject.toml).
After adding the two `__init__.py` files locally and re-installing:

```
(zephyr_venv) pjn@prome:~/git/zview$ zview --help
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/pjn/.venv/zephyr_venv/bin/zview", line 3, in <module>
    from zview_cli import main
  File "/home/pjn/.venv/zephyr_venv/lib64/python3.14/site-packages/zview_cli.py", line 12, in <module>
    from frontend.zview_tui import tui_run
  File "/home/pjn/.venv/zephyr_venv/lib64/python3.14/site-packages/frontend/zview_tui.py", line 43, in <module>
    from orchestrator import ZScraper
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'orchestrator'
(zephyr_venv) pjn@prome:~/git/zview$
```

Because the orchestrator module is missing from the py-modules in pyproject.toml

Those are not issues when using west because the west command imports directly from src/ and does
not uses the wheel.

**Proposal**

Adding the `__init__.py` to the TUI so that it is discoverable and adding the orchestrator and others
to the py-modules. Basically:
```
diff --git a/pyproject.toml b/pyproject.toml
index 8dc6348..00d3286 100644
--- a/pyproject.toml
+++ b/pyproject.toml
@@ -43,7 +43,7 @@ requires = ["setuptools>=61.0"]
 build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

 [tool.setuptools]
-py-modules = ["zview_cli"]
+py-modules = ["logging_setup", "orchestrator", "runner_config", "snapshot", "zview_cli"]

 [tool.setuptools.packages.find]
 where = ["src"]
diff --git a/src/frontend/tui/__init__.py b/src/frontend/tui/__init__.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..e69de29
diff --git a/src/frontend/tui/views/__init__.py b/src/frontend/tui/views/__init__.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..e69de29
(zephyr_venv) pjn@prome:~/git/zview$
```

While this works, one thing that is not ideal with this is that if anything inside the venv ships
anything with a package with the same name as any of the py-modules, the lastly installed would win and someone won´t be happy. Same potential issue with `backend`/`frontend`/`kernel`.
To take this into account, something a bit more involved would be needed, to:
- move everything in src/ into src/zview and have a `__init.py` there. zview_cli.py can become
  zview/cli.py
- The import lines change to the likes of `from zview.orchestrator import ...`
- The different test patches would need the zview prefix
- The py-modules could be removed as zview would now be picked automatically
- The entry in pyproject would become `zview = "zview.cli:main"`

This should be  transparent to the west usage as zview_tui_cmd.py already adds src/ to
sys.path, only the import line changes.

I am happy to open a PR if you think it would make sense and I did not miss something. Either the minimal addition of the two missing `__init__.py` and the py-modules extension, or the more involved change to avoid nameclashing (which I think would be the better thing to do).
Oh and if you agree with the above, another small PR could be done to add a new CI step that would pip
install zview and run zview --help

P.S: Loved your talk at ELCE, thanks!

title: feat(OMN-20867): lab-fill plan fails HEADROOM_UNKNOWN for idle hosts with no fresh bus reading
body:
## Summary
- Ticket OMN-20867, acceptance criterion AC-M2.
- A host probe with idle slots but no fresh headroom reading (missing or older than the contract-declared max age) gives a typed HEADROOM_UNKNOWN failure for that host (a loud failure event, not zero candidates, not success).
- A fresh reading with free slots gives a placement plan for that host.
- A fan-out claim is derived only from dispatch records read back from the bus in the same tick.

## What changed
- node_lab_fill_plan_compute gains operation plan_lab_fill_headroom (HandlerLabFillHeadroomPlan, pure COMPUTE, handle(request) -> result).
- Inputs: the runner's host probes (runner slots, limited marker, refusal, unreadable error, engine logins) and headroom readings that are the pool hosts' capacity advertisements on onex.evt.omnimarket.lab-host-capacity-advertised.v1 (published every 10 s by the lab-work serve process on each pool host), plus observed_at.
- Contract config.lab_fill_plan.headroom: reading_topic onex.evt.omnimarket.lab-host-capacity-advertised.v1, max_age_seconds 60. A reading older than 60 s, or dated more than 60 s in the future, is not fresh.
- A host with idle slots and no fresh reading: zero lanes, reason "headroom-unknown: missing|stale|future", one typed ModelLabFillHeadroomUnknown entry, and the result's terminal_failure_cause = HEADROOM_UNKNOWN.
- A host the runner blocks (limited, refused, unreadable) keeps the existing capacity reason; a host with zero slots and no reading is "runner-cap"; neither is HEADROOM_UNKNOWN.
- Contract declares runtime_dispatch.terminal_events success onex.evt.omnimarket.lab-fill-plan-decided.v1 and failure onex.evt.omnimarket.lab-fill-plan-failed.v1; the failure topic is in event_bus.publish_topics and externally_consumed_topics.
- The runtime's failure-terminal guard (omnibase_infra contract_terminal_events) publishes a result carrying terminal_failure_cause on the failure topic.
- A test derives the failure topic with declared_failure_terminal_topics, the function the event-bus result applier calls, and routes a HEADROOM_UNKNOWN result to it and a placement result to the success topic.
- Operation verify_lab_fill_fanout (HandlerLabFillFanoutReadback, pure COMPUTE): fanned_out counts only dispatch records whose tick id equals the request's tick id; records of other ticks are counted separately and ignored; a claimed lane with no matching record gives terminal_failure_cause = FANOUT_UNPROVEN.
- ModelHostCapacityAdvertisement moved to omnimarket.models.model_host_capacity_advertisement (shared type); node_lab_work_unit_effect re-exports it, so existing imports keep working.
- scripts/ci/check_contract_publish_parity.py: a declared runtime_dispatch failure terminal counts as runtime-published only when the node's Python carries terminal_failure_cause (the field the runtime guard reads); otherwise it is still an offender. Two gate tests cover both cases. The frozen baseline is unchanged at 127 entries; no allowlist or baseline grows.
- This PR edits node_lab_fill_plan_compute/contract.yaml and handlers/__init__.py, which open PR omnimarket#3678 (same ticket) also edits; the two are independent and need a structural union when the second lands.
- No assembler on the lab runtime builds the plan_lab_fill_headroom request from the bus yet; this PR adds the compute operations and the contract-declared failure terminal.

## Bus inputs inventory
- Inventory, read 2026-10-10: host headroom IS on the bus: lab-host-capacity-advertised.v1 on the ci-bus lane broker; in a 25 s window h200 and h201 advertised, h101 and h202 did not.
- On the .201 dev lane broker, lab-host-capacity-advertised.v1, lab-work-unit-completed.v1, lab-fill-plan-decided.v1, remote-lane-decided.v1 and onex.intent.platform.runtime-tick.v1 hold high-watermark 0.
- Inventory: remote-lane runner receipts, limited-host markers and the runner's lane slots have NO bus producer: they are files on the launching host read by the remote-lane runner's placement read. Publishing them is not in this PR (that runner lives outside this repository); until a producer exists, the probe facts arrive in the request.

## No dual owner
- No dual owner: this PR adds pure COMPUTE operations only.
- No node starts acting on any class of PR action, and no landing-controller path changes.

## Tests
- Checks run locally on h201: ruff format and ruff check clean, mypy --strict clean on touched files; contract topic graph CLOSED (937 contracts, 0 unfenced defects); runtime sweep import check clean; check_node_metadata_dependencies PASS; check_topic_drift and check_topic_enum_drift PASS; check_no_hardcoded_topics OK.
- Tests first: tests/nodes/node_lab_fill_plan_compute/test_lab_fill_headroom_plan.py failed at base 3fe55c842 (ModuleNotFoundError: omnimarket.models.model_host_capacity_advertisement) and passes at head.
- lab-run (bus placement) on host h200 at sha ea39f09940a63a3f22ff465e100e38bb391e7a2b: uv run pytest tests/nodes/node_lab_fill_plan_compute tests/gates/test_contract_publish_parity.py tests/unit/lab_work -q -> 446 passed, exit 0.

## Lab

Lab: host=h201 lane=ci-bus (lab-host-capacity-advertised.v1, read with `onex lab-work hosts --bus-lane ci-bus --json`) head=ea39f09940a63a3f22ff465e100e38bb391e7a2b: 2 real readings (h200 08:50:21Z, h201 08:50:19Z) replayed at 08:50:24Z through plan_lab_fill_headroom against the 2026-10-10T0750Z lab-fill STATUS hosts (h101 1 slot, h201 6 slots): placement hosts 0 (h201 load 1.65 per core, reason load), HEADROOM_UNKNOWN 1 (h101, missing).

Lab: same head, the 08:16Z capture (h200 08:16:31Z, h201 08:16:27Z, observed 08:16:35Z) against the same probes: placement hosts 1 (h201, 4 lanes, load 0.43 per core), HEADROOM_UNKNOWN 1 (h101, missing); replayed at 08:50:24Z the same readings give HEADROOM_UNKNOWN 2 (h101 missing, h201 stale).

title: Admit tree-sitter-bash as the shell parser dependency
body:
## **User description** **Supersedes #394 and #395**, the same branch, opened by the machine user `gnostoa-agent-user` under MA0 Phase 1a (#15). #394 was opened as the owner, who cannot approve their own pull request. #395 was opened by the agent App, whose pull requests Codex, Amazon Q and CodeAnt skip. Review history, threads and rounds stay on #394. **Change class:** critical. It changes preparation-authority surfaces under Decision 0090: `pyproject.toml` and both locks. **Work Item:** #393. **Decision:** [0108](knowledge/decisions/0108-read-shell-text-with-a-parser-behind-an-owned-analysis.md). The owner admitted it on 2026-10-07, together with this separate PR: «εγκρίνω τη Decision 0108. ξεκινα το ξεχωριστό PR εξάρτησης προς το main» ("I approve Decision 0108. Start the separate dependency PR to main.") **Pre-change evidence:** the three new tests fail on an image without the pair: - `PackageNotFoundError` for `tree-sitter`; - the probe's `ModuleNotFoundError` for `tree_sitter_bash`, twice. ## What changes - **The pair.** `tree-sitter==0.25.2` and `tree-sitter-bash==0.25.1` are pinned exactly in `pyproject.toml`, as Decision 0108's items 7 and 14 require, with no `[core]` extra. The first revision declared ranges; round 2 replaced them, and a test now fails on any `tree-sitter*` declaration without `==`. - **Locks:** both are pinned in both locks, with every non-yanked wheel hash: 35 and 8. - **Hashes:** the two wheels used in the evaluation matched PyPI's digests (Decision 0095). - **Provenance:** `tree-sitter-bash` 0.25.1 was uploaded with Twine, not Trusted Publishing. The hash allow-list gives artifact identity, not publisher provenance. - **The compatibility smoke**, `tests/test_shell_parser_dependency.py`, parses through a child process, `tests/shell_parser_probe.py`. A native crash therefore fails the test rather than the runner. It asserts: - the exact pair; - the grammar's reading of the constructs the shell reader relies on: a substitution in an assignment, single against double quotes, a quoted newline, a comment's apostrophe, a function body, a process substitution, and a here-document with `2>&1`; - that every shell surface of this repository parses with no error at all. That covers every surface kind of the frozen corpus: - each workflow and action `run:` value, with `${{ }}` masked; - each `sh`, `bash`, `dash` or `ash` script by its shebang's interpreter, anywhere; - `AGENTS.md`'s shell fences, with their `` masked at their width; - the Dockerfile's shell-form `RUN` instructions. - GitLab CI's `before_script`, `script` and `after_script`, and the `ci/` workflow templates. title: docs: fix the onboarding gaps found by a new-user walkthrough
body:
## Summary

A new-user walkthrough was run on real hardware (Litearm 7-axis, `/dev/ttyACM0`,
firmware `Litearm1.10.0-7J`), following only what this repository documents. Several
steps a new user hits first either fail outright or mislead. This corrects the
documentation; no code or behaviour changes.

The blocking one: right after power-up the arm sits in the `EMERGENCY` latch, so the
quick start's first `enable()` throws `ERR{0x10,0x06}` before sending a single retry —
and the quick start never mentions `reset()`. The two Cartesian lines that follow fail
as well: the `movej` before them leaves the arm fully extended (a singular pose), and
both the `move_l` target and the `ik()` target are unusable from there.

## Changes

`README.zh-CN.md` and `README.md`:

- **Quick start** — add the `reset()` that clears the power-on latch, and say why it is
  not optional. Replace `movej([0.1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0])` with a pose whose joints all
  keep a healthy margin to their limits. Drive `move_l` / `ik` from the measured TCP
  instead of `(0.30, 0.0, 0.40, 3.1416, 0.0, 0.0)`, which has no IK solution.
- **Install** — `usermod -aG dialout` is not always required: check
  `ls -l /dev/ttyACM0` first. Document the udev rule that makes the node `crw-rw-rw-`,
  including that any local user on such a machine can drive the arm.
- **Life / safety** — `clear_faults()` clears the single `FAULT` bit; `EMERGENCY` and
  `FB_STALE` are latches only `reset()` clears.
- **Persistence** — `save_params()` requires the arm to be disabled
  (`ERR{0x25,0x04}` otherwise), and disabling drops it out of the position loop, so a
  side-mounted or loaded arm sags. Support it first.
- **Things to watch out for** — new subsection on `mode` / `flags`: the 8 `mode_name`
  values, why `WD_TRIPPED` is normal rather than a fault, why `FB_STALE` is a live
  condition, and that `mode == ZERO_G` (the arm) and `zero_g_active` (this session) can
  disagree. Also the exception to the "`hz` and `timestamp` are both 0" rule: the first
  frame a process reads reports `hz=0.0`.
- **Development** — a ROS 2 install makes `pytest` die during collection
  (`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'lark'`); give the two working invocations.
- Link the troubleshooting guide from the notes section; it had no entry point from
  either top-level README.

`TROUBLESHOOTING.zh-CN.md` and `TROUBLESHOOTING.md`:

- New §17 — the arm is stuck in `ZERO_G` and `zero_g_stop()` does nothing. A new
  session cannot send the exit frame, and the firmware rejects every motion command
  until one arrives. Give the enter/exit pairing that recovers, and how to recognise
  the state (`mode_name == "ZERO_G"` while `zero_g_active` reads `False`).

## Testing

```
$ env -u PYTHONPATH pytest -q          # in litearm-python
638 passed, 22 skipped in 62.99s

$ HOME=$(mktemp -d) env -u PYTHONPATH python -m pytest daemon/tests -q   # in litearm-studio
551 passed, 237 warnings in 74.12s
```

The firmware-sync tests skip unless a `litearm-stm32` checkout is present; they account
for 20 of the 22 skips above.

The replacement quick start was extracted from the edited README and run verbatim on the
arm, from power-up, with no exception handling around it:

```
$ PYTHONPATH=src LITEARM_PORT=/dev/ttyACM0 python3 -u /tmp/qs_zh.py
Litearm1.10.0-7J 7
[0.048511505126953125, 0.3894338607788086, -0.814640998840332, ...]
(0.22064509987831116, 0.3976973295211792, 0.47747859358787537, ...)
[0.061382636427879333, 0.3946659564971924, -0.8173605799674988, ...]
EXIT=0
```

`reset()` → `enable()` → `movej` → `move_l` → `get_state` → `get_tcp` → `ik` → `home`,
every step returning a valid result.

## Issues

None — no issue was filed for this; the findings come from the walkthrough. Happy to
file the code-side findings separately if you want them tracked.

title: fix(mlx): support mlx_lm 0.31 stop-sequence API and add response to math SFT loader
body:
MLX-LM's stop-sequence API drifted across three releases:

| release | API | kwarg |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0.30 | `StopSequenceMatcher` | `stop_matchers=` |
| 0.31 | `SequenceStateMachine` | `state_machines=` (transient) |
| 0.32 | `StopSequences` | `stop_sequences=` |

Upstream #584 already covered 0.30 and 0.32, but on `mlx_lm` 0.31.x
`from mlx_lm.generate import StopSequenceMatcher` still raised `ImportError`
whenever a rollout launched, so RL/GSPO/GRPO/PPO could not run on the
MLX backend. Resolve the API in newest-first order so all three releases
are supported.

Separately, `SFTTrainer` requires each dataset row to carry `prompt` and
`response` (see `areno/api/trainers/sft.py`), but
`examples/math/dataset_loader.py` only returned `prompt` / `solutions` /
`solution`, so `areno train --algo sft` failed with:

  ValueError: SFT dataset loader must return rows with `prompt` and `response`

Add a `response` field holding the full gsm8k reasoning (calculator
markers stripped) followed by `\boxed{final}`, matching the
chat-template-free `prompt` layout the trainer already uses so SFT sees
a real thinking + boxed target instead of a single-token final answer.
`solutions` / `solution` are left unchanged so reward and other consumers
are unaffected.

### Changes
- `areno/api/backend/mlx/generation.py`: resolve `StopSequences` -> `SequenceStateMachine` -> `StopSequenceMatcher` newest-first, with the `stop_sequences` / `state_machines` / `stop_matchers` kwarg chosen accordingly.
- `examples/math/dataset_loader.py`: add a `response` field to the gsm8k record.

### Verified locally
macOS Apple Silicon, MLX backend, `mlx 0.32.2` / `mlx_lm 0.31.3`, Qwen3-0.6B, `gsm8k:main` (modelscope hub):
- `areno train --algo gspo --max-steps 1000` completes, saves five checkpoints, no ImportError, no MLX Insufficient Memory.
- `areno train --algo sft --max-steps 1000` completes, saves five checkpoints.

title: ci: fix lower dependency test
body: `Test lowest dependencies` has failed on `main` and on every PR since pyarrow 26.0.0 came out (2026-10-09) with `ImportError: pyarrow requires NumPy 2.0 or newer, found 1.23.5`. `lowest-direct` only lowers direct dependencies. So numpy went down to its floor (1.23.5), but pyarrow, which comes in through `datasets`, still resolved to the latest version (26.0.0). pyarrow 26 needs NumPy ≥ 2 at runtime, but pyarrow doesn't list numpy as a dependency, so uv can't see the conflict.

title: Setup notes and device info (Windows python3.dll, dependencies, SSDP, README, firmware version / serial / ACE on the device page)
body:
Tested with: Kobra S1, firmware 2.7.2.7, ACE Pro, Windows 10, OrcaSlicer nightly (portable), plugin from `main` as of 2026-10-05.  1. `cryptography` fails with `ImportError: DLL load failed while importing _rust`: OrcaSlicer's bundled Python has no `python3.dll`. Copying one of the same version next to `python.exe` fixes it. 2. The PEP 723 header should say `dependencies = []`. 3. README says SSDP discovery uses port 18910 / `urn:schemas-upnp-org:device:printer:1`, but `start_discovery` sends `ssdp:all` to `239.255.255.250:1900`. The S1 does not answer that; the printer is only found by IP. 4. README clone URL points to `imckellar/...` instead of `ianloic/...`. 5. With the nightly the profile needs `printer_agent = anycubic`; I found no place in the UI for it and created the profile by hand. 
 
**Device page ("Update" tab) shows wrong or missing data**

6. The printer's version shows `1.0.0 (latest version)`. That is the hard-coded fallback in `_push_version_info()`: it reads `version` / `firmwareVersion` from the HTTP `/info` answer (`device_info`), which has no such field. The real firmware version is in the MQTT `info` report (`data.version`, here `2.7.2.7`). Suggestion: use `self._latest_status["version"]` and push the version info again once the first status report has arrived (at connect time it is not known yet).
7. The serial number shows the IP address (`"sn": self.dev_id`). The `/info` answer contains the printer's id in `cn` (here `0949-5B69-C399-C4EE`) and `usn`.
8. The ACE Pro is not part of the `get_version` module list, so its block on that page shows only dashes. The ACE reports no firmware version at all: I queried `multiColorBox/getInfo` and `peripherie`; they only give `model_id` 40001, presence flags, temperature, humidity and the slots. A module entry such as `{"name": "ams/0", "product_name": "ACE Pro", ...}` would at least show the model; I have not yet verified how OrcaSlicer displays an empty version.

title: check_project_complete blocks completion: hermes_cli not importable in cron context
body:
## Bug: `check_project_complete` blocks project completion — `hermes_cli` not importable in cron context

**Repo:** `yzy806806/agora`
**Affected:** `agora/kanban_compat.py` (`_build_bridge`), `agora/leader_loop.py` (`check_project_complete`), `leader_heartbeat.sh`

### Symptom

Leader outputs `PROJECT_COMPLETE` repeatedly (128× in one observed project), but `complete_count` stays 0 and `status` remains `active` forever. The completion gate never fires.

### Root Cause

`check_project_complete` reads the board via `kanban_compat.py` → `importlib.import_module("hermes_cli.kanban_db")` **at module load time**. `hermes_cli` lives in the Hermes core tree (`~/.hermes/hermes-agent/hermes_cli/`) and is only importable when the interpreter has `~/.hermes/hermes-agent` on `sys.path` (the gateway does `sys.path.insert(0, .../hermes-agent)`).

The cron script (`leader_heartbeat.sh` → tools-python) does **not** set that up. So the import raises `ModuleNotFoundError` → `check_project_complete` catches it → `_board_read=False` → **fail-closed: `complete_count` reset to 0** (by design, v2.0.10 CHANGELOG). Because the board read **permanently** fails in the cron context, the 2-consecutive-signal counter never reaches 2 → completion is blocked.

**Verified:** With `PYTHONPATH=~/.hermes/hermes-agent` + full plugin import path → `board read OK`. Without → `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'hermes_cli'`.

### Why not a bypass

Hermes docs are explicit: *"Both surfaces route through the same `kanban_db` layer, so reads see a consistent view and writes can't drift."* A raw `sqlite3` bypass in `leader_loop.py` would break that guarantee. The fail-closed mechanism is correct and should stay; the bug is only that the read never succeeds in the cron context.

### Proposed universal fix (in `agora/kanban_compat.py`, no env workaround)

Add an import-discovery step **before** `_build_bridge()` that finds `hermes_cli` independently of `PYTHONPATH`:

```python
def _ensure_hermes_cli_importable() -> None:
    """Make `hermes_cli` importable for standalone/cron interpreters.

    The gateway inserts <hermes-home>/hermes-agent onto sys.path; a bare
    interpreter (leader_heartbeat.sh cron, dashboard shim) does not, so the
    bridge's importlib.import_module("hermes_cli.kanban_db") raises
    ModuleNotFoundError and check_project_complete fails closed on every
    heartbeat. Discover the core tree and add it to sys.path once.
    """
    try:
        import hermes_cli  # noqa: F401
        return
    except ImportError:
        pass
    import os, sys
    from pathlib import Path
    cands = []
    if os.environ.get("HERMES_HOME"):
        cands.append(Path(os.environ["HERMES_HOME"]) / "hermes-agent")
    # kanban_compat.py is <hermes-home>/plugins/agora/agora/kanban_compat.py
    cands.append(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "hermes-agent")
    for c in cands:
        if (c / "hermes_cli" / "__init__.py").is_file():
            p = str(c)
            if p not in sys.path:
                sys.path.insert(0, p)
            return
```

Call it at module top: `_ensure_hermes_cli_importable()` before `kanban_db = _build_bridge()`.

**Why universal:**
- Plugin-internal, not env-dependent — works in every install (gateway, cron, dashboard, standalone) without per-host `PYTHONPATH` patching
- Respects the documented design — still goes through `hermes_cli.kanban_db` (consistency guarantee intact), no sqlite3 bypass
- Fail-safe — if discovery finds nothing, behaviour is unchanged (import raises, fail-closed)
- Two sources (env `HERMES_HOME` + plugin-relative `parents[3]`) → robust against relocation

### Secondary hardening (optional, separate PR)

The 2-consecutive counter is fragile: it advances only when the **byte window** (since `complete_check_pos`) contains the exact string `PROJECT_COMPLETE`, else reset. In one project: 180 sessions, only 84 (47%) with the token → two consecutive token-bearing windows are rare. Suggestion: anchor detection on **`session_id:` boundaries** instead of byte offsets + symmetric reset (decrement only on 2 consecutive token-**less** windows). Prevents a window gap or a working tick from zeroing the counter.

### Test plan

1. `check_project_complete` with mocked clean board + 2 token-bearing sessions (no `PYTHONPATH`) → `on_project_complete` fires
2. Discovery: `hermes_cli` importable from both `HERMES_HOME`- and `__file__`-path; no `sys.path` duplicate
3. Regression: gateway context (already has `hermes_cli`) → discovery is a no-op, no double-insert

title: fix(rails): make opentelemetry imports optional in the rails import chain
body:
Paired: [GitHub #858](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/agent-core/pull/858) ↔ [GitCode !2462](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/agent-core/merge_requests/2462)

## Problem

`openjiuwen.harness.rails` cannot be imported unless the `observability` extra is installed, even though the core dependencies declare no opentelemetry package at all. `pyproject.toml` puts `opentelemetry-api` and `opentelemetry-sdk` under the `observability` extra only, so a default install produces an import chain that raises `ImportError` at the first `import openjiuwen.harness.rails`.

Two top-level imports break it. Both were found by reproducing the failure, not by reading the tree:

| # | File:line | Import |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `openjiuwen/agent_evolving/trajectory/processor.py:26` | `from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import ReadableSpan, SpanProcessor` |
| 2 | `openjiuwen/extensions/observability/span_context.py:13-14` | `from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import ...` + `from opentelemetry.trace import Span` |

The second one only surfaces after the first is fixed, which is why it is easy to miss. Every other otel reference on the chain is already a lazy in-function import and needed no change.

## Approach

Both sites get the same `try/except ImportError` guard that this tree already uses elsewhere (for example `agent_teams/messager/pyzmq_backend.py`). The guarded symbols degrade safely because their uses are symmetric:

- `ReadableSpan` / `Span` appear only in annotations — both modules already have `from __future__ import annotations` — and as the first argument to `cast()`. They fall back to `Any`.
- `SpanProcessor` is the base class of `TrajectorySpanProcessor` and `ActiveSpanTracker`. In the upstream SDK it is a pure interface whose methods are all no-ops, and both subclasses override everything they use, so it falls back to a stub base class.

A single `logger.warning` fires when the packages are absent, naming the extra to install. Nothing is swallowed silently. In the degraded state no real spans can be produced anyway, since the span-producing code path itself requires opentelemetry; the processors stay constructible and `subscribe`/`drain` continue to behave.

## Test

Adds `test_rails_import_without_opentelemetry` to the existing import-boundary contract test, following the subprocess pattern of its neighbours in that file: a `MetaPathFinder` masks the entire `opentelemetry` namespace, then `import openjiuwen.harness.rails` must succeed, `sys.modules` must contain no otel module, the degraded processors must still subscribe/drain and construct, and both degradation warnings must appear in the output.

## Verification

Run against `develop` @ `4f2c29c`:

- `pytest tests/unit_tests/extensions/observability/test_import_boundary.py tests/unit_tests/agent_evolving/trajectory/test_processor.py` — **10 passed**
- `ruff check` clean on all three changed files
- End-to-end reproduction: with the whole `opentelemetry` namespace masked, `import openjiuwen.harness.rails` fails before the change and succeeds after, emitting both warnings

Diffstat: `processor.py` +16 −1, `span_context.py` +20 −2, `test_import_boundary.py` +48 −0.

## Note

One pre-existing failure is worth flagging so it is not mistaken for fallout from this change: `tests/unit_tests/extensions/observability/test_span_context.py` shows 3 failures in my environment, and it shows the same 3 failures on an unmodified tree. They come from a local otel api/sdk version mismatch (`TraceFlags.RANDOM_TRACE_ID` missing, sdk newer than api), unrelated to this patch.

title: fix(context_evolver): drop undefined export and repair MaTTS import
body:
Paired: [GitHub #990](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/agent-core/pull/990) ↔ [GitCode !2548](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/agent-core/merge_requests/2548)

Two import-time defects in the `context_evolver` extension.

**1. `__all__` lists an undefined symbol**

`openjiuwen/extensions/context_evolver/__init__.py` exports
`create_memory_agent_config` in `__all__`, but the name is neither defined
in the module nor imported into it. Any `from openjiuwen.extensions.context_evolver import *`
raises `AttributeError`.

**2. MaTTS imports `ReasoningBankMemory` from a path that does not exist**

`retrieve/task/reasoning_bank/matts.py` does
`from schema.memory import ReasoningBankMemory` inside a function body.
There is no top-level `schema` module, so the memory-extraction branch
raises `ModuleNotFoundError` the moment it is reached. Because the import
sits in a function, the failure only shows up mid-run rather than at
import time.

**Fix**

- Remove the undefined name from `__all__`.
- Move the MaTTS import to module scope using the correct relative path
  (`from ....schema.memory import ReasoningBankMemory`), so a broken
  import surfaces immediately instead of halfway through a run.

No behaviour change beyond the two failures above.

title: fix(security): let the host supply the tool permission prompt wording
body:
Paired: [GitHub #970](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/agent-core/pull/970) ↔ [GitCode !2540](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/agent-core/merge_requests/2540)

**What type of PR is this?**

/kind bug

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Fixes #969

That report also records two further findings which this PR deliberately does **not**
fix, so neither is closed by this merge:

- an unreachable branch in `_build_always_allow_hint` — repairing it changes behaviour and
  belongs in its own request (see *One template still cannot render today* below);
- a security fail-open in the same code path, where any exception out of the rail's
  `before_tool_call` lets the guarded tool run unconfirmed. It is not caused by the
  hardcoded wording and warranted its own report rather than being folded into either this
  request or the wording issue; it is recorded there only because it constrains where a
  wording seam may validate its input. It now has that report — #971, fixed by
  `fix(security): deny the tool call when the permission gate cannot decide`, filed
  alongside this one — and the two are reconciled under *Checking at construction* below.
  This change does not repair it — it only makes sure the new seam cannot become another
  way into it.

Related but not fixed here:

- #831 reports four other defects in the permission ASK path. None concerns the wording.
- #963 reports that a sub-agent's tool calls run ungated because `create_subagent`
  forwards neither `permissions` nor `permission_host`; it is fixed by
  `fix(harness): gate sub-agent tool calls with the parent's permissions`, filed
  alongside this one. That change edits `deep_agent.py` and one test file, and no
  render site, so it shares no file with this one.

**Rebased onto the merged permission-engine restructure.** This request was first written
against `dce36fc8`, before #866 / PR #792 merged as `20e35736`. That restructure moved and
rewrote every render site this touches, so the change has been re-expressed against the
new layout rather than replayed onto it. What survived, what did not, and what the
restructure added to the problem are set out under *What #792 changed* below.

**What does this PR do / why do we need it**:

The text a person reads before deciding whether a tool may run is assembled from Chinese
string literals compiled into the library. openjiuwen is embedded as a library, so that
wording is what reaches the end user, on whatever channel the host serves them, in
Chinese, whatever language the deployment is otherwise configured for. Nothing in
`openjiuwen.harness` lets a host prevent that: there is no message catalogue,
`AGENT_PROMPT_LANGUAGE` selects the system prompt sent to the model rather than text a
person reads, and `agent_teams.i18n` sits on the wrong side of the dependency. The issue
above has the reproduction, the rendered output and the full account of why each apparent
workaround is not one.

Those literals are also the whole of the permission rail's user-facing text — the issue
has the census — so closing this seam closes the language gap for the rail rather than
part of it.

### What #792 changed, and what it did not

The restructure did not close the gap. On `20e35736`:

- `permission_engine/approve/ask_presentation.py` holds twelve lines containing CJK, and
  **every one of them is a user-visible literal**: six category titles, the parenthetical
  in the `tool` category's summary, four risk names in `_FINDING_LABELS`, and the
  fallback risk name in `_finding_summary`.
- `rails/security/tool_security_rail.py` still holds the four hint literals in
  `_build_always_allow_hint`, untouched.
- A repository search of `openjiuwen/harness/security` for `prompt_texts`, `PromptTexts`,
  `i18n`, `locale` or `language_pack` returns no file.

It also made the problem slightly larger in two ways. It introduced six category titles
where there was one header, so there is more hardcoded prose than before; and it added
`_build_interrupt_metadata`, which hands `ask_title` and `ask_summary` to the host as
structured fields. A host that renders the interrupt itself now receives the Chinese
title as a field of its own, not only as part of a body.

The restructure is released. `v0.1.18` and `v0.1.18.post1` both contain `20e35736`, and `v0.1.16.post20.xiaoyi` has `ask_presentation.py` as well. The earlier releases, from `v0.1.11.post1` to `0.1.17.post2`, have the pre-restructure `_build_message` instead. Which literals a release holds therefore depends on which side of the restructure it was cut from. The four remember-hint literals in `tool_security_rail.py` are in all of them. A user reads Chinese on either side. The restructure therefore did not change the set of affected releases, which now runs to the latest one.

### The change

The wording comes from `PermissionPromptTexts`, a frozen dataclass of `str.format`
templates carried on `ToolPermissionHost` — which is already how this module receives
everything else it cannot decide for itself (permission snapshots, persistence, workspace
resolution, host-side confirmation, scene hooks).

```python
from openjiuwen.harness.security import (
    ENGLISH_PERMISSION_PROMPT_TEXTS,
    PermissionPromptTexts,
    ToolPermissionHost,
)

host = ToolPermissionHost(prompt_texts=ENGLISH_PERMISSION_PROMPT_TEXTS)

host = ToolPermissionHost(
    prompt_texts=PermissionPromptTexts(
        title_tool="This tool needs your approval",
        summary_tool="{tool_name} (confirmation required)",
    ),
)
```

openjiuwen picks **no** language on the host's behalf. That is deliberate: only the host
knows what language its users are served in, and deciding here would also lock out hosts
whose users fall outside the project's `cn`/`en` pair. Each field is independently
overridable, so a host that only wants a different title supplies only a title.

### One seam, two render sites — and one file deliberately left alone

After the restructure the user-visible text is produced in two places, and both had to be
reached from the same host field or the two halves of one prompt could disagree:

- `permission_engine/approve/ask_presentation.py` produces the category, title and
  summary. `build_permission_ask_presentation` takes an optional keyword-only
  `texts=`, defaulting to the built-in set, so its existing callers keep working with the
  three positional arguments they pass today — the rail itself, and upstream's
  `test_ask_presentation.py` and `test_command_canonicalize.py`, all of which pass
  unmodified.
- `PermissionInterruptRail._build_always_allow_hint` produces the remember hint, and reads
  `self._host.prompt_texts` directly.

The rail threads the host's texts into `build_permission_ask_presentation` from **both**
its call sites — `_build_message` and `_build_interrupt_metadata`. Passing them from only
the first would give a host an English body under a Chinese `ask_title`, which is a worse
failure than the one being fixed because it looks deliberate.

`permission_engine/approve/persist_rule_merge.py` is **not** touched, although it holds
thirteen lines containing CJK — more than `ask_presentation.py` does. Every one of them is
a module, function or field docstring, or an inline comment: `"""解析落盘用的 agent 配置
文件路径。"""`, `"""写入 command 类 approval_overrides；path 类忽略..."""`, and so on. None
of that text is ever rendered to a user; it is developer documentation, and it is in the
same language as the docstrings in `host.py` and `models.py` beside it. Translating the
repository's internal documentation is a different project from giving a host a seam for
what its users read, and folding it in would put that translation inside a change whose
subject is what users see. The same reasoning leaves the nine CJK docstrings and comments
in `tool_security_rail.py` alone: only the four literals that render are touched.

### The template set, and why it is shaped this way

The set has been re-derived twice as the render sites moved. `header`, `confirm_instruction`, `arguments` and `external_paths` no longer have a render site. `matched_rule` was deliberately removed from the body, and `test_ask_presentation.py` asserts its absence. The four hint templates survive, two of them reworded, as described below. They are joined by the `tool` and `generic` titles, the `tool` category's summary, and five finding risk names.

`1c22b9f2`, `fix(guardrail): permission engine 统一收编命令行安全检查`, and `13d226d9` then rewrote the title path, which is why the remaining fields are shaped as they are. A title no longer names its category. It names the risk that triggered the confirmation, inside one frame, `title_risk_detected`. The name is the first of these that applies: the matched built-in rule's entry in `rule_risk_labels`, `risk_interpreter_sink`, `finding_shell_too_complex`, a finding name, and last the confirmation's own category (`risk_path`, `risk_network`, `risk_finding`, `risk_shell`). Where nothing names a risk the whole title is `title_tool` or `title_generic`, as before.

`rule_risk_labels` is the one field that is a table rather than a template, and deliberately so. The seventeen built-in rule ids it names are a set that grows between releases. A field per rule would make every added rule a change to this class's field set, and would make a host's catalogue incomplete the moment it did not track one. A host's table replaces the default one whole, and a rule id it does not list falls back to the next name in the order above rather than raising, so a table that has gone out of date costs one named risk and nothing else. Its entries are names used whole rather than templates, so they are checked for type at construction and not rendered.

The finding risk names stay flat fields keyed by reason, and the argument runs the other way: their four reasons are produced by this repository's own command analysis rather than by a rule catalogue, an unknown one already falls back to `finding_other`, and each is one validated template like every other field.

Only prose is templated. A `path` summary is a path. A `network` summary is a URL. A `shell` summary is the tool name and the command. A `finding` summary over a command that reads or writes files is the file access. The verb in front of a path comes from a map whose fallback is the tool name.

### What is deliberately not covered

Not every string in an ASK body is prose. The summary of a `path` confirmation is
`"{action} {path}"`, of a `network` confirmation a URL, of a `shell` confirmation
`"{tool}: {command}"` — data lines, not sentences. The `action` in the first of those
comes from `_PATH_ACTION`, a map from tool name to a canonical verb whose fallback is the
tool name itself; it is in the register of identifiers, not of prose. Only two summary
fragments are sentences a translator would touch — the `tool` category's parenthetical and
the risk name prefixing a `finding` summary — and both are templated. Templating the
composition itself would mean handing the host the summary layout as well as its words,
which is a larger interface than the problem needs.

### Checking at construction

A mistyped override cannot reach a tool call: `PermissionPromptTexts.__post_init__`
renders every field once, and a host's typo fails there. Each field is checked against the
placeholders its own docstring documents rather than against the union of all sixteen — a
union would accept `title_tool="{tool_name}"`, even though a title is rendered with no
placeholders at all. `_FIELD_PLACEHOLDERS` holds that per-field set; a field added without
an entry raises on the first construction, which this module itself performs at import.
Both routes to an instance go through `__init__`, so `dataclasses.replace` on a valid set
re-checks the field it replaces. A misspelt placeholder, a placeholder borrowed from
another field, a malformed format string and a non-string value all raise
`DEEPAGENT_CONFIG_PARAM_ERROR`, naming the field and what was wrong with it — the status
code `Workspace.__post_init__` in `openjiuwen/harness/workspace/workspace.py` already uses
for a host's bad config value, chosen over a bare `KeyError` or a new exception type so
hosts that already map framework status codes need nothing new.

Checking at **construction** rather than at render is load-bearing, not a matter of taste,
and the restructure did not disturb the reason. On `20e35736` a rail's `before_tool_call`
can still stop a call only by raising `AbortError` or by marking the call skipped; any
other exception is swallowed by the callback framework and the tool then runs
unconfirmed. `openjiuwen/core/runner/callback/framework.py` is not among the 52 files
#792 changed, and `PermissionInterruptRail.before_tool_call` still awaits
`resolve_interrupt` with no guard around it. `_build_message` and
`_build_interrupt_metadata` are both reached inside `before_tool_call`, so an exception
raised while rendering an ASK body would not fail the round — it would skip the gate.
Validating at construction turns the same typo into a failure where the host builds its
texts, before any agent exists, so the seam adds no new route into that fail-open.

That premise is the subject of #971, filed alongside this request, and its fix changes it:
with that merged, a raise inside `before_tool_call` is caught at the callback boundary and
the tool call is rejected rather than run, so a render-time raise would fail the round
loudly instead of skipping the gate. The seam is designed the same way either way, for
three reasons that do not depend on it. Every release this request is written against —
`v0.1.11.post1` through `v0.1.18.post1` — carries the fail-open and none of them will
carry that fix, so a host validating at render time is unsafe on all of them. A malformed
template is a startup fault rather than a runtime one: it is wrong for every call the host
will ever make, and reporting it once where the host builds its texts is better than
reporting it as a denied tool call in the middle of a run, however loudly. And a template
that raises only on the branch that happens to be taken — an override of `remember_command`
that a path-only tool never reaches — would otherwise sit undetected until the first call
that renders it. Construction-time validation is therefore the right shape on its own
merits; the fail-open is what makes it not merely better but necessary on every version
currently released.

The check costs one pass over sixteen short templates, and runs once per
`PermissionPromptTexts` — hence once per `ToolPermissionHost`, once per rail.
`dataclasses.replace` on the host, which `build_permission_interrupt_rail` performs when
it supplies `resolve_workspace_dir`, passes the existing instance through and re-validates
nothing; nothing on the per-tool-call path constructs either dataclass.

These templates are reached when `request_permission_confirmation` is unset, which is the
default, or when it is set and returns the literal `"interrupt"`. Every other outcome
short-circuits before them: a `PermissionConfirmResponse`, where the host rendered its own
UI and decided; `None`, where the hosted request failed; a return of any other type; or an
exception out of the hook. Hosts on those paths are unaffected either way.

### Where the module lives, and what it exports

`prompt_texts.py` sits at `openjiuwen/harness/security/permission_engine/`, beside
`models.py` and `host.py`, rather than inside `approve/` next to its main consumer. Two
modules in different packages read it — `permission_engine/approve/ask_presentation.py`
and `rails/security/tool_security_rail.py` — and `host.py` carries it; putting it at the
engine's top level is what keeps `host.py` from importing the `approve` package at module
import time merely to name a type.

The module also names the built-in set, `DEFAULT_PERMISSION_PROMPT_TEXTS`, which exists so
that `build_permission_ask_presentation` has something to fall back on when no `texts=` is
passed without constructing — and so revalidating — a set on every render.
`ToolPermissionHost.prompt_texts` still uses `default_factory=PermissionPromptTexts`
rather than that singleton: it is the idiomatic dataclass default, it keeps `host.py` from
depending on another module's object identity, and it costs one validated construction per
host, which is once per rail.

`PermissionPromptTexts` and `ENGLISH_PERMISSION_PROMPT_TEXTS` are exported from
`permission_engine/__init__.py` and from `openjiuwen/harness/security/__init__.py`, which
is the surface the guide documents — those two names and no others; `host.py`'s own
`__all__` is left as it was, so nothing new leaks through the `import *` in the
compatibility shim. `openjiuwen/harness/security/host.py` is **not** changed at all: it is
a shim for names that used to live at that path, and a name that has never had an old path
does not belong in it.

### What changes for a user

The same ASK on `write_file` with the default `ToolPermissionHost()` emits, byte for byte,
what the unmodified code emits everywhere except inside the "remember" hint, whose wording
is corrected — the reason is two sections below:

````text
write /srv/app/notes.md

> 选择「会话内记住」可在本会话内自动放行 ``write_file`` 的所有调用，而不只是本次针对 ``/srv/app/notes.md`` 的调用；选择「永久记住」可将此规则写回磁盘，所有会话均自动放行。
````

Passing `ToolPermissionHost(prompt_texts=ENGLISH_PERMISSION_PROMPT_TEXTS)` instead, a
difference of one constructor argument at the integration point, renders this body:

````text
write /srv/app/notes.md

> Remembering this for the session allows every ``write_file`` call automatically until the session ends, not only this one on ``/srv/app/notes.md``; remembering it permanently writes the rule to disk, so every session allows them automatically.
````

with this interrupt metadata alongside it:

````json
{
  "ask_category": "path",
  "ask_title": "Protected file path access detected",
  "ask_summary": "write /srv/app/notes.md",
  "matched_rule": "file_guard:defaults"
}
````

### Compatibility

Every default but the tool "remember" hint reproduces the literal it replaces, so a host that injects nothing sees no other change. Sixteen confirmations render byte for byte identically before and after, in the interrupt metadata and in the body alike, except for that one hint. They span every category, the built-in and operator rule-id forms, the interpreter-sink and too-complex titles, all five finding names and every hint outcome the code can reach.

No public name is removed or repurposed. `prompt_texts` is a new field with a default,
`build_permission_ask_presentation` gains a keyword-only parameter with a default, and
`PermissionPromptTexts` / `ENGLISH_PERMISSION_PROMPT_TEXTS` are new exports.

### The two defaults that are corrected rather than reproduced

For a non-shell tool the hint has read this way since `785a0fcf`,
"bugfix(toolrail): remember option optimize", which added the `path_desc` local it
interpolates:

````text
> 选择「会话内记住」可在本会话内自动放行 ``write_file`` 类工具在 ``/srv/app/notes.md`` 下的调用；选择「永久记住」可将此规则写回磁盘，所有会话均自动放行。
````

— the allow bounded by the path in front of the person deciding. It is not bounded by it.

`_get_auto_confirm_key` appends a subcommand only for `bash`, `mcp_exec_command` and
`create_terminal`. For every other tool it returns the bare tool name:

````python
        if tool_name in {"bash", "mcp_exec_command", "create_terminal"}:
            cmd = tool_args.get("command", tool_args.get("cmd", ""))
            return self._build_shell_auto_confirm_key(tool_name, str(cmd or ""))

        return tool_name
````

That same string is what `_store_auto_confirm` writes into the session
(`config[auto_confirm_key] = True`) and what `_is_auto_confirmed` reads back, so an entry
stored from a prompt about one path matches that tool's every later ASK whatever the path.
The permanent half of the sentence is tool-wide too:
`merge_permission_allow_rule_into_permissions` drops the suggestions whose `match_type` is
`path` — paths are written to file_guard instead — and, with nothing else to write for a
non-shell tool, calls `_persist_tiered_tool_allow`, which sets
`permissions.tools[<tool>] = "allow"`.

The value the hint interpolates need not even be a path. `_build_always_allow_hint` falls
back to the first argument value containing a slash, so an ASK on a fetch of
`https://evil.test/a` described the allow as calls "under" that URL.

Both defaults are therefore reworded: the tool is named as the scope, and the path is
presented as the case in hand rather than as the limit.

````text
zh  remember_tool  before  ...自动放行 ``{tool_name}`` 类工具{path_scope}的调用；...
                   after   ...自动放行 ``{tool_name}`` 的所有调用{path_scope}；...
zh  path_scope     before  在 ``{path_hint}`` 下
                   after   ，而不只是本次针对 ``{path_hint}`` 的调用

en  remember_tool  before  ...allows ``{tool_name}`` calls{path_scope} automatically until the session ends;...
                   after   ...allows every ``{tool_name}`` call automatically until the session ends{path_scope};...
en  path_scope     before   under ``{path_hint}``
                   after   , not only this one on ``{path_hint}``
````

Both language sets change together. This request is the reason an English rendering of
that sentence exists at all, and shipping the two saying opposite things would be worse
than either alone. `path_scope` stays a field and stays overridable — the path is real
context for the decision, and only the claim made about it was wrong — and its docstring
now names what the key is, so a host writing its own wording does not restore the reading.
No behaviour changes; the hint is a string, and widening what it says brings it into line
with the allow the code already performs.

Correcting it here rather than beside it: this request is about where the ASK wording
comes from, it is the request that decides the English rendering of this sentence, and it
is the request that promotes `path_scope` from an inline `path_desc` local to a
documented, host-overridable field. Leaving it would publish the wrong claim as API.

### One template still cannot render today

The session-only shell hint in `_build_always_allow_hint` is unreachable, on `20e35736`
exactly as before: `shell_key` and `auto_confirm_key` are computed from the same call on
the same arguments, so `if shell_key:` returns first whenever either is truthy and the
`if auto_confirm_key:` guard beneath that return never runs. The sweep above
confirms it — that hint appears in none of them. The issue has the detail.

That is a defect in the rail as it stands, not one this change introduces or repairs. The
control flow is preserved line for line here; only the literals move.
`remember_command_session_only` is kept as a field, and translated in the bundled English
set, so that the seam covers the code exactly as written and the wording is already in
place when the branch is repaired. Repairing it changes behaviour and belongs in its own
request rather than inside one whose subject is where the wording comes from.

### Why an English wording set ships alongside the mechanism

The seam alone would leave every English-serving embedder translating the same sixteen
templates from the Chinese originals, independently and slightly differently — and one
group of them has a constraint that is invisible to a translator working from the Chinese
text alone. The "remember" hints must describe what each choice *does* rather than naming
the choices, because the buttons are rendered by the host and the rail cannot know what
they are called there. The Chinese originals name them (「会话内记住」, 「永久记住」); a
faithful translation would name them too, and would be wrong on every host that labels
them anything else. Getting that right once, in the tree, is worth more than the strings.

`ENGLISH_PERMISSION_PROMPT_TEXTS` is that translation, and it is data and nothing more —
no language detection, no selection logic, no change of default. A host passes it exactly
as it would pass an instance of its own; a host that passes nothing still gets the Chinese
defaults. So it commits the project neither to shipping a wording set per language nor to
a mechanism that depends on one: if the preference is for openjiuwen to ship no wording
data at all, deleting the constant leaves a working seam behind and the tests that cover
the mechanism keep passing. Shipping it also makes the seam demonstrably sufficient for a
whole real language rather than only plausibly so — the rendered block above is what
proves that, and it cannot be written without the data. The wording otherwise tracks the
Chinese defaults closely, including where those are loose, rather than quietly improving
on them.

### Documentation

Both language editions of the tool permission guide gain a `prompt_texts` row and a
section covering the built-in defaults, the two render sites, the fact that the title
travels in the interrupt metadata rather than the body, the bundled English set, partial
overrides, which strings are deliberately not templated, the template rules and why they
are enforced at construction; the source index gains the new module and
`ask_presentation.py`. Both sections also record that a remember is keyed on the tool
rather than on the path, and why, since that is what a host overriding those two fields
has to know. The section states plainly that `AGENT_PROMPT_LANGUAGE` does not
reach this text, because that is the first place an embedder looks for it. `S_08
security-engine` gains the new module and the matching invariant — but not a bumped file
count: that spec's `（14 文件）` and its module list still describe the pre-`20e35736`
layout, and asserting a corrected number for one module while the rest of the list is
stale would be false precision. Bringing that spec up to date belongs with the
restructure, not here.

**What scenarios were tested, and what were the verification results（Function, performance, reliability, etc.）**：

54 test items are added, in
`tests/unit_tests/harness/security/test_permission_prompt_texts.py`.

The defect behind this change is an absent capability, not a code path that
misbehaves. `openjiuwen.harness` gives a host no way to supply the wording a person
reads before approving a tool call, so there is no interface to call incorrectly and
no test on an unmodified tree can fail and demonstrate it. The tests below state the
contract of the new seam and show which part of the change each one needs. The
standing evidence for the defect is a census: `ask_presentation.py` holds twelve
lines containing CJK that render to a user, `tool_security_rail.py` holds four more
in `_build_always_allow_hint`, and a search of `openjiuwen/harness/security` for
`prompt_texts`, `PromptTexts`, `i18n`, `locale` or `language_pack` returns no file.

Against the merge base the file cannot be collected at all, because the module it
exercises does not exist there:

```
collected 0 items / 1 error
E   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'openjiuwen.harness.security.permission_engine.prompt_texts'
```

so nothing in it passes on `20e35736`. That is a weak claim on its own — it proves the
module is new, not that the seam works — so the file was also run against a base worktree
carrying `prompt_texts.py` and the `ToolPermissionHost.prompt_texts` field but with **both
render sites unmodified**. That run is `24 failed, 30 passed`, and the split is the point:

- **23 of the 24 failures** are exactly the tests that require the seam to reach a render
  site: all six `test_host_titles_replace_the_builtin_titles`, all five
  `test_host_finding_labels_replace_the_builtin_labels`, all three
  `test_host_texts_replace_the_remember_hint`, `test_host_summary_replaces_the_builtin_parenthetical`,
  `test_factory_carries_host_texts_into_the_rail`, all six
  `test_english_texts_render_without_any_chinese`, and
  `test_a_valid_partial_override_still_renders`. Every one of them fails with the built-in
  Chinese wording still in the output, which is the wording a host cannot replace today.
- **The 24th**, `test_default_path_body_scopes_the_remember_hint_to_the_tool`, fails there
  for the other reason: that tree still renders the uncorrected hint. It is the guard on
  the reworded default.
- **13 of the 30 passes** exercise `PermissionPromptTexts` alone — the per-field
  placeholder table, four placeholder mistakes each asserted to name its own field and the
  offending placeholder (including `{tool_name}` in a title, which is only a mistake
  because validation is per-field rather than against the union), four unrenderable format
  strings, a non-string field, both shipped sets passing their own validation, and the
  host wiring refusing to be built from an unrenderable template. They need the new module
  but not the wiring, which is why they pass in that tree and not on the real base.
- **2 more** assert the host's default is the built-in set and that the English set is not
  the default. They need the new field, not the wiring.
- **1 is the evidence for the rewording** and passes on both sides, since it touches no
  render site: `test_the_session_remember_is_keyed_on_the_bare_tool_name` derives the key
  for `write_file` on two different paths, asserts both are `"write_file"`, and asserts
  that the session entry stored from one matches the other.
- The remaining **14 are guards**, and pass on both sides deliberately:
  `test_default_shell_hint_names_the_subcommand`,
  `test_default_body_has_no_hint_for_a_compound_command`,
  `test_default_tool_summary_keeps_the_historical_parenthetical`, five
  `test_default_finding_labels_are_unchanged` and six `test_default_titles_are_unchanged`.
  They quote the shipped wording verbatim. They earn their place because "a host that
  injects nothing sees no change outside the corrected hint" is the compatibility promise
  this change makes, and
  without them that promise is checkable only in the one-off render sweep below and never
  again. They are also what fails if someone later edits a default template without
  meaning to alter what shipped deployments see — which, given that every default is now
  one line in one dataclass rather than a literal buried in a branch, is easier to do than
  it was.

The six category titles are asserted through `_build_interrupt_metadata` rather than the
body, because after the restructure the title never appears in the body at all.

The full unit suite was run on this change and on the base it sits on, serially, in
separate clean worktrees, with `--continue-on-collection-errors` so that a collection
abort cannot masquerade as a matched pair, and `openjiuwen.__file__` was asserted to
resolve inside the worktree under test before either result was believed. Failing and
erroring test **names** were compared, not counts: 138 names on each side, and the two
sets are identical — the same 134 tests fail and the same 4 modules fail to collect.
Passing count 16458 on the base and 16512 on this change, a difference of exactly the 54
items added here. The residual failures are pre-existing and unrelated: a local database
file the environment cannot open, which accounts for the largest group by far; optional
dependencies that are not installed (`pulsar`, and `prompt_toolkit` for the four
`agent_teams/cli` modules that fail to collect); and twelve tests that assume an event
loop already running in the main thread. No CI result is claimed.

`test_ask_presentation.py`, the test file #792 added for the render site this change
touches, passes unmodified — it asserts the built-in Chinese titles and summaries, so it
is itself a check that the defaults are unchanged.

`ruff check` against the repository's own `pyproject.toml` configuration reports the same
finding set on the security tree before and after, and none at all on either file this
change adds.

On performance: instrumenting `PermissionPromptTexts.__post_init__` counts exactly one
call across a whole `build_permission_interrupt_rail` — one still when the factory
supplies `resolve_workspace_dir`, because the `dataclasses.replace` it performs there
rebuilds the host around the existing instance rather than constructing a new one — and
zero across fifty `_build_message` plus `_build_interrupt_metadata` renders. The
rendering path itself gains one attribute lookup and a `str.format` per templated
segment in place of an inline literal; no measurable difference is claimed or expected.

> Two boxes are left unticked rather than ticked untruthfully.
> **Design**: this has had no Maintainer design review yet — the shape is described above
> and is meant to be argued with, in particular the decision that openjiuwen picks no
> language on the host's behalf, the choice of sixteen flat fields over a mapping for the
