title: fix(deps): declare aiosqlite, pypdf and pypdfium2 as runtime dependencies
body:
Paired: [GitHub #1796](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/agent-core/pull/1796) ↔ [GitCode !3105](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/agent-core/merge_requests/3105)

**What type of PR is this?**

/kind bug

**What does this PR do / why do we need it**:

三个在运行时被直接使用的包没有作为主依赖声明：

| 包 | 使用位置 | 现状 | 影响 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `aiosqlite` | `agent_teams/tools/database/engine.py`（`sqlite+aiosqlite://`） | 只在 `[sqlite]` extra | **默认配置直接报错**：`DatabaseConfig.db_type` 默认就是 `sqlite`（`"memory"` 也会被映射为 sqlite），只执行 `pip install openjiuwen` 时 `initialize_engine()` 抛 `ModuleNotFoundError: aiosqlite` |
| `pypdf` | `rsi/.../reporting/bibliography.py`（PDF 引用元数据） | **完全未声明**，uv.lock 中也没有 | 该路径被 `except ImportError` 吞掉，在标准安装中永远不生效；行内注释指向一个不存在的 `[paper_writing]` extra |
| `pypdfium2` | `rsi/.../paper_scoring/ingestion.py`（PDF 图像栅格化） | 未声明，仅经 `pdfplumber` 间接引入 | 目前能用，但依赖于 pdfplumber 的内部依赖；做法与本文件中 `opentelemetry-sdk` 的显式声明一致 |

修改：
- 三个包加入 `[project].dependencies`，下限取当前 uv.lock 中的版本（aiosqlite 0.22.1、pypdfium2 5.5.0）；pypdf 取 `>=6.0.0`
- 保留 `[sqlite]` extra，不破坏 `pip install openjiuwen[sqlite]` 的已有用法
- 修正 `bibliography.py` 中指向不存在 extra 的注释；import 仍保持惰性、失败时降级
- `uv.lock`：仅新增 pypdf 6.19.0 及上述声明，**已有的锁定版本没有任何变化**（+15 行，0 删除），`uv lock --check` 通过

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

（无对应 issue）

**Verification / 验证**:

1. aiosqlite：在 develop 上屏蔽 `aiosqlite` 的 import（`sys.modules["aiosqlite"] = None`，模拟未安装 `[sqlite]` extra 的环境），用默认 `DatabaseConfig()` 调用 `initialize_engine()`：
   ```
   default db_type = sqlite
   FAILED: ModuleNotFoundError import of aiosqlite halted; None in sys.modules
   ```
   我们在真实环境中也遇到过：按 pyproject 安装后运行论文流水线，因缺少 aiosqlite 中断。
2. `uv lock --check`：Resolved 312 packages，通过。
3. 与 !3026（同样修改 pyproject.toml / uv.lock）分别按两种顺序试合并，均无冲突。

**Self-checklist**:

+ - [ ] **设计**：未经 Maintainer 事先评审；是否把 aiosqlite 提为主依赖、还是改为在缺失时给出明确提示，欢迎指正
+ - [ ] **测试**：仅依赖声明变更，未新增 UT
+ - [x] **验证**：见上方验证结果
+ - [x] **接口**：不涉及对外接口变更
+ - [ ] **文档**：不涉及官网文档

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- 新增了第三方依赖（pypdf，BSD-3-Clause）；aiosqlite / pypdfium2 原本已在锁文件中
- 与 !3104（参考文献作者重复）相关：其端到端单测依赖 pypdf，本 PR 合入后该用例在 CI 中不再跳过
- 来源：CCF BDCI 2026「基于 JiuwenSwarm 的 Agent 科研论文自动生成」赛题，队伍「百慕大三角」在实际运行论文流水线时发现

title: feat(pipeline): add plan ownership columns and a one-time ownership backfill [Tier 3]
body:
Lands as part of #10285 (unit, operator decision 2026-10-10); do not merge separately.

## Summary
- `plans`, `plan_executions` and `backbone_runs` in `plans.db` gain `org_id`, `created_by` and `ownership_source` (TEXT NULL) and an `idx_<table>_org_id` index, added through `safe_add_column` in `PlanStore._ensure_table`.
- A once-only, versioned backfill (`SchemaManager` module `plan_store`, v1) assigns an org with `ownership_source='backfilled'` only when ownership is proven: every recorded scheduler user id belongs to exactly one, and the same, org in the user store. Every other row gets `ownership_source='unknown'` with a null org. Per-table counts are logged.
- New `aragora/tenancy/membership.py` resolves a user's org ids from the user store the server registers (falling back to the user store singleton).

## Stack
- Mission: decision workspace (Factory mission 20a3d6fd). Feature: `m1-plan-ownership-store` (stack position 03a of 03a/03b; split to stay under 800 LOC).
- Base: `mission/decision-ws/02-m1-org-scope-layer` (#10282). Review/merge bottom-up; this PR's diff is only this slice.
- Task source: `features.json` feature `m1-plan-ownership-store`; validation-contract assertions VAL-OWN-004, VAL-OWN-005, VAL-OWN-006. The org-scoped store methods and create/save ownership are in 03b.

## Changes
- `aragora/pipeline/plan_ownership.py` (new): column/index setup, the backfill migration and the counts log. Proof sources: execution `metadata_json.scheduled_by`; run intake `origin_metadata.scheduled_by` and run `metadata_json.scheduled_by`; for plans, the users of their linked executions and runs (`plan_id`, or the server-set `metadata.backbone_run_id`). Request-controlled plan metadata (`user_id`, `owner_id`, ...) never counts. Conflicting orgs, users without an org, and unknown users all become `unknown`. `created_by` is backfilled for executions and runs (their scheduler created them), never for plans. Only the three ownership columns of rows that have no ownership yet are written. All decisions are made before the first write, so if the user store cannot be consulted, nothing is written, no version is recorded, and the backfill is retried on the next start.
- `aragora/pipeline/plan_store.py`: `PlanStore(db_path, *, org_membership_resolver=None)`; `_ensure_table` adds the columns and runs the migration.
- `aragora/tenancy/membership.py` (new): `user_org_ids()`, `register_user_store()`, `MembershipLookupError` (store failures mean "could not check", not "no org").
- `aragora/server/unified_server.py`, `aragora/server/initialization.py`: register the server's user store (`nomic_dir/users.db`, or the PostgreSQL store after the upgrade) for membership lookups. Otherwise the backfill would consult the `get_user_store()` singleton, which points at a different `users.db`.
- `tests/pipeline/test_plan_ownership_backfill.py`: seeded pre-migration `plans.db` plus a real `UserStore`. Covers per-row outcomes and logged counts (VAL-OWN-005); a second run changes nothing and the version stays 1, even after membership changes; non-ownership columns are unchanged after the first run (VAL-OWN-006); fresh and legacy DB PRAGMA columns and indexes (VAL-OWN-004); and deferral while the user store is unavailable.
- `tests/tenancy/test_membership.py`: membership lookup cases.

## Type of Change
- [ ] Bug fix  - [x] New feature  - [ ] Breaking change  - [ ] Documentation  - [ ] Refactoring  - [ ] Test improvement

## Test Plan
```bash
PYTHONPATH=$PWD ARAGORA_USE_SECRETS_MANAGER=false python3 -m pytest tests/pipeline tests/tenancy -q -n 8
bash scripts/automation_pr_preflight.sh origin/mission/decision-ws/02-m1-org-scope-layer c450d6b822
```
At this commit: 2234 passed in tests/pipeline + tests/tenancy (the new tests failed with ImportError on the base). Preflight: ok. At the 03b tip, the mission gates gate-lint, gate-typecheck, gate-parity and gate-test (28334 pytest passed / 24 skipped; jest 4035 passed) all exit 0.
Live check on the mission backend: after the first plan-store request, `PRAGMA table_info` / `index_list` show the three columns and `idx_*_org_id` on all three tables. `_schema_versions` has `plan_store|1`. The log shows `plans.db ownership backfill: table=backbone_runs backfilled=0 unknown=4` (four service-authored runs with no scheduler). Their non-ownership columns and the 12 run events are byte-identical to a pre-start copy.

## Skipped validation
- Required CI checks do not run on PRs whose base is not `main`; the local gate scripts above mirror lint, typecheck, sdk-parity and Generate & Validate.

## Risks
- Tier 3 (persistence/migration semantics). No Tier 3 or Tier 4 path prefix is touched (`aragora/server/unified_server.py` and `initialization.py` are not on the Tier 4 list); no startup file is edited.
- Migration is additive (nullable columns, new indexes). The backfill writes only the new columns, and only on rows without ownership. Rows that cannot be proven become `unknown`, so later org-scoped reads hide them from every org (intended fail-closed behaviour).
- Schema setup still happens on first `PlanStore` construction (lazy `get_plan_store()`), not at process start.
- Queue cap: user-approved mission override, one stacked draft PR per feature.

## Operator settlement
Tier 3: requires model-quorum evidence at the exact head, then human risk settlement. This PR stays a draft; the mission never marks ready, merges, or settles.

## Retry context
First attempt.

## Related Issues
None.

## Fix carried forward
The head moved by fast-forward from `c450d6b822` to `b058f9431413db82ebbbdb29edf0c24869017d0d` (03a'). Nothing was amended, rebased or force-pushed.

- `b058f94314`: fix(pipeline), fix F1 from chain-fix-plan-m1-20261010 row 2 (a new commit; no earlier PR carried it). It fixes the Claude [P2] at `c450d6b822`: the one-time backfill marked legacy rows `unknown` for good, and recorded version 1, when it consulted an empty or unrelated user store. `backfill_ownership` now resolves every recorded user first. If at least one user is recorded and none resolves to any org, it raises `MembershipLookupError`: nothing is written, no version is recorded, and the backfill is retried on the next schema setup. A store that knows some recorded users still marks absent (for example deleted) users' rows `unknown`; the operator accepted that edge on 2026-10-10.
- New tests in `tests/pipeline/test_plan_ownership_backfill.py`: `test_backfill_is_deferred_while_the_store_places_no_recorded_user_in_an_org` fails at `c450d6b822` and passes at 03a'; `test_rows_without_a_recorded_user_do_not_defer_the_backfill` guards against deferring too often. Backfill and membership tests: 14 passed.
- Diff against the base: 7 files, +796/-1, 797 changed lines (limit 800). Branch 02 now contains a merge of `main`; the PR diff is still measured from `ed637a0d36`.
- Gates at 03a': lint, typecheck and parity pass; pytest 31700 passed with 1 known failure (gauntlet `test_no_stale_jobs`; its file passes alone, 32 passed); jest 4035 passed.
- Preserved dissent at the old head `c450d6b822`: `/Users/armand/.aragora-decision-mission/logs/review-claude-catchup-10284-land.json` (Claude CHANGES_REQUESTED, the P2 above plus P3s; OpenAI PASS).
- New exact-head pair from both families at 03a': `/Users/armand/.aragora-decision-mission/logs/review-claude-catchup-10284-land-b058f94314.json`.

title: feat(pipeline): persist plan ownership and add org-scoped PlanStore reads [Tier 3]
body:
## Summary
- `DecisionPlan` gains `org_id`, `created_by` and `ownership_source`. `PlanStore.create()` persists them with `ownership_source='created'`. `save()` assigns ownership only to a plan that has none, so an owned or `unknown` plan is never moved to another org. `create_execution_record()` and `create_run()` accept `org_id`/`created_by` the same way.
- New org-scoped store methods require a non-empty `org_id` (`ValueError` otherwise) and only match rows owned by that org, never null-org rows. Routes are unchanged; the next feature (`m1-plan-routes-isolation`) switches them over.

## Stack
- Mission: decision workspace (Factory mission 20a3d6fd). Feature: `m1-plan-ownership-store` (stack position 03b of 03a/03b; split to stay under 800 LOC).
- Base: `mission/decision-ws/03a-m1-plan-ownership-store` (#10284). Review/merge bottom-up; this PR's diff is only this slice.
- Task source: `features.json` feature `m1-plan-ownership-store` (expected behaviour: org-scoped queries never return null-org or other-org rows; the update-status-if-current variant requires a matching org).

## Changes
- `aragora/pipeline/plan_store.py`:
  - New methods: `get_for_org`, `list_for_org`, `count_for_org`, `update_status_for_org`, `update_status_if_current_for_org` (the org filter is part of the same atomic `UPDATE ... WHERE id = ? AND org_id = ? AND status IN (...)`), `get_execution_record_for_org`, `list_execution_records_for_org`, `get_run_for_org` and `list_runs_for_org`.
  - The unscoped methods keep their signatures and behaviour; they now share private query helpers with the scoped ones (`_filters`, `_key_filter`, `_update_status`).
  - `_row_to_plan` and `_row_to_execution_record` expose the ownership fields. Run updates (`_save_run`) never touch ownership.
- `aragora/pipeline/decision_plan/core.py`: three optional ownership fields with `None` defaults. `to_dict()` is unchanged, so API payloads do not change.
- `tests/pipeline/test_plan_store_org_scope.py`: create/save persistence, save never re-owning an owned or unknown plan, one-time assignment of an unassigned plan, execution/run ownership, scoped reads excluding other-org, null-org and `unknown` rows, status updates refused for the wrong org, and `ValueError` for a missing or blank org on every scoped method.

## Type of Change
- [ ] Bug fix  - [x] New feature  - [ ] Breaking change  - [ ] Documentation  - [ ] Refactoring  - [ ] Test improvement

## Test Plan
```bash
PYTHONPATH=$PWD ARAGORA_USE_SECRETS_MANAGER=false python3 -m pytest tests/pipeline tests/tenancy <18 other plan-store consumer test files: handlers/plans, governance runs, fastapi runs, debates bridge, prompt engine, post-debate coordinator, gold-path, meta-planner, unified server, initialization> -q -n 8
~/.aragora-decision-mission/tools/gate-lint.sh
~/.aragora-decision-mission/tools/gate-typecheck.sh
~/.aragora-decision-mission/tools/gate-parity.sh
GATE_TEST_LOG_DIR=~/.aragora-decision-mission/logs/gate-m1-plan-ownership-store ~/.aragora-decision-mission/tools/gate-test.sh
bash scripts/automation_pr_preflight.sh origin/mission/decision-ws/03a-m1-plan-ownership-store 4ef5d45ed6
```
2935 passed (plan-store consumers); GATE-LINT PASS; GATE-TYPECHECK PASS (mypy clean on touched files); GATE-PARITY PASS (11/11, openapi-drift pass); GATE-TEST PASS (28334 pytest passed / 24 skipped, jest 4035 passed); preflight: ok. The new tests failed with ImportError/AttributeError before the change.

## Skipped validation
- Required CI checks do not run on PRs whose base is not `main`; the local gate scripts above mirror lint, typecheck, sdk-parity and Generate & Validate.
- No live HTTP check: routes are intentionally unchanged in this PR.

title: Support Python linked against OpenSSL 4 in tls_versions handling
body:
## Problem

When Python is linked against **OpenSSL 4** (Ubuntu 26.10's Python 3.14.8, for example), the `ssl` module no longer defines the deprecated `PROTOCOL_TLSv1`, `PROTOCOL_TLSv1_1` or `PROTOCOL_TLSv1_2`. Three modules read these constants at import time:

- `mysql/connector/network.py`
- `mysql/connector/aio/network.py`
- `mysqlx/connection.py`

The `try` blocks around them only catch `ImportError`, so both packages fail to import:

```
>>> import mysql.connector
  File ".../mysql/connector/network.py", line 46, in <module>
    "TLSv1": ssl.PROTOCOL_TLSv1,
AttributeError: module 'ssl' has no attribute 'PROTOCOL_TLSv1'. Did you mean: 'PROTOCOL_TLS'?

>>> import mysqlx
  File ".../mysqlx/connection.py", line 42, in <module>
AttributeError: module 'ssl' has no attribute 'PROTOCOL_TLSv1_2'. Did you mean: 'PROTOCOL_TLS'?
```

This happens with the latest release (26.7.0) and with current `trunk`, and it affects every application, including ones that never pass `tls_versions`.

## Fix

When `tls_versions` is given, build the context from `ssl.PROTOCOL_TLS_CLIENT` and express the requested versions with `SSLContext.minimum_version` / `maximum_version`. This replaces the version-specific protocols and the deprecated `OP_NO_TLSv1*` options. Both APIs exist on every supported Python (3.10+, which requires OpenSSL 1.1.1 or newer), so the change also works on OpenSSL 1.1.1 and 3.x.

The change is backwards compatible:

- **Negotiation is unchanged.** `["TLSv1.2"]` is still capped at TLS 1.2. A list that includes `TLSv1.3` stays uncapped, as it was with `PROTOCOL_TLS`.
- **System policy is kept.** The version range is only ever narrowed: the minimum is raised and the maximum lowered, never the reverse. A stricter system-wide setting, such as OpenSSL `MinProtocol = TLSv1.3` (which Debian/Ubuntu and Fedora/RHEL Pythons honor), still applies, as it did with the version-specific protocols. Setting `minimum_version` unconditionally would silently allow TLS 1.2 on such systems.
- **Certificate verification is unchanged.** The classic connectors already set `check_hostname` and `verify_mode` explicitly after creating the context. The X DevAPI path explicitly keeps `CERT_NONE` unless `VERIFY_IDENTITY` or `ssl-ca` is used, which matches what the old `PROTOCOL_TLSv1_2`/`PROTOCOL_TLS` contexts did by default.
- **The `TLSv1`/`TLSv1.1` map entries are removed.** They were unreachable, because option validation already rejects both versions as `UNACCEPTABLE_TLS_VERSIONS`.
- **Fewer warnings.** The deprecated `PROTOCOL_TLSv1_2`, `PROTOCOL_TLS` and `OP_NO_*` usages, and the DeprecationWarnings they emit on 3.10+, are gone from these paths.

## Tests

The PR adds:

- `test_tls_versions_negotiated` in `test_connection.py`, `test_aio_connection.py` and `test_mysqlx_connection.py`. Each test connects with every `tls_versions` combination and asserts the **exact** negotiated version from `Ssl_version` / `Mysqlx_ssl_version`. The existing `test_get_connection_with_tls_version` / `test_get_session_with_tls_version` tests are skipped on servers newer than 8.0.27, so `tls_versions` currently has no coverage against current servers.
- `test_build_ssl_context_tls_versions` and `test_build_ssl_context_keeps_stricter_default` in `test_network.py`. These check the context's version range, and that a stricter default minimum is not lowered.

### Upstream suite

Modules `network`, `connection`, `aio_connection` and `mysqlx_connection` were run with `unittests.py` against a bootstrapped **MySQL Server 26.7.0**, using the pure-Python implementation:

| Code | Python / OpenSSL | Result |
|---|---|---|
| trunk | 3.10.22 / OpenSSL 3.5.9 | baseline |
| trunk + new tests | 3.10.22 / OpenSSL 3.5.9 | the new negotiation tests **pass**, so they encode the existing behavior |
| this PR | 3.10.22 / OpenSSL 3.5.9 | identical to baseline per test, plus the 5 new tests passing |
| trunk | 3.14.8 / OpenSSL 4.0.3 | `AttributeError` on import (all modules) |
| this PR | 3.14.8 / OpenSSL 4.0.3 | classic and asyncio: identical per test to OpenSSL 3.5.9. mysqlx: all TLS tests identical, but 20 other tests hit the separate Python 3.14 zstd issue described below |

To confirm the mysqlx result, I reran it with a local workaround for that zstd issue (a fresh decompressor per frame). The results then match OpenSSL 3.5.9 except `test_compression_sizes`, which fails on the compressing side of the same zstd issue (`5174: Invalid compressed frame`).

A mutation check confirmed the new tests catch both kinds of regression:

- **TLSv1.2 cap removed:** all four negotiation tests fail. Against the server, `["TLSv1.2"]` negotiates TLSv1.3.
- **Unconditional `minimum_version`:** `test_build_ssl_context_keeps_stricter_default` fails.

### TLS behavior comparison

To compare trunk and this PR directly, I ran their TLS setup code (`build_ssl_context` + `switch_to_ssl` for sync and asyncio, `SocketStream.set_ssl` for mysqlx) through real handshakes against local TLS servers: 1.2-only, 1.3-only, 1.2–1.3, and 1.2–1.3 with an untrusted certificate. The cases cover every combination of `tls_versions` (none, 1.2, 1.3, both), `ssl_verify_cert`, `ssl_verify_identity` / X DevAPI `ssl-mode`, `ssl_ca`, hostname match or mismatch, and `tls_ciphersuites`. That is 1,360 cases per run, and each records the negotiated version and cipher, or the failure reason:

| Comparison | Differences |
|---|---|
| trunk vs this PR, Python 3.10.22 + OpenSSL 3.5.9 | **0** (exact outcome text, including error reasons) |
| trunk vs this PR, Python 3.14.8 + OpenSSL 3.5.9 | **0** (exact outcome text) |
| this PR, OpenSSL 3.5.9 vs OpenSSL 4.0.3, same Python 3.14.8 | **0** (outcome, version and cipher) |
| this PR under `MinProtocol = TLSv1.3`, vs trunk's results restricted to TLS 1.3 | **0** (never negotiates TLS 1.2) |

## Unrelated pre-existing issues found while testing

These appear on unmodified trunk too, and are not changed here:

- The certificates in `tests/data/ssl` have **expired**, so `test_connect_with_unix_socket` (sync and asyncio) and mysqlx's `test_ssl_connection` error with `CERTIFICATE_EXPIRED` on every configuration.
- On **Python 3.14**, `mysqlx/protocol.py` uses the stdlib `compression.zstd`. Its `ZstdDecompressor` handles a single frame, and the compressor reuses one instance across messages, so X Protocol `zstd_stream` compression raises `EOFError: Already at the end of a Zstandard frame.` on the second compressed message.
- On **Python 3.14**, the asyncio `MySQLSocket.switch_to_ssl()` calls `StreamWriter.start_tls()` without `server_hostname`. With `ssl_verify_identity=True` it fails with `ValueError: check_hostname requires server_hostname`, whether or not `tls_versions` is given. It works on 3.10, which uses the connector's own workaround. I tested only 3.10 and 3.14, but 3.11+ presumably fails the same way, since that is where the native `start_tls()` is used.

## OCA

I have signed the Oracle Contributor Agreement (Mike Fara), and it is pending approval.

title: paper-drive: standardise gears to 48DP/32DP PA20 inch cutters
body:
## Scope

Stacked on [#1272](https://github.com/pedropaulovc/harmonic-analyzer/pull/1272), with base `exp/gear-std-inch-train`. This is the paper-drive production cutover to the user's selected **12:120 reducer at 48DP PA20**, sharing the cone-drive cutter set, plus a **12T 32DP PA20 feed pinion and true purchased rack**. The PR remains draft until its final stacked head and the required gates are green. No merge is authorized.

## What changes

- Reducer: 120T disc cut with the stock #2/reference-55 form and integral 12T knob-shaft pinion cut with #8/reference-12. Disc pitch diameter is 63.5 mm; the specified blank OD is 64.54 mm. The smaller pinion requires the stepped, integral shaft/core and revised arm/plate centre geometry, running fits and positive locating registration.
- Feed: finite stock #8/reference-12 form at 32DP PA20; cutter translation and the turned blank/span controls are explicit source-derived manufacturing dimensions, not a generating profile-shift claim.
- Rack: SDP/SI **A1B12-Y324**, brass, true 32DP PA20, 3/16-inch square, cut to **269.64 mm** on the existing backer. There is no alternative form-cutter-made rack. Its gear-critical receiving/assembly acceptance uses shop-achievable micrometer/wire and indicator resolution; it is not a supplier accuracy claim.
- Chain: **68 links of ANSI #25**, 6.35 mm pitch, 431.8 mm developed length; sprockets remain **12:24**. The 10:1 reducer ratio is retained. Mean platen feed is **1.496183501272 mm per crank revolution**, 6.25% below the original DP30-feed value of 1.595929068024 mm/rev.
- Gear sheets carry model-linked tooth-space radial-indicator runout to the actual running-bore datum, span/root inspection and the finite stock-form manufacturing controls. These form-cut pairs are labelled **stock-form coverage**, not contact ratio; true-contact-ratio gates remain for conjugate pairs.
- Arm/plate location is carried by two stock **McMaster 93600A189, Ø2 m6 dowels**, not clearance screws or countersink-centering credit. The two oval clamp screws retain their role and installed cut-to-fit geometry; procurement uses verified **91790A199, #8-32 × 1 inch**, quantity two, so conservative published-standard bounds leave enough stock to remove the factory tip before the final cut. Commodity hardware clearance uses vendor/published-standard bounds, not new incoming-metrology procedures.
- Retired front collar-pin plumbing is removed; the replacement integral shaft, drive collar, nut/thrust-ring and cup interfaces are included. Registry/BOM/dimensional facts and the affected drawing contracts are updated.

## Functional and native gates

The stock-form gate requires supported union coverage ≥1.2 throughout the actual centre/fit stack, no phase gap, paid tip/corner handover, positive backlash/clearance, and a correlated introduced platen-error result using one physical paper zero. Exact native cutter form/normals are an explicit conditional model premise, not a received manufacturing certificate. The purchased standard-manufactured PA20 rack's straight, smooth working flanks are a named premise at the same conditional level, backed by a drawn 0.8-mm same-side wire secant with X/Y uncertainty ±0.005/±0.002 mm and a 20°±2° angle acceptance, plus the existing whole-material controls. Neither premise is a supplier-accuracy claim; crest/birth and actual first-carrier/stack guards remain. Numerical enclosure refusal is not reported as a physical failure.

Introduced error is separated from inherited T12/T24 chain polygonal action/link-pitch variation. The original `error_budget.yaml` ±8° term is operator crank-index stop repeatability, not a deterministic gear/rack-TE specification; the former 0.0709301808-mm peak-to-peak gate is removed. Introduced feed error is converted through each design's own mean feed to crank-equivalent degrees and phase per harmonic 1..20, then composed with the signed cone-drive phase matrix before the existing physical readout/paid-bound evaluation. A named **deterministic paper-feed term** must pass the full existing budget without borrowing the operator-index allocation or RSS treatment as random scatter. The same main DP38-reducer/DP30-feed term is reported; any increase must fit the genuine remaining budget margin.

A pure-math, actual 68-link pinned cycle checks purchased-chain fit. The inherited continuous-arc native chain remains a labelled **visual representation**, not a roller-seating certificate. No native-chain rewrite or interference exemption is included.

The **inherited standard ANSI #25 positive-engagement/no-tooth-skip model premise** is explicit for this hand-cranked, very-low-speed instrument: T12 wrap must be ≥120°, sag must be no greater than main at matched states, and the strands must not reverse. Reported comparisons give about 171° wrap and 18.2/20.9 mm sag versus main's 24.1/25.5 mm; real pose/clearance/clock effects still enter the introduced-error model. The deliberately slack historical chain is not judged against a power-transmission 2%-span recommendation. A new 3D linked-roller/tooth-skip proof is outside this PR's scope; this premise does not set the introduced chain-clock term to zero.

## Validation status

Latest pushed WIP: **d54a21286c10c28f811fbe0ccad2ed5ff2672633**, stacked on #1272's **02c54f7c543706567a0b224a58ffaba50733dfc7** with eleven paper-drive commits. It includes the completed native/layout repairs, the pure hardware-catalogue boundary cut and the canonical shared equation-curve helper. Backup refs preserve the earlier heads. The final offline-green parent lease is still pending.

A clean detached checkout of this exact pushed SHA, with exact submodules and a locked environment, passes `check:undefined_names` (2 tests, 0.51 s) and all 47 fresh-process paper-drive recipe imports (26 build + 21 drawing, 144.22 s, zero ImportError). Main's prior narrow farm run on 4e9a4df11 produced 40 successful leaves and eight failures; this checkpoint contains their source repairs and the cup/nut layout fixes. New native results are pending. Assembly and drawing entrypoints read source-bound frozen values without executing the heavy rack proof. The genuine rack and full physical-function packets are still pending; unfinished Math and positive calibration registration are excluded from this native checkpoint.

Current-head root pytest, changed-hunk Ruff, the remaining relevant `check:*` gates and exact-sheet machinist review remain outstanding. The final farm scope is changed paper-drive parts, paper-drive and drive-train assemblies, both soundness gates, every affected paper-drive drawing and `verify:kinematics`. Farm commands use default parallelism and omit `-n`. The historical October 8 runs and narrow diagnostics do not establish final acceptance.

## Known release follow-on

`web/` intentionally stays pinned to the historical v39 release model. Its bindings, regex and seals are unchanged here. The web owner must migrate that model at the next release through the separate native export/census process; this PR does not certify the old web model against the new gear geometry.

title: refactor!: remove the deprecated import shims (TOM-1457, 4d)
body:
**HOLD: merge only after v0.12.0 is tagged; ships as v0.13.0.**

## Summary

This is 4d of TOM-1457, the contract step of ADR-0010. TOM-1618, 4a (TOM-1449) and 4b (TOM-1451) kept each moved import path for one minor version. Each was a shim with a DeprecationWarning. This PR removes them.

- Each old path now raises `ImportError`. The message names the replacement and says "removed in quantbox 0.13.0 (TOM-1457)".
- One list owns the removals: `quantbox._removed.REMOVED` (old path -> replacement). It replaces `quantbox._deprecation`. There is one helper module, not two: `moved` is gone.
- A removed MODULE is a tombstone file that calls `removed(__name__)` at import.
- A removed NAME in a live module is refused by `__getattr__ = removed_names(__name__)`. It raises `ImportError`, not `AttributeError`, because `from m import x` turns an `AttributeError` into a generic message and drops the replacement. Any other missing name is still an `AttributeError`.
- `quantbox.analysis` is one tombstone module now. Its four submodules are deleted. Python imports the parent first, so `import quantbox.analysis.dsr` and the other three get the parent's message, which names all three homes.
- Scope (Tom, 2026-10-09): import shims only. These STAY, with their warnings: `risk.tranches` / `tranches: N`, `execution.shift_signal`, `_pipeline_annualize`, `run()` without `context`, `strategy.carver_trend.v1`, the validate FutureWarning, and the `sweep(..., shift_signal=)` alias.

### Every removed path and its replacement

| removed path | replacement | from |
|---|---|---|
| `quantbox.analysis` (and `.dsr`, `.hac`, `.gates`, `.parameter_grid`) | `quantbox.inference`, `quantbox.gates`, `quantbox.sweep` | TOM-1618 |
| `quantbox.metrics.newey_west_tstat` | `quantbox.inference.newey_west_tstat` | TOM-1618 |
| `quantbox.metrics.newey_west_auto_lags` | `quantbox.inference.newey_west_auto_lags` | TOM-1618 |
| `quantbox.metrics.hac_ols` | `quantbox.inference.hac_ols` | TOM-1618 |
| `quantbox.metrics.require_finite` | `quantbox.inference.require_finite` | TOM-1618 |
| `quantbox.plugins.strategies._universe` | `quantbox.universe` | 4a |
| `quantbox.plugins.datasources._utils.MarketCapProvider` | `quantbox.market_cap.MarketCapProvider` | 4a |
| `quantbox.plugins.datasources._utils.CMCMarketCapProvider` | `quantbox.market_cap.MarketCapProvider` | 4a |
| `quantbox.plugins.datasources._utils.load_pit_market_cap` | `quantbox.market_cap.load_pit_market_cap` | 4a |
| `quantbox.plugins.datasources.local_file_data._load_pinned_dataset` | `quantbox.dataset.load_pinned_dataset` | 4a |
| `quantbox.plugins.backtesting.rsims_engine` | `quantbox.engine.rsims_sim` | 4b |
| `quantbox.simulation.models` | `quantbox.montecarlo.models` (or `from quantbox.simulation import ...`) | 4b |
| `quantbox.simulation.engine` | `quantbox.montecarlo.engine` (same) | 4b |
| `quantbox.simulation.correlation` | `quantbox.montecarlo.correlation` (same) | 4b |
| `quantbox.simulation.stress_testing` | `quantbox.montecarlo.stress_testing` (same) | 4b |

How I found them: `rg` for `_deprecation` / `moved(` callers and for every module `__getattr__` in `src/`, plus the bodies of #265 and #266. #267, #268, #270-#272 added no shim. The other `__getattr__`s (`plugins.backtesting`, `plugins.datasources`, `broker`, `pipeline`, `publisher`) are lazy loaders or the ADR-0005 refusal, not shims.

### Silent back-compat re-exports NOT removed (no warning, not added by 4a/4b)

Tom to decide whether any of these goes in a later minor. Each still returns the same object with no warning:

- `quantbox.execution_schedule` re-exports `quantbox.engine.schedule`.
- `quantbox.plugins.backtesting.metrics` re-exports `quantbox.metrics` (robo-lab imports it).
- `quantbox.plugins.datasources.DuckDBParquetData` is an alias of `LocalFileDataPlugin`.
- `quantbox.validate` re-exports `ValidationFinding`, `UNKNOWN_PLUGIN`, `check_plugin_params` (4b moved them).
- `plugins.datasources._utils` re-exports `is_transient`, `retry_transient`, `with_retry` from `quantbox.retry`.

### Other changes

- Module walkers: `tests/test_base_install.py`, `tests/test_without_vectorbt.py` and `scripts/check_no_vectorbt.sh` read `REMOVED` to tell a tombstone from a broken module. The base-install walk and the client smoke also fail if they meet no tombstone.
- import-linter contracts: `quantbox._deprecation` -> `quantbox._removed`; the four `analysis.*` submodules are dropped from every list. `scripts/layer_map.py` reads the contracts and needed no change.
- ADR-0009 decision 6 and ADR-0010 decision 7 each get a one-paragraph "Amended by TOM-1457" note.
- Docstrings in `universe`, `market_cap`, `dataset`, `montecarlo`, `engine.rsims_sim`, `simulation` no longer say "deprecation shim".

### Cross-repo: no active consumer imports a removed path

`git grep -E` for every removed path (module paths, `from ... import` forms, and the four bare Newey-West names) on each ref:

| repo | ref | sha | hits that import a removed path |
|---|---|---|---|
| quantbox-lab | #125 head `chore/p4-4c-quantbox-v012` | `51d1f9d` | none at the lab root. Two frozen lines, exempt (below). |
| quantbox-datasets | #88 head `chore/p4-4c-quantbox-v012` | `0cabb77` | none |
| quantbox-datasets | `origin/main` (NOT yet on #88) | `d067783` | **`src/quantbox_datasets/crypto_spot_daily_plugin.py:20` imports `plugins.strategies._universe`.** See Merge Danger. |
| robo | `origin/dev` | `8a10358` | none |
| robo-lab | `origin/main` | `6c86240` | none (`qi.newey_west_*` is `quantbox.inference as qi`) |
| quantbox-live | `origin/main` | `cce5839` | none |

quantbox-lab hits, each checked:

- `research/hypertrend-overlays/configs/dated/2026-06-17-H06-...-strategy.py:127` imports `plugins.strategies._universe`. That line pins quantbox `5cfc2d4` in its own `pyproject.toml` / `uv.lock`. Frozen, exempt.
- `research/replication-tsmom-mop2012/diag_replication.py:131,175` import `local_file_data._load_pinned_dataset`. That line pins quantbox `1aa5fda`. Frozen, exempt.
- `research/carver_volatten_carry/diag_inference_parity.py:27` imports `quantbox.analysis` only in an `except ImportError` fallback after `quantbox.inference`, which exists. It never runs on 0.13.0.
- `scripts/lint/check_framework_usage.py`, `tests/test_framework_usage_guard.py`, findings and READMEs: strings and prose, not imports.

## Design

Premise: a stale import must fail at once and say what to write. A removal that leaves `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'quantbox.analysis'` costs each consumer a search.

Candidates:

- Delete the files. The error does not name the replacement.
- A `sys.meta_path` finder in `quantbox/__init__` that refuses the removed module names. No files, no walker changes. But core would gain a dynamic-import mechanism, against ADR-0010's "one lazy door" rule.
- A tombstone file per removed module plus a `__getattr__` per live module, both reading one table.

Chosen: the third. It is explicit, `rg`-able, and costs three walker edits. The table is the single statement of what was removed. The test file restates it independently, so dropping an entry or leaving a shim fails a test.

## Evidence

- **New test** `tests/test_removed_paths.py` (49 tests): every module path and every `from parent import leaf` form raises `ImportError` with "removed in quantbox 0.13.0 (TOM-1457)" and the replacement; six old `quantbox.analysis.*` import statements each name inference, gates and sweep; every removed name raises from both `from m import x` and `getattr`; unknown names on live modules stay `AttributeError` and `hasattr` is False; every replacement resolves; the table equals the test's own list.
- **Red check:** I copied base `metrics.py` (the shim) over head and ran `-k metrics`: 4 failed, "DID NOT RAISE ImportError". I restored the file and checked it by md5 (`a4bc033a…`, the same before and after).
- **Removed tests:** the DeprecationWarning tests of the old paths, in `test_inference_shims.py` (renamed `test_one_name_one_meaning.py`; its three non-shim tests are unchanged), `test_public_surface.py`, `test_layer_edges.py`, `test_metrics_research_stats.py`, and one `quantbox.analysis` snippet in `test_without_vectorbt.py`. This is the stated requirement change of TOM-1457; no other assertion changed.
- **Full suite.** Base is `git archive 7280d3b` run on the head venv with its own `src` first on `PYTHONPATH`.
  - Base: 3741 passed, 34 skipped, 2 failed (3777 collected). Both failures are the archive: `git ls-files` and the git sha need a checkout.
  - Head: 3703 passed, 32 skipped, **1 failed** (3736 collected: 90 shim tests removed, 49 added).
  - The head failure is `tests/test_new_line.py::test_acceptance_new_line_then_uv_sync_then_one_run`. It scaffolds a line on quantbox-datasets **main**, and `quantbox run` dies in `PluginRegistry.discover()`: `quantbox_datasets/crypto_spot_daily_plugin.py` -> `quantbox.plugins.strategies._universe` -> "removed in quantbox 0.13.0 (TOM-1457): use quantbox.universe". That is datasets main `d067783`; #88 fixes it. This is the test doing its job, and the reason for the merge order below.
- `pytest -m "pipeline_smoke or canonical_reproduction"`: 42 passed, 20 skipped at both.
- `bash scripts/check_no_vectorbt.sh`: PASS at both. Base: 193 modules, 186 imported (70 core). Head: 189 modules, 175 imported (66 core), "7 removed paths refuse". The 4 fewer modules are the deleted `analysis` submodules; the 7 tombstones are not imported.
- `lint-imports`: 5 contracts kept, 0 broken (247 files). `ruff check` clean, `ruff format --check` 428 files formatted.
- **Cookbook configs, base vs head** (`/home/tom/workspace/tmp/p4w4/4d/snapshot.py`, the #265/#266 method, both trees run at the same time): 24 configs. 6 ran to artifacts at both (both canonical reproductions, `run_backtest_crypto_trend`, `run_backtest_overlay_reversal_derisk`, `run_fund_selection`, `run_synthetic_backtest`). Every parquet and every `metrics.json` value is identical. The 18 differing leaves are provenance only: the run-id second, the git sha (the base tree is an archive, so it records none) and one `NaN != NaN` (`annual_volatility`). The other configs fail or skip the same way at both (missing data, keys or accounts; live mode).
- `cz changelog --dry-run --unreleased-version v0.13.0` renders the seven footers under `### BREAKING CHANGE`. `cz bump --get-next` from 0.11.0 says 0.12.0: a minor bump, so the next one after the v0.12.0 tag is v0.13.0.

## Merge Danger

- **HOLD.** This must not reach `dev` before v0.12.0 is tagged, or v0.12.0 would ship the removal.
- **Merge order: quantbox-datasets #88 first.** quantbox-datasets main still imports `quantbox.plugins.strategies._universe`. Its entry point loads in `PluginRegistry.discover()`, so on 0.13.0 every `quantbox run` in an env that installs datasets@main fails at start, not only the datasets plugin. The lab root tracks `quantbox-datasets@main`, and `quantbox new line` scaffolds on it. #88 removes the import. Do not release v0.13.0 until #88 is on datasets main.
- **Breaking for any consumer still on an old path.** The table above says no active consumer is. Frozen lab lines pin old SHAs and are not affected.
- **`hasattr(quantbox.metrics, "hac_ols")` now raises `ImportError`** instead of returning True. The same holds for the other seven removed names. `hasattr` only swallows `AttributeError`. Nothing in the searched repos does this.
- **CHANGELOG.** commitizen writes it at `/ship` from the commits. The commit carries seven `BREAKING CHANGE:` footers, one per removed path. `cz changelog --dry-run` renders them as a `### BREAKING CHANGE` section with all seven lines. Squash-merge keeps them: this PR has one commit, and the repo's squash message is `COMMIT_MESSAGES`. If the PR gains more commits, the footers stay in the squash body. `cz bump --get-next` gives a minor bump (`major_version_zero = true`), so after v0.12.0 it is v0.13.0.

Related to TOM-1457

title: fix(utils): functional group validation and NFS mount detection
body:
## PR Title

fix(utils): functional group validation and NFS mount detection

## PR Description

### Description of the Solution

Fixes functional group validation to support OS/version-agnostic naming in the utils domain and corrects NFS mount detection in the iso_creation role. The validation now uses regex pattern matching instead of fixed lists, accepting both bare form (`slurm_node_x86_64`) and OS/version-qualified form (`slurm_node_rhel_10_0_x86_64`). NFS mount detection now checks if the mounted export actually covers the requested directory using prefix matching, preventing false positives when unrelated exports from the same server are mounted.

### Related Issue
Fixes https://github.com/dell/omnia/issues/4849

- Fixes OMNIA-ISSUE-866 - collect_pxe.yml missing login_compiler_node_x86_64 functional group
- Fixes OMNIA-ISSUE-867 - iso_creation role fails when NFS is mounted at a child path of the export
- Fixes OMNIA-ISSUE-818 - utils/setup_env.sh missing --help and --venv options
- Fixes OMNIA-ISSUE-819 - ImportError: get_collect_output_path not exported (regression test)

### Changes

#### Functional Group Validation (`src/utils/`)
- Updated `collect_pxe_config_validator.py` to use regex pattern matching for functional groups
- Updated `collect_pxe_config.json` schema to use `patternProperties` instead of fixed properties
- Updated `validate_collect_config` role to use regex match/reject logic
- Updated `log_collector/prepare.yml` and `vars/main.yml` to aggregate all matching keys per role+arch bucket
- Updated input documentation and example to reflect OS/version-agnostic naming

#### NFS Mount Detection (`src/utils/roles/iso_creation/`)
- Added filtering logic to check if mounted export actually covers requested directory
- Uses prefix matching: `requested_dir.startswith(mounted_export)`
- Prevents false positives when unrelated/child exports from same server are mounted

#### Test Infrastructure (`test/utils/`)
- Added unit test suite (59 tests) covering functional group validation, NFS mount detection, library exports, and CLI options
- Updated test support functions (`utils_func.py`, `common_vars.py`) to use regex-based validation
- Updated test data generator to support OS/version-agnostic naming
- Fixed `setup_env.sh` CLI options (--venv, --force, --debug, --help)
- Updated documentation to reflect new naming convention

### Files Changed

|------|-------------|-------------|

| `src/utils/input/collect_pxe.yml` | Modified | Updated example with OS/version-qualified group names |

| `test/utils/datasets/README.md` | Modified | Updated test data documentation |

| `test/utils/library/functions/utils_func.py` | Modified | Updated validation function to use regex |

| `test/utils/setup_env.sh` | Modified | Added --venv, --force, --debug, --help options |

### Testing

- **Unit Tests**: All 59 unit tests pass (functional group validation, NFS mount detection, library exports, CLI options)
- **Pylint**: Score 9.18/10 (above 8.0 threshold)
- **Manual Test**: Ran install_os playbook in build mode with unrelated NFS exports mounted - confirmed auto-mount works correctly when requested export is not covered by existing mounts

No breaking changes. The fix is backward compatible - both bare form (`slurm_node_x86_64`) and OS/version-qualified form (`slurm_node_rhel_10_0_x86_64`) are accepted. Existing configurations using bare form continue to work unchanged.

title: fix(api): 재생성이 마지막 턴의 스탯을 되돌려 새 응답으로 다시 판정한다
body:
## 무엇

재생성이 원 턴의 스탯 효과를 그대로 둔 채 응답만 바꿔 새 응답과 스탯이 어긋나던 것을 고친다. 마지막 턴을 재생성하면 그 턴의 스탯을 되돌리고 새 응답으로 **스탯 판정만** 다시 한다. (B7 — ENG-5·16·17·18)

| 조건 | 동작 |
|---|---|
| 기록 있음 · 기록에 엔딩 없음 · 방이 엔딩 전 · 기록 `turn_number == turn_count` | 기록의 반영 전 값을 메모리에서 판정 입력으로 → 새 응답으로 스탯 판정 → 되돌림 + 새 값을 응답과 한 커밋에. 새 기록 = 새 변화(턴 시작 값 대비). 카운터 한 번. `statChange` 는 지금 DB 값과 달라진 스탯만 |
| 기록에 엔딩 / 기록 없음 / 엔딩 뒤 방 / 메시지 삭제로 앞 응답이 마지막(기록 턴 < turn_count) | 지금 동작 — 스탯 그대로, 새 기록은 옛 기록 이어받기(턴 번호 포함) |
| 재판정 끝내 실패 | 되돌리지 않음 — 스탯·`statChange` 0, 응답은 교체·`done` 정상, 새 기록은 옛 기록 이어받기 |
| 엔딩 판정 | 재생성에서 하지 않는다 |
| 생성 프롬프트(상황 노트) | 지금처럼 현재 DB 값으로 조립(되돌림은 판정 뒤 쓰기 구간) |
| 기록의 반영 전 값이 빔(`None`) | 그 스탯의 시작값(`initial_value`)으로 되돌려 판정에 참여 — `load_room_stats` 가 행 없는 스탯을 시작값으로 채우는 것과 같은 뜻(사용자 결정, 리뷰 F-3). 지금은 보내기가 빈 값을 남기지 않아 닿지 않는 경로 |

**재시도 분류** — `is_retryable_judgment_failure`(`llm/client.py`, 예외의 원인 `__cause__` 를 보는 순수 함수). 재생성 재판정만 부르고, 보내기·수정의 스탯 판정은 그대로 1회.

| 실패 | 재판정 호출 |
|---|---|
| Gemini `APIError` 5xx(504 제외) | 2 |
| 타임아웃 아닌 `httpx.TransportError`(연결 거부·끊김) | 2 |
| 파싱 실패(원인 없는 정확한 `LLMClientError`) | 2 |
| `httpx` 타임아웃·`TimeoutError`·504 | 1 |
| 429 · 안전 차단 · 그 밖의 4xx · 원인 있는 그 밖 실패 | 1 |

## 운영 원가 증가 (병합 = 배포 승인 질문)

- 재판정 조건(기록 있음·엔딩 없음·마지막 턴)을 채운 재생성 1회당 **스탯 판정 1회 추가**, 일시 오류·파싱 실패로 재시도하면 **1회 더**. 판정 모델 `GEMINI_STAT_JUDGMENT_MODEL_NAME`. 사용자 차감은 늘지 않는다(클로버는 턴 단위).
- 운영 "스탯 판정 실패" 비율 사전 측정은 하지 않았다(이 작업은 운영 접근 금지). 실패한 호출마다 경고 한 줄(`… 재생성 스탯 판정 실패 — 한 번 다시 부른다` / `… — 옛 응답의 스탯 효과를 그대로 둔다`)이 남아 배포 뒤 같은 방법으로 셀 수 있다.
- 최악 꼬리: 타임아웃은 재시도하지 않으므로 늘지 않는다. 재시도는 실패 종류로 가른다 — 파싱 실패는 응답을 다 받은 뒤에 오므로 재시도가 판정 한 번만큼(최대 판정 타임아웃) 더할 수 있다.

## 기대값 변화

- `llm_request_ledger.json`: `regenerate-story-shortcut` 한 경우에 `chat_stat_judgment` 호출 1건이 더해짐(그 경우만 마지막 턴 기록이 있다). 생성 요청 항목은 그대로. 다른 경우·다른 기대값 파일 diff 0, `_EXPECTED_CALL_SITES` 같음.
- 재생성 뒤 판정 호출을 단언하던 테스트 3개(미디어 칸 재판정 둘, 상황 노트 재생성 하나)를 새 동작으로 고침 — 상황 노트 테스트는 이제 "재생성 프롬프트는 되돌리기 전 지금 값으로 조립"까지 본다.
- openapi(재생성 라우트 docstring)·`api-types` 재생성.

## 검증

- 빨강 먼저(5-4 행렬 전 줄): 구현 전 14 실패(재판정 호출 0) + 분류 함수 ImportError, 부재·불변 단언 9개는 초록 — 신호는 뮤테이션으로.
- 분류 단위 테스트 16경우는 SDK 경계만 가짜로 둔 실제 `GeminiLLMClient.generate_structured` 가 올린 예외로. 라우트 테스트도 스탯 판정은 실제 Gemini 구현을 지난다.
- 뮤테이션 15개(조건 셋 각각 제거, 타임아웃 재시도, 5xx 비재시도, 원인 없음 검사 제거, 504 줄 제거, 재시도 두 번, 끝내 실패 때 되돌림, 판정 입력을 DB 값으로(카운터 이중 적용), 재생성 엔딩 판정, 공통 경로 재시도, T2 이어받기 지우기, 턴 번호 비이어받기, 쓰기·이벤트를 턴 시작 값 대비로) — **15/15 예측 일치, 생존 0**.
- mypy·ruff·citations 통과, 전체 스위트(`-n 4`, 커버리지 98%): 1차 5739 passed·3 failed(재생성 뒤 판정 호출 수를 단언하던 옛 기대 3개 → 고침), 2차 5741 passed·2 failed — 실패 둘(`test_chat_turn_settlement` 끊김 환급, `test_novelize_chain` 시간 상한)은 1차에선 통과했고 단독 재실행도 통과, 실행 시 load average 30 안팎의 시간 의존 플레이크로 판단(이 변경이 닿지 않는 경로). CI 결과로 확인.

## 문서와 다른 점

- 행렬의 "5xx 뒤 성공 → `llm_calls` 에 두 호출": 응답 없이 끝난 5xx·연결 오류는 공급자 구현이 사용량을 남기지 않으므로 기록에는 성공한 호출 하나만 남는다(파싱 실패는 응답을 받았으므로 둘). 테스트가 이것을 단언한다.
- 뮤테이션 "T2 이어받기 지우기"는 문서가 기대한 "B7 이전 재생성 기록 줄만"이 아니라, 이어받기를 단언하는 줄 전부(끝내 실패·비재시도·엔딩 기록·삭제 뒤 재생성)에서 빨개진다 — 이어받기가 그 줄들의 기대 동작이라서다.

## 배포·되돌리기

마이그레이션 없음. 관측 하루. 되돌리기는 revert(재시도 분류 함수도 함께 빠진다). 이미 바뀐 스탯 값은 되돌리지 않는다(사용자 데이터) — 이 코드가 쓴 재생성 기록은 그 응답에 귀속된 새 효과라 revert 뒤 재생성이 이어받아도 맞다.

title: Bring the docs and badges up to date
body:
Docs-only refresh after #210, #212 and #213. No code changes except one hard-coded string in the benchmark renderer.

**Type check and Bandit rules (#213).** CONTRIBUTING (workflow line plus a "What CI enforces" entry), AGENTS, TESTING, the PR template and USAGE's verification block now name `make typecheck`; SECURITY.md lists Ruff's `S` rules and mypy next to pip-audit. The Typed badge reads `type-checked | mypy` and links to mypy.

**How `sage` is found (#210).** README, INSTALLATION, USAGE (the `SAGEMATH_MCP_SAGE_BINARY` row and the ModuleNotFoundError tip), SUPPORT, CLAUDE.md and `packaging/conda/README.md` said only "on PATH" / "`sage -python`". They now say: PATH first, then beside the server's own Python (an unactivated conda env or venv), and a console-script `sage` runs the worker on the interpreter it names. The conda-forge install instructions themselves stay in #211, which waits for 0.9.4.

**10.9 → 10.10, where it states the present.** The paper's SageMath citation (the paper body already reports 10.10 figures) and the doctest-corpus test's baseline comment (now the 2026-10-05 10.10 sweep). Dated measurements, security findings ("confirmed against 10.9") and changelog history are left as they are.

**Benchmark.** `write_benchmark_stats.py` hard-coded "SageMath 10.9"; it now reads `sageVersion` from the result (the 2026-09-07 result records 10.9), so re-rendering reproduces `benchmark-stats.md` byte for byte. The 24 gold answers were recomputed on 10.10 and are unchanged; `cases.json` says so. A fresh 10.10 benchmark run is not in this PR — today's attempt was invalid and was discarded.

**New badges.** CodeQL, Scheduled audit and Fuzz (live workflow status); Python from PyPI's classifiers (3.12 | 3.13, replacing the static "3.12+"); "Sage doctests 98.88% accepted" linking to `doctest-corpus-stats.md`; Glama's score for the existing listing. Each has a test in `tests/test_readme_badges.py` (workflow badges must name a workflow that runs on main; classifiers must equal the CI matrix; the doctest figure must equal the last sweep), and each test was checked to fail when its claim is broken.

body:
Paired: [GitHub #6179](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/jiuwenswarm/pull/6179) ↔ [GitCode !6823](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/jiuwenswarm/merge_requests/6823)

---

## 变更概述

将鸿蒙 PC（HarmonyOS，OfficeClaw relay 场景）平台适配线完整合入，覆盖：运行时平台层、部署安装链、DeepResearch 子进程环境、专家团（预设团队）端到端修复。

**核心设计原则：全部改动条件触发**——非 OHOS 运行时（Linux/Windows/macOS、企业版、桌面/编辑器等场景）不进入任何新逻辑分支，行为与合入前一致。

## 分组明细

### A. 平台运行时层（B1/B3）
- 新增 `jiuwenswarm/common/platform.py`：`is_ohos_runtime()`（HNP 运行时三级判定：`JIUWENSWARM_RUNTIME_PLATFORM` / `JIUWENCLAW_RUNTIME_PLATFORM` / `sys.platform`）与 `sandbox_supported()`（OHOS 无 jiuwenbox 宿主能力）
- 5 处业务文件 OHOS 守卫移植：沙箱自动拉起跳过（`agent_ws_server.py`）、cron 调度直连（`cron_runtime.py`）等平台分支

### B. 部署与安装链（B2a/B2b/B6/B6b/B6c/B6c-2/B6c-3）
- 鸿蒙部署资产带入与模块路径适配（vendor 双布局：venv site-packages 与 `vendor/jiuwenswarm` 两份拷贝）
- 安装链加固：venv 健壮创建（用户盘失败兜底）、`PIP_CONSTRAINT` 全局约束、fastmcp 血统钉版、新设备克隆链薄弱点修复、PowerShell Set-Content 编码损伤修复
- 离线依赖：mathml2omml-as 离线 wheel 上库；pandas 双平台 wheel 走 LFS（10MiB 平台钩子）

### C. 进程内客户端与子进程环境（B5/B7-11/B7-12/B7-15）
- B5：`InProcessAgentServerClient` 请求改经 dispatch 分发表路由（与外部 WS 客户端行为一致），不再直连 agent pool
- B7-12：DeepResearch 子进程环境透传 `PYTHONPATH`（仅非 venv 解释器分支，venv 分支不变）
- B7-15：OHOS 分支从 `__file__` 推导 vendor 根并追加到子进程 `PYTHONPATH`（`is_ohos_runtime()` 门控 + try/except 兜底）——修复 DeepResearch runner MaaS 凭据分支 `ModuleNotFoundError: jiuwenswarm`（设备 no terminal marker 事故根因）
- B7-11：rust 依赖诊断措辞消毒——`RUSTC=NOT_FOUND` 横幅明确标注 informational / not required at runtime，防止 LLM 代理误读为致命故障

### D. 专家团端到端修复（B7-19/B7-20，本 PR 主要 bugfix）

修复 8/24 HTTP/SSE 重构（bc03bab4b）与 relay 协议演进叠加导致的四个回归，恢复预设团队全链路：

| # | 缺口 | 修复 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | relay `sync_agents_configs` 的 teams 载荷（预置团队拓扑）从未被消费，租户 spec.config 无 `modes.team`，团队入口报 "no team template configured"（用户侧 OA.05000090） | `validate_sync_payload` 提取可选 teams（`_validate_teams_payload` 结构校验，破损降级不阻断 agent sync）；`_build_sync_modes_team` / `_inject_sync_modes_team` 注入 `spec.config.modes.team`（None 不动 / 非空整表替换 / 空清除，与 relay 声明语义对齐） |
| 2 | 团队成员模型客户端于 chat 流期间构建（无 overlay 绑定窗口），tip `default_headers`（Authorization）无人合并，成员调用 401（APIG.0303） | `team_helpers._hydrate_team_model_auth`：绑定窗口读取 tip `default_headers`，镜像单专家 `_build_model_from_entry` 合并规则（Authorization 覆盖、其余 setdefault）合入 `models.defaults[*].custom_headers`；凭据仅内存态，团队模板快照不落盘 |
| 3 | relay 8/7 协议演进（91e1fa6c0）将团队成员引用 `agent_key` 改为 `agent_id`，`_build_modes_team_mapping` 只认 `agent_key` | `_front_team_member_agent_ref`：`agent_key` 优先、`agent_id` 回退，输出归一为 `agent_key`（web 编辑器旧协议行为不变） |
| 4 | 自动绑定写入的 session 元数据根（handler 阶段 env ns 未绑定 → `agent_default`）与 team 流读取根（deep adapter 绑定 ns → `agent_agentteam`）错位，绑定身份读不到 → `has_binding=False` 永远回落 `templates[0]`（选 A 团队跑了 B 团队） | `_ensure_auto_team_binding_for_chat` 外层绑定租户 env ns（`TenantAgentPool.extract_ids`），元数据读写落到 team 流实际读取的根 |

## 与团队代码的冲突解决（2 处）

1. `agents/harness/common/tools/cron/cron_runtime.py`：团队已将 `run_now` 重构为 `context`/`_with_route` 路由模式并新增 `toggle_job`/`preview_job`。本 PR 将 OHOS 直连调度器守卫嵌入新结构（置于 `_with_route` 之前，保持原"路由前守卫"位置）；route push/reset 清理由 `_with_route` 统一承接（与原 `token/try/finally` 语义等价）
2. `server/agent_ws_server.py`：团队新增的企业版沙箱跳过守卫与本 PR 的 OHOS 平台守卫互补，两者均保留（企业级 → OHOS/不支持平台 → 非 Linux/Windows 三级判定）

另 4 个双改文件（`common/config.py`、`team_helpers.py`、`deepresearch/tools.py`、`app_agentserver.py`）自动合并，已逐项语义核对：团队新增（TTSE 配置、workflow 持久化、错误码归一、报告 HTML 写盘）与本 PR 改动（团队映射、认证水合、PYTHONPATH 注入）互不重叠。

## 兼容性说明

- relay 不带 teams 载荷 / 无 tip 凭据 / `params.team_name` 未命中模板与绑定 → 全部走原有路径（生成式建团等旧行为完整保留）
- `agent_key` 协议输入（web 团队编辑器）解析结果与旧代码逐字节等价（下游 `_require_non_empty_string` 本就做 strip）
- 非 officeclaw 渠道的 ns 绑定为 (default, default)，与不绑定等价
- 对外接口无破坏性变更：sync 载荷新增可选 `teams` 字段，旧客户端不发送则行为不变
- Windows 桌面 relay（officeclaw 渠道）与 OHOS 共享同一 bug，获得同样修复；本地 / 编辑器 / CLI 场景不受影响

## 验证结果

- **设备集成实测**（HarmonyOS PC 真机）：专家团全链路跑通——选择预设团队（备考教练）→ 正确加载对应模板成员（`team config loaded: oc_team_preset-exam-prep`，修复前为 software-dev）→ 团队成员认证正常 → 团队对话执行。sidecar 日志证据链：`sync teams payload consumed: templates=6` / `bound requested team` / `hydrated tip default_headers` / `team config loaded`
- **合并后回归**：9 个涉改文件 `py_compile` 全过；teams 载荷六态校验（结构破损降级 / 空 team[] 清除语义等）与映射协议回归（relay `agent_id` / 旧 `agent_key` / 幽灵引用报错降级）本地链路测试全过
- **历史实测**：B6 系列安装链（全新装）、B7-12/B7-15（DeepResearch 子进程 import 修复）均已在设备验证中确认

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- 前向兼容：不破坏——全部改动条件触发，非触发场景行为与合入前一致
- 三方库：新增 mathml2omml-as 离线 wheel 上库；pandas 双平台 wheel 改走 LFS（仅存储方式，版本不变）；fastmcp 血统钉版（`PIP_CONSTRAINT`）

title: test: the baseline generator reproduces the baseline it made
body:
The scoring-baseline generator no longer reproduced the baseline it made (found while refreshing country data in #432).

## What was wrong, measured

`tests/generate_baseline_testclient.py`:
- posted "UK" and "USA", while `tests/baseline_scores.json` holds "United Kingdom" and "United States" -- the names `/evaluate` accepts. Against the current app it skipped 12 of 42 cases and would have overwritten the baseline with the 30 it could compute;
- could not start as documented: `import conftest` failed with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tests._database_url'` unless the repository root was on `sys.path`;
- wrote to `tests/baseline_scores.json` relative to the current directory.

`tests/generate_baseline.py` (the live-server variant) had the same names and relative path.

## What changes

- Both generators use the names the baseline holds and write next to themselves (`Path(__file__).parent`); the TestClient generator puts the repository root on `sys.path` and does all its work in `main()`, so importing it has no side effects; `generate_baseline.py`'s docstring states it needs a live server at localhost:8000.
- `tests/test_baseline_generator_matches_the_baseline.py`: the generator's COUNTRIES x PRESETS are exactly the (country, preset) pairs in the baseline, and each preset's payload equals the stored one -- read by importing the generator, not copied.

## Verification

- Run from outside the repository, the generator wrote 42 cases, skipped 0, and `git diff --exit-code tests/baseline_scores.json` reported no difference -- it reproduces the committed baseline byte for byte.
- Putting "UK" back fails both new tests; the new file and `test_scoring_baseline.py`: 45 passed.
- No absolute paths; CI's backend-tests job collects `tests/` (only `test_api.py` is excluded), so the new file runs.

Only `tests/` changes. Written by Sonnet; verified independently.

title: refactor(P5): move the review verdicts and the security gate out of pipeline.py (#776)
body:
This change moves two parts of `ComponentPipeline` out of `kstrl/pipeline.py` into two new modules. The bodies do not change. It is slice P5 of the plan for #776.

## Moves

- `kstrl/pipeline_verdicts.py` (583 lines) holds the class `ReviewVerdicts` (parent `AttemptRecorder`) with 9 members: `_COVERAGE_UNVERIFIED`, `_budget_refusal`, `_claim_blocking`, `_claim_failure`, `_coverage_failure`, `_divergence_failure`, `_has_unconfirmed_claim`, `_review_did_not_run`, `_review_failure`. It also holds `ReviewPhaseResult`, `_gate_failure_count` and `_produced_a_reading`.
- `kstrl/pipeline_security.py` (279 lines) holds the class `SecurityGate` (parents `ReviewVerdicts`, `UsageLedger`) with 3 members: `_phase_security`, `_security_budget_branch`, `_security_failure`. It also holds `SecurityPhaseResult`.
- `ComponentPipeline` has the parents `KnowledgePhase`, `SecurityGate`, `MechanicalChecks` and `Transitions`. `kstrl/pipeline.py` has 1915 lines (2710 before). It keeps more than 800 lines because slice P6 moves the merge phase and the PR phase. Also, the four members above a complexity gate stay: `_phase_review`, `_phase_verify`, `process_result` and `repoll_merge_pending`.
- No name is re-exported. The readers in `kstrl/pipeline.py` import from the new modules.

## Checks on the head 125a6159 (base commit 788473ec, which is `origin/main`)

title: [Ascend] Vendor the PTODSL SIMT allreduce helpers
body:
PTOAS commit [f5eff3ee2](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/commit/f5eff3ee249697f6157088f649c6434fcc9d7c5b) ("refactor(ptodsl): remove the SIMT allreduce helpers") removed `ptodsl/_allreduce.py` with the expectation that TileLang would vendor the implementation. However, `tilelang/contrib/ptodsl/simt.py` still imported the removed module, so compiling any operator with the TileLang PTO target against the latest CANN Weekly package (09-30) fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'ptodsl._allreduce'`.

This PR vendors the removed module as `tilelang/contrib/ptodsl/allreduce.py`, merging contrib.ptodsl's integer-signedness compatibility, previously applied as monkey patches from `simt.py`, directly into the reducer tables and the dtype dispatch, restoring the PTO target. It also adds PTO reduce primitive tests ported from the pto-main branch: reducer-v2 int32 runtime coverage, the bfloat16 allreduce rejection, and the bitwise collective rejection parametrized over the ascend and pto targets.

Validation (Ascend 950 host):

title: Add --evaluator-args flag forwarding kwargs to evaluate() via signature sniffing
body:
Fixes #474

Implements the approach @codelion outlined in the issue: a `--evaluator-args` CLI flag that accepts a JSON object and forwards the parsed kwargs to the user's `evaluate()` function, using `inspect.signature` so that existing single-argument evaluators keep working unchanged.

@ai-nikolai — this implements the approach discussed in #474. I left a comment on the issue before starting; if you had work in flight since July, happy to coordinate or step back in favor of your PR.

## What it does

- **New config field**: `evaluator.evaluator_args: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]` (`openevolve/config.py`), settable from YAML or the CLI. It round-trips through `Config.to_dict()` → `EvaluatorConfig(**d["evaluator"])`, so it propagates to process-pool workers with no extra serialization work.
- **CLI flag**: `--evaluator-args '{"weight": 2.0, "label": "exp-1"}'` (`openevolve/cli.py`). Invalid JSON or a non-object value exits with code 1 and an actionable message. Only kwarg key names are logged, never values (they may contain secrets).
- **Signature sniffing** (`Evaluator._resolve_evaluator_kwargs`, `openevolve/evaluator.py`):
  - `evaluate()` accepts `**kwargs` → all configured kwargs are forwarded.
  - `evaluate()` has named parameters covering the configured keys → forwarded on every call via `functools.partial` at the `run_in_executor` call site.
  - `evaluate()` cannot accept a configured key → **startup error** naming the offending keys and the actual signature (this also catches a kwarg colliding with the positional program path, e.g. `evaluator_args={"program_path": ...}`), instead of failing on every evaluation.
  - No `evaluator_args` configured (the common single-`program_path` case) → behavior is completely unchanged.
- **Docs**: new README section "Passing Arguments to Your Evaluator" (CLI + YAML), noting this replaces the env-var workaround and that custom top-level `config.yaml` keys are silently dropped by the config parser (as @codelion pointed out in the issue).

## Out of scope (as discussed in #474)

Cascade `evaluate_stage1/2/3` functions are not touched — the issue covers `evaluate()` only. Positional-argument forwarding is also not included.

## Testing (red → green)

New `tests/test_evaluator_args.py` (15 tests, `unittest`, fully offline):

- kwargs forwarding to named-param and `**kwargs` evaluators
- backward compat: single-param evaluator with no/empty args unchanged
- startup validation: unsupported key, `program_path` collision, actual signature included in the error message
- YAML load of `evaluator.evaluator_args` and worker config dict round-trip
- `parse_evaluator_args`: valid / empty / invalid-JSON / non-object
- end-to-end CLI subprocess: invalid `--evaluator-args` JSON → exit code 1

Red on `main` (tests added first, source unchanged):

```
ImportError: cannot import name 'parse_evaluator_args' from 'openevolve.cli'
FAILED (errors=1)
```

Green after the change:

```
$ OPENAI_API_KEY=test-key-for-unit-tests python -m unittest tests.test_evaluator_args -v
...
Ran 15 tests in 0.543s
OK
```

Full suite:

```
$ OPENAI_API_KEY=test-key-for-unit-tests python -m unittest discover tests
Ran 620 tests in 72.887s
OK
```

Format: `black --line-length 100` / `isort --profile black --line-length 100` applied to all changed files (isort also removed two pre-existing duplicate imports in `evaluator.py`).

title: Extract OVERSTOCK_CATEGORIES into a runpy-safe data module
body:
## Problem

Airflow's `listing_dags.py` failed to import entirely (`Broken DAG`):

```
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'common.spiders'; 'common' is not a package
  File "overstock_listing_spider.py", line 10, in <module>
    from common.spiders.base_listing_spider import BaseListingSpider
```

`dags/listing_category_groups._module_values()` loads a spider's category inventory with `runpy.run_path()`. For `overstock_listing` (PR #29) that path was pointed at `overstock_listing_spider.py` — a real spider that imports `common.spiders`. At DAG-parse time the top-level `common` resolves to the DAG package's `dags/common.py` (a module, **not** a package), so `common.spiders` is unreachable and the whole `listing_dags` DagBag fails.

Every other listing DAG sources its inventory from a pure-data `*_categories.py` module, which is `runpy`-safe.

## Fix

- Extract `OVERSTOCK_CATEGORIES` into `common/spiders/overstock_categories.py` (pure data, no scrapy import).
- Express it in the base-class contract's **grouped mapping** shape — `{department: {leaf: {url, subcategory}}}` — matching the other `*_categories.py` modules, and keeping the per-row `subcategory` as a rich leaf field.
- The spider resolves its target via `category_entry()`; its tests iterate with `iter_categories()`.
- The DAG points at the data module.

## Verification

- `DagBag("/opt/airflow/dags")` in the running `airflow-scheduler`: **import errors: []**, `overstock_listing` loaded, 20 tasks across 9 task groups.
- `airflow dags list-import-errors` → "No data found"; `airflow dags list` shows `overstock_listing`.
- `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_overstock_listing_spider.py` → 3 passed.

title: fix(feishu): bind card action symbols in the ImportError fallback
body:
Paired: [GitHub #942](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/jiuwenswarm/pull/942) ↔ [GitCode !3939](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/jiuwenswarm/merge_requests/3939)

## What

The `except ImportError` fallback in `feishu_connect.py` leaves two names unbound, which turns a missing optional SDK into a module-level `NameError`.

## Why it breaks

`feishu_connect` guards its `lark_oapi` imports and exposes `FEISHU_AVAILABLE` so the gateway can run without the Feishu SDK — the same pattern the Telegram, Discord and DingTalk channels use. But the fallback only rebinds two of the imported names:

```python
try:
    import lark_oapi as lark
    from lark_oapi.api.im.v1 import (...)
    from lark_oapi.event.callback.model.p2_card_action_trigger import (
        P2CardActionTrigger,
        P2CardActionTriggerResponse,
    )
    FEISHU_AVAILABLE = True
except ImportError:
    FEISHU_AVAILABLE = False
    lark = None
    Emoji = None          # P2CardActionTrigger / ...Response left unbound
```

Both missing names are used as annotations on `_on_card_action_trigger_sync` (line 2772):

```python
def _on_card_action_trigger_sync(self, data: P2CardActionTrigger) -> P2CardActionTriggerResponse:
```

This module has no `from __future__ import annotations`, so those annotations are evaluated eagerly while the `FeishuChannel` class body executes. The import fails before the module finishes loading:

```
NameError: name 'P2CardActionTrigger' is not defined
```

So the degraded path never runs, and the `if not FEISHU_AVAILABLE:` guard at line 344 is unreachable — `FEISHU_AVAILABLE = False` is assigned, but the module raises a few hundred lines later.

Importing the four channel modules with their SDKs absent shows Feishu is the only one affected:

| channel | result |
| --- | --- |
| **feishu** | ❌ `NameError: name 'P2CardActionTrigger' is not defined` |
| telegram | ✅ degrades |
| discord | ✅ degrades |
| dingtalk | ✅ degrades |

Also worth noting: `lark-oapi>=1.5.3` is declared with an open upper bound, and `lark_oapi.event.callback.model.p2_card_action_trigger` is a deep internal path. If a future release moves it, the `ImportError` is real — and users would hit a confusing `NameError` instead of the intended "Feishu SDK unavailable" degradation.

## Changes

Two lines in the fallback branch:

```python
except ImportError:
    FEISHU_AVAILABLE = False
    lark = None
    Emoji = None
    P2CardActionTrigger = None
    P2CardActionTriggerResponse = None
```

`None` matches how `lark` and `Emoji` are already handled, and the two names are only referenced under `FEISHU_AVAILABLE` guards or inside handlers that never run without the SDK. Checked the rest of the `try` block: no other imported symbol is referenced at module scope, so these two are the only gaps.

An alternative fix would be `from __future__ import annotations` to defer annotation evaluation — but `P2CardActionTriggerResponse` is also *called* at runtime (line 2862), so it needs a real binding either way. The two-line fallback is the smaller, more consistent change.

## Tests

`tests/unit_tests/channel/test_feishu_import_fallback.py` reloads the module with `lark_oapi` masked out of `sys.modules` and asserts the degraded contract: import succeeds, `FEISHU_AVAILABLE is False`, both symbols are `None`, and `FeishuConfig` / `FeishuChannel` stay usable. The fixture restores `sys.modules` afterwards so the rest of the suite is unaffected.

Both tests fail on `develop` and pass with this change:

```bash
uv run pytest tests/unit_tests/channel/test_feishu_import_fallback.py
# without the fix: 2 failed
# with the fix:    2 passed
```

## How to test

```bash
uv run pytest tests/unit_tests/channel/
```

Verified locally on Python 3.12. No behaviour change when `lark_oapi` is installed — the `try` branch is untouched.

title: fix(rail): classify a tool result stating ok: false as a failed call
body:
Paired: [GitHub #7692](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/jiuwenswarm/pull/7692) ↔ [GitCode !7709](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/jiuwenswarm/merge_requests/7709)

**What type of PR is this?**

/kind bug

**What does this PR do / why do we need it**:

`_infer_tool_result_error` in
`jiuwenswarm/agents/harness/common/rails/stream_event_rail.py` decides whether a
finished tool call failed. `_emit_tool_result` calls it and writes `success`,
`status` and `is_error` onto the `tool_result` event from its verdict. The web
timeline, the TUI tool lines and the debug trace all read those fields.

The function reads `success`, `is_error` / `isError`, `status` and the four
exit-code spellings. It then reads the same keys again inside `data`,
`raw_output`, `rawOutput` and `result`. It does not read `ok`.

So a tool that states its outcome as `{"ok": false, "error": "<reason>"}` was
classified as nothing. The function returned `None`, `_emit_tool_result` set no
`success`, `status` or `is_error` field, and every reader of that event showed
the call as one that worked.

`ok` with `error` beside it is a shape this repository produces:

- `sdd_advance`, the stage-advance tool that `RailStateMachineBase` registers as
  a `LocalFunction` (`agents/harness/code/rails/sdd/common/rail_state_machine.py`
  lines 176-179), returns `{"ok": False, "error": ...}` from `_handle_advance` at
  lines 264, 294, 300, 309, 325 and 345. That return value is the tool result the
  model reads. `server/runtime/agent_adapter/interface_code.py` mounts the rail
  through `_build_design_rail` (line 1797) when `modes.code.sdd.enabled` is true.
- `channels/cli/render.py` lines 225-230 build `{"ok": true, "content": ...}` or
  `{"ok": false, "error": ...}` as the CLI JSON output.
- The shipped skill scripts under `resources/agent/workspace/skills/` print the
  same shape. `huawei-cloud-maas-setup/SKILL.md` line 89 instructs the model to
  read `{"ok": false, "stage": "...", "error": "..."}` as a failed step.

Production code already reads `ok` as an outcome.
`server/runtime/skill/skill_manager.py` lines 2947 and 4292 map
`not out.get("ok")` onto `{"success": False, ...}`. `server/agent_ws_server.py`
lines 7025 and 7030 answer `command.add_dir` with
`ok=bool(persist.get("ok", False))`.

Two tool-result error detectors in this repository also disagreed on the same
input. For `{"ok": False, "error": "invalid stage: 'design'"}`,
`ToolResultErrorDetector.has_error` in
`agents/harness/common/rails/execution_guard/circuit_breaker_rail.py` returns
`True` through its `error` key (line 251), while `_infer_tool_result_error`
returned `None`. `CircuitBreakerRail` counted the refusal as a failure of that
tool. The event stream showed the same call as a success.

The fix adds the `ok` read to `_infer_tool_result_error`, after the exit-code
loop and before the nested walk. It changes seven lines, three of them a comment.

The change adds no reason string. `_infer_tool_result_error` returns
`bool | None`, so it has nowhere to carry one. The reason already reaches every
reader inside the emitted `raw_output` or `result` field, which the test asserts.

Two notes for reviewers:

- #1746 addresses the same symptom, a call that did not succeed rendering as a
  success, by a different mechanism. It adds the `[PERMISSION_DENIED]` and
  `[PERMISSION_REJECTED]` markers to the string branch of
  `_infer_tool_result_error`, which covers a denied call that returns bare text.
  This PR adds the `ok` key to the dict branch, which covers a tool that returns
  a structured outcome. Neither covers the other's input, and the overlap is the
  symptom alone. At merge time the two are independent in either order: the
  backend hunk of #1746 applies cleanly on top of this branch, because the two
  edit different branches of the function. A maintainer can take either first.
- `ToolResultErrorDetector` does not read `ok` either. It catches the common
  `{"ok": false, "error": ...}` shape through its `error` key, so a bare
  `{"ok": false}` is the only case it still misses. Aligning the two detectors
  would change what trips the circuit breaker, so this PR leaves it alone.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Fixes #7691

**What scenarios were tested, and what were the verification results（Function, performance, reliability, etc.）**：

All runs used a rootless container on Python 3.11.

1. Reproduction on unmodified `develop` (`f0a69728c9`). A harness drove
   `JiuSwarmStreamEventRail.after_tool_call` with the real refusal that
   `_handle_advance({"stage": "design"})` returns, and printed the emitted
   `tool_result` payload:

   ```
   [1] sdd_advance returned: {"ok": false, "error": "invalid stage: 'design'"}
   [2] emitted tool_result payload: {"tool_name": "sdd_advance", "tool_call_id": "tc-1",
       "result": "{'ok': False, 'error': \"invalid stage: 'design'\"}",
       "raw_output": {"ok": false, "error": "invalid stage: 'design'"}}
   [3] verdict fields on the event: {}
   [4] a reader asking payload.get('success'): None
   ```

   The event carries no `success`, no `status` and no `is_error`. A reader cannot
   tell this refused call from a call that worked.

2. The same harness on this branch:

   ```
   [1] sdd_advance returned: {"ok": false, "error": "invalid stage: 'design'"}
   [2] emitted tool_result payload: {"tool_name": "sdd_advance", "tool_call_id": "tc-1",
       "result": "{'ok': False, 'error': \"invalid stage: 'design'\"}",
       "raw_output": {"ok": false, "error": "invalid stage: 'design'"},
       "success": false, "status": "error", "is_error": true}
   [3] verdict fields on the event: {"success": false, "status": "error", "is_error": true}
   [4] a reader asking payload.get('success'): False
   ```

3. The two detectors, on unmodified `develop`, for the same refusal:

   ```
   ToolResultErrorDetector.has_error: True
   _infer_tool_result_error: None
   ```

4. No regression. `tests/unit_tests/agentserver/test_stream_event_rail_ok_convention.py`
   holds 38 tests. On unmodified `develop`, 11 fail and 27 pass. On this branch,
   all 38 pass. The 27 that pass on both are the no-regression evidence. They
   pin every pre-existing convention (`success`, `is_error`, `isError`, `status`,
   the exit-code keys, the nested containers, the string forms), and they pin
   precedence: for `{"success": True, "ok": False}`, `{"success": False,
   "ok": True}`, `{"is_error": True, "ok": True}`, `{"status": "error",
   "ok": True}`, `{"exit_code": 1, "ok": True}` and `{"exit_code": 0,
   "ok": False}`, the key the function already read decides, and the verdict is
   the one it gave before.

5. Test suites run on this branch, all green:

   ```
   tests/unit_tests/agentserver/test_stream_event_rail_*.py
   tests/unit_tests/agentserver/rails/
     => 216 passed in 24.08s
   ```

   Readers of the `tool_result` event, run as a wider sweep:

   ```
   tests/unit_tests/channels/cli/  tests/unit_tests/e2a/  tests/unit_tests/process_cli/
   tests/unit_tests/agentserver/test_debug_trace.py
   tests/unit_tests/agentserver/test_agentserver_acp.py
   tests/unit_tests/agentserver/test_history_tool_result_restore.py
   tests/unit_tests/agentserver/rails/
     => 2 failed, 1218 passed, 1 skipped in 58.62s
   ```

   Both failures are
   `process_cli/test_machine_entry.py::test_bootstrap_import_failure_emits_safe_terminal_result`
   (`ImportError` and `RuntimeError`). Both fail the same way on unmodified
   `develop` and do not touch this code path.

**Self-checklist**:（**Please check carefully,and mark an x in the [] brackets. We will review your completion status.**）
