title: B70: launch.sh checks the GraspGen-X host the runtime dials; no test port released before use
body:
## B70 — launch.sh checks the GraspGen-X host the runtime dials; no test port is released before use

Backlog B70 (follow-ups of B41 and B64, from `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` Known limitations).

### (a) `launch.sh --graspgenx local|external` dials the runtime's host

`load_demo_config` applies `CASCADE_GRASPGENX_HOST` last over `grasp.graspgenx.host` (B41), so the runtime dials that host — but the launcher's `external` check probed `127.0.0.1:$CASCADE_GRASPGENX_PORT`, and `check_graspgenx.py` (run for `local` and `external`) never got the host. A server on the other machine failed the launch; a loopback server the runtime would never use passed it.

Now, for `local` / `external` with the variable set (non-empty), `scripts/launch.sh`:
- parses it with the runtime's own rule (`cascade.config.env_host`, in a bash-3.2-safe heredoc); a malformed value stops the launch with the runtime's message (`[launch] ERROR: CASCADE_GRASPGENX_HOST='gx10:5556' is not a host ...`) **before anything is dialled or started**;
- prints `[launch] GraspGen-X endpoint: HOST:PORT (CASCADE_GRASPGENX_HOST); the checks below dial it`;
- probes that host (`external`; the failure names it: `no GraspGen-X server on HOST:PORT`), passes `--host HOST` to `check_graspgenx.py` (both modes) and shows `graspgenx: HOST:PORT (mode)` in the banner.

Unset or empty, and in the `stub` / `none` modes whatever the variable says: argv and output are **byte-identical** (golden-pinned; the tests pass on 38f6d08). `scripts/demo_proof.py` is unchanged (its own `int()` read of `CASCADE_BRIDGE_PORT` stays). No new `CASCADE_*` variable is read in `src/cascade` (the launcher reads the already-classified `CASCADE_GRASPGENX_HOST`).

### (b) No test port is bound, released, then used

`tests/test_hug_backend.py::_free_port` (also imported by `tests/test_hug_runtime.py`) and the `tests/test_openclaw_gateway.py` fixture bound port 0 and released it before their dead endpoint / fake gateway used it.
- Dead HUG servers (both files) are now `held_dead_port()` (B64 helper; short client timeouts unchanged: 500 ms / 200 ms).
- The OpenClaw gateway double must be TOLD its port (`gateway run --port P`), so it cannot bind 0 itself. New `tests/owned_server.handed_over_port()` binds the port and hands that very socket to the server process (`take_handed_port`, SCM_RIGHTS over a private Unix socket, stdlib only); the server refuses a socket bound to another port, and the fixture drops its copy so the port closes with the server. Until taken it is a held dead port. The "unowned port" test now `claim()`s the held socket to be the foreign listener.
- An AST guard (`test_no_test_module_takes_a_port_by_binding_zero_and_releasing_it`) fails on any new bind-0 / read number / release (`close()` or end of `with`) / use-number-after site in `tests/`. It lists the 4 older sites it still finds, with reasons (3 conversation-provider tests whose code under test bind-checks the port itself, so a held port would be refused by design; `tests/test_spark_install.py::launch_fixture`, a dead Qwen endpoint — open). Guard self-tests cover 3 positive and 4 negative shapes.

### Measured (CPU only)

`tests/test_endpoint_port_followups.py` runs the launcher's own block (the GraspGen-X part of section 3b, `port_open`, `log`/`warn`/`die`, the banner line, cut from `scripts/launch.sh`; `start_sidecar` and `check_graspgenx.py` replaced by recorders) under `bash` and `/bin/bash`, against listeners this test owns on OS-assigned ports; "another host" = 127.0.0.2 (skipped where the platform has no second loopback address, i.e. macOS):
- server only on 127.0.0.2: 38f6d08 reached it **0** times and stopped the launch; the new block reaches it **once** and passes `--host 127.0.0.2`;
- server only on 127.0.0.1 (127.0.0.2:P held): 38f6d08 **passed** its check; the new block refuses (`no GraspGen-X server on 127.0.0.2:P`, **0** connections to loopback);
- malformed host: 38f6d08 dialled loopback / started `local`; the new block stops first (0 connections, nothing started, no check).

### Results

- RED on a `git archive origin/main` (38f6d08) export with the new file: **`14 failed, 16 passed in 1.91s`** (16 pass by design: 4 premises — the runtime resolves the host variable, `check_graspgenx.py --host` reaches its client, `bash -n` / `/bin/bash -n` — 5 golden pins, 7 guard self-tests; the 14 fail by behaviour, the 5 hand-over tests by ImportError).
- GREEN: new file **`30 passed`**; related set (every test file naming launch.sh / owned_server / check_graspgenx / hug_backend / openclaw_gateway, + mcp_env_forwarding, graspgenx_backend, occupancy, hug_runtime) **`969 passed, 2 skipped`**; doc-reading tests **`240 passed`**.
- bash 3.2: `bash-3.2.57 -n scripts/launch.sh` OK; new file + openclaw file with bash-3.2.57 first on PATH: **`70 passed, 1 skipped`** (the skip is the Darwin-only ps test). The new heredoc inside `$( )` is quote/paren balanced (`test_mcp_env_forwarding` guard green).
- Mutation (scratch copies, `-x`): **25/25 killed** — 13 on launch.sh (host guard ×3, refusal swallowed, loopback probe, die message, `--host` dropped / always, banner, log line, ValueError swallowed, raw env without the rule, uninitialised var), 8 on owned_server.py (fixture keeps its copy, port not checked, claim leaves it handable, double claim, `handed` never set, close does not wake the thread, failed send drops the port, empty hand-over accepted), 4 on the guard. Each killed by the test written for that path.
- Full suite (rebased tree = 38f6d08 + this commit): **`3 failed, 10760 passed, 346 skipped, 4 deselected, 2 warnings in 1613.81s`** (`EXIT=1`, HEAD 3ab08e3). The 3 failures are exactly the known MuJoCo placement ones (`test_memory_task_mujoco::test_memory_frames_record_two_physics_confirmed_picks`, `test_mujoco_withdrawal_physics::test_withdrawal_home_preserves_first_cube_and_occupied_target_refuses_before_carry`, `::test_explicit_reset_replans_new_generation_but_retains_debt_until_physical_reset_and_observation`). Baseline 38f6d08 on this box: `3 failed, 10730 passed, 346 skipped, 4 deselected`; 10760 = 10730 + the 30 new tests.

### Not claimed

- No check against a GraspGen-X server on another machine, and no live launch: the host path is measured only against listeners on 127.0.0.2 (those tests skip on macOS CI).
- `--graspgenx stub` still starts its stub on this machine whatever `CASCADE_GRASPGENX_HOST` says (and checks nothing); `local` starts its server here but checks the runtime's host.
- `scripts/demo_proof.py` unchanged.
- `tests/test_spark_install.py::launch_fixture` still releases its dead Qwen port (follow-up); other server tests still bind port 0 without checking who answers (B64 remainder).

### Live validation owed (parent)

On the GPU box, private ports (example block 47200–47299), real GraspGen-X bound to a second loopback address:

```bash
# 1. a real GraspGen-X server on 127.0.0.2 (same env as scripts/serve_graspgenx.sh)
SRC=.graspgenx-src; GRASPGENX_CHECKPOINT_DIR=$SRC/ext/graspgenx_checkpoints \
GRASPGENX_GRIPPER_CFG_DIR=$SRC/ext/gripper_descriptions PYTHONPATH=$SRC CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
  .graspgenx/bin/python scripts/graspgenx_server.py --config $SRC/ext/graspgenx_checkpoints/release \
  --assets-dir $SRC/ext/gripper_descriptions --host 127.0.0.2 --port 47210 &
# 2. the launcher must check THAT endpoint
CASCADE_GRASPGENX_HOST=127.0.0.2 CASCADE_GRASPGENX_PORT=47210 CASCADE_BRIDGE_PORT=47211 \
CASCADE_OCCUPANCY_PORT=47212 ./scripts/launch.sh --sim isaac --graspgenx external --occupancy none --no-robot-turn --no-judge
#    expect: "[launch] GraspGen-X endpoint: 127.0.0.2:47210 (CASCADE_GRASPGENX_HOST); the checks below dial it",
#            graspgenx-readiness.json with "learned": true, banner "graspgenx: 127.0.0.2:47210 (external)"
# 3. negative: same with CASCADE_GRASPGENX_HOST=127.0.0.3 -> "[launch] ERROR: no GraspGen-X server on 127.0.0.3:47210"
```

### Proposed AGENTS.md line

> Test ports: a server binds port 0 itself; a dead endpoint is `held_dead_port()`; a server that must be told its port up front gets the bound socket from `tests/owned_server.handed_over_port()`. Never bind 0, close and reuse the number (`tests/test_endpoint_port_followups.py` fails on it).

########### Changelog ###########

.. towncrier-draft-entries:: Unreleased

.. towncrier release notes start

4.1.0 (2026-10-09)

  • Import :data:~filelock.OwnerMode, :data:~filelock.CompromiseReason and :data:~filelock.has_fcntl from filelock. :pr:790
  • :class:~filelock.AcquireReturnProxy is generic in the lock type, so with lock.acquire() as held: types held as the lock's own class. :pr:803
  • A :class:~filelock.Timeout from a soft lock names a holder on another host or in another PID namespace, which no contender ever reclaims. :pr:815
  • :attr:~filelock.SoftFileLock.is_lock_held_by_us and :attr:~filelock.MarkerSoftFileLock.is_lock_held_by_us return False for a marker an earlier process with the same PID left behind. :pr:774
  • :class:~filelock.SoftFileLock removes its marker when writing it fails and closing the descriptor fails too, so the lock path no longer stays blocked. :pr:775
  • :meth:~filelock.BaseFileLock.acquire and :meth:~filelock.BaseAsyncFileLock.acquire no longer wait past timeout when poll_interval is longer than the time left. :pr:777
  • :class:~filelock.SoftReadWriteLock ignores a generation-log entry whose name is not 20 ASCII digits, which used to stop its heartbeat thread or delete real generations. :pr:778
  • :class:~filelock.ReadWriteLock, :class:~filelock.SoftReadWriteLock and their async wrappers treat a :data:math.inf timeout like -1 and raise :class:ValueError for a blocking nan one. :pr:779
  • :class:~filelock.ReadWriteLock and :class:~filelock.SoftReadWriteLock accept a timeout above :data:threading.TIMEOUT_MAX instead of raising :class:OverflowError. :pr:780
  • :meth:~filelock.BaseFileLock.acquire raises :class:ValueError for a blocking nan timeout or a poll_interval above :data:threading.TIMEOUT_MAX, and treats a :data:math.inf timeout like -1. :pr:781
  • :class:~filelock.SoftFileLock and :class:~filelock.MarkerSoftFileLock treat a marker cut before its final newline as malformed, so a crash-truncated record self-heals and a read mid-write no longer breaks a live lock. :pr:782
  • :class:~filelock.UnixFileLock no longer deletes another process's live marker when it falls back to a soft lock on ENOSYS, and on macOS a lock path ending in a separator raises :class:FileNotFoundError instead of retrying. :pr:785
  • :class:~filelock.SoftFileLock and :class:~filelock.SoftFileLease put back a live successor's marker that a racing stale break moved aside, so a third contender no longer acquires beside the successor. :pr:786
  • :class:~filelock.StrictSoftFileLock removes every claim a failed acquire published, counts an EEXIST link that landed as published, and no longer reports is_locked after a failed claim cleanup. :pr:787
  • On Python 3.10 without the exceptiongroup backport, a release failure under the default context_error_policy no longer turns into :exc:ModuleNotFoundError; cleanup failures chain instead of grouping, and on_acquired is allowed. :pr:788
  • :class:~filelock.AsyncReadWriteLock and :class:~filelock.AsyncSoftReadWriteLock drop a task's hold when a caller cancels it during a release that still completes, instead of blocking every later writer. :pr:789
  • :class:~filelock.SoftFileLease releases a lease dropped while held, at garbage collection or interpreter exit, and raises :class:ValueError for a heartbeat_interval above :data:threading.TIMEOUT_MAX. :pr:791
  • :class:~filelock.StrictSoftFileLock judges an abandoned private record's age by the filesystem's clock, so a client clock ahead of an NFS server no longer aborts live publications. :pr:792
  • :class:~filelock.BaseAsyncFileLock raises :class:RuntimeError instead of :class:asyncio.CancelledError when its executor shuts down with the call still queued, and a waiter interrupted by anything else no longer wedges later calls. :pr:793

title: fix: follow-ups from the dev QA fixes (dataset-limit refusal, typed limit result, cleanups)
body:
Follow-ups to #3067 tracked in Linear TH-8105. Three of its five groups are fixed here: the Observe "Add to new dataset" limit refusal, a typed dataset-limit result, and three small cleanups. The other two need production measurements that are not authorized yet. They are not part of this PR; see "Not in this PR".

## Summary

**A. Observe "Add to new dataset" refuses a reached dataset limit like the other dataset-create routes (TH-8105 item 1)**
- Before: `POST /tracer/dataset/add_to_new_dataset/` at a reached limit answered **400** with the plan-limit message, shown as a toast. Every other dataset-create route answers **429** and sends the upgrade alert (websocket). The frontend shows a 429 only through that alert.
- Now: **429**, the same message, and the same upgrade alert to the caller's org. The alert comes from `send_dataset_limit_alert`, which is factored out of `log_and_deduct_cost_for_resource_request`.
- **Usage accounting is unchanged.** This route still writes no `DATASET_ADD` APICallLog row and emits no `dataset_creation` usage event, as before. Sending it through `log_and_deduct_cost_for_resource_request` would add both for every Observe create, which is a charging change, so it is not done. The limit counts Dataset rows, so enforcing it does not need the usage row.

**B. A typed result for the dataset-limit check (item 2)**
- `check_if_dataset_creation_is_allowed` returns `DatasetLimitCheck(outcome, limit)`. The outcome is `ALLOWED`, `LIMIT_REACHED` or `UNVERIFIED`. It replaces a `(bool, dict)` pair that had grown a third state through an `error_code` key. Both callers branch on the outcome.
- The SDK exemption is decided in one place, `model_hub.utils.dataset_limit.dataset_limit_binds(sdk_source)`. The usage-entry dispatcher asks it for an unverified limit, and `dataset_add_refusal` asks it for a reached one.
- APICallLog rows, their config JSON, alerts and status codes on every other dataset-create route are unchanged. That includes the SDK-at-limit `RESOURCE_LIMIT` row, which the route later marks `SUCCESS`.
- The new module lives outside `ee/`, so open-source views can import it. The `ImportError` fallbacks for OSS builds are unchanged.

**C. Cleanups (item 5)**
- **Filter-value pickers:** "Filter values are temporarily unavailable. Please retry." was a literal at 21 sites in `tracer/views/dashboard.py`. It is now `FILTER_VALUES_UNAVAILABLE` in `tfc/utils/error_codes.py`, and every site answers with `ApiErrorCode.SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`. Status, message and wire code are unchanged.
- **`PaymentMethods.test.jsx`:** imports the app's real `handleError` instead of keeping its own copy.
- **`ee/voice/services/vapi_service.py`:** `_normalize_to_fagi_call_data` and `_find_customer_vapi_call_id` read `customer` through the shared `vapi_customer` helper. A Vapi API call whose `customer` is a string, list or number now normalises with no customer number. Before, it failed with "An error occurred while parsing the data sent from VAPI". One such candidate also no longer voids the whole customer-call match.

## Linked issues

Closes: none (internal follow-up to #3067)
Linear: TH-8105

## Not in this PR (need a production read)
- **Item 3, the Voice toggle cost-gate constants** (`_RAW_LOG_GRANULE_SCAN_MS`, `_RAW_LOG_MEMBERSHIP_GRANULE_SCAN_MS`). The only production evidence covers 7, 30 and 90 days on one project. Production `spans` uses tiered storage, so recalibrating from hot windows alone could admit a cold, older window onto the interactive wall. A bounded read-only measurement is prepared and waiting for authorization.
- **Item 4, re-polled duplicate rows in the trace and span exact charts.** A local fixture confirms the mechanism:
  - 4 logical spans, one of them a root written twice with merges stopped.
  - The raw exact path counts 5 on both charts and averages latency over the stale version: 16,200 ms against 15,250 ms.
  - How often this happens on production, and what the latest-state reduction costs in memory there, still need the same measurement. The shared builder is unchanged.

## Tests

Every behaviour change has a test that fails on `dev` (b186d3a96) and passes here.

**`tracer/tests/test_dataset.py`**
- `test_dataset_creation_limit_reached`: 429, the plan-limit message, the upgrade alert to this org, no `DATASET_ADD` row, no dataset, nothing logged as an error.
- `test_denied_entitlement_answers_429_with_upgrade_alert`: the real check drives the same refusal.
- `test_reached_limit_still_refuses_when_the_alert_cannot_be_sent`: a failing websocket push still answers 429 and creates nothing (review follow-up; narrowing the helper's `except` clause makes it fail).
- The other `add_to_new_dataset` cases and `TestCreateNewDatasetEntitlement` now use the typed outcome.

**`ee/usage/tests/test_dataset_creation_entitlement.py`**
- The check returns `LIMIT_REACHED(limit)`, `ALLOWED`, or `UNVERIFIED` on a cloud entitlement error, and `ALLOWED` self-hosted.
- `test_refusal_without_a_limit_value_reports_zero`
- `test_reached_limit_lets_sdk_file_upload_through_without_alert`: characterises the unchanged SDK usage row.
- `test_sdk_exemption_is_decided_by_one_policy`: flipping `dataset_limit_binds` makes the SDK upload refuse on both paths, 503 unverified and 429 reached.
- The existing 429, 503 and alert cases on the sibling routes still pass unchanged.

**`model_hub/tests/test_dataset_limit_outcome.py`**: the three outcomes, the default limit, and who the limit binds.

**`tracer/tests/test_filter_values_unavailable.py`**
- The message is registered with its wire text.
- All 21 sites read it with the typed 503 code (AST check).
- A real `filter_values` deadline answers the same body as before.

**`ee/voice/tests/test_vapi_customer_guard.py`**
- Normalisation with a `customer` of `None`, a string, a list, a number or an object.
- A customer-call match with a malformed candidate still picks the exact-time call.

**Frontend `PaymentMethods.test.jsx`**: with the real handler imported, a regression in `queryErrorHandler.js` (the `errorHandled` check removed) fails this test. The old copied handler let it pass.

```
RED on dev (new tests): items 1+2 17 failed / 17 passed; filter-values 2 failed / 1 passed (the wire-compat case passes on dev by design); Vapi guard 7 failed / 2 passed
Targeted after the fix: 53 passed
Regression, run serially on the isolated test stack:
  dataset-create routes, ee/usage, ee/voice, synthetic datasets: 724 passed, 112 skipped
  dashboard, filter-value, dataset-choice, property-catalog, trace-filter and the new suites: 1917 passed, 1 skipped
Frontend: PaymentMethods + BillingV2 + datasetLimitCheckToast: 23 passed; prettier and eslint clean
```

## Review and verification
- **Independent review** (reviewer agent, head 3d9633dd): no blockers. Its one test gap is closed in 00622da7 by the alert-failure test.
- **Adversarial verification** (verifier agent, head 00622da7): VERIFIED by independent code trace.
  - Every caller of the dataset-limit check behaves identically before and after across ALLOWED, LIMIT_REACHED and UNVERIFIED, SDK and non-SDK, cloud and self-hosted. The one exception is the Observe 400 → 429 with the upgrade alert.
  - The OSS/EE import boundary is clean.
- **Executed at 00622da7:**
  - The five touched test files: 66 passed.
  - The head's Vapi guard tests against `dev`: 7 fail, 2 pass.
  - The except-clause mutation fails the alert test.
  - PaymentMethods: 2 passed.
- **Same requests through the real views and database on `dev` and on this head.** Only two scenarios differ: the Observe route at the limit, and a Vapi call with a string `customer`.
  - The other dataset-create route at the limit, the unverified-limit case and SDK uploads return the same status, alert and usage rows on both.
  - The Observe route writes no usage rows on either.
- **Found during verification, not changed here:** `model_hub/services/dataset_service.py` imports `log_and_deduct_cost_for_resource_request` from the `ee.usage.utils` namespace package. That import always fails, so dataset creation through the AI tools skips the plan limit. This is already tracked as TH-5275 and the root cause is noted there. Fixing it changes usage recording, so it is left to that ticket.
- **CI on `fdcc65f68`** (this branch with `dev` @ `51c57380f` merged in, no conflicts): backend pytest shards 1-10, Backend Tests Pass, API Contracts, quality-and-tests, build-check, essential-tests, standalone install and lint passed. `integration-tests` fails on the same 8 `RunTraceTable.test.jsx` cases that fail on `dev` @ `51c57380f` ([dev run](https://github.com/future-agi/future-agi/actions/runs/37586398519/job/112682084206)). They are being repaired in #3357. `e2e (distributed)`: the first attempt also failed OBS-E2E-008 with a `socket hang up` on `list_voice_calls`. The re-run passed it, so that was a one-off. On both attempts the only other failures were the 9 `flows/observe/list-pagination.spec.ts` cases (OBS-E2E-027 to OBS-E2E-036), which fail the same way on `dev` @ `51c57380f` ([dev run](https://github.com/future-agi/future-agi/actions/runs/37586398205/job/112677473373)). This PR does not touch Observe pagination.

## Behaviour changes
- Observe "Add to new dataset" at a reached limit answers 429 instead of 400. The UI shows the upgrade alert instead of a toast. There is still no usage row.
- A Vapi API call with a non-object `customer` normalises with an empty customer number instead of raising.
- No API schema change. Like its siblings, the route does not declare 429, so the generated clients and MCP manifest are unchanged.

AI use: Rick (Claude Opus 5.5 agent) wrote the changes and tests and ran the RED/GREEN and regression runs. An independent reviewer agent reviewed head 3d9633dd (no blockers; its one test gap is fixed in 00622da7), and a separate verifier agent checks the final head. Product decisions follow the TH-8105 fix spec.
E2E: exempt (harness-gap cloud-only dataset entitlement and picker read failures cannot be produced in the E2E stack)

## Video demo
Narrated product and technical demo, 8:51, recorded on head `00622da70bc5` against `dev` `b186d3a96` (both SHAs shown on camera). The video, transcript, chapters, captions and verification evidence are attached to Linear issue TH-8105. They are private to the Future AGI workspace and not linked from this public PR.

Chapters:
1. `00:00` Title and checkouts
2. `01:01` UI before and after. A harness with the real `AddNewDataset`, the app's error handler and `UploadLimitNotification`, replaying the backend response each commit returned. Before: a 400 toast. After: a 429 with the "Dataset limit reached." upgrade alert.
3. `02:39` Backend proof, live. The same requests through real views and DB on both commits; only the Observe-at-limit and string-customer Vapi cases differ.
4. `04:23` Code walkthrough
5. `06:49` Tests on camera: 66 backend tests passed, 2 frontend tests passed
6. `07:38` Not in this PR (items 3 and 4)
7. `08:09` Verdict: charging and usage rows unchanged

## Remediation 2026-10-10

Current head is `ffc624837a2b99ec1998f361210d3bc8c95f779c`. It merges `dev` `ea12cc3f4456fc568d9694a215c661b15be1cea2` into previous head `fdcc65f68`. Fast-forward push only. No force-push.

The dataset-limit refusal is unchanged. `DatasetLimitOutcome` is still allowed, limit_reached, and unverified. SDK uploads still do not bind. `send_dataset_limit_alert` is still the 429 alert path. An isolated load of `futureagi/model_hub/utils/dataset_limit.py` confirmed those three facts. Django was not installed in that shell, so the database entitlement tests were not re-run here.

`frontend` `PaymentMethods.test.jsx` on this head: 2 tests, exit 0. That was inside a 7-file run of 118 tests, exit 0. The extra files are date and agent-node code that arrived from `dev`. They are not a new change in this PR.

The "1917 passed, 1 skipped" figure above was measured on `00622da70`, not on this head. It is left as written. It was not re-run here, and it was not reworded to satisfy the admission heuristic. The admission gate still wants a maintainer-labelled `accepted` issue. None was created or labelled.

Previous-head `integration-tests` failed only `RunTraceTable.test.jsx` (`status: [undefined]`). That repair is #3357, still open. It was not copied into this branch. This merge does include pagination commit `caa64e5616e1671a45a1d2a18f91a0486ca04f6e`. E2E has not been re-run on this head, so it is not claimed green.

The video above is still the private recording on `00622da70`, not this head.

Not merge-ready. Review is still required. khushalsonawat remains requested. Exact-head CI has not finished. Exact-head video is missing. The RunTraceTable dependency is still open.

title: Declare pytz runtime dependency for pandas 3 installations
body:
Fresh pandas 3 installations cannot import empyrical because the package imports `pytz.UTC` but does not declare pytz. Declare that existing runtime dependency without changing timezone behavior.

Closes #60.

Validation on Python 3.12.11 with pandas 3.0.6:

title: refactor: remove unsafe runtime pip install; fail fast with clear error message
body:
## Summary

**Safety and reliability**: `core/retriever.py` called `subprocess.check_call([pip install ...])` at runtime to auto-install missing database driver packages. This is unsafe in production and makes server startup unpredictable.

**Problem**: `_ensure_package_installed()` (lines 122-132) would:
1. Spawn a subprocess to run `pip install --quiet`
2. Succeed silently if install worked — server continues
3. Fail with cryptic `ValueError("Failed to install...")` if pip failed

Runtime package installation is risky because:
- It requires network access from the server host
- It bypasses supply-chain security policies
- It can hang indefinitely on a slow pip index
- It hides dependency problems until the server is actually needed

**Solution**: Removed the `subprocess.check_call()` block entirely. The function now simply collects all missing packages and raises a descriptive `ImportError` that lists exactly which packages are missing and gives the correct `pip install` command. Operators must pre-install dependencies via `requirements.txt` before starting the server.

## Changes

- `code/python/core/retriever.py`: Removed runtime pip install; added clear ImportError with install instructions

**Stats**: +22 lines added, -12 lines deleted, 1 file changed

title: feat(OMN-20743): PR-state schema v2 per-check facts and webhook red-check path
body:
## Summary
Repo omnimarket, base dev, ticket OMN-20743 (slice S1 of the plan that retires the landing controller into the lifecycle nodes). PR-state event schema version 2 carries, per red check, conclusion, workflow run id, workflow name and completed_at, plus base_red_checks and base_read. Version 1 is unchanged, digest included. pr_state_event_from_wire types either version; node_projection_pr_state and the PR handoff ingress accept both. ModelCiRunFailedEvent gains failing_runs, base_red_checks and base_read. EventCiRedFactsReader, now the triage default, takes the facts from the event and calls GitHub only for an event that lacks them, so the runner and dev-head classes are decided from the event. node_pr_state_emit_effect gains two routed handlers: detect_ci_red_check_run emits ci-run-failed when a red check-run observation arrives on onex.evt.github.check-run.v1, and record_workflow_run learns workflow names from onex.evt.github.workflow-run.v1. Both topics are declared as externally produced by omnibase_infra node_github_webhook_ingress_effect. The three detectors share one process-wide index because the runtime builds one handler instance per routing entry. A check the watcher already observed red at the same head is not emitted twice.

## Pairing and order
omnibase_infra PR (webhook ingress fold and the two topics) and omnibase_internal PR (watcher version 2 payload behind ONEX_PR_STATE_SCHEMA, default 1). Merge order: this PR and the omnibase_infra PR first; set ONEX_PR_STATE_SCHEMA=2 on the watcher only after the omnimarket runtime that accepts version 2 is rolled on the dev lane. The webhook path stays silent for a run until a workflow_run delivery names its workflow, so it needs the GitHub App to deliver workflow_run events; that subscription is not verified.

## Dual owner
This change adds no acting node. The contract flag ci_red_triage.act stays false, so the triage records decisions and starts nothing, and the landing controller keeps every action for every red class. No controller path needs to stop in this PR. The flip to acting is a later slice.

## Premises checked
node_github_webhook_ingress_effect lives in omnibase_infra, not omnimarket, so the fold change is in a paired omnibase_infra PR and omnimarket consumes its topics. onex.cmd.github.webhook-delivery.v1 on the dev lane has log-start 10 and high-watermark 10, so no delivery is retained and none could be replayed. The gh read the brief placed in detect_ci_red is in GhCiRedFactsReader in the orchestrator handler. The ticket could not be read live because the Linear tool was not authorized in this headless session.

## Tests
296 passed in the focused set (pr_state_emit_effect, the triage reader, projection, handoff, triage compute), exit 0, on host Stickybeatz.local at head cef56429af98a6da36d001e7ede71fda506c7a83. New tests: test_pr_state_v2 (both versions, digest, wire parser, invalid cases), test_detect_ci_red_check_facts (watcher v2, v1, webhook path, dedupe, peers, refusals), test_ci_red_event_facts (runner and dev-head from the event, fallback), test_pr_state_schema_versions (projection and handoff accept both). The new tests fail at the base commit with an ImportError on ModelPrCheckFact and pass at the head.

Lab: host Stickybeatz.local, lane landing-nodes-s1-5d21, replay of real dev-lane records read from the dev broker (SASL from the broker container's own environment) through the changed handlers with inline python, no committed script. Observed: 3008 pr-state-observed records (offsets 138400 to 141407), 0 refused, 0 schema version 2; the changed detector emitted 36 ci-run-failed events, and 33 of the 33 recorded ci-run-failed events whose source observation is in that window were reproduced with the same event_id. Webhook path: 16 check-run observations produced by the real signed-ingress handler from real failed check rows of the watcher's snapshot (run ids and completed_at are real; the pull request association and the workflow names were supplied by the lab, so the names are synthetic) gave 16 ci-run-failed events, 16 of 16 naming run id, workflow and completed_at, and the watcher path then emitted 27 events over the window instead of 36 because 9 were already emitted. Handler time per check-run observation was p50 0.042 ms and max 0.177 ms. Baseline of the recorded watcher path, ci_read_at to bus, 33 events: p50 120.4 s, max 517.5 s. The end-to-end conclusion-to-bus lag of the webhook path was not measured because the dev lane holds no retained delivery.

.. towncrier release notes start

4.1.0 (2026-10-09)

  • Import :data:~filelock.OwnerMode, :data:~filelock.CompromiseReason and :data:~filelock.has_fcntl from filelock. :pr:790
  • :class:~filelock.AcquireReturnProxy is generic in the lock type, so with lock.acquire() as held: types held as the lock's own class. :pr:803
  • A :class:~filelock.Timeout from a soft lock names a holder on another host or in another PID namespace, which no contender ever reclaims. :pr:815
  • :attr:~filelock.SoftFileLock.is_lock_held_by_us and :attr:~filelock.MarkerSoftFileLock.is_lock_held_by_us return False for a marker an earlier process with the same PID left behind. :pr:774
  • :class:~filelock.SoftFileLock removes its marker when writing it fails and closing the descriptor fails too, so the lock path no longer stays blocked. :pr:775
  • :meth:~filelock.BaseFileLock.acquire and :meth:~filelock.BaseAsyncFileLock.acquire no longer wait past timeout when poll_interval is longer than the time left. :pr:777
  • :class:~filelock.SoftReadWriteLock ignores a generation-log entry whose name is not 20 ASCII digits, which used to stop its heartbeat thread or delete real generations. :pr:778
  • :class:~filelock.ReadWriteLock, :class:~filelock.SoftReadWriteLock and their async wrappers treat a :data:math.inf timeout like -1 and raise :class:ValueError for a blocking nan one. :pr:779
  • :class:~filelock.ReadWriteLock and :class:~filelock.SoftReadWriteLock accept a timeout above :data:threading.TIMEOUT_MAX instead of raising :class:OverflowError. :pr:780
  • :meth:~filelock.BaseFileLock.acquire raises :class:ValueError for a blocking nan timeout or a poll_interval above :data:threading.TIMEOUT_MAX, and treats a :data:math.inf timeout like -1. :pr:781
  • :class:~filelock.SoftFileLock and :class:~filelock.MarkerSoftFileLock treat a marker cut before its final newline as malformed, so a crash-truncated record self-heals and a read mid-write no longer breaks a live lock. :pr:782
  • :class:~filelock.UnixFileLock no longer deletes another process's live marker when it falls back to a soft lock on ENOSYS, and on macOS a lock path ending in a separator raises :class:FileNotFoundError instead of retrying. :pr:785
  • :class:~filelock.SoftFileLock and :class:~filelock.SoftFileLease put back a live successor's marker that a racing stale break moved aside, so a third contender no longer acquires beside the successor. :pr:786
  • :class:~filelock.StrictSoftFileLock removes every claim a failed acquire published, counts an EEXIST link that landed as published, and no longer reports is_locked after a failed claim cleanup. :pr:787
  • On Python 3.10 without the exceptiongroup backport, a release failure under the default context_error_policy no longer turns into :exc:ModuleNotFoundError; cleanup failures chain instead of grouping, and on_acquired is allowed. :pr:788
  • :class:~filelock.AsyncReadWriteLock and :class:~filelock.AsyncSoftReadWriteLock drop a task's hold when a caller cancels it during a release that still completes, instead of blocking every later writer. :pr:789
  • :class:~filelock.SoftFileLease releases a lease dropped while held, at garbage collection or interpreter exit, and raises :class:ValueError for a heartbeat_interval above :data:threading.TIMEOUT_MAX. :pr:791
  • :class:~filelock.StrictSoftFileLock judges an abandoned private record's age by the filesystem's clock, so a client clock ahead of an NFS server no longer aborts live publications. :pr:792
  • :class:~filelock.BaseAsyncFileLock raises :class:RuntimeError instead of :class:asyncio.CancelledError when its executor shuts down with the call still queued, and a waiter interrupted by anything else no longer wedges later calls. :pr:793

title: fix: Android APK startet ohne optionales dnspython
body:
Der Android-Chaquopy-Build bündelt `dnspython` nicht, aber `app/master_cluster.py` importierte `dns` global. Dadurch konnte die APK bereits beim Import mit `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'dns'` abbrechen.

Der Import ist jetzt optional. Nur bei tatsächlichem DNS-TXT-Authority-Lookup wird das Paket benötigt. In der Android-Client-Rolle ist die Funktion nicht erforderlich, während Server mit installiertem dnspython unverändert auflösen.

CI und Laufzeittest in der APK stehen aus.

### [`v2.16.0`](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#v2160)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/compare/v2.15.1...v2.16.0)

v2.16.0 is a feature release with the following features, fixes and enhancements:

##### Enhancements

- `confluent_kafka` now declares itself GIL-safe, enabling real multi-core parallelism on free-threaded CPython builds. See the [Multithreading Guide](docs/multithreading-guide.md) for thread-safety details and free-threaded caveats. ([#​2347](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/issues/2347))
- Add Python 3.14t wheels ([#​2352](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/issues/2352))
- Add Linux s390x (IBM Z) wheels, including Python 3.14t ([#​2360](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/issues/2360))
- Producer `close()` now aborts any open transaction ([#​2347](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/issues/2347))
- Async IO Consumer's default worker pool size has been increased from 2 to 100 ([#​2347](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/issues/2347))
- Add support for CPython free-threading (PEP 703) to enable true multi-core parallel execution in No-GIL environments ([#​2347](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/issues/2347))
- `SerializingProducer` and `DeserializingConsumer` accept a *serde builder*
  when not passing a ready-made serde, through the new `key.serializer.builder` /
  `value.serializer.builder` and `key.deserializer.builder` /
  `value.deserializer.builder` configuration properties. Serdes built this way,
  and any Schema Registry client the builder created for them, are owned by the
  client and closed by its `close()`; ready-made serdes remain the
  application's. This API is experimental ([#​2364](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/issues/2364)).
- Serdes that resolve subjects through the Schema Registry *associated* subject
  name strategy are now given the Kafka cluster id automatically. The id is
  resolved lazily, on the first subject lookup, so creating a client never
  waits on a broker, and concurrent lookups share a single `cluster_id()`
  call; until a broker has been reached the lookup raises a
  `SerializationError` naming `subject.name.strategy.kafka.cluster.id`, which
  can be set to supply the id explicitly. The new serde hooks
  (`set_cluster_id_resolver()`, `close()`) are experimental ([#​2364](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/issues/2364)).
- New `Producer.cluster_id()`, `Consumer.cluster_id()` and
  `AdminClient.cluster_id()` (also on `AIOProducer` and `AIOConsumer`),
  returning the id of the cluster the client is connected to. This API is
  experimental ([#​2364](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/issues/2364)).
- New asyncio clients `AsyncSerializingProducer` and `AsyncDeserializingConsumer`
  in `confluent_kafka.aio`, the counterparts of `SerializingProducer` and
  `DeserializingConsumer` built on `AIOProducer` / `AIOConsumer`, accepting the
  asyncio Schema Registry serdes and their builders. These classes are
  experimental ([#​2364](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/issues/2364)).
- New `Message.deserialized_key()` and `Message.deserialized_value()`, which
  return the same objects as `key()` and `value()` but are typed with the
  deserialized types on a `DeserializingConsumer`. `SerializingProducer` and
  `DeserializingConsumer` are now generic in their key and value types. This
  API is experimental ([#​2364](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/issues/2364)).
- Add support for saving Azure key version with DEK ([#​2306](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/issues/2306))
- Pass context when clients make KEK calls to DEK Registry ([#​2308](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/issues/2308))
- Schema Registry: add support for the DLQ (dead-letter-queue) rule action
  (`DlqAction`). When a rule fails, the record is teed to a configured DLQ
  topic and the original serialize/deserialize call still raises. With the
  default (global) `RuleRegistry` the DLQ is best-effort; set
  `dlq.auto.flush=true` or give the serde its own `RuleRegistry` (closable on
  shutdown) for durability.
- Add support for inline validation rules ([#​2326](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/issues/2326))
- Add Variant, Decimal, and Timestamp CEL functions ([#​2332](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/issues/2332))

##### Fixes

- Raise `SerializationError` for Unicode encoding and decoding failures in string serializers.
- Fix concurrency safety issues in `Producer`, `Consumer`, `AdminClient`, and
  `Message` classes ([#​2347](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/issues/2347))
- Serialize concurrent access to a shared `Consumer` instance across threads
  instead of leaving it as undefined behavior ([#​2347](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/issues/2347))
- Prefer httpx2 over httpx for Schema Registry to avoid Authlib deprecation warnings ([#​2351](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/issues/2351))
- Fix KafkaError error strings raising/garbling on non-UTF-8 locales ([#​2331](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/issues/2331))
- Fix crash on nullable array of $ref items in JSON Schema CSFLE ([#​2370](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/issues/2370))
- Fix `Producer.purge()` ignoring `in_queue`, `in_flight` and `blocking` set to `False` on big-endian platforms such as s390x ([#​2345](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/issues/2345))

### [`v2.15.1`](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/releases/tag/v2.15.1)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/compare/v2.15.0...v2.15.1)

##### Fixes

- `DeserializingConsumer` and `DeserializingShareConsumer` now deserialize the
  message key before the value, matching `SerializingProducer` and the Java
  client. When both key and value fail to deserialize, the key error is now
  surfaced instead of the value error.
- Minor fix for subjectPrefix parameter in subjects API ([#​2311](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/issues/2311))
- Fix race conditions ([#​2315](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/issues/2315))
- Fix segmentation fault after calling `AdminClient.delete_records()` followed
  by another Admin API call (e.g. `list_topics()`) on Python 3.14.
- Use `asyncio.get_running_loop()` instead of `asyncio.get_event_loop()` to avoid creating a new event loop and raise an error in case a loop isn't available ([@​AlexCai26](https://redirect.github.com/AlexCai26), [#​2339](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/issues/2339)).

confluent-kafka-python 2.15.1 is based on librdkafka 2.15.1, see the
[librdkafka release notes](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/librdkafka/releases/tag/v2.15.1)
for a complete list of changes, enhancements, fixes and upgrade considerations.

### [`v2.15.0`](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/releases/tag/v2.15.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/compare/v2.14.2...v2.15.0)

#### [KIP-932](https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/display/KAFKA/KIP-932%3A+Queues+for+Kafka) Queues for Kafka – Now in **Preview**

confluent-kafka-python 2.15.0 adds a **Preview** implementation of the KIP-932 share consumer (Queues for Kafka). Members of a share group cooperatively consume from the same partitions with per-record acquire/acknowledge semantics and redelivery, providing queue-like consumption on top of Kafka.

- New `ShareConsumer` and `DeserializingShareConsumer` clients: subscribe, batch poll (`poll()` returns a `Messages` batch), and close (with context-manager support).
- Implicit (default) and explicit acknowledgement modes (`share.acknowledgement.mode`), with `AcknowledgeType` ACCEPT / RELEASE / REJECT and `Message.delivery_count()`.
- Synchronous and asynchronous commit (`commit_sync` / `commit_async`) and an acknowledgement-commit callback.
- Runtime SASL credential updates (`set_sasl_credentials`) and new `IllegalStateException` / `ConcurrentModificationException` exceptions.
- ([#​2217](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/issues/2217), [#​2239](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/issues/2239), [#​2241](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/issues/2241), [#​2252](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/issues/2252), [#​2253](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/issues/2253), [#​2265](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/issues/2265), [#​2273](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/issues/2273), [#​2277](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/issues/2277), [#​2279](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/confluent-kafka-python/issues/2279))

See the [Share Consumer guide](docs/kip-932-share-consumer.md) and the [Share consumers section of librdkafka's INTRODUCTION.md](https://redirect.github.com/confluentinc/librdkafka/blob/master/INTRODUCTION.md#share-consumers-queues-for-kafka).

**Note:** The share consumer is currently in **Preview** and should not be used in production environments. Its public interfaces may change before General Availability, and known limitations apply (see the guide). The share consumer is single-threaded and not thread-safe. It requires a broker with share groups enabled (generally available in Apache Kafka 4.2.0).

##### Features

- New optional install `confluent-kafka[oauthbearer-aws]` provides AWS IAM-based
  OAUTHBEARER authentication via AWS STS `GetWebIdentityToken`. Activate by setting `sasl.oauthbearer.method=oidc`,
  `sasl.oauthbearer.metadata.authentication.type=aws_iam`, and
  `sasl.oauthbearer.config="region=...,audience=..."`. See the
  [AWS IAM OAUTHBEARER guide](docs/oauthbearer-aws.md) for full configuration, and
  [`examples/oauth_oidc_ccloud_aws_iam.py`](examples/oauth_oidc_ccloud_aws_iam.py)

title: fix(z3): statically gate solver code to the declared z3/sympy subset
body:
Fixes #303

## Root cause

The z3 approach `exec()`s LLM-generated code and injects the **full `z3`/`sympy` module objects** into the execution globals (`execution_globals['z3'] = z3`, plus `set(dir(z3))`/`set(dir(sympy))` dumped into globals). Anyone who can influence the model output — a direct query, or indirect prompt injection via RAG/tool content — can traverse module attributes (`__class__` → `__bases__` → `__subclasses__`, or `z3.__loader__`/`__spec__` chains) to reach interpreter internals and run arbitrary OS commands on the server. The code's own docstring concedes: *"WARNING: This is NOT a security sandbox."* Meanwhile the analysis prompt explicitly promises the model: *"The code will be executed in an environment with Z3 and SymPy available, so do not include any other libraries or modules"* — with zero enforcement.

## Framing

This is **not** a sandbox and does not claim to be one. It statically enforces the library contract the system prompt already makes — the lightweight version of the alternative proposed in #303 ("restrict to a declarative Z3 IR rather than allowing arbitrary Python generation"). Process-level isolation (nsjail/containers) remains out of scope, as stated below.

## Change (2 files, +243/-2)

- **`optillm/z3_solver.py`**
  - New `_validate_solver_ast(tree)` raising `ValueError` listing every violation:
    - import whitelist: `z3, sympy, math, itertools, fractions` — exactly the modules `execute_code_in_process()` already provides;
    - dangerous-call denylist: `eval, exec, compile, __import__, open, input, breakpoint, globals, locals, vars`;
    - dunder-attribute denylist (`__class__, __bases__, __subclasses__, __mro__, __globals__, __builtins__, __init__, __code__, __closure__, __loader__, __spec__, __import__, __reduce__`) blocking module-object traversal escapes — a fixed list rather than banning all dunders, so legitimate solver code is not rejected.
  - Wired into `extract_and_validate_expressions()`: after the existing regex extraction the block is `ast.parse`d and gated. Rejection raises `ValueError`, which the existing handler in `process_query()` catches → graceful degrade to `standard_llm_inference`. Raising (instead of returning an `"Error:"` string) keeps rejected code **out of the 3-round fix-up loop** in `solve_with_z3_sympy` — the gate result is never fed back to the model as a "fix the code" prompt. `execute_solver_code()`'s existing `ast.parse` stays unchanged as a second layer.
  - Docstring updated: the gate is defense-in-depth, not a sandbox.
- **`tests/test_z3_solver_guard.py`** (new, 29 tests, offline; allow-cases really execute in the local venv): 15 refusal cases (imports, calls, dunder traversals incl. `().__class__.__bases__[0].__subclasses__()` and `z3.__loader__`), allow cases that pass the gate and execute (z3/sympy/fractions/math/itertools), wiring tests through `extract_and_validate_expressions`, and behavior tests proving a malicious formulation goes straight to standard inference with `execute_code_in_process` never called and **no fix-loop prompt sent**.

## Red → green evidence

- **Before** (test file applied, `optillm/z3_solver.py` fix stashed):
  - `pytest tests/test_z3_solver_guard.py` → collection `ImportError: cannot import name '_validate_solver_ast' from 'optillm.z3_solver'`
  - probe: `extract_and_validate_expressions(malicious_analysis)` returned `"import os\nos.system('id')"` verbatim — handed straight to the exec path; the end-to-end probe showed the error fix-up loop engaging (a "Fix the Z3 or SymPy code" prompt sent to the model) instead of a static rejection.
- **After**: same probe → `ValueError: solver code rejected by static safety check: import of 'os' (allowed modules: ['fractions', 'itertools', 'math', 'sympy', 'z3'])`; `pytest tests/test_z3_solver_guard.py` → **29 passed**; CI subset `pytest tests/test_plugins.py tests/test_approaches.py tests/test_reasoning_simple.py` → **40 passed**; `OPTILLM_API_KEY=optillm python tests/test_ci_quick.py` → all checks pass; `compileall` clean.

## Compatibility

Compliant solver code (z3/sympy/math/itertools/fractions only — the prompt contract) is unaffected; allow cases cover realistic formulations end to end. Code importing other libraries (e.g. numpy) now degrades to standard inference, which matches today's behavior for that code (ImportError → error path → degrade); not worse than status quo.

## Out of scope

No process-level sandboxing (nsjail/gVisor/containers), no IR rewrite, no opt-out flag (the path already promises not to import other libraries). Pure stdlib (`ast`), no new dependencies.

@CrepuscularIRIS this lands the lightweight version of your suggested alternative. @codelion security-hardening PR following the pattern of #334 — happy to tune the allow/deny lists.

AI disclosure: implementation and tests were prepared with AI assistance, reviewed and submitted by @akushonkamen.

title: fix(deps): update dependency selectolax to v1
body:
This PR contains the following updates: | Package | Change | [Age](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Confidence](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | |---|---|---|---| | [selectolax](https://redirect.github.com/rushter/selectolax) ([changelog](https://redirect.github.com/rushter/selectolax/blob/master/CHANGES.md)) | `>=0.4,<0.5` → `>=1,<1.1` | ![age](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/age/pypi/selectolax/1.0.0?slim=true) | ![confidence](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/confidence/pypi/selectolax/0.4.13/1.0.0?slim=true) | --- ### Release Notes
rushter/selectolax (selectolax) ### [`v1.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/rushter/selectolax/blob/HEAD/CHANGES.md#Version-100) [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/rushter/selectolax/compare/v0.4.13...v1.0.0) This release contains **breaking changes**. The main change is that the Modest backend is no longer available. It is outdated and unmaintained, contains bugs, and does not follow modern HTML5 standards. The second is that `parse_fragment()` is gone. It re-implemented fragment parsing by guessing whether the input was a document or a fragment; `LexborHTMLParser(html, is_fragment=True)` already does this properly, so the guessing layer has been removed. The rest of the changes fix corner cases where the bugs were happening rarely, usually when heavily modifying the tree. - **Breaking**: Remove the Modest backend. `selectolax.parser` is now a stub that raises `ImportError` on import. Use the lexbor backend (`from selectolax.lexbor import LexborHTMLParser`) instead. - **Breaking**: Remove `parse_fragment()`. - **Breaking**: Fix `css_matches` and `any_css_matches` missing matches outside the first top-level node of an HTML fragment. They now search the same scope as `css`. - **Breaking**: Fix `tags` and `strip_tags` doing nothing on an HTML fragment. `tags` returned an empty list and `strip_tags` removed nothing, because the fragment was not reachable from the document node. - **Breaking**: Fix the internal `` wrapper of an HTML fragment being reported as a match. - **Breaking**: Fix `scripts_contain` and `script_srcs_contain` missing matches outside the first top-level node of an HTML fragment. They now search the same scope as `css`. - **Breaking**: Fix `scripts_contain` and `script_srcs_contain` answering from another scope's cached result. The cache is keyed by the node the search is rooted at rather than the node it was called on. - **Breaking**: Fix `select()` missing matches outside the first top-level node of an HTML fragment. It now searches the same scope as `css`. - **Breaking**: Fix `traverse()` covering only the first top-level node of an HTML fragment, and yielding nothing when the fragment starts with a text node. - **Breaking**: Fix `attribute_longer_than` and `any_attribute_longer_than` returning inconsistent results - **Breaking**: `attributes` and `attrs` now report an attribute's qualified name instead of its local name. An element carrying both `href` and `xlink:href` used to collapse them into a single `href` key. - **Breaking**: Fix `iter()` skipping the remaining children when a node is removed during iteration - **Breaking**: Fix an HTML fragment whose first node is text dropping the rest of the fragment. `LexborHTMLParser('as', is_fragment=True).text()` returned `'a'` instead of `'as'`. - Fix `text()` silently returning truncated text instead of raising when a fragment fails to be collected. - Fix `scripts_contain` and `script_srcs_contain` sometimes returning wrong results due to HTML mutations. - Fix a single undecodable byte in an untrusted document making `html`, `inner_html`, `html_pretty`, `attributes`, `attrs`, `id`, `tag`, `text_lexbor` and `text_content` raise `UnicodeDecodeError`. Bytes Lexbor passes through verbatim are now substituted with U+FFFD, the way `text()` already did. - Fix `text_lexbor` sometimes holding temporary memory longer than needed - Improve memory consumption, potential stack overflow and slow extraction in `merge_text_nodes()`. It is now up to 10 times faster. - Improve speed of `__eq__` - Improve speed of `attrs.items()` and `attrs.values()`. - Fix the `inner_html` setter attaching element children to non-element nodes - Fix `head` and `body` dangling after setting `inner_html` on the `` element - Fix the `inner_html` setter freeing the replaced children - Fix `root` going stale on an HTML fragment. - Fix a segfault when walking the tree from the root of an HTML fragment that had been detached from the fragment, for example by `unwrap()`. - Avoid segfaults when hitting OOM - Improve performance of the `text` method. Text fragments are now concatenated as raw bytes, up to 5x faster. - Fix `skip_empty` being ignored by `text(deep=True)` - Fix `text()` raising `UnicodeDecodeError` on undecodable bytes when `deep=False`. It now substitutes U+FFFD, like the deep path always did - Fix handling of the `id` method on text nodes - Fix `attrs[key] = value` raising `AttributeError` instead of `TypeError` when `value` is not a string - Prevent segfaults when instantiating `LexborNode` or `LexborAttributes` directly. - Fix `unwrap()` corrupting the tree in some cases. - Fix `head` and `body` going stale once ``/`` is removed from the document. - Fix `attrs` reading freed memory when it outlives the node it was obtained from. - Fix memory leak in `attrs[key] = None`; it leaked the value buffer header on every call. - Fix possible memory leak in `clone()` - Add `encoding=True` to `LexborHTMLParser`, which detects the encoding of `bytes` input and transcodes it to UTF-8 before parsing.

title: feat!: framework-optional core + registration-time route verifier
body:
## Summary

Lands the framework-optional split: express and fastapi become **optional** — the core SDK installs and imports without either — and node conformance becomes **verifiable** for any server, including self-hosted ones built without this SDK. Closes the architectural follow-up from #102/#104.

## Issue Reference

Closes #104

## Changes

### TypeScript — express as optional peer
- `express` moves from `dependencies` to `optional peerDependencies` (`^5.3`) — fresh installs no longer pull it
- Server construction lives at **`@betekk/canvastekk-workflow-sdk/express`** (subpath export); the root bundle ships **zero** express imports (proven by dist grep)
- `BaseNode.createApp()` is now **async** (lazy adapter load); core-safe structural `CreateNodeAppOptions` in core, express-typed version on the subpath
- `auth.ts` express types replaced with structural equivalents — the emitted core declarations resolve without `@types/express`
- `express` retained in devDependencies (tests exercise the adapter)

### Python — fastapi as the `[fastapi]` extra
- `pip install canvastekk-workflow-sdk` no longer pulls fastapi; `[fastapi]` extra provides it (`[serve]` still provides uvicorn)
- `create_node_app` / `create_multi_node_app` / `NodeAuth` keep their import paths and resolve **lazily**; without the extra, access raises a guided `ImportError` naming `[fastapi]`
- Proven by `tests/test_lazy_server.py`: subprocess with `sys.modules["fastapi"] = None` — core import + `__all__` intact, guided errors raised
- Note: fastapi/pydantic resolve string annotations (PEP 563) against module globals at registration — the lazy path publishes the imported names via `globals()` at first entry (documented in code + LEARNINGS)
- CI: `poetry install -E fastapi` (3 sites in ci-python.yml)

### Route verifier — the enforcement half
- New `conformance.py`: `verify_node(base_url)` probes **GET /health** (200), **GET /manifest** (200 + `WorkflowNodeManifest` validation), **POST /execute** (malformed payload must 4xx) — framework-free (httpx), so self-hosted nodes are judged by the same contract
- `register_node(..., verify=True)` refuses registration with a per-route report when any probe fails (opt-in; default unchanged)
- CLI: `python -m canvastekk_workflow_sdk verify <url> [--api-key KEY] [--timeout S]` — per-route PASS/FAIL, exit 0/1
- node-builder skill template (bundled + mirror) installs `[fastapi,serve]`

## Breaking changes (both carry **BREAKING** via commit subjects)

- TS: root-entry import of `createNodeApp`/`createMultiNodeApp` → `@betekk/canvastekk-workflow-sdk/express`; `node.createApp()` returns a Promise
- TS: consumers pinning express get it as a peer they must install
- Py: deployments relying on the SDK to transitively install fastapi must add the `[fastapi]` extra
- Python import paths are unchanged (lazy, not relocated); Python consumers otherwise unaffected

## Quality Checks

Gated per PLANS/PLAN-104.md Trace — `RE-GATE (post-rebase final tree) tier=full` (rebased onto main post-#106; package.json union-resolved, lock regenerated):

- Python: `poetry check` + `--lock` green, `ruff` clean, `pytest` **833 passed** (9 new: conformance pass/fail modes, registration refuse/accept/require-invoke-url, CLI exit codes, lazy-server subprocess proof)
- TypeScript: `npm audit --omit=dev` 0, build OK, `vitest` **378 passed**, `eslint` clean, `tsc --noEmit` src+tests clean
- Dist laziness: root bundle 0 express refs; `/express` emits js/cjs/d.ts
- Skill mirrors byte-identical (`skill-mirror-guard`)

## Files Modified

- TS: `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `tsup.config.ts`, `src/express.ts` (new), `src/index.ts`, `src/base-node.ts`, `src/auth.ts`
- Py: `pyproject.toml`, `poetry.lock`, `__init__.py`, `app.py`, `auth.py`, `router.py`, `conformance.py` (new), `registry.py`, `__main__.py`, `tests/test_lazy_server.py` (new), `tests/test_conformance.py` (new)
- CI: `.github/workflows/ci-python.yml`
- Docs: node-builder `SKILL.md` ×2, `PLANS/PLAN-104.md`, `LEARNINGS/*` (1 new entry)

## Checklist

- [x] No manual version bump (release workflow owns it)
- [x] Deferred: none from #102 — all three follow-ups (#104/#105/#106) land this run

_Requested by **Matthias** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KfygGZNB8WR6RKnLJS8BXE?thread=cmsg_01KfygGZNB8WR6RKnLJS8BXE2DBQA8EkFjHvBpLHoueQ41)_

Before: #16 gated MLX to Apple Silicon and moved dependencies to the latest releases, but its `numpy>=2.4.6` floor made MLX and nodetool-huggingface 0.8.2 unresolvable together (mistral-common caps numpy below 2.4 on Python 3.11). Its platform guard raised a plain `ImportError`, which nodetool-core logs as a broken install on Windows and Linux. It kept version 0.7.2, which PyPI already has with the old dependencies.

After: MLX and HF resolve together on macOS arm64, Linux x86_64 and Windows x64 (numpy 2.3.5, torch 2.14.1). Off Apple Silicon the provider is skipped quietly. The package is 0.7.3.

This branch contains #16's two commits plus three fixes, so it supersedes #16.

How:
- numpy floor is `>=2.3.5`, matching core. CI now resolves MLX together with nodetool-huggingface for all three platforms. That step fails when the old floor is restored.
- The guard raises `ModuleNotFoundError(name=__name__)`, which core 0.8.2's `_is_pack_absent` treats as an absent pack. The core floor is now `>=0.8.2`, since that check exists only there. The test asserts both.
- Version 0.7.3 in pyproject, uv.lock and the metadata JSON. The metadata was regenerated with core 0.8.2's scanner and the enriched model fields were carried over, because a plain scan drops them. The rescan also fixes list fields with default factories that were recorded as required.

Checks: `uv lock --check` ok, ruff and black clean, pytest 239 passed and 9 skipped. The macOS CI job was not run locally.

Fixes NP1, NP8 and NP9 from the local inference setup re-audit.

title: refactor(P4): move the checks and the knowledge phase out of pipeline.py (#776)
body:
This change moves two parts of `ComponentPipeline` out of `kstrl/pipeline.py` into two new modules. The bodies do not change. It is slice P4 of the plan for #776.

## Moves

- `kstrl/pipeline_checks.py` (400 lines) holds the class `MechanicalChecks` (parents `InboxDesk`, `AttemptRecorder`) with 8 members: `_before_gates`, `_judged_change`, `_phase_acceptance`, `_phase_diff`, `_set_up_gate_worktree`, `_waivable_evidence`, `_warn_not_measured`, `_write_gate_logs`. It also holds `DiffPhaseResult`, `VerifyPhaseResult` and `_verify_routing`.
- `kstrl/pipeline_knowledge.py` (486 lines) holds the class `KnowledgePhase` (parents `AttemptRecorder`, `UsageLedger`) with 5 members: `_measure_utilization`, `_phase_distill`, `_store_fact_utilization`, `record_fact_utilization`, `record_injected_knowledge`. It also holds `DistillPhaseResult` and `FactUtilization`.
- `ComponentPipeline` has the parents `KnowledgePhase`, `MechanicalChecks` and `Transitions`. `kstrl/pipeline.py` has 2710 lines (3539 before). It keeps more than 800 lines because slices P5 and P6 move the remaining phases.
- No name is re-exported. The readers import from the new modules: `kstrl/pipeline_state.py` (a `TYPE_CHECKING` import), `tests/test_pipeline.py`, `tests/test_gate_output_logs.py` and `tests/helpers/verify_phase.py`.

## Checks on the head 8682ac72 (base commit 378989b0, which is `origin/main`)

- A2: `integ_move_check.py` gives 86 same, 0 changed and 0 missing. A second script compared each top-level statement and each member with its decorators. The only text that is not in the base commit is the class header of `ComponentPipeline` and the docstrings of the two new layer classes.
- A3: the full suite gives `7974 passed, 171 skipped, 109 xfailed`. The counts of the base commit in `base-counts.txt` are the same.
- A4: `mypy --strict` (211 files), `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean.
- A5: `pre-commit run --files` on the 13 changed files gives no failure, with `complexipy`, `cyclomatic-ratchet` and `file-length-ratchet`. No moved function is above a gate, thus decision B1 does not apply.
- A7: the patch lookup on the base commit and on the head gives 0 pairs to examine and no `UNBOUND` row.
- A8: the new modules have 400 and 486 lines.
- A9: each new module imports first in a new interpreter, then `kstrl.cli`. No `ImportError` occurs.
- A10: `origin/main` did not move after the base commit.
- No test function and no `parametrize` row is added. No prompt text changes, thus H2 and H3 do not apply.

## Pins (each value comes from a guard run)

Six guard files change a pin: `test_encoding_readers.py`, `test_check_result_measurement.py`, `test_journal_one_writer.py`, `test_prompt_record_census.py`, `test_signature_spellings.py` and `test_language_vocabulary_ratchet.py`. Each row moves from `pipeline.py` to the new module that holds the site at this time. No guard is widened.

## Plants (A6)

Each plant edits a new module, operates one guard file with a 420 s limit, and then writes the first text of the file again. The `__pycache__` directories were removed first.

| Plant | Module | Guard | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| counted word `pytest` in the docstring | knowledge | `test_language_vocabulary_ratchet.py` | caught |
| signature `diffz:fetch-failed` | checks | `test_signature_spellings.py` | caught |
| phase `provisioningz` with no signatures | checks | `test_check_name_enrolment.py` | caught |
| no `recording_prompts` in `_phase_distill` | knowledge | `test_prompt_record_census.py` | caught |
| one more `util.measured` read | knowledge | `test_check_result_measurement.py` | caught |
| `read_text()` with no encoding | knowledge | `test_encoding_readers.py` | caught |
| one more `"evolution.jsonl"` string | knowledge | `test_journal_one_writer.py` | caught |
| `RunEnvelope.load` in a phase | knowledge | `test_config_guard.py` | caught |
| `atomic_write_text` read through `kstrl.atomicio` | checks | `test_gate_output_logs.py` | caught |

One plant was at an incorrect site, thus it is not counted. It changed `check="git_diff"` on a failure that also gives `signatures=`. The guard does not read that check name, and the same plant in `pipeline.py` of the base commit also gives no failure.

## Patch retargets

`tests/test_gate_output_logs.py`: `kstrl.pipeline.atomic_write_text` becomes `kstrl.pipeline_checks.atomic_write_text`. The last plant in the table shows that this patch must change the name in `pipeline_checks`.

title: OWNER-PATH chart_facts divergence DROP DEFAULT, N-349 (prepared, not run)
body:
## What

SS N-347/N-349. DRAFT, HELD, not armed, **NOT RUN against anything**. An **owner-path package** (D6 in-process pattern, as `exec/reader_grants/reader_grants.py`), deliberately outside `platform/migrations`, that drops the `0.0` column default of `chart_facts.cross_ayanamsha_divergence_arcsec`. Kāla: ACCEPT WITH NOTES at 12675f2df ("safe on production as it stands"); the notes are fixed in the commits below.

**Why.** A default of 0.0 for a cross-method divergence is a false green (§N.8) for EVERY writer that does not name the column. Catalog read as `suvarna_reader` on production (N-347, catalog tables only): `attnotnull = false`, `default = 0.0`, `double precision`, ordinary table, **owner `data_plane_l1_owner`** (not `amjis_app`), PostgreSQL 15.18, 0 inheritance children, not a partition (Kāla re-checked, SELECT only).

**What.** One statement under `SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s'` (now the FIRST statement of the transaction, before the transient GRANT), run as the table owner:

`ALTER TABLE public.chart_facts ALTER COLUMN cross_ayanamsha_divergence_arcsec DROP DEFAULT`

Metadata only; no backfill. Existing 0.0 values stay until each writer's next rebuild rewrites its rows.

**Guards (each a refusal that changes nothing):** `public.chart_facts` is an ordinary table (relkind `r`; not a partition; no inheritance parent or child); the column is `double precision` and nullable (NOT NULL stops the job); the owner is `data_plane_l1_owner`; the default is exactly `0.0`; already dropped = idempotent no-op; after the statement, before/after snapshots must be EQUAL for everything but that one default: column names / types / NOT NULL, CHECK and other constraints, indexes, row-level security and policies, table and column comments, triggers, ACL, role membership. `--expect-plan H` must equal the plan hash. The inverse (`SET DEFAULT 0.0`) exists with its own hash.

Modes: `--dry-run` | `--apply --expect-plan H` | `--rollback-dry-run` | `--rollback --expect-plan H2`.
**Plan hashes (changed by the review fixes; pinned as literals in the test):** drop `dd01bbd2f9757da26f24c9bdea20f6621efd08e48e4768e17b475136bbe0f5f8`, rollback `1f18ae40261a6e20fd4ac0244b79f30b919839627710af8d2f86e110a0f2a0b7`.

## FOR THE OWNER AND THE SCHEDULER (SS N-410, Kāla note 8): the digest fan-out

The column is a digested value column in the output-digest specs of 13 migrations (875, 876, 883, 886, 887, 889, 891, 892, 893, 914, 919, 1042, 1086, 1221, 1223) and in `mv_chart_sensitive_points_summary`. After the apply, every writer that OMITS the column from its INSERT stores NULL instead of 0.0, so its output digest changes at its next rebuild. **The apply must be scheduled with a round that rebuilds every affected writer, not on its own.** Affected writers (they do not name the column; checked in the writer sources): `ga_positions`, `ga_panchanga`, `ga_nakshatra`, `ga_strength`, `ga_ayurdaya`, `ga_sensitive_degree`, `ga_structural`, `ga_sade_sati`. NOT affected by the apply itself (they name the column explicitly): `ga_vargas` (writes NULL already) and `ga_sensitive` (writes NULL after PR-H1 #3400; its digest moves with that PR). Any other `chart_facts` writer outside these digest specs gets NULL silently.

## Fixtures that keep `DEFAULT 0.0` and will drift from production after the apply (not changed here)

`tests/test_karaka_readers_pg.py:399`, `tests/test_migration_1262_chart_fact_identity_registration.py:99`, `tests/fixtures/pratijna_v4_snapshot/schema.sql:119` (Kāla), and found by a repo-wide search: `platform/tests/integration/gochara_b6_am5_search_inventory.db.test.ts:204`, `..._am14_moon_domain.db.test.ts:193`, `..._rehearsal_volume.db.test.ts:191`, `00_ARCHITECTURE/briefs/suvarna/exec/f_a2_key_widening/tests/schema/01_prereq_tables.sql:33`, `verification_artifacts/PARISESA_V4_GA3_REBUILD_20260821/rehearsal_schema.sql:111`; and the historical migration `platform/supabase/migrations/209_ga5_sensitive_points_mv.sql:89` (must not be edited).

## Run

Exec, in the protected window, with the owner's approval at run time. The Engine never runs it. CURRENT_STATE §2 carries the owner-path entry (no migration number).

## Evidence

- `platform/python-sidecar/tests/test_n349_divergence_default_owner_path.py`: **45 tests**. PostgreSQL 15.17 (local; production is 15.18): 44 passed. PostgreSQL 17.10: 42 passed, 2 skipped with a visible reason (on 16+ a CREATEROLE role cannot GRANT without ADMIN OPTION, and with it the administrator counts as a member, so the package skips its transient GRANT: **the transient-membership path cannot be modelled on 16+**; the 42 other tests run on 17 but take the "already a member" branch, not the production path).
- New in this round: relkind / partition / inheritance / column-type pins (view, partitioned table, partition, inheritance parent and child, numeric, real, text: all refused, nothing changed); 13 sabotage tests for the widened diff (CHECK, PRIMARY KEY, two ALTER COLUMN TYPE, index, ENABLE and FORCE row security, policy, three comments, trigger, DISABLE TRIGGER); lock-timeout order and a SHARE lock on `pg_auth_members` proving the transient GRANT is bounded too; the two plan hashes pinned; with `CI` set the module imports psycopg directly, so a missing driver is a loud collection failure, not a skip.
- Deliberate breaks (backup copy, mutate, test, restore, empty diff): relkind pin removed 3 fail; partition check 1; inheritance 2; type pin 4; each of the six widened-diff categories skipped, one at a time, fails its own tests (2, 2, 1, 3, 3, 2); lock_timeout moved back after the GRANT 2; never executed 3; plan text / DROP / ROLLBACK statement edited: the hash pin fails each time; CI branch back to importorskip: fails.
- **CI placement (Kāla REQUEST CHANGES at 3e6874c57, fixed in the next commit).** The first attempt installed psycopg in the shared `governance-tool-tests-shard` job so this file would stop being silently SKIPPED. That un-skipped ~404 other tests and, in this PR's own CI run, three files broke there (`test_formgap_decl_remedies` 8 errors: `psycopg2` missing; `test_n283_forms` 16 errors: one huge psql argument exceeds Linux's per-argument limit; and this file's own stub test used a plain ImportError where pytest 9 only skips on ModuleNotFoundError). **That install is reverted (`ci.yml` is unchanged by this PR) and the test file moved to `platform/python-sidecar/tests/`**, whose CI jobs install psycopg from `requirements-ci.txt` (the py-sidecar shards, a non-"Governance Tool Tests" job). The fragile subprocess stub test is replaced by a static check of the CI-loud import branch (with `CI` set the module imports psycopg directly, so a missing driver is a collection failure). The two older failing governance test files are NOT fixed here (out of scope; they are now un-touched).
- **Trigger definitions (Kāla note):** the trigger snapshot now includes `pg_get_triggerdef`, so a same-name trigger repointed at another function is refused (new test; deliberate break: without it the test fails). The suite is 45 tests; PG15.17 45 passed, PG17 43 passed + 2 skipped (transient-membership path not modellable on 16+). Fixture DDL retries on cluster-wide collisions (an intermittent setup error was seen twice while the machine was loaded and never reproduced on an idle one: that retry is a guard, not a diagnosis).
- Test-suite note: the shared `public.chart_facts` names are hard-coded in the package, so each test builds a fresh database.

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>google/adk-python (google-adk)</summary>

### [`v2.11.0`](https://redirect.github.com/google/adk-python/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#2110-2026-10-01)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/google/adk-python/compare/v2.10.0...v2.11.0)

##### Highlights

This release adds graceful cancellation and tool confirmation to workflows, a tool for consulting another model mid-task, and a built-in SQLite memory service.

- **Execution cancellation**: Pass an `abort_signal` to `Runner`, `Workflow`, and nodes to stop a run gracefully; `/run_sse` now cancels the run when the client disconnects. See the [unit guide](https://redirect.github.com/google/adk-python/blob/main/docs/guides/runners/runner/abort.md) for more details. ([ef5bbcf](https://redirect.github.com/google/adk-python/commit/ef5bbcfe51670bd211645a043914c162e7c1cd60), [3d73603](https://redirect.github.com/google/adk-python/commit/3d73603deb180a6518982b2b60f036c764f0cf7e))
- **Tool confirmation in workflows**: Tool nodes now pause for user approval via `RequestInput`, the same way an `LlmAgent` does, instead of passing an error downstream. ([ce132b9](https://redirect.github.com/google/adk-python/commit/ce132b92d471b8df903524593d863171b000a764))
- **ModelConsultTool**: Let an agent consult another model mid-task, capped by per-turn and per-session budgets. See the [unit guide](https://redirect.github.com/google/adk-python/blob/main/docs/guides/tools/model_consult/model_consult_tool/index.md) for more details. ([84cc99a](https://redirect.github.com/google/adk-python/commit/84cc99abd53010817a85b51fdcdc5d4f48366769))
- **SQLite memory service**: Keep agent memory in a local SQLite database, selected with a `sqlite://` memory service URI. ([9625b06](https://redirect.github.com/google/adk-python/commit/9625b06c9a1be6b9ecd85225657690ae5c0e9d3e))
- **MCP SDK 2.x**: Connect to MCP servers over the modern protocol through a new opt-in path. ([e738c26](https://redirect.github.com/google/adk-python/commit/e738c26fe5abcecffe2fbeba31f8d837086aad8a))

##### Breaking changes

- **Dev UI runtime config is served by the server**: The web server now serves `/dev-ui/assets/config/runtime-config.json` per request and no longer writes `runtime-config.json` into the installed package. If you edited or read that file, set the logo with `--logo-text` and `--logo-image-url` and fetch the config from the server instead. ([3722746](https://redirect.github.com/google/adk-python/commit/3722746568a33226d54ba51876801c5948479eb5))
