### [`v2.10.0`](https://redirect.github.com/google/adk-python/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#2100-2026-09-24)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/google/adk-python/compare/v2.9.2...v2.10.0)

##### Highlights

This release introduces advanced skill lifecycle management, expands database and model integration support, and brings richer efficiency metrics to agent evaluation.

- **Skills**: Control resource usage and tool persistence dynamically using new ephemeral lifecycles and active skill limits (experimental; enable with `ADK_ENABLE_SKILL_LIFECYCLE=1`). ([43b73e4](https://redirect.github.com/google/adk-python/commit/43b73e4fc0920c08693bcec3985c832c7d9870b0))
- **Database Integrations**: Perform high-performance vector and hybrid searches seamlessly within your agent flows with the new MongoDB toolset. ([0961ced](https://redirect.github.com/google/adk-python/commit/0961ced3e3dd92056ecf10c7b10aa736eead08f1))
- **Evaluation**: Optimize agent execution costs and latency with new evaluation metrics for tracking duration, token consumption, and model call counts. ([2d428ea](https://redirect.github.com/google/adk-python/commit/2d428ead3860fbc131de362b485eb15551373665))
- **Model Support**: Integrate OpenAI reasoning models more effectively with automated request parameter adaptation and precise reasoning token reporting. ([52a2f0f](https://redirect.github.com/google/adk-python/commit/52a2f0f09f2910043127042e6ba3dd805d5a1479))

##### Behavior changes

- **BigQuery protected write mode** now runs a non-SELECT statement only when the dry run places it in the session's anonymous dataset, so multi-statement scripts, `CALL`, `EXPORT DATA` and other statements the dry run gives no destination are rejected. ([8b883d0](https://redirect.github.com/google/adk-python/commit/8b883d07147f62f8e9979ec8e6b1205437d60f4f))
- **BigQuery protected mode** keeps its BigQuery session in process memory instead of session state, so its temporary tables do not survive a restart or carry over to another replica. ([094012b](https://redirect.github.com/google/adk-python/commit/094012b4509fc136083e6be95f273ad1163fbf2c))
- **`OpenAIResponsesLlm`** ignores `thinking_config` (`thinking_level` / `thinking_budget`) with a warning; use `OpenAIGenerateContentConfig.effort` instead. ([b3d1392](https://redirect.github.com/google/adk-python/commit/b3d1392a1a9caf382b9483c5fecd4b9140949abb))
- **`AgentEvaluator.evaluate` and `evaluate_eval_set`** raise `ValueError` when no eval cases are evaluated, instead of passing. ([9dbc2ae](https://redirect.github.com/google/adk-python/commit/9dbc2aebd7a0ad88183d166c19398bbbab93d507))
- **Instruction templating** leaves `${var}` and backslash-escaped `\{var}` as written instead of filling them from state. ([0caecd2](https://redirect.github.com/google/adk-python/commit/0caecd236f95131da625a3bf1de282130f6aa437))

Test suites run with `-W error` will fail on these imports. ([bf2bc56](https://redirect.github.com/google/adk-python/commit/bf2bc561ef9c2b9cfaec5bc6ca441b6c1d3b3496))

title: refactor(core): System Prompt 内联为常量，删除 Settings.load()
body:
## 改动一：System Prompt 内联为常量

角色设定从外部 `system_prompt.txt` 搬进 `app/core/prompts.py` 的 `CUSTOMER_SERVICE_SYSTEM`，文件删除。连带清掉：

- `load_system_prompt()` 整个函数
- `Settings.system_prompt_path` 字段 + `ensure_system_prompt_exists()` 启动检查 + `Path` import
- `.env` / `.env.example` 的 `SYSTEM_PROMPT_PATH`
- 3 个只测文件加载的测试、fixture 里造 prompt 文件的语句

**迁移正确性是断言出来的**：先留底再搬，用 Python 比长度与逐字符相等，而非肉眼比对。

```
原文件长度 398，常量长度 398
逐字（含末尾换行）完全相同: True
```

末尾的 `\n\n` 一并保留，所以常量在源码里末尾多一个空行——那是故意的，为的是让 `orig == C` 这个断言成立。

保留 `build_chat_prompt(system_text: str = CUSTOMER_SERVICE_SYSTEM)` 的参数：4 处测试传自定义文本验证模板编排（花括号原样保留、history 顺序、system 必须排第一），保留参数它们一字不用改，生产调用点写 `build_chat_prompt()`。

`SystemMessage(content=...)` 实例注入这条约束**没有跟着删**——与是否读文件无关，常量里出现 JSON 示例花括号时元组形式一样会炸。spec、CLAUDE.md、`prompts.py` docstring 三处都保留了。

## 改动二：删除 `Settings.load()`

`load()` 的独有价值只有 `ensure_system_prompt_exists()` 那一句文件 I/O 检查。文件删除后它只剩 `return cls()`，与 `Settings()` 完全等价。

**fail-fast 一直由 `@field_validator("openai_api_key")` 在构造期承担，从未在 `load()` 里**——实测 `Settings()` 直接构造即抛 `ValidationError`。

留着一个名字叫 load、实际只是构造的方法，会在 lifespan 里误导读者。

9 处调用点（5 个文件：`app/main.py`、`app/core/llm.py`、`app/services/chat.py`、`evals/run_eval.py`×2、`tests/test_config.py`×3）全部机械替换为 `Settings()`，无需额外 import 改动。`test_load_reads_all_fields` 随之改名 `test_reads_all_fields`。

## 验证

- TDD：先跑出 `ImportError: cannot import name 'CUSTOMER_SERVICE_SYSTEM'`（RED），再实现
- `make test` → 59 passed（原 60：删 2 个 load 测试、加 1 个常量测试）；`make lint` clean
- 删文件后重跑全量，确认无隐藏依赖
- **真实进程冒烟**（pytest 用假 key，须另验真 `.env` 路径）：uvicorn 启动 0 traceback；`GET /` 200、`/docs` 200、空 messages 422；真实对话一轮，模型回「我是喵喵优选平台的智能客服小喵，很高兴为您服务」——这条才真正证明常量进了对话
- **删 `load()` 后重跑上述冒烟**，结果同上
- **空 key fail-fast 单独实测**：

  ```
  pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for Settings
  openai_api_key
    Value error, OPENAI_API_KEY 为空，请在 .env 中填写后再启动
  ERROR:    Application startup failed. Exiting.
  ```

  异常由 lifespan 里的 `Settings()` 抛出，进程退出、端口从未监听。删除未改动该行为分毫。

## 代价

改文案要动 Python 文件并重启，不能再直接编辑文本文件。若后续频繁调 Prompt 文案，应改回文件或引入提示词管理工具。

## 顺带发现（未处理）

`dev-notes/ch01.md` 阶段 12 写着「`system_prompt.txt` 里根本没有这些入口信息」，但该文件第 17 行实际写着「App内【人工客服】入口或官方客服热线」——笔记写完后文件被改过。历史记录不改，仅在阶段 16 记一笔备查。

title: Restore a clean documentation build on Python 3.12
body:
The documentation cannot build from the declared doc extra on Python 3.12. The pinned pydata-sphinx-theme imports distutils, which is no longer included in Python 3.12.

Base reproduction (after declaring the separately reported pytz runtime dependency in #60): `uv run --extra doc make -C docs html` fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named distutils`.

Supplying setuptools restores the existing theme's import. The resulting Sphinx build also reports 39 pre-existing warnings/errors from an invalid language setting and malformed API docstring examples. These leave portions of the published API documentation incorrectly rendered.

Restore a build using only declared doc dependencies and preserve the README/API content. Correct the malformed reStructuredText so a fresh Sphinx build can pass with warnings treated as errors. Do not redesign the documentation theme as part of this repair.

AI assistance: Codex reproduced the failures and drafted this issue under maintainer authorization.

title: feat(presentation): hide the quiet turn pair in the TUI and relay folds (S1)
body:
Slice **S1 — core presentation** of the quiet-turn design (`no_reply`): hide the persisted quiet pair at the TUI and relay folds' paint seams. Design: `docs/design/quiet-turns.md` §5/§8 (S1). Branched from S0a's merge, `975522da08`.

## What

- **`harness/rows.py`** — `QUIET_TURN_TOOL = "no_reply"` + `is_quiet_turn_name` / `is_quiet_turn_call` / `is_quiet_turn_result` (the marker read, strict `is True`, matching the loop's and the session's readers). One vocabulary, both folds.
- **Deliberately NOT a `HIDDEN_TOOL_NAMES` entry** — that set is subtracted from the display pages, the served journal rows and the transcript index's counts, and the dashboard reads the persisted call as the structural close of its settled turn (§5, the quiet-close rule). A unit test pins the exclusion, and a window-level test pins the pair staying in display pages while the patience arm beside it is still dropped.
- **Relay fold** (`mobile/projection.py`): the stored fold skips a quiet call (the `SEND_TOOL_NAME` shape) — its result then settles into nothing through the documented missing-row tolerance; `_tool_row` refuses to mint on all four live arms (compose/start/update/end); the end arm drops by the marker, beside the ask gate's divert arm.
- **TUI fold**: the replay-loop skip; the skipped-live restore painter; both live seams (compose/start); and the settle seam's marker read in `on_tool_ended`.

No version bump. Every suppression sits where the `patience` / `send` precedents sit; none touches the served rows.

## Testing evidence

All runs use an isolated `HOME`/config dir and the worktree's own editable venv. Fold probe (`$SCRATCH/quiet-s1-probe.py`, product-shaped rows: peer + quiet pair + ordinary control pair):

```
before (base 975522da08), both folds:
  {"kind": "tool", "tool_name": "no_reply", "tool_state": "done"}     <-- the sentinel row
  {"kind": "tool", "tool_name": "read",     "tool_state": "done"}
after, both folds:
  {"kind": "tool", "tool_name": "read",     "tool_state": "done"}     <-- control only
result-only page: 0 rows (the result settles into nothing)
```

Targeted pytest (exact files):

```
tests/unit/harness/test_quiet_turn_rows.py tests/unit/mobile/test_fold_parity.py
  -> 60 passed in 4.81s
tests/unit/tui/test_hidden_wake_surfaces.py \
  tests/unit/tui/test_peer_message.py::test_a_peer_turn_answered_with_no_reply_replays_as_the_card_alone
  -> 10 passed in 5.39s
tests/unit/session/test_history_window.py -k "patience or quiet"
  -> 3 passed in 2.31s
post-format re-run of the five files, -k "quiet or no_ledger or live_seams"
  -> 11 passed in 3.77s
```

Each new test was run against the pre-change tree first (production files stashed in this session's own worktree only) and **failed** there — the four TUI/peer tests `4 failed`, the rows+parity import `ImportError: cannot import name 'QUIET_TURN_TOOL'` — so they pin this change rather than a green host.

## Visual evidence

Rendered from the **real `OperatorApp`** under the repo stylesheet via `scripts.visual_capture.save_capture`, 100×30; same script run against the pre-change tree (throwaway worktree at `975522da08`) and this branch.

Before — the persisted pair paints a ledger row:

![before: a peer message, then the no_reply sentinel row, then the read control](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/damianvtran/7691c04860aa7efc6ffdb2d5bd25c108/raw/before-quiet.png)

After — the sentinel row is gone; peer card and the ordinary `read` row unchanged:

![after: peer card and read control only](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/damianvtran/7691c04860aa7efc6ffdb2d5bd25c108/raw/after-quiet.png)

Geometry, both frames: `screen.size=(98, 28)`, `screen.virtual_size=(98, 28)`, `show_vertical_scrollbar=False` — no reflow, no scrollbar; the only difference is the row. Painted transcript, before: `morning / peer / ▸ no_reply ✓ / ≡ read ✓`; after: `morning / peer / ≡ read ✓`.

Footer caveat (design round 1, D1): the frames differ outside the transcript only in the footer band — the capture host's worktree string (`quiet-s1-before` vs `.worktrees/quiet-s1`) and the resulting bar-label shift. That is capture environment, not this change: no footer/status code is touched, and a re-capture with a normalized cwd is held-class under the fleet hold.

## Gates

- `flake8 7.4.1`, `black 26.1.0 --check`, `isort 5.13.2 --check-only` clean over all nine changed files (run before the fleet hold landed).
- Under the active **fleet resource hold** (Aida): pyright and `make check-changed` are deferred to CI. A pyright run from this worktree was terminated by the hold owner; it has not been restarted.

## Not addressed (flagged, not changed)

- The relay's stored-page arm (`visible_transcript_rows` via `network/relay.py` / `desktop_sessions`) still serves the pair's raw journal rows; the design hides the pair at the folds, and the native-side "the relay hides the quiet pair" reading belongs to S3. Not touched here.
- The two end-seam marker drops are belt on current builds (the name gates are build-independent, so no row can be minted): kept as the marker-read half of the contract beside the ask-gate divert arm; a reviewer may prefer them dropped.

title: test(models): no swallowed ImportError in the models hub may drop tables silently (GDXA-433)
body:
## Summary
`gdx_dispatch/models/__init__.py` registers module tables on `TenantBase.metadata` inside 37 `with suppress(ImportError)` blocks; before this PR only the 4 tables of #48 were pinned, so a typo, missing module or circular import silently dropped tables. The new `test_models_hub_imports.py` parses the hub, finds every ImportError-swallowing block from the AST (never hard-coded), and for each one: (1) in a fresh interpreter asserts every name the block binds is on `gdx_dispatch.models`; (2) re-executes the body without the suppression to surface the real error; (3) asserts imported ORM classes map onto `TenantBase.metadata`. `agent_ownership.txt` gains 5 lines (hub + two registration tests were unowned; claimed for platform-core). No production code, migration or router changed.

Class:     a block that swallows ImportError in the models hub drops a module's tables from TenantBase.metadata with no test failing
Searched:  gdx_dispatch/models/__init__.py (the only registration hub; every with-suppress(ImportError) and except-ImportError block, found by AST)

body:
## What

`benchweave_sdk.interfaces` grows `DatasetServices(HostServices, Protocol)` — the seven dataset-service members of the pinned extension contract §3 (`dataset_publish`, `dataset_lookup`, `artifact_read`, `payload_create`, `payload_append`, `payload_finalise`, `payload_abort`), with docstrings faithful to the corpus text, plus the invoke-minting note on `OperationContext.dataset_id`. The protocol is rendered in the API reference (`great-docs.yml`) and pinned by six new tests in `tests/test_dataset_services.py`.

## Why

Slice 1 of three for gateway issue #146, per the design of record (`.claude/deep-review/2026-09-25-issue146-invoke-dataset-design.md` §2.5, committed in the main repo). The invoke/dataset lane needs the SDK protocol shape first: the gateway's dataset services (slices 2/3) and any future SDK-side writer both implement this one structural shape. Additive protocol only — no `ADAPTER_API_VERSION` motion (the `CaptureServices` precedent: capability protocols grow beside the base without an API bump) and no corpus bytes.

No SDK-side issue exists by design — the single issue stream files all work on the gateway tracker (madeinoz67/benchweave#146); this PR is that issue's slice 1.

## Gates

All run locally before review (invoked from a worktree whose venv lives outside the repo tree: a venv under `.claude/worktrees/` sits on a dot-directory component, where `.pth` processing is silently skipped — the known dot-dir trap. Same locked env, `uv sync --locked --extra test`):

- [x] `uv run pytest -q` — 496 collected / 494 passed / 2 skipped / 0 failed (junitxml attributes)
- [x] `uv run ruff check .` — all checks passed

      block merge (main #69).

RED-first evidence: the new test module fails on import before the protocol exists (`ImportError: cannot import name 'DatasetServices' from 'benchweave_sdk.interfaces'`); with the protocol present but unrendered, the existing `tests/test_docs_reference.py` pin fails (`public but neither rendered nor excluded: {'interfaces.DatasetServices'}`) until the `great-docs.yml` entry lands.

## Notes for reviewers

- **Deferral (design §6 row 6):** the standalone (hostless) dataset/payload writer — SDK parity with `StandaloneCaptureWriter` — is deferred out of slice 1. This PR-body note is the row-6 carrier, exactly as the design of record specifies ("SDK-side note in slice 1's PR"); gateway issue madeinoz67/benchweave#146 tracks the increment but is the tracking issue, not the carrier; reopen trigger: a plugin-dev need for dataset authoring without the gateway. Rows 1/5/7 (class-semantic M-checks, acquisition-scoped dataset identity, demo-lattice fixture) take follow-on issues at slice-3 merge on the gateway tracker, by design.
- The protocol docstring says plainly that no implementation ships in this SDK yet — the gateway dataset path (slices 2/3 of #146) is the intended first implementation. A docstring-honesty pin holds that wording and flips when an implementation lands (the `test_capture_writer` B14 discipline, inverted).

title: feat(region): editor build service on ionos1 with queue, limits and retention (editor phase 3)
body:
The build service on ionos1 (VPS DE): Docker container behind Traefik, POST/GET `/api/jobs`, SQLite queue with one worker (MemoryMax 3 GB), the limits table, dedupe by world id, static `/worlds/<id>/…` with CORS, 30-day retention and nightly cleanup, weekly Geofabrik Swiss extract update, Cloudflare DNS via the homelab-service-routing skill. Public-endpoint protection: an **ALTCHA human check on `POST /api/jobs` for new builds only** (`GET /api/challenge`; never for playing, polling, downloading or a cache hit) on top of the per-IP and global limits, and a cheap, rate-limited `GET /api/preview` (name, Gemeinden, race feasible) that builds nothing.

Spec: [`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-09-region-editor-design.md`](https://github.com/freaxnx01/game-rhyflitzer/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-09-region-editor-design.md), section(s) 1, 2, 3, 5.

Part of the region editor (phases 1–5). Phase 3 of 5; needs phase 1.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `service/` holds the package `rhyflitzer_api` (Starlette API + one worker), its tests, `requirements*.txt`, a `Dockerfile` and a `README.md` with the compose block and the operator checklist; nothing under `pipeline/`, `prototype/` or `data/` changes.
- [ ] `POST /api/jobs` takes `{"lv95": [...]}` or `{"lonlat": [...]}`, snaps and checks the frame with phase 1's `frame`, and answers `202` (queued/building), `200` (already built, free), `400` (`bad-request`, `bad-bbox`, `too-small`, `too-big`, `outside-ch`), `403` (`human_check_failed`, new builds only), `429` (`one-at-a-time`, `daily-limit`, `server-daily-limit`) or `503` (`busy`); the same frame is one job (job id = world id).
- [ ] **Human check (ALTCHA):** `GET /api/challenge` issues an HMAC-signed PoW-v2 challenge (`PBKDF2/SHA-256`, `ALTCHA_COST` 5000, ~1 s on a phone, 10-minute expiry). `POST /api/jobs` for a **new** build needs a valid, unexpired, unused solution in `"altcha"`, else `403 {error: "human_check_failed"}`; a built world, a queued or building identical frame and every GET need none. The solution is spent in the admission transaction (a `429`/`503` leaves it unspent; used signatures kept until expiry in SQLite). Key: Docker secret file `ALTCHA_SECRET_FILE`, missing file fails closed. Per-IP and global limits unchanged.
- [ ] **Preview:** `GET /api/preview?bbox=e0,n0,e1,n1` (LV95, snapped, `400` codes as for jobs) → `{id, exists, name, gemeinden, raceOk, reason?}` (`id` = the world id of the snapped frame, `exists` = built or queued, so the editor skips the human check), no build, no human check; `raceOk` `true`/`false` (`few-major-roads`)/`null` (`no-road-index`) from a road index the worker builds from the extract; `name` `null` when swisstopo fails; 60 requests a minute per client IP (`429 preview-rate-limit`).
- [ ] The limits table holds: queue ≤ 20, 1 active job and 5 new builds per IP per UTC day, 100 per day overall, 10-min job timeout, > 20 000 buildings or > 50 000 road points → `too-complex`; all checks and the insert run in one SQLite `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`.
- [ ] IPs are stored only as `sha256(daily salt : ip)[:16]`; salts and per-day counts of past days are deleted nightly; the client IP is the rightmost `X-Forwarded-For` entry.
- [ ] `GET /api/jobs/<id>` reports `state` (queued, building, ready, failed, expired), `step`, queue `position`, `error`/`message`, `lv95`.
- [ ] **#167's contract:** `GET /api/worlds/<id>` → `{id, status, bbox: {lv95: [e0, n0, e1, n1]}}` (`status` = the job's `state`: queued, building, ready, failed, expired; progress is `GET /api/jobs/<id>`), also after the world expired; ids are exactly `^[0-9a-f]{12}$`; `GET /worlds/<id>/{world.json, terrain.mmh, meta.json}` with CORS for `https://github.freaxnx01.ch` on `/worlds/*` and `/api/*`; fetching `world.json` bumps `lastPlayed` (store + `meta.json`, at most hourly); `world.json`/`meta.json` `no-cache`, `terrain.mmh` `public, max-age=86400`; a world that is not ready → `404 {error: expired | not-ready | unknown}`.
- [ ] One worker builds one job at a time in a subprocess (`python -m rhyflitzer_api.build` → `region.build_world`), relays the steps, kills it after 10 min, publishes `worlds/.<id>.tmp` → `worlds/<id>` by one rename only on success, retries `source-unreachable` twice (30 s apart), requeues interrupted builds on start.
- [ ] Nightly (after 03:00 UTC): worlds unplayed for 30 days are deleted and marked `expired`; the 10 GB store cap evicts least-recently-played first (also after every build); gallery worlds are exempt from both; stray temp dirs removed; swisstopo tile caches pruned to 1 GB each.
- [ ] Weekly (Monday after 04:00 UTC, or at once when missing): Geofabrik's Swiss extract is downloaded to `.part`, verified against its `.md5`, swapped in atomically; any failure keeps the old file and is retried at most hourly; builds wait while no extract exists.

Used over SSH only (tunnel or `docker exec`).

## Assumptions

- **A1** [med] **Web framework: Starlette 1.x + uvicorn** (new runtime deps, BSD-3; `httpx` dev-only for `TestClient`; `altcha` for the human check, A14). Rejected: stdlib `http.server` (the Python docs say it is not for production, and this endpoint is public); FastAPI (pulls pydantic; nothing here needs schemas). Starlette brings CORS and file responses; uvicorn is the server it needs.
- **A2** [high] **SQLite** (stdlib, WAL) for queue, limits and metadata, one row per world doubling as its job. Rejected: Redis/a queue library (another container and dependency for ≤ 100 jobs a day).
- **A3** [med] **Two compose services from one image:** API (`mem_limit 512m`, behind Traefik) and worker (`mem_limit 3g`, `memswap_limit 3g`, `cpus 2`, no Traefik), sharing one volume. Rejected: one container with both processes (an OOM kill during a build would also take the API down). `cpus: 2` is my choice so builds do not starve ~65 other containers on 6 cores.
- **A4** [med] Each build runs as a **subprocess** of the worker (timeout kill, the memory cap hits only the build). Rejected: in-process (a hung or runaway build would block or kill the worker).
- **A5** [med] **Complexity is checked on the built world** (`world.json` counts), not before the build: `region.build_world` (#166) has no early hook, and the 10-min timeout bounds the cost. An earlier check inside the pipeline would be a later improvement.
- **A6** [high] **Rate-limit day = UTC day**, same as the salt day; a cache hit or joining a queued job is free; a `too-complex` frame is answered from its row without rebuilding; other failures can be retried (counts as a new build).
- **A7** [med] **Client IP = rightmost `X-Forwarded-For`** (`PROXY_HOPS=1`): Traefik appends the real peer and the container publishes no port; the DNS record is unproxied (`proxied: false`, per the routing skill), so there is no Cloudflare hop.
- **A8** [med] **Play signal = fetching `world.json`** (#167, A3), so it is served `no-cache` (each load revalidates; ~0.5 MB); `terrain.mmh` (~4 MB) keeps a 1-day cache. Rejected: the play signal on `meta.json` (my first draft) — #167 asked for `world.json`.
- **A9** [med] **`GET /api/worlds/<id>` is a tombstone status** (#167): expired worlds keep their row and `lv95`, only the files go. **No server zip route**: #167 packs the download in the browser.
- **A10** [med] **Admin gallery endpoints ship here** (`PUT`/`DELETE /api/admin/gallery/<id>`, internal listener only, SSH access), because the eviction exemption needs a gallery flag and the token plumbing is a phase 3 item; phase 5 adds `GET /api/gallery` and the start-screen row.
- **A11** [med] **Image built on ionos1 by compose from the git URL** (`build.context: https://github.com/freaxnx01/game-rhyflitzer.git#main`, `dockerfile: service/Dockerfile`). Rejected: a GHCR publish workflow (more CI, nothing gained for one host).
- **A12** [high] Tile caches pruned to 1 GB per collection (`region.prune_tiles`), not deleted after each build: neighbouring frames reuse tiles. Disk budget ≈ 14 GB of the 58 GB free.
- **A13** [high] Cleanup 03:00 UTC, extract Monday 04:00 UTC, both run by the worker between builds (no cron, no extra container).
- **A14** [med] **Human check: the `altcha` package from PyPI** (`altcha>=2.3,<3`, new runtime dependency): official `altcha-org/altcha-lib-py`, **MIT** (licence file in the wheel), zero dependencies, 2.3.0 of 2026-10-04 after seven 2026 releases, PoW v2 like the `altcha` 3.x widget of #169. Rejected: our own HMAC/SHA-256 verify in a pure module (v2 signs a JS-number-formatted canonical JSON and would drift from the widget). `challenge.py` is a thin wrapper; replay protection and admission order are ours (`store.human_gate`).
- **A15** [med] **Parameters:** `PBKDF2/SHA-256`, `cost` 5000 (`ALTCHA_COST`), key prefix `00` (one try in 256), ~1 s on a phone (one sample: 0.9 s single-threaded on a workstation), expiry 10 minutes; verification is one derivation. The error shape stays `{error, message}` like every refusal here.
- **A16** [low] **Preview = an estimate:** names from swisstopo's identify service (centre point + envelope, cached per frame, "A" or "A · B"), `raceOk` from a road index (major roads per 500 m cell via `osmium tags-filter` + pyosmium, ≥ 3000 m in the frame, `RACE_MIN_ROAD_M`). Rejected: a cut per preview (hundreds of MB, seconds). The build's own `race` stays authoritative; calibrate in operator step 7.
- **B1 — public hostname: RESOLVED (no longer blocking).** The user confirmed **`rhyflitzer-api.freaxnx01.ch`** (A record → ionos1, unproxied) on 2026-10-10. It exposes a public endpoint that accepts anonymous build requests, which is why the human check and the rate limits exist.
- ✅ **B2 — admin access (resolved):** the admin routes are **not routed through Traefik at all**; they run on a separate internal listener (`rhyflitzer-admin`, `127.0.0.1:8081` on the host, no Traefik labels, excluded from the public router) and are used over SSH only (`ssh -L 8081:127.0.0.1:8081 ionos1`, or `ssh ionos1 docker exec rhyflitzer-admin …`), from any IP and without the homelab. The bearer token (generated by the user, kept in Passbolt, placed as the Docker secret file on ionos1) stays as a second layer; the code only reads `ADMIN_TOKEN_FILE`; no agent creates, sees or commits the token. No public admin rate limit is needed.
- ⛔ **B4 — ALTCHA HMAC key (needs the user; credentials):** generate it (`openssl rand -hex 32`), store it in Passbolt as "rhyflitzer altcha secret", place it as the Docker secret file `rhyflitzer_altcha_secret` on ionos1 (API container only). The code only reads `ALTCHA_SECRET_FILE`; no agent creates, sees or commits the key. Rotating it invalidates open challenges (players just retry).
- ⛔ **B3 — go-live on ionos1 (needs the user):** adding the two services to `mydocker-compose` and the DNS record are outside this repo (operator checklist below). No money is spent: existing VPS, free data (Geofabrik weekly ~550 MB, swisstopo STAC/WMTS), no new paid service.

## Consequences

- ionos1 load: up to 3 GB RAM and 2 cores during a build (~1 min per 15 km²), at most 100 builds a day; ~14 GB disk at the cap.
- Geofabrik traffic: ~550 MB per week; swisstopo tile downloads per new area (~920 MB raw per 15 km², fewer with the cache).
- `world.json` is re-downloaded on every game load of a hosted world (no-cache without a 304 path in Starlette's `FileResponse`).
- A world rebuilt after expiry gets the same id and link, so browser and IndexedDB caches of the old build stay valid.
- Every Build press costs the player one ~1 s proof of work; a new build is refused with `403` before any limit is looked at. The preview calls swisstopo (2 requests per uncached frame); the worker builds a road index (a few minutes, < 1 GB) after each extract update, until then `raceOk` is `null`.
- Until #166 is merged this issue cannot start (Task 1 Step 1 checks it); #179's race adds a `race` step that the service relays without changes.
- `PIPELINE_VERSION` is part of the world id: bumping it gives every frame a new id (old links expire normally).

```python
    """Admin only; run by the rhyflitzer-admin service on an internal port that Traefik never sees."""
    if settings is None:
        logs.setup()
        settings = Settings.from_env()
    app = Starlette(routes=ADMIN_ROUTES)
    app.state.settings, app.state.store = settings, store or Store(settings.db_path)
    return app
```

title: fix(deploy): 宿主机采集兼容 Python 3.10，容器改为非 root
body: Refs #28, Refs #29 ## 问题与复现 #28：生产机上 `tsp-news-collector.service` 每 5 分钟失败一次。宿主机 venv 是 Python 3.10.12，`backend/app/news/collectors.py` 使用 `datetime.UTC`（3.11 才有），导入即 `ImportError`。容器是 Python 3.11.17，同一份代码在容器里可以导入。库里钉钉 / 知识星球条目在宿主机单元失败期间停在大约 12:00–14:00（上海时间）。 #29：`data/` 属主是 root，容器进程是 uid 0，所以 `news.sqlite`、`-wal`、`-shm` 和 `push_state.json` 是 root。`data/news` 和它的 inbox 已经是 ubuntu，宿主机采集器今天能写入收件箱。 ## 根因 宿主采集器（`deploy/tsp-news-collector.service` + `scripts/news_host_collector.py`）不是多余的第二条链路。容器调度对 dws / zsxq 只跑 `collect_inbox()`，读 `data/news/inbox`。容器里没有 `dws` / `zsxq-cli`，也没有令牌；令牌在宿主机 `~/.dws` 等目录。单元失败时，这两路资讯停止入库。 有人在服务器上给 `collectors.py` 打了一个未提交的 UTC 回退补丁。仓库里的修复用 `timezone.utc`，部署后应丢掉那份本地补丁，避免和仓库再次分叉。 容器以 root 写挂载的 `data/`，新文件继续是 root。只在宿主机 chown 一次会被下一次容器写入盖回去。 ## 解决方案 1. 宿主采集器导入闭包里的模块不再使用 `datetime.UTC`，naive 的 RFC 822 时间用 `timezone.utc`。闭包含 `host_collector`、`collectors`、`config`、`app.config`，以及登录提醒才会导入的 `dingtalk`。测试静态扫描这个闭包；本机有 Python 3.10.22 时还会实际导入。 2. `scripts/news_host_collector.py` 一开始检查 Python >= 3.10，不够就退出并指向文档。推荐仍是用 3.11 重建 `~/.venvs/tsp-collector`（deadsnakes 或 `uv python install 3.11`），写在 `docs/news-sources.md`。 3. compose 的 app 使用 `user: "${APP_UID:-1000}:${APP_GID:-1000}"`。镜像把 `HOME`、`XDG_CACHE_HOME`、`UV_CACHE_DIR` 放到任意 uid 可写的 `/home/app`，Codex 登录态挂到 `/codex-home`（`/root` 是 0700，非 root 进不去）。启动使用 `uv run --no-sync`，避免非 root 改构建阶段留下的 `.venv`。`.env.example` 增加 `APP_UID` / `APP_GID`。 4. `scripts/deploy_preflight.py` 检查 `data/` 和 `data/news` 对这对 uid/gid 可写、采集 venv 的 Python 版本，以及 `data/` 下的属主漂移。失败时退出码非 0。 ## 兼容性 面板和容器仍要求 Python 3.11+。只有宿主采集器的导入闭包降到 3.10。 已有部署升级后，容器默认不再是 root。切换前执行一次： ```bash sudo chown -R 1000:1000 data ``` `1000` 必须等于 `id -u ubuntu`（以及 `.env`、`~/.codex` 的属主）。不是 1000 就改 `APP_UID` / `APP_GID`，chown 用同一对数字。然后跑 `python3 scripts/deploy_preflight.py --data-dir ./data`。 回滚：把 `APP_UID` 和 `APP_GID` 改成 `0`，再 `docker compose up -d --force-recreate`。root 可以写已经属于 1000 的文件。若要把整个 `data/` 改回 root，之后还要 `sudo chown -R ubuntu:ubuntu data/news`，否则宿主机定时器写不进收件箱。细节在 `docs/deployment.md`。 ## 性能 不在行情或列表热路径上。预检会 `stat` `data/` 下的全部文件，只在部署时跑。大目录会多花一些时间，不改运行时。 ## 验证结果 ```bash cd backend uv run ruff check app/news/collectors.py \ tests/test_host_collector_py310.py tests/test_deploy_preflight.py \ ../scripts/deploy_preflight.py ../scripts/news_host_collector.py TSP_PYTHON310=/tmp/py310/bin/python uv run pytest \ tests/test_host_collector_py310.py tests/test_deploy_preflight.py \ tests/test_foreign_news.py tests/test_news.py tests/test_news_push.py \ tests/test_dsa_integration.py::test_compose_mounts_etf_job_next_to_bootstrap -q # 81 passed git diff --check ``` 另用 Python 3.10.22 加 pydantic 2.14 / pydantic-settings 2.15 执行 `import app.news.host_collector, app.news.dingtalk`，成功。pytest 里的 3.10 导入用例因此没有跳过。 没有 Docker，没有构建镜像，也没有连接生产机。 ## 界面证据 无界面改动。 ## 风险与回滚 - 镜像没有在本环境构建。非 root 依赖 `HOME` / 缓存目录 / `UV_NO_SYNC` / Codex 挂载路径，compose 和 Dockerfile 有契约测试，但没有容器启动验证。 - 预检只看属主、主组和 other 位，不看附加组或 ACL。当前进程就是目标 uid 时会实际写一次临时文件。 - `APP_UID` 和 ubuntu、`.env`（通常 600）、`~/.codex`（通常 700）不一致时，容器读不到配置或登录态。 - 服务器上那份未提交的 UTC 补丁部署后应删除。 回滚见上面的 `APP_UID=0` / `APP_GID=0`。代码回滚即还原本 PR。

title: feat(standards): #367 D1 — one corpus-rooted normative-row resolver, one vocabulary
body:
D1 of the normative-row trust work — issue #367, deferred from #238. Both runtime sites that parsed `standards-manifest.json` raw now resolve normative rows through one corpus-rooted loader discipline.

What lands: `load_manifest`'s parse core extracted verbatim to `_entries_from_document`; the corpus-rooted twin `load_manifest_from_corpus` (inheriting `_read_corpus_manifest`'s corruption wrap); the shared resolver `normative_path_from_corpus` (exactly-once basename match, `standards/`-prefix refusal); one-move delegations at `documents.py`'s `_otdp_normative_path` and `provider_settings.py`'s `provider_contract_validator`; one vocabulary (`normative_document_unresolved` / `standards_entry_absent` / `normative_row_not_corpus`, old prefixes gone repo-wide); a parity pin arm asserting the twin-shared message stays string-equal; the CON-7 amendment naming the D4 byte-drift residual.

RED evidence: both site arms failed `DID NOT RAISE` pre-fix with the planted `../` row resolving into corpus bytes (the laundering demonstrated through the real control paths — pre-fix, both validators built on dev-tree bytes); the library arms failed on the missing-API ImportError; a withheld-delegations midpoint isolated exactly the two site arms; a toggle-off control proved the site wiring carries the fix.

Refute: two independent adversary lanes — zero executable code defects. Sweep completeness verified repo-wide (no live second parser; scripts D2b-held with no runtime reachability; SDK boundary clean; pointer unmoved); twin parity byte-verified; all traversal/absolute/backslash/duplicate-basename forms refused at load before the resolver. Five record-accuracy rows folded: the acceptance-arm clause met in substituted form; the parity pin; the D4 clause; behavior delta 3 — the sites' manifest read widened from strict UTF-8 to the loader family's bytes-read semantics (a UTF-16 manifest refused at base now loads at tip; disclosed as deliberate alignment with `load_manifest`, no trust boundary crossed, contrasted with the admitted-document strict-UTF-8 posture); and the backslash description corrected as Windows-conditional.

Owner calls: D2 (the open-dev-head laundering form) stays deferred, reopen trigger amended to the MERGE of the head-opening corpus train — the old wording would have reactivated it one train after the exposure window opened. One vocabulary per F3. Open row call: pin strict-UTF-8 manifest refusal with an arm (rec: accept the delta as disclosed — the loader family itself reads bytes; revisit if the family ever unifies on strict UTF-8).

Gates: ruff 0; fresh-cache mypy 0 (374 files); focused 471/0/0; full battery 3524/0/0/11; both standards tripwires 0 bytes.

Closes #367 — D2 rides its amended trigger, documented in the addendum and CON-7.

title: fix(ci): keep minimal policy tests independent of publisher imports
body:
The minimal policy test job installs only pytest and PyYAML. Its global publication-witness fixture eagerly imported the publication package, so the admission import added in #5064 caused all 100 policy tests to fail during setup with missing Pydantic. This repair sets the existing witness-path environment binding without importing the package, and clears the real writer's idempotency cache when that module is loaded. Looking up the module again at teardown covers imports during the test.

The existing six test files remain in the command. Three subprocess regression cases cover no writer import, collection-time import, and test-time import, including per-test file isolation, inherited child-process writes, duplicate suppression, and setup/teardown cache cleanup. No dependency, skip, workflow condition, required context, or advisory membership changes.

Task: `ci-minimal-policy-test-dependency-closure-20261008`
AuthorityCase: `CASE-SDLC-REFORM-001`
Parent spec: `30-areas/hapax/frame/coordinator-succession-20261007/TICK-20261008T0426Z/CI-MINIMAL-POLICY-DEPS-COMMISSION.md`
Continuation: `CI-SIGNED-BRANCH-ADMISSION-CONTINUATION-20261008T2005Z.md` beside that parent.

This is the existing CI repair separated into its own source subject and matching CI task. title: fix(deployer): db 멈춰있을 때 새로 신청하면 계속 만드는 이슈
body:
## 요약 (Summary)
멈춘 Postgres 사이드카(`<app>-db`)가 있으면 그 앱은 재배포할 때마다 실패하던 문제를 고쳤습니다.

있는지 확인할 때 `docker ps`에 `-a`가 없어서 멈춘 컨테이너는 "없음"으로 나왔습니다. 그래서 같은 이름으로 `docker run --name <app>-db`를 다시 실행했고, `Conflict. The container name ... is already in use`로 배포가 실패했습니다. `cleanup_local`은 재배포 때 DB를 일부러 남기기 때문에(`drop_database=False`) 같은 실패가 계속 반복됐습니다.

- 로컬 (`deployer.ensure_local_postgres`): `docker ps -aq`로 확인합니다. 컨테이너가 있으면 `docker start`(실행 중이면 아무 일도 안 함), 없으면 지금처럼 `docker run`
- 노드 (`nodes.ensure_postgres`): `docker start <db> || docker run ...`. 기존에는 `run` 실패가 `;`로 넘어가서 멈춘 컨테이너에 `pg_isready`를 60초 동안 시도하다가 `postgres not ready`로 끝났습니다
- 데이터는 이름 붙은 볼륨 `<app>-dbdata`에 있어서 다시 켜도 그대로입니다

컨테이너가 멈춰 있는 건 주로 누군가 `docker stop`을 했을 때입니다 (`--restart unless-stopped`라서 크래시는 docker가 알아서 다시 띄웁니다).

## 관련 이슈 (Related)
없음 (리뷰 중에 발견)

## 변경 모듈 (Area)
- [ ] analyzer
- [x] deployer
- [ ] healer
- [ ] api (main.py)
- [ ] contract (schemas.py / docs/interfaces.md)
- [ ] frontend
- [ ] sample-apps
- [ ] infra / docs

`nodes.py`(노드 풀)도 같은 패턴이라 같이 고쳤습니다.

## 테스트 방법 (How to test)
- `test_local_postgres_restarts_a_stopped_sidecar_instead_of_recreating_it`: 컨테이너가 목록에 있으면 `docker start`만 하고 `docker run`은 하지 않음. 없으면 `docker run`
- `test_node_postgres_restarts_a_stopped_sidecar_instead_of_recreating_it`: 노드 명령이 `docker start <db> || docker run`
- 고치기 전에는 세 경우 모두 실패하는 것을 확인했습니다
- **실측 (로컬 docker, postgres:16-alpine)**: 사이드카 생성 → 테이블에 `42` 넣기 → `docker stop` → `ensure_local_postgres` 다시 호출하니 `docker start (postgres)` 단계로 다시 켜지고 `42`가 남아 있음. 다시 멈춘 뒤 `nodes.ensure_postgres`의 명령을 로컬 bash로 실행해도 다시 켜짐. 테스트 컨테이너와 볼륨은 정리함

이번 PR에서 바꾸지 않은 것: `scripts/demo-down.sh`는 여전히 `-db` 컨테이너를 지우지 않습니다. 이번 수정으로 멈춘 DB가 남아 있어도 다음 배포에서 다시 켜지기 때문에 그대로 뒀습니다. 데모 종료 때 DB까지 지울지는 따로 정하면 좋겠습니다.

## 체크리스트 (Checklist)
- [x] `ruff check app tests`, `ruff format --check` 통과. `pytest -q`는 209 passed, 8 failed. 실패 8개는 `tests/test_healer.py`의 `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'langchain_openai'`(이 노트북 venv에 패키지가 없음)이고, 이 변경 없이 origin/main에서도 같은 8개가 실패합니다
- [x] `ref/`, `.env`, API 키, GCP 자격증명이 포함되지 않음
- [x] `schemas.py` 변경 없음
- [x] 실측 컨테이너·볼륨 정리 완료

title: hermes update rebuilds the staged runtime venv without plugin dependencies — provider plugins fail silently
body:
### Summary

Since Hermes switched to staged runtime venvs under `~/.hermes/installs/.../venv` (Python 3.14), a
`hermes update` rebuilds that venv with only the core dependencies. Native provider plugins (e.g.
`mnemosyne`) keep their *tools registered*, but their Python dependencies are gone. The failure is
completely silent: memory simply stops working on every profile.

### Observed behavior (v0.21.5+8673, git install, Linux, Python 3.14.7)

- After `hermes update` (201 commits pulled), all agent sessions report
  `{"status": "memory_unavailable", "reason": "Mnemosyne not initialized"}` — the tools exist, the
  provider can't import its core.
- `hermes plugins doctor` reports **OK** ("import, and registration passed") because its probe runs
  against the *old* 3.11 venv (`~/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv`), not the staged runtime venv.
- Worse silent failure: plugin config readers that catch `ImportError` (e.g. mnemosyne's PyYAML-based
  `profile_isolation` check) fall back to defaults — profile-isolated banks were bypassed and new
  memories written to the wrong DB path. No log line anywhere points at the cause.
- The staged venv has **no pip**, so `mnemosyne-hermes install` cannot bootstrap itself into it.
- `hermes mnemosyne stats` (plugin CLI) errors `No module named 'mnemosyne'` for the same reason.

### Expected behavior

Either (a) plugin dependencies declared in plugin manifests get installed into the staged runtime
venv during `hermes update` / venv rebuild, or (b) the plugin system surfaces a loud, actionable
warning (doctor + gateway startup) when a provider's core module cannot be imported in the *runtime*
venv — and doctor's import probe must use the same interpreter the gateway actually uses.

### Workaround currently in production

External daily systemd timer that import-tests the staged venv, reinstalls plugin deps via
`uv pip install --python <staged-venv> mnemosyne-memory==3.11.1 mnemosyne-hermes==0.3.1 PyYAML fastembed sqlite-vec cryptography`,
and restarts gateways — plus a hook at the end of the local update script. Works, but shouldn't be
necessary.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install a native provider plugin whose Python package lives in Hermes' venv (e.g. mnemosyne).
2. Run `hermes update` (pulls enough commits to rebuild the staged venv).
3. Ask the agent to call any tool of that provider → provider unavailable.
4. `hermes plugins doctor` → green, masking the failure.

### Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.21.5+8673.g90a7ccc (2026.9.24), install method: git
- Linux 6.8.0-146-generic, Python 3.14.7 runtime venv (staged), legacy venv: Python 3.11.15
- Gateway: systemd (user) units, 6 profiles

title: Weekly audit: web-scanner 2026-07-19
body:
## Summary

Six bugs fixed across dependencies, tests, and production code. All 92 runnable tests pass after these changes (up from 74 pass / 7 fail / 11 error in the pre-audit baseline).

---

## Fixes

### 1. `requirements.txt` — missing deps and broken bcrypt pin
**File:** `requirements.txt`

- `passlib` 1.7.x reads `bcrypt.__about__` which was removed in bcrypt 5.x. Added `bcrypt>=3.2,<4.0` to keep the compatible series. This fixed 7 password-hashing test failures.
- `beautifulsoup4` is imported by `scanner/extractor.py` but was absent from `requirements.txt`, causing `ModuleNotFoundError` on collection. Added `beautifulsoup4>=4.12`. This fixed 11 test collection errors.

### 2. `tests/conftest.py` — `app_client` fixture never started the worker
**File:** `tests/conftest.py:69`

`TestClient(main.app)` was returned without a context manager, so the FastAPI lifespan never fired and `start_worker()` was never called. Scans queued during tests stayed `"pending"` forever. Fixed by switching to `with TestClient(main.app) as client: yield client`.

### 3. `tests/test_graph_api.py`, `tests/test_integration_scan_flow.py` — POST /scan/ sent query params instead of JSON body
**Files:** `tests/test_graph_api.py:60,201`, `tests/test_integration_scan_flow.py:30`

Commit `9df4bcb` moved `POST /scan/` to `Body(...)` (JSON body) but the tests still used `params=` (query string), getting 422 from FastAPI. Fixed all three call sites to use `json=`.

### 4. `app/scans/scans_router.py` — stale `response_model` on `GET /scan/{job_id}`
**File:** `app/scans/scans_router.py:186`

`response_model=Union[List[ScanTarget], Dict[str, str]]` was left over from when the endpoint only returned targets. After the task-queue was extended to return a rich result dict (findings, stats, crawl_graph, etc.), FastAPI raised `ResponseValidationError` on every completed-scan fetch. Removed the constraint.

### 5. `app/db/database.py` — `insert_vulnerability` hardcoded `confirmed=1`
**File:** `app/db/database.py:806`

All vulnerabilities were stored as `confirmed=1` regardless of whether the scanner confirmed the finding via a second request. `VulnerabilityTester.confirm_findings` controls this flag at scan time; the DB layer must honour it. Added `confirmed` keyword argument (default `False`) and updated the `task_queue.py` call site to extract and pass `confirmed` from each finding.

### 6. `app/scanner/vulnerability_tester.py` — three bugs
**File:** `app/scanner/vulnerability_tester.py`

**6a. Dead code (`_test_sqli_error_based`, line ~744):** `response_text = resp.text.lower()` was assigned but never read; the subsequent loop used `resp.text` directly with `re.IGNORECASE`. Removed the dead assignment.

**6b. `_confirm_xss` drops all params except the one under test (line ~1040):** `test_params = {param: variation}` replaced the full params dict, so endpoints that require multiple parameters (e.g. forms with hidden fields) received incomplete requests and never reflected the payload — causing false negatives. Added `params` argument and replaced with `params.copy(); test_params[param] = variation`.

**6c. `_test_security_headers` checks wrong Set-Cookie header per cookie (line ~1655):** `resp.headers.get('Set-Cookie', '')` is inside a `for cookie in resp.cookies` loop but returns only the last collapsed header value, not the one belonging to the current cookie. When a response sets multiple cookies, HttpOnly/SameSite attributes are checked against the wrong cookie's header. Fixed by collecting all Set-Cookie lines with `.getlist()` once before the loop and finding the line whose name prefix matches the current cookie.

### 7. `app/scans/scans_router.py` — `GET /scan/{job_id}/logs` bypassed `_authorize_job_access`
**File:** `app/scans/scans_router.py:228`

The logs endpoint had its own inline auth check that was inconsistent with the `_authorize_job_access` helper used by every other scan endpoint. The inline code checked `request.state.user` but skipped the DB-level ownership/role check performed by `get_scan_by_id` inside `_authorize_job_access`. Replaced the ad-hoc code with a single `_authorize_job_access` call.

---

## Noticed but not fixed

- **`_test_xxe` bypasses `_make_request`** (`vulnerability_tester.py`): uses `self.session.post(...)` directly, skipping the rate-limit delay and thread-safe session logic in `_make_request`. Leaving as a TODO — fixing requires threading through proxy/timeout settings or calling `_make_request` with raw XML body support, which touches more than 5 lines of supporting logic.
- **`ScanTarget` import is unused after response_model removal** (`scans_router.py`): the `from scanner.models import ScanTarget` import is now dead. Low risk; left for a cleanup pass.
- **`validate_session` manual datetime parsing** (`database.py`): parses SQLite datetime strings with multiple format fallbacks instead of using `CAST(... AS REAL)` comparison in SQL. Functional but fragile; left as a TODO.
- **`_reconstruct_cycle` self-loop edge case** (`graph_analyzer.py`): when `from_url == to_url` the while loop never executes and returns a 1-element path. Cosmetic and confined to diagram rendering; left as a TODO.

title: feat(env): Import Origin PR3 环境覆盖度——检查带脚本所需 import，not_found / import_error 分开，授权检查如实标注已执行
body:
## 这个 PR 做什么

Import Origin Resolver 的第三步（PR3，`risk:high`）：**环境覆盖度**。用户点了「检查环境」之后，每个候选环境不只回答「它能不能跑 Tavotto」，还回答「这个脚本要的 import 它装齐了没有」，而且把「没装」和「装了但导入失败」分开说。依赖门 / 自动检测读的是同一份结论，不再各量一遍。

默认采用模式仍是叠栈的 `detect`（ADR 0114 §六）：本 PR **不重做**自动检测，也不改任何推荐顺序或决定。

### 改了什么

1. **探测脚本只加字段**（`projectenv._PROBE_SRC`）：`modules_detail`（`found` / `not_found` / `import_error` / `deferred`）。包在、但它自己的依赖缺（`ModuleNotFoundError.name` 不是被要求的名字）算 `import_error`，不算没装。`modules_ok` 的布尔口径、`ok` / `code` 语义一个字没动。宿主侧每个探测结果带 `execution`（是否运行了环境代码、真 import 了哪些名字），由宿主按自己发出的参数算，不信子进程自报。
2. **`envadvice.check(modules=)`** / `POST /api/engine/environment/check {modules?, coverage?}`：`coverage: true` 由后端从脚本静态算出要量哪些（`deprepair.script_import_names`，即依赖门 / 检测同一份 `_plan_imports`）；名字只认合形状的顶级名、最多 64 个，被丢掉的数出来。不带 `modules` 时调用形状与以前逐字相同。
3. **覆盖度只有一份缓存**：写进 `userenvs._probe_cache`（`remember_probe`），键 = 路径 + 环境代 + import 集合（排序，顺序无关）+ 是否内置 + 方式。依赖门 `cache_only`、自动检测、`recommend(modules=)` 读的都是它；`envadvice._verdicts` 仍只存健康摘要。
4. **结构化 detail**（不是发布的错误码，不进 `ERROR_CODES`）：`module_not_found_in_user_environment` / `module_missing_in_target_environment` / `environment_not_checked` / `environment_unusable`，另加 `module_import_failed_in_user_environment` / `..._target_environment`（包在、导入失败——装它救不了）。状态 `covered / partial / missing / unusable / not_checked`：环境本身跑不了 Tavotto（Python 不支持 / 没 matplotlib / worker 起不来）是 `unusable`，**不看模块、不当缺包**；没量过 / 被重建换代 / 延后到运行是 `not_checked`，不冒充装齐也不冒充没装齐。`versions_checked` 恒 false——已装版本满不满足声明归 `distmeta`。
5. **授权检查不宣称无副作用**：它真 import 那些包 = 执行它们的 `__init__`（解释器正常启动，`.pth` 也会跑）。结果的 `executed`（起了几个候选、import 了哪些名字、`side_effect_free: false`）与每个候选覆盖度的 `executed_user_code` 如实标注。
6. **顺带修 #889**（单独一个提交，`distmeta`）：①有未建模的 `.pth` 钩子（`uncovered_paths > 0`）不确认唯一提供者，报 `unverified`；②editable finder 读得到却读不出 `MAPPING`（`dict(...)`、推导式、变量、语法错误、没有 `MAPPING`）置 incomplete；③声明约束与已装版本的冲突在所有 provenance 下都报。
7. `web/src/lib/api.ts`：类型与请求参数（同源对已登记，测试读 TS 导出数组、顺序也比）。没有改任何组件，展示归 PR6。

### 安全

- 默认扫描 / `recommend` / 依赖门 `cache_only` / `distmeta` 静态解析：候选环境子进程 **0**、不执行用户代码。测试武装 `Popen` / `exec*` / `spawn*` / `socket.connect`，用恶意包（`__init__` 写 `SIDE_EFFECT`）+ 启动期 `.pth` 验证默认路径后文件不存在；授权检查后文件存在，且结果标注已执行。AST 门禁：读侧函数不引用探测入口，探测入口只被 `_check` / `adopt_candidate` 引用。
- 没有安装、没有猜 PyPI 名、没有新增或改动已发布错误码；覆盖度只回名字与状态，HTTP 响应不含绝对路径。

### 测试

- 新增 `tests/test_environment_coverage.py`：夹具 A–J（A 无第三方 / B `.venv` 装齐 / C 缺一个 + 装了但坏 / D 内置缺而用户环境有 / E 版本冲突不被覆盖度掩盖 / F 同 base 两个 venv 不因 realpath 合并 / G 被重建旧结论对不上 / H 不支持的 Python / I worker import 失败 / J 全局解释器设置），显式选择不被覆盖、unsupported 与 missing 分对、缓存合一、零子进程、有副作用声明、HTTP 校验、同源对。
- `tests/test_import_origin_metadata.py::TestIssue889`。`test_reading_and_scanning_execute_no_pth_sitecustomize_package_or_finder` 的预期随 #889 ① 变化（那个环境里有一行没建模的 `import` `.pth`，`evilpkg` 现在是 `unverified`）。
- 每条新判据做过变异反证（见 PR 评论 / 实施记录）。

### 风险与未验证范围

- Codex 安全评审已于 4b458e62a 自动完成，未发现安全问题。
- 评审跟进：完整评审 2 条 P2 + 定向复核 1 条 P2 + 后续自动评审 2 条 P2 已修；1 条 P2（全局覆盖下的 target 角色标签）转 #908，须在 PR4 消费覆盖度前修。
- 没有跑 `full-ci`（Windows 重腿）：真 venv 用例在 macOS 本机验证；Windows 上假解释器脚本用例按 `posix_only` 跳过，真 venv 用例依赖 `WORKER_PY`。
- 没有真机验证 Conda / pyenv 候选的覆盖度（候选枚举未改，探测同一入口）。
- 内置 runtime 的覆盖度只读依赖门留下的缓存，`check` 仍不把内置当候选。

### 留给 PR4

`depplan` 消费来源字段与覆盖度（`import_failed` 不算「装它就好」、`unverified` / 多候选不再算 `missing`）；依赖门展示覆盖度 detail；把 `distmeta.Index` 接到默认扫描；PR6 的展示。详见 `docs/implementation/import-origin-resolver/00_BASELINE.md` §11。

_Requested by **Leigh** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_015qz9BUWm96Jk8Xa9bYoMqw?thread=cmsg_015qz9BUWm96Jk8Xa9bYoMqwTQJea9aXXWy974fyaCshQK)_

Before: following CONTRIBUTING (`pip install -e ".[dev]"`, then `pytest`) gave a red suite. 39 TER 3 tests failed with `ModuleNotFoundError: sentence_transformers`, so a new contributor's first run looked broken.

After: the same setup gives `3386 passed, 39 skipped`. Each skip names the install command (`pytest -rs` lists them). CI installs the extra and sets `TER_REQUIRE_EMBEDDINGS=1`, which turns the skip off, so in CI those tests always run and a missing model fails loudly instead of hiding behind a skip.

How: the 39 tests that run the real embedding model carry an `embeddings` marker (in `.feature` files, an `@embeddings` scenario tag). The marker was applied per test, matched exactly to the 39 that fail without the extra. A `pytest_collection_modifyitems` hook in the root `conftest.py` adds the skip only when `sentence_transformers` is not importable and `TER_REQUIRE_EMBEDDINGS` is unset. `constraints/dev.txt` now caps ruff below 0.16 like `constraints/ci.txt`, so a local lint matches CI. CONTRIBUTING, the contributing guide and the testing guide describe the new behaviour.

Vision points: none. This changes contributor tooling only, not TER 4 behaviour.

Checked locally: ruff format/check clean, `ter-req lint --strict` clean, full suite `3386 passed, 39 skipped` without the extra, and with `TER_REQUIRE_EMBEDDINGS=1` the same 39 run (and fail here, since the extra isn't installed).

title: feat(harness): OpenSpec minimum runnable Hatchet/PG dual-SDK loop + Run Inspector
body:
## Scope / verified behavior

Implements OpenSpec `minimal-run-closed-loop` (Proposal / **4** Specs / Design / Tasks) with **real PostgreSQL 16 in Docker** and *separate engine vs business databases*.

- Thin POC `PgFacts`: own Domain Run/Step, initial Plan, Outbox, Provider WorkflowRun Binding, monotonic Event log and business terminal, with no second scheduler/Worker history.
- Actual Hatchet Embedded v0.110.5 + SDK 1.42.1 DAG, invokes **real** public Pydantic AI 2.54.0 then OpenAI Agents 0.23.1 SDK via existing runtime SPI; deterministic local model (zero external LLM).
- Model-only task: **0 Cube Sandbox**, no Shell/privileged Tool.
- Required localhost-only Run Inspector: POST a real Run, query PG Step/Attempt/results/Provider ID and 14 persisted Events, restart Inspector and requery original Run.
- Docker Compose service, optional trusted mirror/cache base image, embedded Sidecar binary cache volume.
- Separate backend HTTP contract tests and **real Hatchet/SDK/PG/Inspector black-box** CI. No faked SDK as real POC evidence.
- Explicit post-implementation retrospective under `docs/retrospectives/MINIMAL_CLOSED_LOOP_20261010.md` and permanent AGENTS.md **Red→Green→Refactor→Live→Retrospective** engineering policy.

## Architecture review / ownership

**Affected Gxx:** G01/G02 Domain ownership, G05 model-only zero Sandbox, G07 UNKNOWN & side-effect safety, G08 business terminal, G19 Process SPI decoupling (and corresponding HC-01/02/03 boundaries). **No Accepted Contract was changed.**

- Harness: business Run/Step state, fact projection, Outbox and Event; Hatchet: technical Workflow/Task/DAG/Worker/Retry state; public AgentRuntime SDK adapter: model invocation; Cube: NOT_REQUIRED_MODEL_ONLY.
- Provider Workflow IDs remain opaque bindings; SDK `runtime.run.completed` is distinct from the single platform `run.completed`; UNKNOWN workflow creation ACK blocks blind repeat dispatch.
- No direct domain import of Hatchet, no shell in shared Host, no 2PC, no new orchestration scheduler.
- Local passwords are disposable development fixtures, never production credentials; Inspector binds only 127.0.0.1 on Host.

## Test-first evidence

- **Red**: Inspector contract test initially failed `ModuleNotFoundError`; PG negative test exposed 3 accidental `run.completed` events due to SDK/Domain conflation.
- **Green**: `PgFacts`, `create_app`, static Inspector and event namespacing; seven **non-skipped** Docker PG/API contract tests PASS; eight architecture guard tests PASS; strict OpenSpec validation PASS.
- **Real E2E**: Local `docker compose --profile demo run --rm loop` => Run `loop-58d0a1b9d4e94fc395dfc9c65baaf1f0`, Workflow `28ffde83-762e-4c97-8fe6-6889486d312e`, 2 SDKs / one Attempt per Step / 14 events / business COMPLETED. Browser backend E2E Run `run-1f9cc8929f534de3b5f273701c59c543`, Workflow `9ab4e1ad-7ef0-416e-9d51-94c6291bc4d0`; Inspector restart+same Run query PASS.
- **Clean CI PASS**: [Real combined workflow](https://github.com/Bulls1986/Agent-Harness-Platform/actions/runs/38037718378), [architecture checks](https://github.com/Bulls1986/Agent-Harness-Platform/actions/runs/38037718366). Later revisions to docs/AGENTS only, final head CI must pass before merge.
- Documentation/navigation: 185 links/no broken targets in current local validation; `git diff --check` PASS.

## Deferrals are NOT completed scope

OpenSpec change accepts only the **limited model-only** closed loop. Full HC-02 Provider-side ACK dedup/reconciliation and real non-idempotent Tool Receipt; HC-03 true Cube/Lease/Fencing Worker A→B recovery; live Token SSE/Approval/100 concurrent Run capacity; legacy PDLC M0–M4 migration remain OPEN in Development Backlog and architecture TODOs. No production GO claimed.

## Review/merge gate

Once CI on final head SHA is fully green, squash merge. Follow-up: mark last OpenSpec merge checkbox, archive completed change into baseline Specs and write final closure note; do not archive future production gates as completed.

title: fix(camera): load on Home Assistant before 2026.1 (#574)
body:
Since 1.23.1 `camera.py` imports `homeassistant.components.web_rtc`, which only exists from HA 2026.1. On 2025.11/2025.12 (our declared floor) setup fails with `ModuleNotFoundError`.

The import is now feature-detected. Older versions read the ICE server getters the camera component keeps in `hass.data["camera_webrtc_ice_servers"]` (which includes HA's STUN default), the same list the camera component itself uses there. The new test reloads `camera.py` with `web_rtc` absent; it fails on main with the reporter's error.

I also checked every HA import in the integration against the 2025.11.0 source. This was the only one missing.

Requests to Ajax: none added. Bumps to 1.24.0-beta.2.

Relates to #574

--- ### Release Notes
pytest-dev/pytest (pytest) ### [`v9.0.3`](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/releases/tag/9.0.3) [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/compare/9.0.2...9.0.3) ### pytest 9.0.3 (2026-04-07) #### Bug fixes - [#​12444](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12444): Fixed `pytest.approx` which now correctly takes into account `~collections.abc.Mapping` keys order to compare them. - [#​13634](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13634): Blocking a `conftest.py` file using the `-p no:` option is now explicitly disallowed. Previously this resulted in an internal assertion failure during plugin loading. Pytest now raises a clear `UsageError` explaining that conftest files are not plugins and cannot be disabled via `-p`. - [#​13734](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13734): Fixed crash when a test raises an exceptiongroup with `__tracebackhide__ = True`. - [#​14195](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14195): Fixed an issue where non-string messages passed to unittest.TestCase.subTest() were not printed. - [#​14343](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14343): Fixed use of insecure temporary directory (CVE-2025-71176). #### Improved documentation - [#​13388](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13388): Clarified documentation for `-p` vs `PYTEST_PLUGINS` plugin loading and fixed an incorrect `-p` example. - [#​13731](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13731): Clarified that capture fixtures (e.g. `capsys` and `capfd`) take precedence over the `-s` / `--capture=no` command-line options in `Accessing captured output from a test function `. - [#​14088](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14088): Clarified that the default `pytest_collection` hook sets `session.items` before it calls `pytest_collection_finish`, not after. - [#​14255](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14255): TOML integer log levels must be quoted: Updating reference documentation. #### Contributor-facing changes - [#​12689](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12689): The test reports are now published to Codecov from GitHub Actions. The test statistics is visible [on the web interface](https://app.codecov.io/gh/pytest-dev/pytest/tests). \-- by `aleguy02` ### [`v9.0.2`](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/releases/tag/9.0.2) [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/compare/9.0.1...9.0.2) ### pytest 9.0.2 (2025-12-06) #### Bug fixes - [#​13896](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13896): The terminal progress feature added in pytest 9.0.0 has been disabled by default, except on Windows, due to compatibility issues with some terminal emulators. You may enable it again by passing `-p terminalprogress`. We may enable it by default again once compatibility improves in the future. Additionally, when the environment variable `TERM` is `dumb`, the escape codes are no longer emitted, even if the plugin is enabled. - [#​13904](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13904): Fixed the TOML type of the `tmp_path_retention_count` settings in the API reference from number to string. - [#​13946](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13946): The private `config.inicfg` attribute was changed in a breaking manner in pytest 9.0.0. Due to its usage in the ecosystem, it is now restored to working order using a compatibility shim. It will be deprecated in pytest 9.1 and removed in pytest 10. - [#​13965](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13965): Fixed quadratic-time behavior when handling `unittest` subtests in Python 3.10. #### Improved documentation - [#​4492](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/4492): The API Reference now contains cross-reference-able documentation of `pytest's command-line flags `. ### [`v9.0.1`](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/releases/tag/9.0.1) [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/compare/9.0.0...9.0.1) ### pytest 9.0.1 (2025-11-12) #### Bug fixes - [#​13895](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13895): Restore support for skipping tests via `raise unittest.SkipTest`. - [#​13896](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13896): The terminal progress plugin added in pytest 9.0 is now automatically disabled when iTerm2 is detected, it generated desktop notifications instead of the desired functionality. - [#​13904](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13904): Fixed the TOML type of the verbosity settings in the API reference from number to string. - [#​13910](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13910): Fixed UserWarning: Do not expect file\_or\_dir on some earlier Python 3.12 and 3.13 point versions. #### Packaging updates and notes for downstreams - [#​13933](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13933): The tox configuration has been adjusted to make sure the desired version string can be passed into its `package_env` through the `SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION_FOR_PYTEST` environment variable as a part of the release process -- by `webknjaz`. #### Contributor-facing changes - [#​13891](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13891), [#​13942](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13942): The CI/CD part of the release automation is now capable of creating GitHub Releases without having a Git checkout on disk -- by `bluetech` and `webknjaz`. - [#​13933](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13933): The tox configuration has been adjusted to make sure the desired version string can be passed into its `package_env` through the `SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION_FOR_PYTEST` environment variable as a part of the release process -- by `webknjaz`. ### [`v9.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/releases/tag/9.0.0) [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/compare/8.4.2...9.0.0) ### pytest 9.0.0 (2025-11-05) #### New features - [#​1367](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/1367): **Support for subtests** has been added. `subtests ` are an alternative to parametrization, useful in situations where the parametrization values are not all known at collection time. Example: ```python def contains_docstring(p: Path) -> bool: """Return True if the given Python file contains a top-level docstring.""" ... def test_py_files_contain_docstring(subtests: pytest.Subtests) -> None: for path in Path.cwd().glob("*.py"): with subtests.test(path=str(path)): assert contains_docstring(path) ``` Each assert failure or error is caught by the context manager and reported individually, giving a clear picture of all files that are missing a docstring. In addition, `unittest.TestCase.subTest` is now also supported. This feature was originally implemented as a separate plugin in [pytest-subtests](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-subtests), but since then has been merged into the core. > \[!NOTE] > This feature is experimental and will likely evolve in future releases. By that we mean that we might change how subtests are reported on failure, but the functionality and how to use it are stable. - [#​13743](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13743): Added support for **native TOML configuration files**. While pytest, since version 6, supports configuration in `pyproject.toml` files under `[tool.pytest.ini_options]`, it does so in an "INI compatibility mode", where all configuration values are treated as strings or list of strings. Now, pytest supports the native TOML data model. In `pyproject.toml`, the native TOML configuration is under the `[tool.pytest]` table. ```toml # pyproject.toml [tool.pytest] minversion = "9.0" addopts = ["-ra", "-q"] testpaths = [ "tests", "integration", ] ``` The `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` table remains supported, but both tables cannot be used at the same time. If you prefer to use a separate configuration file, or don't use `pyproject.toml`, you can use `pytest.toml` or `.pytest.toml`: ```toml # pytest.toml or .pytest.toml [pytest] minversion = "9.0" addopts = ["-ra", "-q"] testpaths = [ "tests", "integration", ] ``` The documentation now (sometimes) shows configuration snippets in both TOML and INI formats, in a tabbed interface. See `config file formats` for full details. - [#​13823](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13823): Added a **"strict mode"** enabled by the `strict` configuration option. When set to `true`, the `strict` option currently enables - `strict_config` - `strict_markers` - `strict_parametrization_ids` - `strict_xfail` The individual strictness options can be explicitly set to override the global `strict` setting. The previously-deprecated `--strict` command-line flag now enables strict mode. If pytest adds new strictness options in the future, they will also be enabled in strict mode. Therefore, you should only enable strict mode if you use a pinned/locked version of pytest, or if you want to proactively adopt new strictness options as they are added. See `strict mode` for more details. - [#​13737](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13737): Added the `strict_parametrization_ids` configuration option. When set, pytest emits an error if it detects non-unique parameter set IDs, rather than automatically making the IDs unique by adding 0, 1, ... to them. This can be particularly useful for catching unintended duplicates. - [#​13072](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13072): Added support for displaying test session **progress in the terminal tab** using the [OSC 9;4;](https://conemu.github.io/en/AnsiEscapeCodes.html#ConEmu_specific_OSC) ANSI sequence. When pytest runs in a supported terminal emulator like ConEmu, Gnome Terminal, Ptyxis, Windows Terminal, Kitty or Ghostty, you'll see the progress in the terminal tab or window, allowing you to monitor pytest's progress at a glance. This feature is automatically enabled when running in a TTY. It is implemented as an internal plugin. If needed, it can be disabled as follows: - On a user level, using `-p no:terminalprogress` on the command line or via an environment variable `PYTEST_ADDOPTS='-p no:terminalprogress'`. - On a project configuration level, using `addopts = "-p no:terminalprogress"`. - [#​478](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/478): Support PEP420 (implicit namespace packages) as --pyargs target when `consider_namespace_packages` is true in the config. Previously, this option only impacted package imports, now it also impacts tests discovery. - [#​13678](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13678): Added a new `faulthandler_exit_on_timeout` configuration option set to "false" by default to let faulthandler interrupt the pytest process after a timeout in case of deadlock. Previously, a faulthandler timeout would only dump the traceback of all threads to stderr, but would not interrupt the pytest process. \-- by `ogrisel`. - [#​13829](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13829): Added support for configuration option aliases via the `aliases` parameter in `Parser.addini() `. Plugins can now register alternative names for configuration options, allowing for more flexibility in configuration naming and supporting backward compatibility when renaming options. The canonical name always takes precedence if both the canonical name and an alias are specified in the configuration file. #### Improvements in existing functionality - [#​13330](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13330): Having pytest configuration spread over more than one file (for example having both a `pytest.ini` file and `pyproject.toml` with a `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` table) will now print a warning to make it clearer to the user that only one of them is actually used. \-- by `sgaist` - [#​13574](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13574): The single argument `--version` no longer loads the entire plugin infrastructure, making it faster and more reliable when displaying only the pytest version. Passing `--version` twice (e.g., `pytest --version --version`) retains the original behavior, showing both the pytest version and plugin information. > \[!NOTE] > Since `--version` is now processed early, it only takes effect when passed directly via the command line. title: Build the FastAPI test app with LOCAL_DEV off
body:
Closes #13587

`docker compose run --rm home make test` — the command in the Quick Start — fails on a clean checkout while CI is green on the same commit. It is now **5** failures, up from the 4 in the original report: `test_qrcode.py::TestQRCodeEndpoint::test_only_get_is_registered` joined as more routes landed, so this grows with the FastAPI migration.

### Technical

`create_app()` registers a catch-all proxy to web.py only in local dev:

```python
# openlibrary/asgi_app.py:279
if get_ol_env().LOCAL_DEV or get_deployment_name() == "testing":
    @app.api_route("/{path:path}", methods=[...])
    async def fallback(request: Request, path: str) -> Response:
```

The `home` container sets `LOCAL_DEV=true`. The five failing tests assert that a path or method is *not* registered — `test_only_get_is_registered` POSTs `/qrcode` expecting 405 — and the proxy captures those requests and forwards them to `web:8080`, which the test container cannot resolve. The assertion sees a `ConnectError` rather than the status it wanted.

The fix builds the test app with the flag off. `LOCAL_DEV` is a `cached_property` on a singleton and is read once, at registration time, so the patch wraps `create_app()` only — request handling still sees the real value.

The other gate on that branch is `get_deployment_name() == "testing"`. The `home` service does not set `OL_DEPLOYMENT_NAME`, so forcing `LOCAL_DEV` off is enough.

This takes option (a), which @pnelson1337 had already shown was safe in the issue thread.

### On the alternative

(b) would keep the proxy registered and give just those five tests their own app. I went with (a) because these five tests assert the route shape CI and production actually have, and (a) costs nothing in coverage: `proxy_to_webpy` is already tested directly in `test_proxy.py`, which builds its own app and is unaffected. What stays untested is the registration branch in `create_app()` — and that had no coverage before this change either.

Happy to switch to (b) if you would rather the test app match the dev app exactly.

### Testing

In the `home` container, where `LOCAL_DEV=true`:

```
before:  5 failed, 617 passed
after:     622 passed
```

Broader run, `openlibrary scripts`: 3241 passed, 16 skipped, 1 xfailed, 0 failed.

Also checked the patch does not leak past `create_app()` — a throwaway test asserting `get_ol_env().LOCAL_DEV is True` after the fixture runs passes, so everything downstream still sees the real value.

`make test-py` with no arguments still cannot complete here — `openlibrary/tests/core` fails to collect with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pytest_postgresql'`. That reproduces on clean master, so it is unrelated to this change, but it does mean the Quick Start command is not fully green even with this fix. Worth a separate issue if it is not already known.

### Stakeholders

@RayBB @pnelson1337

title: Restore CONTROl_TOKENS_PATTERN, used by words-segmentation
body:
## Restore `CONTROl_TOKENS_PATTERN`, used by words-segmentation

#4 removed `CONTROl_TOKENS_PATTERN` from `utf8_tokenizer.control` as unused in this repo. But [words-segmentation](https://github.com/sign/words-segmentation) imports it (`pretokenizer.py`, `languages.py`), so with v0.8.3 `import words_segmentation` fails with an `ImportError`.

The constant is restored byte-identical to v0.8.2. A test now pins it as public API: it matches exactly the non-whitespace control characters.

It was the only top-level name removed between v0.8.2 and v0.8.3.

`python -m durfheilig.modeltest` crashed inside the Docker image with `No module named 'durfheilig.dev'`: modeltest imported `laad_env` from `dev.py`, which `.dockerignore` leaves out of the image on purpose. `laad_env` now lives in its own `env.py`; `dev.py` and `modeltest.py` both import it from there.

- Reported from the server: `docker exec durfheiligtezijn /app/.venv/bin/python -m durfheilig.modeltest --ping ...` raised the ModuleNotFoundError (traceback in the report).

title: ci: run backend, Vitest and E2E tests as required PR checks
body:
Closes #49

## Was und warum

**Workflow `.github/workflows/ci.yml`** – ausgelöst bei `pull_request` und wiederverwendbar per `workflow_call` (für #50). Drei parallele Jobs:

| Job | Inhalt |
|---|---|
| `backend` | Python 3.13 (wie Dockerfile), `pip install -e ".[dev]"`, `pytest tests/ --ignore=tests/e2e` |
| `js` | Node LTS, `npm ci`, `npx vitest run` |
| `e2e` | wie `backend` + Chromium (`playwright install --with-deps`, bei Cache-Treffer nur `install-deps`), `pytest tests/e2e/ --tracing retain-on-failure --screenshot only-on-failure`; bei Fehlschlag/Timeout Upload als Artefakt `playwright-traces` (14 Tage) |

- Actions in ihren aktuellen Major-Versionen (Node-24-Runtime): `checkout@v7`, `setup-python@v7`, `setup-node@v7`, `cache@v6`, `upload-artifact@v7`. Release-Notes geprüft – keine Breaking Changes betreffen diesen Workflow (kein `pull_request_target`, kein `pip-install`-Input, npm-Cache explizit gesetzt).
- Caching: pip, npm, Playwright-Browser (Key = aufgelöste Playwright-Version).
- `concurrency`: neuer Push auf denselben PR bricht den alten Lauf ab; bei `workflow_call`-Aufrufen ohne PR eigene Gruppe pro Lauf, damit #50 keine Läufe verliert.
- Keine automatischen Wiederholungen; `permissions: contents: read`.
- `test_collection_ordering.py` läuft im `backend`-Job (Collect braucht nur das pytest-playwright-Plugin, keinen Browser).

**Traces für alle E2E-Tests** – pytest-playwright zeichnet nur Contexts aus der eigenen `new_context`-Fixture auf. `CompetitionHelper` (und damit u. a. der Regression-Gate `test_competition_flow.py`) sowie die manuellen `browser.new_context`-Aufrufe in 5 Testdateien nutzen jetzt `competition.new_context()` (Locale `en-US` kommt weiterhin aus `browser_context_args`, geprüft). Ohne das wären bei ~2/3 der E2E-Tests keine Traces im Artefakt gelandet. Einzige Ausnahme: `test_rejoin_via_qr_keeps_connect_button_visible` in der VPortal-geschützten `test_vportal_integration.py` – bewusst nicht angefasst, in `docs/testing.md` dokumentiert.

**Doku**: `docs/testing.md` (Abschnitte „Continuous integration“ und „Claude cloud environment setup“ mit Setup-Skript), `.claude/CLAUDE.md` (Unterabschnitt CI), `.gitignore` (`test-results/`).

### Entscheidungen (mit dir geklärt, im Issue festgehalten)
- Action-Referenzen per Major-Tag (auf aktuelle Node-24-Majors gehoben); Trigger nur `pull_request` + `workflow_call` (Push auf `main` → #50); kein CHANGELOG-Eintrag (für Nutzer/Deployer nicht sichtbar).
- Setup-Skript in den Umgebungseinstellungen, Playwright nicht gepinnt, Domain-Freigabe statt Version-Pinning.

### Ohne Rückfrage gewählte Umsetzungsdetails
- `node-version: lts/*`, Job-Timeouts 15/10/30 min, Artefakt-Aufbewahrung 14 Tage.
- `python -m pytest` in CI (robust gegen fremde `pytest`-Binaries im PATH).
- Das Setup-Skript entfernt das vorinstallierte uv-`pytest` der Cloud-VM, das sonst das Projekt-pytest überschattet (`ModuleNotFoundError: httpx`).

## Einrichtung durch den Maintainer (erledigt)
- [x] Netzwerkfreigabe der Claude-Cloud-Umgebung: `cdn.playwright.dev`, `cdn.jsdelivr.net` (letztere bis #54)
- [x] Setup-Skript aus `docs/testing.md` eingetragen – Verifikation in der nächsten neuen Cloud-Session (Pfad `/home/user/iron_verdict`, komplette Suite ohne Workaround)
- [x] Branch Protection auf `main`: PR erforderlich, Checks `backend`/`js`/`e2e` erforderlich, Branch muss aktuell sein, keine Pflicht-Freigabe (im Chat bestätigt)

## Testnachweis

Lokal (Cloud-Sandbox, Python 3.11):
- `python -m pytest tests/ --ignore=tests/e2e -q` → **159 passed**
- `npx vitest run` → **14 passed**
- `python -m pytest tests/e2e/ -q` → **74 passed** (lokal mit einem nicht committeten Shim, der die jsdelivr-Dateien aus dem npm-Registry liefert, weil die Sandbox das CDN damals blockierte; Playwright 1.56 passend zum vorinstallierten Chromium)
- Trace-Nachweis: temporärer, absichtlich roter Test mit `competition`-Fixture → 3 Traces + 3 Screenshots in `test-results/` (Test danach gelöscht)

CI (Python 3.13.15) – Details im [Nachweis-Kommentar](https://github.com/abti247/iron_verdict/pull/75#issuecomment-5994741894):
- [x] Alle drei Jobs grün ([Lauf](https://github.com/abti247/iron_verdict/actions/runs/37311005431); nach Revert: [Lauf](https://github.com/abti247/iron_verdict/actions/runs/37311937061); mit neuen Action-Versionen: [Lauf](https://github.com/abti247/iron_verdict/actions/runs/37631462554), keine Node-20-Warnung mehr)
- [x] Laufzeit: backend ≈ 25–35 s, js ≈ 10 s, e2e ≈ 3 min 10–25 s → **Pipeline ≈ 3,5 min**
- [x] Demo: absichtlich roter Test (`d70ab20`) → `e2e` rot ([Lauf](https://github.com/abti247/iron_verdict/actions/runs/37311461908), `1 failed, 74 passed`), Artefakt `playwright-traces` herunterladbar, revertiert in `50a2136`
- [x] Branch Protection aktiv – ein roter Pflicht-Check blockiert damit den Merge

## Review (`live-reliability-reviewer`)
- 1. Lauf: keine Blocker. **Should:** (a) Traces fehlten für alle Tests mit selbst erzeugten Contexts → behoben (s. o.); (b) Concurrency-Gruppe hätte bei `workflow_call` Läufe von `main` verwerfen können → behoben. Notes umgesetzt: Upload auch bei Timeout, Doku-Präzisierungen (Tabelle, Branch-Protection-Formulierung in CLAUDE.md, jsdelivr-Hinweis).
- 2. Lauf: keine Blocker/Should; doppeltes Schließen und Artefakt-Zeitpunkt geprüft und unkritisch. Notes umgesetzt: Workflow-Name wieder in der Concurrency-Gruppe, Trace-Umfang bei Timeout präzisiert, Hinweis auf Tracing-Overhead bei CI-only-Flakes.

title: Spook 5.10.0 fails to load on HA 2026.11.0.dev: cannot import name 'CONF_STOP_ACTIONS'
body:
### Describe the issue

Spook 5.10.0 fails to load on Home Assistant Core `2026.11.0.dev202610090234`. The import of `spook/timed_states.py` fails because `CONF_STOP_ACTIONS` no longer exists in `homeassistant.components.automation`, so the whole integration is not set up.

### Environment

- Spook version: 5.10.0 (latest release)
- Home Assistant Core: 2026.11.0.dev202610090234 (dev channel)
- Installation type: Home Assistant OS
- Python: 3.14

### Log output

```
ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.setup] Setup failed for custom integration 'spook': Unable to import component: cannot import name 'CONF_STOP_ACTIONS' from 'homeassistant.components.automation' (/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/automation/__init__.py)
...
  File "/config/custom_components/spook/__init__.py", line 32, in <module>
    from .timed_states import async_setup_timed_states
  File "/config/custom_components/spook/timed_states.py", line 12, in <module>
    from homeassistant.components.automation import (
    ...<2 lines>...
    )
ImportError: cannot import name 'CONF_STOP_ACTIONS' from 'homeassistant.components.automation'
```

### Additional context

`timed_states.py` (new in the 5.9/5.10 line) imports `CONF_STOP_ACTIONS` from `homeassistant.components.automation`. That constant is not available in the current HA dev build. Possible fix: define the constant locally (`"stop_actions"`) or fall back via `try/except ImportError` instead of importing it from core.
