Updates `multidict` from 6.7.1 to 6.9.1
Release notes

Sourced from multidict's releases.

6.9.1

Bug fixes

  • Fixed the C extension reading freed memory on free-threaded builds when a list handed to :py:meth:~multidict.MultiDict.update, :py:meth:~multidict.MultiDict.extend, :py:meth:~multidict.MultiDict.merge or the :py:class:~multidict.MultiDict and :py:class:~multidict.CIMultiDict constructors, a [key, value] item inside any iterable handed to them, or a list tested with in against :py:meth:~multidict.MultiDict.items, is changed by another thread; a call that catches the list shrinking under it now raises :py:exc:RuntimeError -- by :user:rodrigobnogueira.

    Related issues and pull requests on GitHub: #1437.

  • Fixed a data race on the free-threaded build where a retired hash table's reader count used relaxed atomics, letting a lock-free get()/getone()/ __getitem__() read race a concurrent free of that table. The reader-exit decrement and the drain's free check now use release/acquire ordering instead -- by :user:asvetlov.

    Related issues and pull requests on GitHub: #1481.

  • Fixed a free-threaded build bug where two threads calling update(), merge(), or __setitem__() on the same key at the same time could lose the key entirely instead of just racing on which value wins. A decref of the replaced value could transiently suspend the writer's critical section, letting a second writer for the same key observe the first writer's in-progress entry as absent and, once both settled, mistake it for a stale duplicate and delete it. Every such decref is now deferred until the writer has released its critical section, so the window can no longer open. setdefault() had an unrelated instance of the same blind spot (it could insert a duplicate rather than recognizing an in-flight key), fixed alongside it -- by :user:asvetlov.

    Related issues and pull requests on GitHub: #1483.

  • Fixed a free-threaded build bug where getall() and the items()/ keys()/values() equality path could raise KeyError or report a present, never-deleted key as missing. A concurrent update()/extend()/ __setitem__() call can have its critical section transiently suspended (a decref triggering a blocking allocator call) while an entry is marked as part of its own bookkeeping; a reader landing in that window used to treat the mark as "not found" instead of "still there, in flight" -- by :user:asvetlov.

## Moves

This slice moves the component transitions out of `kstrl/pipeline.py` into the layer class `Transitions` (L7) in `kstrl/pipeline_transitions.py` (581 lines).

- The module names `Transition`, `FailureAction` and `PhaseFailure` also move.
- `Transitions` has the parent classes `InboxDesk`, `AttemptRecorder` and `UsageLedger`. `ComponentPipeline` has the parent class `Transitions`.
- `kstrl/pipeline.py` has 3539 lines (4096 before the move). It has more than 800 lines because the slices P4 to P6 move the remaining phases (B3).
- No name is re-exported. Six test files import `Transition` or `FailureAction` from the new module.

## Checks on head 4645e943 (base commit `0e181d1c`)

- A2: `integ_move_check.py` gives 104 same, 0 changed and 0 missing. A script compares each full class text of `Transition`, `FailureAction` and `PhaseFailure`: all same. A second script compares the removed lines and the added lines of the diff. The lines that did not move are imports, the module docstring and the two class headers.
- A3: the full suite gives 7974 passed, 171 skipped and 109 xfailed. These counts are the same as the counts of the base commit.
- A4: `mypy --strict` (209 files), `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean.

## Pins and plants (A6)

Each pin value comes from a guard operation. For each guard with a changed row, one mutation was planted in `kstrl/pipeline_transitions.py`, with no `__pycache__`, `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` and a 420 s limit. All 10 plants were caught. No plant stayed green, hung or could not be planted.

title: docs: stop describing the SDK's scale as a 120 mm nominal
body:
## Summary

The console's prose and one self-test fixture were built on an assumption the SDK no
longer holds: that `rad_to_mm` in a calibration file is a nominal 120 mm of stroke over
the recorded span. That 120 mm belonged to no gripper in the family.

The SDK now derives its scale from the **measured 85 mm jaw travel plus the probe's 1 mm
inset** (`86 / 1.409552 = 61.01229326764816`), and `max_stroke_mm` defaults to that same
measurement. A file the SDK writes at its default therefore reproduces the console's own
`derive_scale` bit-for-bit, which is what makes the two numbers comparable at all.

Nothing the console *does* changes here — no threshold, no formula, no default. What
changes is that the console's own documentation and its self-test no longer describe the
SDK as carrying a number it does not carry. Each passage keeps the conclusion it was
written to support; only the premise is corrected.

The console still **never** reads `rad_to_mm` from a file (it derives it from the recorded
travel), because files written before 2026-10-10 genuinely do carry the older number, and
because a file's copy describes the stroke it was *configured* with rather than the unit
on the bench — the corrected wording says exactly that, which is the reason that rule
survives.

## Changes

- `src/litegrip_studio/constants.py` — `DEFAULT_TRAVEL_MM` is no longer described as
  "deliberately NOT the SDK's number"; it agrees with the SDK's default now, and diverges
  from any file written before 2026-10-10. The `RAD_TO_MM_MIN`/`RAD_TO_MM_MAX` comment
  stops calling the field a measurement.
- `src/litegrip_studio/calibration.py` — `validate_limits` and `limits_from_file`
  docstrings now say the field is a configured stroke over a recorded span; this is why
  the accepted range stays as wide as it is.
- `src/litegrip_studio/units.py` — `derive_scale` and `Limits` docstrings carry the same
  correction, so "never read the file's scale" keeps its reason.
- `README.md`, `README_ZH.md` — the three passages that quote the SDK's 120 mm nominal,
  including the date the default changed.
- `src/litegrip_studio/selftest.py` — the dataset that carried `120/1.14` as "the SDK
  default" is relabelled for what it is (a file written before 2026-10-10), and a fourth
  entry pins today's default (`86/1.14`), which agrees with the derivation by
  construction. The direction check's name no longer counts the datasets it walks. The new
  entry is appended **last** on purpose: the direction check addresses the first three by
  index.
- `tests/test_selftest.py` — the docstring of the test that defeats the travel check says
  which file's scale it is restoring, instead of "what the SDK does".

## Testing

```console
$ env -u LITEGRIP_SDK_PATH QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen python3 -m pytest -q \
    tests/test_selftest.py tests/test_calibration.py tests/test_units.py \
    --continue-on-collection-errors
186 passed in 0.29s

$ env -u LITEGRIP_SDK_PATH ./run_litegrip_studio.sh selftest
10/10 项通过

$ env -u LITEGRIP_SDK_PATH QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen python3 -m pytest -q \
    --continue-on-collection-errors
1 failed, 766 passed, 1 skipped, 11 errors in 7.89s

$ npx --yes markdownlint-cli2@0.23.3 "README.md" "README_ZH.md" "src/litegrip/VENDORED.md"
Summary: 0 issues in 0 files
```

Two limitations in the full-suite run, neither caused by this change:

- **11 collection errors**: `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'PyQt5'`. PyQt5 is
  installed nowhere on this workstation and `litegrip_studio` is not pip-installed here,
  so the UI half of the suite cannot run locally. CI installs the package and covers it.
- **1 failure**: `tests/test_suite_isolation.py::TestTheSuiteHasAHomeOfItsOwn::test_an_exported_calibration_path_does_not_reach_the_suite`,
  `subprocess.CalledProcessError` exit status 1. **Verified pre-existing and unrelated** by
  running that single test on a pristine checkout of `main` in a throwaway worktree:
  `1 failed, 3 passed`. The subprocess is handed `PYTHONPATH=SDK_PATHS` only, so it cannot
  import a non-installed `litegrip_studio`.

The console's derived coefficient was checked against the SDK's written one directly:

```console
$ env -u LITEGRIP_SDK_PATH PYTHONPATH=src python3 -c \
    "from litegrip_studio.units import derive_scale; print(repr(derive_scale(1.409552)))"
61.01229326764816
```

which is `(85 + 1) / 1.409552` — the same double the SDK now writes.

## Issues

None. No issue tracks this; it is the console half of the geometry correction already
open as litegrip-python#38 and litegrip-cpp#24.

title: feat(presence): declare the agent's status in the chat snapshot
body:
## Summary

The `kazi` bot is a room participant but never opens a WebSocket, so the presence snapshot always reported it `offline`, and `notify_room_message` treated it as an offline human and created an unread notification for it.

This declares the bot's status instead of inferring it from a socket. A new `chatbot/presence.agent_status()` returns `online` when a message sent now would reach a model (at least one catalog provider has a key configured) and `offline` otherwise. The snapshot loop uses that for the bot, tags every entry with `kind` (`agent` or `human`), and `notify_room_message` skips the bot.

This is PR 1 of two; the per-connection store follows separately.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Test-only

## Scope

- `Backend/chatbot/presence.py` (new) — `agent_status()` only.
- `Backend/chatbot/consumers.py` — the snapshot loop uses `agent_status()` for the bot and adds `kind` to every entry.
- `Backend/notifications/services.py` — `notify_room_message` skips the bot.
- Tests: `Backend/chatbot/test_presence.py` (new), `Backend/notifications/tests.py`.

## Validation

- [x] `python Backend/manage.py test chatbot notifications`
- [ ] `python Backend/manage.py check`

title: [github_actions] `extra-arguments` can override run-identity inputs and desynchronize the litellm install
body:
## Problem

```python
# .github/scripts/action_runner.py:44-49
command += extra + ["--output", outputs["json"], "--junit-output", outputs["junit"]]
```

User `extra-arguments` are appended **before** the action's own output flags, and only
three tokens are filtered:

```python
# .github/scripts/action_runner.py:47
if item.split("=", 1)[0] in ("--output", "--junit-output", "--resume"):
```

Because argparse takes the last occurrence, `extra-arguments: '["--model",
"openai/gpt-4o"]'` with `model: baseline` silently switches the run to a live
provider. `install_spec` (`action_runner.py:14-19`) derives `extra='[llm]'` from
`INPUT_MODEL` only, so litellm is never installed and the job dies with
`ImportError: litellm is required...`.

`--tasks`, `--task`, `--solution`, `--reference`, `--tier`, `--category`,
`--tasks-root` and `--samples` are equally overridable, so the documented contract at
`action.yml:39` ("artifact paths and resume cannot be overridden") understates the
real surface. `--save-solutions` is not filtered at all and can write candidate C
files anywhere in the consumer repository.

Two related defects in the same file:

- `exit-code` is published raw (`action_runner.py:72,76`). On POSIX, a
  signal-terminated run yields a negative code (`-9`), and `sys.exit(-9)` is truncated
  to 247 by CPython -- so the advertised output and the job's actual status diverge.
- The reservation test is a prefix comparison against a hard-coded tuple, so it will
  miss any future alias (the CLI already ships aliases such as `--multi-turn` and
  `--solutions-dir`).

## Proposal

- Derive the reserved set from the parser's registered option strings for the
  artifact **and** identity options rather than a literal tuple, or reject any `extra`
  token whose flag already appears in the command being built.
- Reserve `--save-solutions`, or default it to a path under `output-directory`.
- Normalize the exit code: `code if code >= 0 else 128 - code`, and publish both the
  raw and normalized values.
- Add a workflow-level test covering `extra-arguments: ["--model", ...]` with
  `model: baseline`.

`spec-kitty next --answer --json` now includes a factual `warnings` entry when the decision log's Git commit fails. An agent can see that decision events may remain uncommitted while the JSON response stays parseable. Existing event writes and commit failure handling are preserved.

body:
## Summary
New Python package `traceAI-ag2-classic` for AG2 Classic (TH-8237): the `autogen` 0.14.x distribution from `ag2ai/ag2classic` @ `86fa5ccb`. It is a native-first enabler on `autogen.opentelemetry` plus an `AG2ClassicSpanProcessor`. It depends on `autogen>=0.14.0,<0.15` only; there is no dependency on `ag2`, `pyautogen` or `autogen-agentchat`.

The provisional mapping cells from the architecture were replaced with what the installed source actually emits (paths under `autogen/opentelemetry/`):

- **Kinds:** the span kind is the custom key `ag2.span.type` (`llm_wrapper.py:74`, `reply.py:36`, `chat.py:33`, `tool.py:26`, `pattern.py:163`). It maps chat to LLM, invoke_agent to AGENT, execute_tool to TOOL, and conversation and speaker_selection to CHAIN.
- **Usage and cost:** usage is emitted (`llm_wrapper.py:121-125`), so no `generate_reply` wrapper is needed. Cost is emitted too (`gen_ai.usage.cost`), and is copied to `gen_ai.cost.total` on LLM spans only.
- **Session:** `session.id` comes from `gen_ai.conversation.id`, on the outermost conversation only. Nested speaker-selection chats would otherwise split the trace into several sessions.
- **Token double-count fixed:** conversation spans put the chat-wide `aggregate_usage` sum on `gen_ai.usage.*` (`chat.py:81-82, 146-147`). fi-collector promotes those keys on any span, and Observe sums tokens over a trace. Now every `gen_ai.usage.*` key, cost included, stays on LLM spans only; the conversation aggregate moves to `ag2.usage.*`. The README notes how cost behaves for cached responses.
- **Content:** the upstream flag only covers the LLM wrapper. Agent, conversation, tool, human-input and code spans always record content (`reply.py:51,58`; `tool.py:36,47`; ...). The processor drops those keys unless `capture_content=True`.
- **Errors:** upstream catches tool exceptions and only sets `error.type`. The processor sets ERROR status from it and runs first, ahead of fi's `BatchSpanProcessor`, which would otherwise turn UNSET into OK.

## Decisions (approved: Nikhil 2026-10-03 blanket)
- **Version guard:** PyPI `autogen==0.14.0` is an alias that installs `ag2==0.14.0`, and that package ships the top-level `autogen` module with an identical `opentelemetry` tree. The guard accepts exactly the autogen 0.14.x + ag2 0.14.x pair and rejects every other `ag2` owner, including 1.x.
- **`setup()` signature:** `setup(agents=..., patterns=...)` returns a handle with `instrument_agent`, `instrument_pattern`, `instrument_a2a_server` (opt-in) and `uninstrument`. Upstream instruments objects one at a time (`agent.py:27`, `pattern.py:23`).

## Tests (run on 2f1a5fc, clean tree, by the coordinator)
```
PYTHONPATH="python/frameworks/ag2-classic:python:python/tests" uv run --no-project --python 3.11 --with pytest --with opentelemetry-api --with opentelemetry-sdk --with opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http --with wrapt --with requests --with jsonschema --with "autogen[openai]==<v>" pytest python/frameworks/ag2-classic/tests python/tests/harness/test_harness.py -q -p no:cacheprovider --noconftest -o addopts= -rs
autogen 0.14.1: 90 passed
autogen 0.14.0: 90 passed
```
The implementer also ran autogen 0.14.1 on Python 3.10 and 3.13 (90 passed each). The documented install was smoke-tested in clean venvs. The old line fails with `ImportError ... 'openai' is not installed`; the new `"autogen[openai]"` line runs the quick start. No files changed outside the package.

## Limits
- No live vendor call, and no real fi-collector.
- Code execution, human input, `initiate_chats`, remote agents and the A2A server are checked by mapping only.
- A classic `GroupChatManager` emits no conversation span of its own upstream.
- LLM spans bind to the first provider that is set up (upstream patches `OpenAIWrapper.create` once).
- The docs draft in company-brain PR #62 still has the provisional cells; the README tables here are the checked versions.

## Review
Round 1, an independent fresh-context review of 96ef5b3 (a subagent, not an installed card): CHANGES_REQUESTED. Fixed test first. All final tests run against 96ef5b3 give 22 failed / 59 passed (assertion or KeyError failures only).

| ID | Finding | Resolution | Commit |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | `uninstrument()` left content dropping off | Content dropping kept after uninstrument | 10e9dd7 |
| R2 | A later `add_span_processor` removed the processor | Kept first across the call | 911cabf |
| R3 | A user span split one trace into two sessions | Non-AG2 spans followed to the outer conversation; tracking bounded | 5805ca0 |
| R4 | `using_attributes` ignored on AG2 spans | Copied on start, without overwriting upstream values | a383f20 |
| R5 | `initiate_chats` sessions | `using_session` gives one session; the default (one per chat) is pinned by a test | a383f20 |
| R6 | `setup()` not atomic | The LLM patch is rolled back when an agent fails | e4540e4 |
| Contract | No usage/cost keys on non-LLM spans | Every `gen_ai.usage.*` key off non-LLM spans (13 failed before) | cb44a2f |
| Missing test | LLM exception path | Real-autogen HTTP 400 test plus contract assertions | 54a587c |
| Nit | `_guard.py` alias description | Corrected (the 0.14.0 wheel is 6 metadata entries) | af1845a |

Round 2: installed pr-reviewer, then pr-verifier, on af1845a. Verdicts will be added here.

### Round 2 follow-ups (af1845a..2f1a5fc)
The installed review passed this PR at `af1845a`: pr-reviewer t_7aba4044 APPROVE, pr-verifier t_52edde89 VERIFIED. Its findings were fixed before the demo. Run against `af1845a`, the new tests give 3 failed and 87 passed (the N4, N5 and N6 tests).

The delta does not touch `_processor.py` or the mapping. The new setup code can only re-enable filtering (N4), add a log line (N5) or skip a restore (N6).

title: CI: torchtitan_features_integration fails at collection with "pyarrow requires NumPy 2.0 or newer, found 1.26.4"
body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

The `torchtitan_features_integration` job fails during pytest **collection** (before any test case runs) with an environment-level dependency conflict:

Failing example (triggered via ciflow on an unrelated dynamo PR):
https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/actions/runs/38022285205/job/114127342177?pr=198099

**How it happens**

1. The workflow uses the `pytorch-linux-jammy-cuda*-py3.12-gcc11` image (since #194260). That image pins `numpy==1.26.4` for py3.11/py3.12 in `.ci/docker/requirements-ci.txt`.
2. The job then runs `pip install torchtitan` (torchtitan 0.2.2 in the failing run), which pulls `datasets==4.7.0` → `pyarrow==26.0.0`. pyarrow ≥ 17 requires numpy ≥ 2.0.
3. pip resolves this as only a warning during install (numpy stays at 1.26.4 to match the torch binary built against the numpy-1.x ABI), and the conflict only explodes at import time:


Since #197604 removed `torchtitan_models_integration` from the matrix, `torchtitan_features_integration` is now the only remaining torchtitan suite — so every PR that gets the torchtitan ciflow tag will hit this wall regardless of its own changes. It is expected to fail identically on trunk scheduled runs of the same workflow.

### Error messages / logs

(install log of the same run shows: `Successfully installed ... datasets-4.7.0 ... pyarrow-26.0.0 ... torchtitan-0.2.2`, with numpy pinned at 1.26.4 from the CI image)

### Proposed fixes (any of)

- Constrain the torchtitan install to a numpy-1-compatible pyarrow, e.g. `pip install "pyarrow<17"` after/before installing torchtitan, or pin `datasets` to a version that does not require pyarrow ≥ 17.
- Install torchtitan in a separate venv from the pinned CI environment for this job.
- Long-term: migrate the py3.12 CI image (and the torchtitan job) to numpy 2.x where the torch binary supports it.

### Repro

Any PR where the torchtitan ciflow tag is applied, e.g. rerunning the failing job above; locally inside the py3.12 CI docker image:

```bash
pip install torchtitan
python -c "import datasets"   # ImportError: pyarrow requires NumPy 2.0 or newer


### Versions

Environment-level issue, not runtime/user-facing. CI job: torchtitan-x-pytorch-build / torchtitan_features_integration, py 3.12, torch nightly 2.16.0a0+gitec0a803

title: fix: lock and verify config rollback
body:
## Result
- Config rollback now takes the per-device config push lock. A second push or rollback on the same device gets HTTP 409 and does not contact the device.
- After apply, Manager reads the config back and compares its hash to the target snapshot. A mismatch or a failed read returns HTTP 502 `rollback_not_verified`, not `success`.
- **Risk: HIGH.** This changes a device write path. Merge waits for exact-head bench proof. The lead runs that proof. This PR has no device or host evidence.

## Issue
Issue URL: https://github.com/sixtyops/manager/issues/311

Closes #311. Closes #37. Closes #39.

## Change
Route: `rollback_device_config` in `updater/app.py`. No OIDC code changed.

- The route validates the target snapshot and device first. It then adds the IP to `_config_pushing_ips` under `_config_push_lock`. This is the same lock that `push_to_device` uses in the immediate push and the phased rollout.
- If the IP is already in the set, the route returns 409 `config_change_in_progress`. It does not log in.
- The device work moved into `_rollback_device_config_locked`. A `finally` block removes the IP from the set on every exit path. A refused request does not remove the other writer's entry.
- After a successful apply, the route calls `get_config()` and computes `_compute_config_hash` on the result. It compares that hash to the hash of the target snapshot config.
- Match: the response adds `rollback_verified: true` and `config_hash`.
- Mismatch, empty read, or read error: the route returns 502 with `code: rollback_not_verified`, `rollback_verified: false`, `expected_hash`, `actual_hash`, and `safety_snapshot_saved`. It logs an error and writes a `config.rollback.unverified` audit entry.
- The background config re-poll still runs in both cases. The stored snapshot then shows the device's actual state.
- The UI needs no change. `rollbackToSnapshot` already shows `detail.message` on an error.

## Validation
- CI lane and run URL: pending on this head.
- Local: `pytest -v --ignore=tests/test_snmp.py`: 2413 passed, 59 skipped. `tests/test_snmp.py` fails to collect in the local venv only (ImportError). CI runs it.
- Tests added in `tests/test_config_push.py`, class `TestRollbackLockAndVerify`:
  - Two concurrent rollbacks on one IP: one applies; the other gets 409 before login.
  - Rollback while a push holds the lock: 409, no device contact, lock entry kept.
  - Read-back hash mismatch: 502 `rollback_not_verified`, audit entry written.
  - Empty read-back: 502 `rollback_not_verified`.
  - Success: `rollback_verified: true`, correct hash, lock released.
- Tests changed: two `TestRollbackSafetySnapshot` tests now give a matching read-back. Before, they reused one `get_config` result for both reads.

## Device test plan
Bench only, on lab devices that Isaac names. No production devices.

1. **Bench, exact head.** Deploy this head to the dev host. Pick one lab AP with two config snapshots.
   - Roll back to the older snapshot. Expect 200 with `rollback_verified: true`.
   - Read back #1: fetch the config from the device and hash it. It must equal `config_hash` in the response.
   - Read back #2: wait for the next config poll. The latest stored `config_hash` must equal the same value.
   - Roll forward to the newer snapshot. Repeat both read-backs.
2. **Lock.** Start a config push to the lab AP. While it runs, request a rollback on the same AP. Expect 409 `config_change_in_progress` and no second login in the device log.
3. **Mismatch check.** Record whether a real Tachyon device returns a config that hashes equal to the snapshot it accepted. If the device adds or reorders values, every rollback will report 502. Report the diff before merge.
4. **Canary.** After bench passes, run one verified rollback on one more lab device of a different model family.
5. **Window.** Run the bench steps inside a maintenance window on the dev host. Confirm the scheduler does not start a firmware wave on that device during the test.
6. **Rollback of this change.** If bench fails, revert this PR. No schema or data migration is involved. Old responses lacked `rollback_verified`, so a revert only removes the new fields and the lock.
7. **Waves.** This PR does not change the firmware rollout engine or `rollout_gate.py`. Waves stay 10% → 50% → 100%, one wave per window. No wave test is needed beyond a check that the scheduler status is unchanged after the test.

## Risks and limits
- The hash check is strict. If Tachyon firmware normalizes config on apply, valid rollbacks will report 502. Bench step 3 must check this first.
- The lock is in process memory, like the existing push lock. It does not cover a second Manager process.
- The auto-enforce rollback paths are out of scope here.

## Documentation
- Docs changed: none.
- CHANGELOG: added under Unreleased, Fixed.

title: feat(discoveryengine): trace Google Discovery Engine search and answer calls (TH-8332)
body:
## Summary
New Python package `traceAI-discoveryengine` (`python/frameworks/discoveryengine`, import `traceai_discoveryengine`, 0.1.0). It instruments the search and answer calls of the `google-cloud-discoveryengine` client (Google Discovery Engine / Vertex AI Search).

**Why a wrapper.** The client emits no spans of its own (AC-01). At 0.20.5, an uninstrumented `search`, `search_lite` or `answer_query` produces no span. That holds even with `GOOGLE_SDK_EXPERIMENTAL_PYTHON_TRACING_ENABLED=true`, because google-api-core traces only methods whose transport passes `method_name`, and these transports pass none (`google/api_core/gapic_v1/method.py:290-295` at google-api-core 2.40.0, `:292-296` at 2.41.0, `search_service/transports/base.py:150-159`). The first commit (`efe02e3`) measures this before any wrapper exists. With `opentelemetry-instrumentation-grpc` added, you get transport spans only, with no query, result count or retriever kind.

**Spans:**
- **Methods wrapped.** Exactly six v1 methods, one span per user call:
  - `SearchServiceClient.search` and `.search_lite`;
  - `ConversationalSearchServiceClient.answer_query`;
  - the async twins of all three.
- **Span names and kind.** `discoveryengine.search`, `discoveryengine.search_lite` and `discoveryengine.answer_query`, all with `fi.span.kind=RETRIEVER`.
- **Nesting.** The span is current during the RPC, so gRPC spans nest under it. Nested wrapped calls add no span.

**Attributes:**
- `discoveryengine.serving_config` and `discoveryengine.result_count`.
  - For search, the count covers the first page.
  - For answers, it is the number of `references`.
- `discoveryengine.answer.length`, `discoveryengine.answer.state`, `discoveryengine.session`.
- `discoveryengine.error.status` and `.code`, `discoveryengine.cancelled`.
- No model, token or cost keys. The 0.20.5 answer response carries no model field (`types/conversational_search_service.py:1332-1367`).

**Privacy:**
- **Query.** Query text is off by default. `capture_query=True` records `gen_ai.retrieval.query` and `input.value`.
- **Query in error text.** Whenever the query is not recorded (the default, or `hide_inputs`), every verbatim copy is removed from error text. Removal happens after credential removal and before PII redaction and the caps.
- **Credentials** are removed wherever the client keeps them:
  - transport credentials: token, refresh token, client secret;
  - `client_options.api_key`;
  - per-call `authorization` / `x-goog-api-key` metadata;
  - token shapes: `ya29.`, `AIza…`, `1//…`.
- **Fail-closed.** If the credential store cannot be read, no query and no error text is recorded. The package never triggers ADC or a token refresh.
- **FITracer.** Spans come from `FITracer`, so TraceConfig masking, `pii_redaction` and `using_*` context apply.

**Errors:**
- The status code comes from `google-api-core`; for a `RetryError`, it is taken from the last attempt.
- Message is capped at 1 KB and the stacktrace at 16 KB, both after redaction.
- The exception is re-raised unchanged. A FAILED answer state is returned, not raised, as ERROR `answer state FAILED`.

**Robustness.** Instrumentation failures never reach the caller. `uninstrument()` restores each original by identity. `google.genai` is not imported or instrumented (AC-09).

**Versions:**
- `google-cloud-discoveryengine>=0.20.5,<1`; only 0.20.5 was tested.
- `fi-instrumentation-otel>=1.1.0`.
- Python 3.10, 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13.

## Deviations from the spec (with pinned vendor evidence; approved: Nikhil 2026-10-03 blanket)
- **D1 pagination (PRD J4):** later pages are separate RPCs issued by the pager through the transport method (`search_service/client.py:814,837`, `pagers.py:100-110`), not through `search()`. Following the architecture, the package records one span per call, and `result_count` covers the first page. Tested and documented.
- **D2 model attribute (PRD R-04/J3):** never written, because 0.20.5 responses carry no model field. Tested.
- **D3 v1 only:** the unversioned `google.cloud.discoveryengine` alias re-exports v1beta (`discoveryengine/__init__.py:52-55,136-139`). PRD section 3 targets v1, so the alias, v1beta and v1alpha produce no spans. Tested, and the README says so prominently.
- **D4 PRD G3** says a GCP project is needed even on the mocked import path. That is false: the suite runs with no project, ADC or credentials, and ADC is read only when a transport has neither credentials nor a channel (`transports/base.py:113-114`).
- **D5 scope:** `converse_conversation` and `stream_answer_query` are not wrapped. The architecture lists only search, search_lite and answer_query, and the architecture wins over the PRD.
- **D6 retries:** these methods have no default retry at 0.20.5. Success-after-retry and retry exhaustion each give one span (tested).
- **D9 test transport:** the wrapper tests use the real gRPC and gRPC-asyncio transports against a loopback gRPC fake. That covers real serialization, metadata, retries, paging and error mapping, which is stronger than `unittest.mock`. The AC-01 measurement keeps the mock transport the architecture specifies.
- **Runtime range:** the PRD gives `>=0.20.5,<1` rather than an exact pin. An exact pin would make `instrument()` a silent no-op on every other version (lesson from TH-8324 R6 / TH-8325 N1). The range is enforced at runtime and tested.

## Acceptance (PRD section 6)

| AC | Test |
|---|---|
| AC-01 stock spans | `test_discoveryengine_stock_spans.py` (first commit; also run with `opentelemetry-instrumentation-grpc`) |
| AC-03 search span | `test_discoveryengine_search.py` (exact attribute dict, search and search_lite) |
| AC-04 answer span, no model | `test_discoveryengine_answer.py` |
| AC-05 no admin spans | `test_discoveryengine_scope.py` (identity diff over every v1/v1alpha/v1beta client method) |
| AC-06 errors | `test_discoveryengine_errors.py` |
| AC-07 async parity | `test_discoveryengine_async.py` |
| AC-08 secrets | `test_discoveryengine_errors.py`, `test_discoveryengine_contract.py` (on the OTLP wire) |
| AC-09 not google.genai | `test_discoveryengine_scope.py` (fresh interpreter) |

Tests were written first. With no package present, they gave 51 failed, 7 passed and 4 collection errors, all `ModuleNotFoundError` or the missing example.

## Tests
Head `7ea99f1`. Coordinator rerun from the repo root on a clean tree (`tickets/TH-8332/exact-head-7ea99f1.txt`):
```
env -u PYTHONPATH PYTHONPATH="python/frameworks/discoveryengine:python:python/tests" uv run --no-project --python <py> \
  --with pytest --with pytest-asyncio --with opentelemetry-api --with opentelemetry-sdk --with opentelemetry-instrumentation \
  --with opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http --with wrapt --with requests --with jsonschema --with protobuf \
  --with opentelemetry-proto --with 'google-cloud-discoveryengine==0.20.5' \
  pytest python/frameworks/discoveryengine/tests -q -p no:cacheprovider --noconftest -o addopts= -rfEs
              README command   stock spans + opentelemetry-instrumentation-grpc (README second command)
Python 3.10   130 passed       6 passed   (Google FutureWarnings: Python 3.10 end of support)
Python 3.11   130 passed       6 passed
Python 3.12   130 passed       6 passed
Python 3.13   130 passed       6 passed
```
- **Outside the package:** three README table rows only: the root `README.md` package table and Compatibility Matrix, and the `python/README.md` package table. No secret-like lines were added (one test constant, `ya29.a0AfB_unseenTokenValue-123`, is a fake token shape used to prove a token minted during the call is removed).
- **Test harness:** real google-cloud-discoveryengine 0.20.5 clients over their own gRPC transports, against a loopback gRPC fake on 127.0.0.1. No Google credentials, ADC or GCP project.
- **Contract tests:** the real `register()` OTLP exporter sends into the shared harness `Receiver`, plus `harness.post_otlp()` of captured spans. They check `/tracer/v1/traces`, both auth headers, resource attributes, parentage, and that no credential, query or content is exported.

## Review round 1 (pr-reviewer t_6d02f969 APPROVE, pr-verifier t_eabd7921 VERIFIED at `e32e76d`)
No blocking findings. The behaviour-affecting P3s were fixed test-first before the demo (approved: Nikhil 2026-10-03 blanket); RED: the new tests against the `e32e76d` package code gave 13 failed, 111 passed (every failure a new regression test).
| Finding | Commit | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| R5: the wrapper consumed a one-shot `metadata` iterable, so the RPC could lose the caller's headers | `fe305e3` | `metadata` is read once and passed on as a tuple; if reading raises, the vendor gets the pairs read so far and the same error, and no free text is recorded (fail closed) |
| R2: a token minted during the call, and self-signed JWTs | `651c124` | credentials are read again when an error is recorded (attribute reads only); a JWT shape (`eyJ…`, three base64url parts) joins the token shapes |
| N1 / R1: escaped copies of a hidden query in error text | `ef7bf59` | the query's repr, JSON, protobuf-text and CHexEscape copies are removed too, longest first |
| R6: the switch-on stock-span run was not in the documented gate | `19d5076` | README Tests has the second command (`--with opentelemetry-instrumentation-grpc`) |
| R4: v1beta import | `19d5076` | v1 only, kept; README says `from google.cloud import discoveryengine` gives no spans and to import `discoveryengine_v1` |
| R3 | - | refuted by the verifier; unchanged |

## Review round 2 (pr-verifier t_a88e29ab VERIFIED at `19d5076`)
No P1/P2 findings. One P3 was fixed before the demo, because it was a gap in this PR's own privacy claim (approved: Nikhil 2026-10-03 blanket):
- **NEW-1:** protobuf text format writes ASCII control characters other than `\n`, `\r` and `\t` (and DEL) as 3-digit octal (`\013`), and none of the hidden-query copies had that form. With `capture_query` off, a query containing for example a vertical tab or ESC that a status detail quotes stayed in the error text.
- **Fix:** `7ea99f1`. `_c_escaped` now writes those characters as octal.
- **Tests:** a new test pins `_c_escaped` to the installed protobuf's own `str()` of a `FieldViolation`, covering all of 0x00-0x1F, DEL, quotes, backslash and non-ASCII. An end-to-end test sends `\x0b`, `\x1b` and `\x7f` through the loopback fake's `BadRequest` detail, in both default and `hide_inputs` mode.
- **RED:** against `19d5076` the new tests gave 4 failed: both end-to-end hide cases and two protobuf-pin cases.

## Review round 3 (pr-verifier t_92a1c3c5 VERIFIED at `7ea99f1`)
No P1/P2 findings. NEW-1 is fixed for both protobuf backends' string-field escaping rules, and the new tests pin `_c_escaped` to the installed protobuf output. Retained P3 (post-merge follow-up): **NEW-2**, an unknown custom `Any` detail can expose non-ASCII UTF-8 bytes of a hidden query as octal in error text; it is pre-existing (not introduced by this delta). The demo and the companion docs state it; the README does not yet name it. Proposed follow-up: add the bytes-field octal form to the hidden-query copies and a README sentence.

Remaining follow-ups, not in this PR:
- **R4 (product):** whether to also wrap v1beta (the unversioned alias).
- **R2 residual:** a token minted on api-core's scoped-credentials copy is removed by shape only (`ya29.`/`eyJ`). This is documented.

## Limits
- No live Google endpoint; behaviour against real error texts and answer payloads is unverified.
- Only 0.20.5 was tested; `<1` admits untested 0.21+. Only the gRPC transports were exercised (REST goes through the same wrapped methods but is untested).
- Query hiding matches the verbatim text and the escaped copies the client libraries produce (Python repr, JSON, protobuf text format including its octal escapes, gRPC CHexEscape); a reworded or truncated server copy is not matched, and a very short query over-redacts. `filter` and `user_pseudo_id` are not removed from server error text.
- A token carried by caller-built gRPC call credentials on a channel instance is invisible to the package; only token shapes are removed.
- With `pii_redaction`, a GCP project number in a resource name loses its last ten digits, and FITracer's second PII pass can push an attribute a few bytes past the 1 KB cap.
- The 16 KB stacktrace cap keeps the head; `exception.message` keeps the message.
- Not done here:
  - the PRD 9.3 round trip through a real fi-collector and backend;
  - the two-project tenant check (PRD 9.5);
  - a run against the published `fi-instrumentation-otel` 1.1.0 wheel (the suite ran on the in-repo source).

## Video demo
**Recorded build:** head `7ea99f125aa0a1b26804eed39975529dfd107bd1` (this PR), real CLI chapters run from a clean worktree; 6:48, 11 chapters, narrated with captions.

The video, captions (SRT), transcript, chapter list, preview, terminal-evidence ZIP and media-verification notes are private attachments on Linear issue **TH-8332** (Future AGI workspace; sign-in required). They are not linked here as raw upload URLs.

Chapters: problem and safe test setup · exact revision and change boundary · stock SDK produces no retrieval spans · real `register` exporter to the harness Receiver · error privacy without changing caller errors · hidden query copies and capture-on control (NEW-1 octal fix) · one-shot metadata preserved · async clients match sync shape · committed metadata and redaction source · executed tests and logged Python matrix · verified review and explicit limitations.

Independent media checks (Rick): full audio/video decode exit 0, 11 embedded chapters match the chapter list, no audio gaps over 1.5 s, end-of-chapter frames inspected, 77 files/ZIP members scanned with zero secret or path/port/header hits. The video uses the real Google client and gRPC transport against a local fake; it does not show live Google access, a running fi-collector, tenant isolation, storage or a rendered trace view.

Companion docs/architecture drafts were corrected to this head in company-brain #63 (`886fe7d`, open, unmerged).

Stacked on #203 (shared harness, `3eaadc8`), base `dev`. Not merged.

title: [Cherry-pick][releases/v0.30.0][Performance][MoE] Improve shared expert multistream overlap
body:
## What this PR does / why we need it

Backport #17255 to `releases/v0.30.0`. The registered shared-expert linear-wrapper path previously submitted dynamic activation quantization only after the routed MoE path had been queued. This backport submits Gate-Up input preparation on the auxiliary stream before the internal Router MatMul, submits Gate-Up after `router_output_ready` but before routed TopK/dispatch, and retains backend-specific activation/Down and combine milestones.

The v0.30.0 branch has independent MoE fixes. This backport preserves its existing pre-cast Router Gate behavior, its registered-forward fallback for gates without `weight_fp32`, and its token-padding and communication changes. It adds a regression test for the no-precast fallback and early shared preparation.

Source: #17255 (head `316033ee29e22a02a81a49ebc6da2a59840b55b8`).

## Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

No API or configuration change. With shared-expert multistream overlap enabled, eligible quantized paths submit the same work earlier to expose more overlap.

## How was this patch tested?

- `ruff format --check` on all 21 changed Python files: passed.
- `ruff check` on all 21 changed Python files: passed.
- `python -m compileall -q` on all 21 changed Python files: passed.
- Targeted `mypy --follow-imports=skip --ignore-missing-imports` on `fused_moe.py` and `shared_experts.py`: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Targeted pytest could not collect on this Windows host because the matching `vllm` package is unavailable (`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'vllm'`).
- Ascend NPU correctness, graph-mode, profiling, and performance validation are **pending**. This PR remains draft until those checks are completed.

AI assistance was used for the backport and conflict resolution; the author should review the full diff before marking ready for review.

title: [Model][Qwen4Exp] FP8 QSA main KV cache on Ampere (sm_80, sm_86)
body:
## Summary

`--kv-cache-dtype fp8` crashes for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on Ampere (sm_80, sm_86): the QSA Triton kernels use an `fp8e4nv` pointer, which Triton supports only from sm_89. Below sm_89 this PR reads the e4m3 cache as bytes and decodes it exactly with a bit cast. Same flag and cache format; BF16 and sm_89+ do not change.

**Why Ampere:** vLLM already enables an FP8 KV cache on sm_80 for other backends (FlashInfer, #24577); this model's QSA path is the gap. We serve Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on 8× A100, where FP8 doubles the KV capacity, and @nkuhn-vmw runs it on 4× RTX 3090 (sm_86).

## Results (8× A100-40GB, TP8 + EP)

- Fixes the crash: 4 FP8 attention tests that fail on `main` at sm_80 now pass, plus a new decode test (55 → 60 pass).
- KV cache capacity ×1.83 (1.16M → 2.13M tokens). sm_86 (4× RTX 3090, by @nkuhn-vmw): ×1.87, GSM8K unchanged.
- Attention kernel time, FP8 vs BF16 cache: 0.92–1.14×. End to end at concurrency 8, client TPOT p50 is 6 % higher with FP8 (see "Decode cost").
- Prompt-logprob difference FP8 vs BF16 is close to BF16 run-to-run noise (σ 0.115 vs 0.111 nats, 150k tokens).
- Serving the full MLPerf agentic dataset (multi-turn coding, prompts up to ~200k tokens), 3 runs per row:

| Concurrency | KV cache | Requests/s | TTFT p95 (s) | Prefix-cache hit | Prompt tokens received / computed in prefill, per run (M) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | BF16 | 1.15–1.24 | 1.1–1.3 | 97–98 % | 301–319 / 5.0–7.8 |
| 8 | FP8 | 1.20–1.23 | 1.2 | 98.5 % | 322–326 / 4.7–4.9 |
| 12 | BF16 | 0.96–1.09 | 18–27 | 90–92 % | 235–277 / 21–23 |
| 12 | FP8 | **1.59** | **1.5** | 98.5 % | **457–462 / 6.8–7.1** |
| 16 | BF16 | 0.58–0.64 | 73–83 | 73–77 % | 126–143 / 32–33 |
| 16 | FP8 | **1.58–1.63** | **7.5–10.4** | 96–97 % | **426–445 / 14–15** |

At concurrency 16, FP8 serves 2.7× the requests with ~9× lower p95 TTFT: it receives 3.4× more prompt tokens but computes less than half as many in prefill, because more prefixes stay cached. At concurrency 12, FP8 serves 1.5–1.6× the requests with 12–18× lower p95 TTFT and computes about a third as many prompt tokens in prefill. No preemptions in either arm. Pending: a prefix-caching-off control, and a run without our scheduler hook.

## Changes

- `ops/qsa.py`: below sm_89, load e4m3 pages as `uint8` and decode with a bit cast (`2⁸` folded into the K/V scales on the host); on sm_80 FP8, 128-column / 4-warp tiles.
- `qsa.py`: below sm_89 with FP8, skip the fused prepare/cache-write kernel (also an FP8 pointer); use the separate path.
- Test: all 254 finite byte codes decode exactly.

**NaN:** below sm_89 the two e4m3 NaN codes decode to ±480, as in vLLM's merged bit-cast FP8 decoders (Marlin FP8 on Ampere, #5975; CPU FP8 KV attention, #39445). A NaN-preserving decode costs 2.2× kernel time on A100, so it is not included. Details and a question for reviewers are under "NaN handling".

No new CPU/GPU sync. Validated outside CI (no A100 in CI). Written with AI assistance (Claude Code); the submitter reviewed every line.

<details>
<summary>NaN handling</summary>

**What this PR does.** Below sm_89, the decode places the e4m3 sign, exponent and mantissa bits into an fp16 and folds `2⁸` into the scales. All 254 finite codes are exact. The two NaN codes (0x7F, 0xFF) decode to ±1.875 · 2⁸ = ±480. The cache can only hold a NaN code if a NaN was written: the CUDA cache writer uses `__nv_cvt_float_to_fp8(..., __NV_SATFINITE, ...)`, which saturates finite overflow to ±448.

**Merged vLLM precedents with the same behaviour:**

| Path | How FP8 is decoded | NaN codes become |
|---|---|---|
| Marlin FP8, Ampere weights (#5975, `csrc/.../marlin/dequant.h`) | bits placed into fp16/bf16 fields, bias by one multiply | finite (±480) |
| CPU FP8 KV attention, AMX/AVX-512 (#39445, `cpu_attn_amx.hpp`) | payload placed into a bf16 field, bias `2¹²⁰` folded into the K/V scales on the host, as here | finite (±480); its writer also clamps NaN input to ±448, so no NaN code is stored |
| ROCm FP8 weights (`w8a8_utils.py`, `fp8_utils.py`) | e4m3fn → e4m3fnuz | the fnuz NaN pattern is set to 0 |

TurboQuant (#38479) handles Ampere differently: it stores keys in Triton's `fp8e4b15`, so its cache format depends on the architecture. This PR keeps one e4m3 format on all architectures.

**What this kernel does with NaN today, on every architecture** (from the code): a NaN value element makes only that output element NaN. A NaN key makes the row's softmax normalizer NaN; `has_values = normalizer > 0` is then false and the row is written as zeros. So a NaN key is already not propagated on sm_89+.

**NaN-preserving decode, measured and not included.** We tried two variants on one A100 against this PR's kernel, on the same inputs:

| Variant | FP8 kernel time vs this PR (8 / 32 / 80 / 128 / 512 / 1,024 / 2,048 rows) |
|---|---|
| per-tile check of `byte & 0x7F` over K and V, NaN row at the end | 1.02 / 1.22 / 1.59 / 1.69 / 2.03 / 2.15 / 2.19 |
| branch-free decode (`(low + 1) & 0x80` sets the top fp16 exponent bit) | 1.00 / 1.26 / 1.62 / 1.86 / 2.26 / 2.25 / 2.35 |

**Question for reviewers:** is ±480 acceptable under the precedents above, or should NaN handling for this kernel be addressed for all architectures in a follow-up?

</details>

<details>
<summary>Decode cost</summary>

At concurrency 8 the BF16 cache does not limit anything, so this compares the decode cost of the two paths. Three runs per arm:

| | BF16 | FP8, this PR | Change (medians) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Client TPOT p50 (Endpoints) | 8.1–8.2 ms | 8.6–8.7 ms | +6 % |
| Request inter-token latency, mean (`vllm:inter_token_latency_seconds`: time between a request's output events; with MTP one event can carry several tokens) | 24.4–25.6 ms | 25.3–25.5 ms | +2.9 % |
| MTP mean acceptance length per verification step (1 + accepted / drafts) | 2.73–2.75 | 2.68–2.72 | −0.9 % |
| MTP draft acceptance rate | 0.576–0.583 | 0.560–0.573 | −0.8 points |
| Mean decode time per request (`vllm:request_decode_time_seconds`) | 3.98–4.12 s | 3.97–4.11 s | no change |

- The vLLM values are means over each run's window of `/metrics` scrapes. The windows come from the client's session markers and are approximate.
- The MTP difference is small, and these runs do not establish its cause.
- At concurrency 16, the request inter-token latency is 38–39 ms with FP8 and 50–55 ms with BF16, where BF16 decode shares the batch with more prefill.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Duplicate check</summary>

Earlier attempts in this area (unmerged):
- #59943 (closed): byte decode for this kernel. The code owner asked whether FP8 KV on Ampere is needed and normally supported; the author had no deployment that reached this path and closed it. This PR adds the deployment data and the serving results.
- #60491 (closed by its author in favour of this PR): a new `fp8_e5m2` dtype for Ampere. The code owner asked why e5m2 instead of e4m3; this PR keeps e4m3.
- #54846 (open): e4m3 and NVFP4 for QSA; its FP8 part landed as #55557, which this PR extends below sm_89.

```
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "QSA fp8"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "fp8e4nv"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "Qwen4Exp sm80"
```

- **#60491** (closed by its author in favour of this PR after a side-by-side test on sm_86) added a new `fp8_e5m2` dtype for Ampere and makes `fp8_e4m3` fail early below sm_89. This PR keeps the existing `fp8_e4m3` instead:
  - no new dtype or flag;
  - 3 mantissa bits (e5m2 has 2);
  - one cache format read the same way on all architectures.

  This answers the reviewer question on #60491: "Is there a reason we should support e5m2 instead of just e4m3?"
- **#54846** (open) targets sm_120 (e4m3 and nvfp4) and does not cover sm_80.
- **#59943** (closed) is the earlier byte-decode attempt for this kernel. It used an `exp2` decode and 32-column tiles, and had no serving data.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Tests and kernel timing</summary>

**Environment:**
- 8× A100-SXM4-40GB (sm_80), driver 570.124.06, CUDA 12.9.
- vLLM `81198e97` (`0.31.1rc1.dev88+g81198e97b`, image `vllm/vllm-openai:cu129-nightly-81198e97…`), with this PR's two files bound over the image's copies. Both files are byte-identical between 81198e97 and this PR's base.
- PyTorch 2.13.0+cu129, Triton 3.7.1, Python 3.12.3.

**Existing and new tests, one A100:**

```
python -m pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py
```

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| passed | 55 | 60 |
| failed | 13 | 9 |
| errors | 6 | 6 |

- **Fixed:**
  - `test_qsa_sparse_paged_attention_correctness[tp1_r1_fp8]`, `[tp1_r128_fp8]`, `[tp1_r2048_prefill_fp8]` and `[tp1_r2048_uniform_fp8]`, which fail on `main` with the error above;
  - the new 256-code decode test.

Each server runs alone on the 8 GPUs, one after another (BF16, BF16 again, FP8):

```
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 --served-model-name flash-fp8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 4 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --enforce-eager --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload": true}' --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype": "bf16"}' \
  --mamba-cache-dtype bfloat16 --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float32 \
  --kv-cache-dtype {bfloat16 | fp8}
```

Client steps (script below, sha256 `e8a77f55c7053dca05e7af47c0597c97b2feb96a3797f112900a6be271d957a2`):

```
python3 logprob_trace.py build   http://127.0.0.1:8000 out mlperf_agentic_inference_dataset.jsonl   # once, on the first BF16 server
python3 logprob_trace.py run     http://127.0.0.1:8000 out bf16_a    # then bf16_b and fp8, each on its own server
python3 logprob_trace.py compare out bf16_a bf16_b fp8
```

- `build` tokenizes through the server's `/tokenize` and fixes the prompt token ids once. Every server then gets the same ids, and `compare` checks their hashes.
- Prompt sources: the official MLPerf agentic dataset (sha256 above), and the Python standard library inside the vLLM image (`/usr/lib/python3.12/*.py`, sorted) for the code prompt and the needle haystack.
- `run` sends each prompt to `/v1/completions` with `max_tokens: 1, temperature: 0, prompt_logprobs: 1`. It keeps the logprob of the actual next prompt token at each position, and fails on a missing or non-finite value.
- `compare` reports, per prompt, the standard deviation and mean of the per-position difference, and the share of positions that differ by more than 1 nat.

```python
"""Per-position prompt-logprob trace and needle check against one running vLLM server (upstream #60602 evidence).

Method of vllm-project/vllm#55557: send identical prompt token ids with prompt_logprobs=1 at temperature 0, keep the
logprob of each actual next prompt token, and compare FP8-KV against BF16 with the BF16-vs-BF16 run-to-run noise as the
floor. Prompt ids are fixed once (build) and reused verbatim by every arm; each arm records the prompt hash it served.

This is a numerical diagnostic of the KV-cache dtype only (prefix caching and MTP off, eager). It is not a task-quality
or serving result. Every step fails loudly: a short source, a missing position or a non-finite logprob is an error.

  logprob_trace.py build   <base_url> <out_dir> <dataset.jsonl>
  logprob_trace.py run     <base_url> <out_dir> <arm>
  logprob_trace.py compare <out_dir> <arm_a> <arm_b> <arm_fp8>
"""
import hashlib
import json
import math
import os
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

MODEL = "flash-fp8"
TARGETS = {"agentic_150k": 150_000, "code_30k": 30_000, "text_8k": 8_000}
NEEDLE_TOKENS = 125_000
NEEDLE_DEPTHS = (0.1, 0.5, 0.9)
NEEDLE = "The secret passphrase for the archive is amber-falcon-42."
NEEDLE_ANSWER = "amber-falcon-42"
QUESTION = "\n\nQuestion: What is the secret passphrase for the archive? Answer: The secret passphrase is"
CODE_ROOT = Path("/usr/lib/python3.12")
METADATA_TYPE = "dataset_metadata"  # the full dataset's header row, skipped as MLCommons Endpoints does
REQUEST_SECONDS = 1500


def post(base, path, body):
    request = urllib.request.Request(base + path, json.dumps(body).encode(), {"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=REQUEST_SECONDS) as response:
        return json.loads(response.read())


def tokenize(base, text):
    return post(base, "/tokenize", {"model": MODEL, "prompt": text, "add_special_tokens": False})["tokens"]


def ids_sha256(ids):
    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(ids).encode()).hexdigest()


def write_private(path, value):
    path.write_text(json.dumps(value))
    os.chmod(path, 0o600)


def code_text(limit_chars):
    parts, size = [], 0
    for path in sorted(CODE_ROOT.glob("*.py")):
        text = path.read_text(errors="replace")
        parts.append(text)
        size += len(text)
        if size >= limit_chars:
            return "\n".join(parts)
    raise ValueError(f"code source has {size} characters, fewer than {limit_chars}")


def agentic_text(dataset, limit_chars):
    """Messages of the longest conversations, as role-tagged text, until limit_chars."""
    conversations = {}
    for line in open(dataset):
        row = json.loads(line)
        if row.get("_type") == METADATA_TYPE:
            continue
        text = " ".join(str(row.get(key) or "") for key in ("content", "reasoning_content", "tool_calls"))
        conversations.setdefault(row["conversation_id"], []).append(f"[{row['role']}] {text}")
    parts, size = [], 0
    for conversation in sorted(conversations.values(), key=lambda c: -sum(map(len, c))):
        for message in conversation:
            parts.append(message)
            size += len(message)
            if size >= limit_chars:
                return "\n".join(parts)
    raise ValueError(f"dataset text has {size} characters, fewer than {limit_chars}")


def exactly(ids, count, name):
    if len(ids) < count:
        raise ValueError(f"{name}: source gives {len(ids)} tokens, fewer than {count}")
    return ids[:count]


def build(base, out, dataset):
    out = Path(out)
    sources = {"agentic_150k": agentic_text(dataset, 1_200_000), "code_30k": code_text(300_000),
               "text_8k": agentic_text(dataset, 80_000)}
    prompts = {name: exactly(tokenize(base, sources[name]), TARGETS[name], name) for name in TARGETS}
    needle, question = tokenize(base, " " + NEEDLE + " "), tokenize(base, QUESTION)
    body = NEEDLE_TOKENS - len(needle) - len(question)
    haystack = exactly(tokenize(base, code_text(1_200_000)), body, "haystack")
    needles, positions = {}, {}
    for depth in NEEDLE_DEPTHS:
        name, at = f"needle_{int(depth * 100)}", int(body * depth)
        needles[name] = haystack[:at] + needle + haystack[at:] + question
        positions[name] = at
    write_private(out / "prompts.json", {"trace": prompts, "needle": needles})
    summary = {"lengths": {k: len(v) for k, v in {**prompts, **needles}.items()}, "needle_positions": positions,
               "sha256": {k: ids_sha256(v) for k, v in {**prompts, **needles}.items()}}
    write_private(out / "prompts-summary.json", summary)
    print(json.dumps(summary["lengths"]))


def trace(base, ids, name):
    result = post(base, "/v1/completions", {"model": MODEL, "prompt": ids, "max_tokens": 1, "temperature": 0,
                                            "prompt_logprobs": 1})
    choice, usage = result["choices"][0], result.get("usage") or {}
    rows = choice["prompt_logprobs"]
    if len(rows) != len(ids) or usage.get("prompt_tokens") != len(ids):
        raise ValueError(f"{name}: {len(rows)} logprob rows, usage {usage.get('prompt_tokens')}, sent {len(ids)}")
    values = []
    for position in range(1, len(ids)):
        chosen = (rows[position] or {}).get(str(ids[position]))
        if chosen is None or not math.isfinite(chosen["logprob"]):
            raise ValueError(f"{name}: no finite logprob for the prompt token at position {position}")
        values.append(chosen["logprob"])
    return values, {"usage": usage, "finish_reason": choice.get("finish_reason")}


def run(base, out, arm):
    out = Path(out)
    prompts = json.loads((out / "prompts.json").read_text())
    record = {"arm": arm, "trace": {}, "needle": {}, "seconds": {}, "api": {}, "sha256": {}}
    for name, ids in prompts["trace"].items():
        start = time.time()
        record["trace"][name], record["api"][name] = trace(base, ids, name)
        record["seconds"][name], record["sha256"][name] = time.time() - start, ids_sha256(ids)
    for name, ids in prompts["needle"].items():
        answer = post(base, "/v1/completions", {"model": MODEL, "prompt": ids, "max_tokens": 16, "temperature": 0})
        choice = answer["choices"][0]
        record["needle"][name] = {"text": choice["text"], "found": NEEDLE_ANSWER in choice["text"],
                                  "finish_reason": choice.get("finish_reason"), "usage": answer.get("usage")}
        record["sha256"][name] = ids_sha256(ids)
    write_private(out / f"{arm}.json", record)
    print(json.dumps({"arm": arm, "needle": {k: v["found"] for k, v in record["needle"].items()},
                      "seconds": record["seconds"]}))


def spread(first, second, name):
    if len(first) != len(second):
        raise ValueError(f"{name}: {len(first)} and {len(second)} positions differ")
    diffs = [b - a for a, b in zip(first, second)]
    mean = sum(diffs) / len(diffs)
    sigma = math.sqrt(sum((d - mean) ** 2 for d in diffs) / len(diffs))
    return {"positions": len(diffs), "sigma_nat": round(sigma, 4), "mean_nat": round(mean, 5),
            "share_over_1_nat": round(sum(abs(d) > 1 for d in diffs) / len(diffs), 5)}


def compare(out, arm_a, arm_b, arm_fp8):
    out = Path(out)
    a, b, f = (json.loads((out / f"{x}.json").read_text()) for x in (arm_a, arm_b, arm_fp8))
    if not a["sha256"] == b["sha256"] == f["sha256"]:
        raise ValueError("arms served different prompt ids")
    table = {name: {"bf16_noise": spread(a["trace"][name], b["trace"][name], name),
                    "fp8_vs_bf16": spread(a["trace"][name], f["trace"][name], name)} for name in a["trace"]}
    table["needle"] = {arm["arm"]: {k: v["found"] for k, v in arm["needle"].items()} for arm in (a, b, f)}
    write_private(out / "compare.json", table)
    print(json.dumps(table, indent=1))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    {"build": build, "run": run, "compare": compare}[sys.argv[1]](*sys.argv[2:])
```

title: fix(ci): run the base branch copy of the review checks, so older branches pass (#1561, #1563)
body:
Fixes the Review check failing on #1561 and #1563.

The workflow ran the check script and its self-tests from the PR head. A branch cut before the script existed has neither file, so the job failed with ImportError: Start directory is not importable: scripts/tests. Both #1561 and #1563 were branched before #1565.

The workflow now:
- takes the script and its self-tests from origin/<base> and runs them from the runner temp directory against the PR head;
- reports a notice and runs nothing when the base has no script.

It also means a PR cannot weaken the checks that judge it. A PR that changes the checks still runs its own copy of the tests in the spec-governance job. Spec 11.06 and the docs are updated to match.

Whole-Change-Verification: ran=the workflow steps emulated locally (the base copy of the 34 self-tests passes from outside the repo; the base copy reports 0 findings on the #1561 head ade65494 and the #1563 head 91899f93), YAML lint of the workflow, and python3 scripts/validate_specs.py --changed-base on be84678d (84 specs, PASSED); result=pass

title: The Mill into 0.6: app gateway + proxy security fixes
body:
Brings the Mill (#472, the app gateway) into integration/0.6, with the first security fixes from a first-principles review. When this lands, #472 is superseded.

## Commits
1. **Merge integration/0.6 into the Mill.** Two conflicts only (`git show --remerge-diff` shows nothing else): README takes integration's rewrite, which already covers `uv tool update-shell`; Settings keeps the Access tab and drops the removed Desktop tab.
2. **Gateway proxy: apps never see visitor credentials.**
   - The Access token header, every `cf-access-*` header and the `CF_Authorization` cookie are stripped before proxying. All apps share one Access audience, so a token handed to app A opened app B as that visitor.
   - Apps get one trusted header, `x-woltspace-user`, set by the gateway after its checks. Any copy the visitor sends is dropped.
   - Hop-by-hop headers are dropped both ways.
   - The upstream timeout bounds only connect/pool. Quiet streams (SSE, long polls) no longer die after httpx's 5s default, and any upstream HTTP error is a 502 instead of an unhandled 500.
   - The websocket bridge carries binary frames. When either side ends, the other is cancelled and the visitor's socket closes. Before this it hung forever.
3. **Merge leftovers:** a duplicated `_starter_seed_lock` in `server/state.py`, and a dead `ImportError` fallback around `.access`.

## Tests
New tests in `test/test_app_gateway.py`: credential stripping, identity header (spoofed copy replaced), cookie-only-Access case, timeout -> 502, binary frames + identity over a real websocket server, and close propagation (with a 10s guard so a regression fails instead of hanging). Four fail on the old proxy; the close test hung outright on it.

CI's focused list + the Mill test files in a clean env: 588 passed, 3 skipped. Node: 58 passed.

## Not in this PR (parked for a decision)
- Apps whose manifest says `"public": true` still open an unauthenticated per-app quick tunnel that bypasses the gateway. Seeds can't set it (seed install forces `public: false`), but a wolt can. Removing it also removes app sharing for lodges without their own domain.
- A remote lodge request with no Access settings is let in unchecked (also true on main). The gateway already refuses that case.

## Before integration/0.6 goes to main
A throwaway-lodge run from a fresh install: gateway, an app, a websocket, a shared visitor.

title: ci(prompt-eval): skip the model A/B for dependency-only changes; import smoke instead
body:
## Why

`poetry.lock` is listed in the `shared_files` of 6 of the 11 prompts (every non-judge prompt except `requirements-section` and `structured-fallback`; `src/cqc_cpcc/config/prompt_registry.json`), so that a change to the LLM request stack re-runs the prompt suites (docs/PROMPT_EVAL_PLAN.md: "the `poetry.lock` entries for pydantic/openai/langchain"). The detector matched the whole file, so any lockfile change ran every suite with model calls. #372 removes an unused dependency; its lock diff removes 36 packages and changes 6 other entries (colorama, humanfriendly, onnxruntime, orjson, pygments, uvicorn). It ran all 7 suites and `prompt-eval/ab` failed on run-to-run variance with identical prompts (run 38021500255).

## What

- `prompts-affected` (`src/cqc_cpcc/model_eval/prompt_automation.py`): when every changed path is in the dependency-only class below, it compares `poetry.lock` with the base and counts it as a prompt change only when a package inside the **LLM request stack** changed.
  - The request stack is the transitive dependency closure of `openai`, `pydantic`, `httpx`, `tiktoken`, `langsmith`, `openrouter` and every `langchain*` package, computed from the `[package.dependencies]` tables of **both** the base and the head lock (60 of 285 packages in the current lock).
  - A package counts as changed when anything in its lock entry changes (version, source, file hashes, dependencies, markers, optional, groups, extras), per PEP 503-normalised name. A name listed more than once on either side (marker-split entries) always counts as changed.
  - If either lock cannot be read, the previous behaviour applies (all suites listing the lockfile).
- New output `dependency_only`: no suite to run or re-score, no judge prompt changed, and every changed path is `poetry.lock`, `pyproject.toml`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md` or a Markdown doc, with at least one of the first two. No `.py` file can be in that set.
- New job `dependency-smoke` (pull requests, when `dependency_only`), no secrets, $0:
  1. restores the cached virtualenv, then runs `poetry install --with test --sync`, so packages the head lock does not list are uninstalled;
  2. `scripts/import_smoke.py --import cqc_cpcc --resolve cqc_streamlit_app --removed-since origin/<base>`: imports every `cqc_cpcc` module (catching `BaseException` per module); resolves every absolute import statement in both packages' source with `importlib.util.find_spec`, function-level imports included (relative, standard-library, first-party and `try/except ImportError` imports are skipped and counted); fails if any package removed from the lock since the base is still installed;
  3. uploads the log as `prompt-eval-dependency-smoke-<run id>`.
- `report` sets `prompt-eval/ab` to success, "No prompt suites affected (dependency-only change; import smoke passed)", or failure if the smoke job fails.
- docs/PROMPTS.md: trigger table, the closure rule, smoke coverage (`cqc_streamlit_app` by resolution only; the UI is exercised by the required `e2e-tests` check), Dependabot auto-merge interplay, who acts on a failed smoke and how to re-run it, and the known limit that `detect` runs the PR head's detector.
- Unchanged: secrets handling, the `prompt-eval` environment, trusted-author gating, the merge-queue mirror, thresholds, push-to-master behaviour.

## Behaviour

| Change | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `poetry.lock` only, no change inside the request-stack closure | all suites with model calls | no suites; dependency smoke; `prompt-eval/ab` from the smoke ($0) |
| `poetry.lock` only, any change inside the closure (a root, or e.g. `typing-extensions`, `h11`, `certifi`; same-version source or hash edits; marker-split entries) | all suites listing the lockfile | same |
| `poetry.lock` + a prompt source file | all suites listing the lockfile | same |
| `poetry.lock` + any other non-doc file | all suites listing the lockfile | same |
| `poetry.lock` + a judge prompt | suites + judges | judges as before; no smoke |
| Docs only | no suites | same |
| Lock unreadable | all suites | same |

Note on #372: under this rule its lock diff changes `colorama` and `orjson` markers, both inside the closure, so #372 still runs the suites after a rebase.

## Cost

Removes model spend for dependency-only PRs. The smoke job is one install plus imports (no API keys).

## Rollback

Revert this PR. Lockfile changes then trigger every suite again.

## Checks

- CI on bc255a8: all required checks pass. unit-tests run 38034445725: 2424 passed, 2 skipped, 80 deselected; it includes `tests/unit/test_import_smoke.py::test_first_party_packages_pass_the_smoke`, which runs `scripts/import_smoke.py --import cqc_cpcc --resolve cqc_streamlit_app` over the installed package (no network). integration-tests 38034445670, e2e-tests 38034445765, model-registry-guard 38034445678, Student PII guard 38034445710, CodeQL 38034445712: pass. codecov/patch: 88.13% of diff hit (target 80.00%).
- Prompt Evaluation run 38034445741: detect reported `run: []`, `rescore: []`, `dependency_only: false`, so estimate/rescore/ab/dependency-smoke were skipped and `prompt-eval/ab` = success "No prompt suites affected", with no model calls. This PR changes `.py` files, so `dependency-smoke` does not run on it; its first real run will be on a lockfile-only PR.
- Import smoke with `--removed-since origin/master` on the full command: local, unverified in CI (0 failures, 0 removed packages). Against #372's lock in an unsynced local environment it reports chromadb and other removed packages as still installed, which is the case `--sync` prevents.

title: test: start every in-container process in a minimal real container on a GPU-less host
body:
## Problem

Moving agents into Docker moved several processes from the host into the editor container, and each silently depended on the host's environment, Python path, `/tmp`, groups or uids (#1595, #1589, #1587, D18). No test started them in a real container on a host without GPUs, so each was found in a live run. Closes #1614.

## Solution

An opt-in tier in the style of #1606: marker `minimal_container`, env var `VIBESYS_MINIMAL_CONTAINER=1`, a session fixture, `scripts/run_minimal_container_tests.sh`, and a "Minimal-container tier" section in `docs/contributing/development.md`. Real Docker, no LLM, no GPU.

For each default base image (`cpu`, `cuda`, `rocm`, taken from the backends, so a changed default changes the tier) the fixture opens the editor through `open_run_environment` on the `slurm-gpu` environment: the real `docker build` of the agent layer, production's mounts, env and uid remap, and a real host broker whose `srun` is a local program. The editor holds no accelerator, so nothing runs on a GPU. It then starts, in the container:

| Process | How it is started | Check |
|---|---|---|
| `claude` | `claude --version` | exits 0 |
| `codex app-server` | `docker exec -i` | answers `initialize` |
| core evaluation tool server | the descriptor from `AgentEvaluationBridge.servers` | MCP `initialize`, tools equal `CORE_EVALUATION_TOOLS` |
| per-role evaluation tool server | `evaluation_mcp_descriptor` | MCP `initialize`, lists `submit_evaluation` |
| profiler MCP server | the `profiler` tool binding, support dir mounted as a run mounts it | MCP `initialize`, lists tools |
| `vibesys-gate`, `vibesys-gpu` | the view's gate commands | a gate and a job run through the broker; the benchmark result lands in the workspace |
| agent identity | `id`, `getent` | user and group are both `agent`, ids equal the host's |

A small stand-in base (`ubuntu:24.04`, which owns uid 1000 as `ubuntu`) runs only the identity check, so a host that cannot pull the large images still covers #1589.

**Findings.** The tier found four bugs beyond the three it was written for. Each is filed and marked as a strict expected failure (`expect_failure_for(..., issue)`, as the #1606 tier does), so fixing one fails the tier until the marker is removed:

- #1625: the linux-cpu profiler server cannot import `vs_runtime` in the Docker editor.
- #1626: the per-role evaluation server has the #1595 import failure still (only the core-run descriptor was fixed).
- #1627: on the ROCm default image `python` is conda Python 3.10, so the core evaluation server and rocprof server die on `StrEnum`.
- #1589 (open PR): the base image's uid-1000 group is not renamed. The tier shows it on the ROCm image (`jenkins`), the CUDA image (`ubuntu`) and the stand-in; on a host whose uid is 1000 the sandbox skips the remap, so only the identity check sees it.

### Design

- Owner: `tests/minimal_container`, beside `tests/slurm_cluster`; it reuses that tier's `docker` helpers.
- Interface: no production interface changes. The tier uses public APIs (`open_run_environment`, `create_compute_backend`, the bridge and descriptors).
- Direction: tests depend on the product, never the reverse; no `tach.toml` edge.
- Drift: the editor is opened through `SlurmGpuEnvironment` because it is the existing environment that brings a broker without a cluster. The tier does not depend on the split: when the environments are unified (D260) only `editor.py`'s environment construction changes.

### Architecture

n/a: tests only.

## Verification

### Correctness properties

- Each process above starts and answers a basic request inside the container on every selected base image.
- The tier fails at the merge base of each fix it was asked to cover (see Testing).

### Testing

- `scripts/run_minimal_container_tests.sh` with bases `cpu,rocm,ubuntu-uid-1000` (images cached): 15 passed, 7 expected failures, 51 s wall, about 15 s per base. A cold agent layer on the Ubuntu stand-in took 4 min 28 s (apt, Node and four CLIs); the CPU and ROCm layers were already cached.
- CUDA: the agent layer builds on `nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:25.04-py3` (checked with a `docker-container` BuildKit builder, 6 min 38 s cold, which also showed `existing=ubuntu` for uid 1000). This host's containerd store has a leaked snapshot that makes `docker pull` of that image fail (`unable to prepare extraction snapshot: AlreadyExists`), so the CUDA container tests were not run here.
- Merge bases, with this tier copied onto a checkout of the parent commit:
  - parent of #1587 (`9de4e3c67^`), `rocm`: the editor fails to start with `Unable to find group render: no matching entries in group file`.
  - parent of #1595 (`9f5214270^`), `cpu`: `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'vs_evaluation'` from `vs_evaluation.agent_core_mcp`.
  - #1589 is open, so its merge base is `main`: with `--runxfail`, the identity check fails on `rocm` (`['agent', 'jenkins']`) and the stand-in (`['agent', 'ubuntu']`).
- `./scripts/check_format.sh`, `./scripts/check_lint.sh`, `./scripts/check_types.sh`, `check_tach.py`, `check_test_isolation.py`, `check_lint_waivers.py`: clean. Without the env var the tier is skipped (`pytest tests/minimal_container tests/architecture`: 294 passed, 43 skipped).
